confirmed.title: Pages deploy trusts workflow_run.head_branch == 'main', so a fork pull request from a branch named main gets built with secrets and deployed to the production Pages site
confirmed.description: deploy-pages.yml runs on `workflow_run` after any completed 'Drider CI' run. Drider CI also runs on `pull_request`, including pull requests from forks. The build job's only check is `github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' && github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == 'main'`. For a fork pull request, head_branch is the fork's branch name, so a fork whose branch is called `main` passes the check. The job then checks out `github.event.workflow_run.head_sha`, which is the fork's commit (GitHub can fetch it through refs/pull). It runs `flutter pub get` and `flutter build web` on that attacker-controlled tree, with `secrets.newmap131189` in the environment and a job token that has `pages: write` and `id-token: write`. `deploy-pages@v4` then publishes the result. A workflow_run event runs in the default-branch context, so the github-pages environment's default-branch rule does not stop it. Nothing checks `workflow_run.event == 'push'` or `workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository`. The concurrency key (`pages-${{ ... github.event.workflow_run.head_branch ... }}`, line 21) also puts that fork run into the `pages-main` group, where `cancel-in-progress: true` lets it cancel a real main deployment.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An outside contributor forks the repository and opens a pull request from their fork's `main` branch, changing web/index.html or lib/ to show a phishing page. If CI runs without approval and passes, deploy-pages builds the fork's head_sha with the maps secret and publishes it to the official Movera Driver Pages URL. Any running main deployment in the `pages-main` concurrency group is cancelled.
confirmed.evidence:
deploy-pages.yml:3-8 `on: workflow_run: workflows: [Drider CI] types: [completed]`
deploy-pages.yml:26-33 `if: ... github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' && github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == 'main'`
deploy-pages.yml:39 `ref: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_run' && github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.sha }}`
deploy-pages.yml:53 `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.newmap131189 }}`
deploy-pages.yml:11-14 `pages: write`, `id-token: write` (workflow level, so the build job has them too)
drider-ci.yml:9-12 `pull_request: branches: [main, 'audit/phase-*']`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Also require `github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push'` and `github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository` in the `if:` and in the concurrency key. Move `pages`/`id-token` permissions to the deploy job only.

confirmed.title: An OSRM 'continue' or 'new name' step with a turning modifier (uturn, left, right, sharp …) reads "Continue straight 300 m" while the arrow shows the turn
confirmed.description: In RouteInstructionCopy.cue, the continueStraight/newName branch special-cases only highway 'slight left'/'slight right' and tunnel/toll. Every other modifier falls through to RouteCueKind.continueStraight. OSRM routinely emits type 'continue' with modifier 'left'/'right'/'sharp …', which osrm-text-instructions reads as "Turn left to stay on X", and 'continue' + 'uturn' for turnarounds ("Make a U-turn"). symbolFor() handles the same step correctly: the uturn branch at line 879 and the modifier switch at 909-921 draw a U-turn or left arrow. NavigationController._bannerFor (navigation_controller.dart:575-588) builds banner.primary and banner.instruction from cue(), so the words contradict the arrow. Because continueStraight isOnward, the line is also worded as cruising ('Continue straight 300 m') instead of 'in 300 m'. build() at 573-575 has the same gap ('Continue on X').
confirmed.failure_scenario: The route reaches a junction where the main road bends left (OSRM: {type:'continue', modifier:'left'}), or OSRM routes a U-turn as {type:'continue', modifier:'uturn'}. The trip banner and island read "Continue straight 300 m" while the icon shows a left or U-turn arrow. A driver who trusts the words drives straight on.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In the continueStraight/newName branch, return _turn(modifier) for any modifier other than ''/'straight' (and map 'uturn*' to uTurn), the same way the turn branch does. Mirror this in build().

verdicts.reason: osrm_route_parser maps OSRM 'continue' and 'new name' to RouteManeuverType.continueStraight/newName (route_instruction.dart:364-383). In cue() (route_instruction.dart:651-663) that branch special-cases only highway slight left/right and tunnel/toll. Every other modifier (uturn, left, right, sharp) returns RouteCueKind.continueStraight. symbolFor (route_instruction.dart:879-921) does honour uturn and turn modifiers, and NavigationController._bannerFor (navigation_controller.dart:575-599) uses cue() for primary/instruction and instruction.symbol for the arrow. So the words and the arrow contradict each other on a main navigation path. build() at route_instruction.dart:573-575 has the same gap.
verdicts.repro: Wrote throwaway test test/_audit_u39c_test.dart calling RouteInstructionCopy.cue + livePrimary(meters:300, strings: AppLocalizationsEn()) and symbolFor for type continueStraight. Output: 'uturn -> Continue straight 300 m / NavigationBannerSymbol.uTurnLeft', 'left -> Continue straight 300 m / NavigationBannerSymbol.left', 'sharp right -> Continue straight 300 m / NavigationBannerSymbol.sharpRight'; 'All tests passed!'. File deleted afterwards.

verdicts.reason: In RouteInstructionCopy.cue (route_instruction.dart:651-663), the continueStraight/newName branch maps every modifier except highway slight left or right to RouteCueKind.continueStraight. symbolFor (lines 879-884 and 909-921) maps the same steps to U-turn, left, sharp right and so on. OsrmRouteParser keeps OSRM's type 'continue' unchanged (route_instruction.dart:382-383), and NavigationController._bannerFor (navigation_controller.dart:575-588) builds banner.primary and banner.instruction from cue() but takes the symbol from instruction.symbol. So the live trip banner's words contradict its arrow. OSRM does emit continue+left/right where the road continues through a turn, and continue+uturn for turnarounds, so this is the main navigation path.

"Continue straight 300 m" symbol=NavigationBannerSymbol.left'; 'sharp right -> ... "Continue straight 300 m" symbol=NavigationBannerSymbol.sharpRight'; 'slight left -> ... "Continue straight 300 m" symbol=NavigationBannerSymbol.slightLeft'. All tests passed.

confirmed.title: A screen-reader scroll action on the trip slide runs the trip step with no confirmation dialog
confirmed.description: PHASE_53 says assistive-technology activation of the slide shows a confirmation dialog before the trip action runs. Only the Semantics onTap (_accessibleConfirm) does that. The inner GestureDetector has onHorizontalDragUpdate/onHorizontalDragEnd and is not excluded from semantics, so Flutter's RawGestureDetector adds SemanticsAction.scrollLeft/scrollRight to the same node. In Flutter (checked in /opt/flutter widgets/gesture_detector.dart:1786-1806 and rendering/proxy_box.dart:4253), scrollRight calls onHorizontalDragUpdate with delta = size.width*0.8 and then calls onEnd straight away. _update sets _fraction = 0.8w/(w-58) >= 0.78, which snaps to 1. _finish() then sees _fraction >= _trigger and awaits widget.onConfirmed(), which is _advanceRide(): Start trip, Complete trip, Go to stop. No dialog is shown. The regression test (test/audit/accessible_confirmation_test.dart) only fires SemanticsAction.tap.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A VoiceOver user focuses the slide ('Complete trip') and does a three-finger horizontal swipe, or a TalkBack user does the scroll gesture. The trip advances (completed, or started before the rider boards) with no 'Confirm this trip action?' dialog.
confirmed.evidence:
accept_ride.dart:1670-1681
  return Semantics(
    button:true, enabled:!_confirming,
    label:widget.label.replaceFirst('Slide to ',''),
    onTap:_confirming ? null : _accessibleConfirm,
    child:FocusableActionDetector(...
      child:GestureDetector(
        behavior: HitTestBehavior.opaque,
        onHorizontalDragUpdate: (details) => _update(details.delta.dx, maxTravel),
        onHorizontalDragEnd: (_) => _finish(),
accept_ride.dart:1619-1624 _update: _fraction = next >= _trigger ? 1 : next;
accept_ride.dart:1631-1637 _finish: if (_fraction < _trigger) {...return;} ... await widget.onConfirmed();
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass excludeFromSemantics: true to the slide's GestureDetector (or wrap it in ExcludeSemantics/BlockSemantics), so the only assistive path is the Semantics onTap that opens the confirmation dialog. Add a test that performs SemanticsAction.scrollRight and expects no stage change.

verdicts.reason: The slide's GestureDetector (accept_ride.dart:1676-1681) is not excluded from semantics, so its horizontal-drag recognizers add scrollLeft/scrollRight actions to the same node as the Semantics onTap (accept_ride.dart:1670-1673). When scrollRight runs, Flutter sends a drag update of 0.8*width followed by an end. _update (1619-1625) snaps _fraction to 1, and _finish (1633-1645) then awaits onConfirmed, which is _advanceRide (accept_ride_panel.dart:941-944). _accessibleConfirm's dialog is never shown. The existing test accessible_confirmation_test.dart only performs SemanticsAction.tap.

It pumps AcceptRide at waitingForRider, finds the 'start trip' semantics node and performs SemanticsAction.scrollRight. Output: 'hasScrollRight=true hasScrollLeft=true' and then 'DIALOG=0 STAGE=ActiveRideStage.onTrip'. The trip started with no confirmation dialog. I deleted the file afterwards.

verdicts.reason: The slide's GestureDetector (accept_ride.dart:1710-1715, onHorizontalDragUpdate/End) is not excluded from semantics, so it adds scrollLeft/scrollRight to the slide's node. A scrollRight action sends a drag delta of about 0.8 x width, which _update (accept_ride.dart:1653-1660) snaps to _fraction = 1 since it is at least _trigger 0.78. _finish (1667-1680) then awaits widget.onConfirmed() directly. The confirmation dialog in _accessibleConfirm (1682-1692) is skipped. The existing regression test only exercises SemanticsAction.tap.

confirmed.title: Terminal exits call Navigator.pop() on whatever route is on top, so a rider cancel (or any authoritative outcome) while Chat/Preferences/a modal sheet is open leaves the dead trip screen mounted
confirmed.description: Every authoritative exit from the trip screen ends with a plain pop of the navigator: `_handleRiderCancelled` (lines 452-458 `final home = Navigator.of(context); if (next == null && home.canPop()) { IslandMessages.show(...); ... home.pop(); return; }` and 478-481), `_leaveAfterAuthoritativeOutcome` (388-389), `_leaveAfterRelease` (403-407) and `_submitTripCancellation` (1444-1446). `Navigator.pop()` removes the topmost route, not the AcceptRide route. The trip screen itself pushes other routes onto the same navigator while the trip is live: `_messageRider` pushes `Chat` (accept_ride_panel.dart:860-867), `_openRidePreferences` pushes `Preferences` (536-541), `_openDestinationPicker` pushes the picker, the island pushes `DriverRideHistory` (accept_ride.dart:1307-1308), plus modal sheets (trip options, rider profile, cash collect, waiting time, safety toolkit, the accessible-confirm AlertDialog). A realtime `rider_cancelled`/terminal/`searching` event arriving while any of those is on top therefore pops that page instead of the trip: `_handleRiderCancelled` has already journaled the cancel, set the lifecycle terminal, run `_pauseLiveUpdates()` (GPS off, wait timer off), `_waybills.discardCurrent()` and queued an island notice for a Home that is never shown. The driver is left on a terminal AcceptRide: the slide/arrive actions return silently (`_advanceRide` checks `_rideLifecycle.terminal`), cancel says it cannot be cancelled, `PopScope(canPop:false)` blocks Back. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test (Home -> AcceptRide waiting -> a page pushed on top -> `realtime.emit(riderCancelled)`): result `chatPopped=true tripStillMounted=true homeVisible=false island=Rider cancelled`. Rider cancelling while the driver is in the chat with that rider is a very plausible sequence.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver is waiting at pickup, opens Message rider (Chat page on top). The rider cancels; realtime delivers rider_cancelled. The Chat page closes, the trip screen stays with GPS stopped and the waybill discarded; nothing on it works any more and Back is blocked. The 'Rider cancelled' island notice is queued for Home, which is not reached.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pop to the trip's own route instead of the top route: capture `ModalRoute.of(context)` in the trip state and use `navigator.popUntil((r) => r != tripRoute && !r.isCurrent ...)` / `removeRoute`-style exit (e.g. `Navigator.of(context).popUntil((route) => route.isFirst)` when Home is the root, or `navigator.removeRoute(tripRoute)` after closing routes above it); for the `pushReplacement` branches first pop everything above the trip route.

verdicts.reason: _handleRiderCancelled (accept_ride_trip.dart:452-458) calls `Navigator.of(context).pop()`, which removes the topmost route. The trip screen pushes routes on the same navigator while live: Chat via pushSingle (accept_ride_panel.dart:860-867), Preferences (:537-540), the destination picker and history (accept_ride.dart:1307). Nothing closes those routes before the pop. By then the cancel is journaled, the lifecycle is terminal, live updates are paused and the waybill is discarded. The driver is left on a dead AcceptRide, and the island notice is queued for a Home that is not shown. The same pattern is at :388-389 and :403-407.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test test/_audit_d40pop_test.dart (since deleted): Home -> AcceptRide(waitingForRider, MemoryDriverRealtime) -> pushed a page 'CHATPAGE' on the root navigator -> realtime.emit(riderCancelled). Output: `RESULT chat=0 trip=1 homeVisible=0` (the pushed page was popped, AcceptRide is still mounted, Home is not visible); test passed.

verdicts.reason: _handleRiderCancelled (accept_ride_trip.dart:452-458) does `final home = Navigator.of(context); if (next == null && home.canPop()) { ... home.pop(); }`, and _leaveAfterAuthoritativeOutcome (388-389) and _leaveAfterRelease (403-407) do the same. Navigator.pop removes the topmost route, not the AcceptRide route. The trip screen pushes routes such as Chat (accept_ride_panel.dart:860-867) onto that same navigator, so a terminal event while one of them is on top pops it instead. By then the lifecycle is already terminal, GPS is paused and the waybill is discarded, so the trip screen stays mounted and dead, and the island notice waits for a Home that is never shown. No guard checks ModalRoute.isCurrent. Caveat: realtime events need the future backend adapter (driver_composition_guard.dart:9).
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test (since deleted): a navigatorKey-backed Home, then a pushed AcceptRide (waitingForRider, MemoryDriverRealtime), then a pushed 'CHAT' page, then realtime.emit(riderCancelled). Output: `A40 RESULT chat=0 trip=1 homeOnstage=0`. The chat page was popped, AcceptRide is still mounted and Home is not shown.

confirmed.title: After a driver cancel or no-show the session never ends the trip, so Home stays 'on trip': no offers and Go online does nothing
confirmed.original_title: After a driver cancel or no-show the session never ends the trip, so Home stays 'on trip': no offers and Go online does nothing
confirmed.description: Every other way a trip can end releases the trip in the session controller: rider cancel (accept_ride_trip.dart:456/469), an authoritative outcome (:379), an admin release (:402) and completion (ride_completed.dart:71) all call `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip()` (endTrip). `_submitTripCancellation`, which handles both a driver cancel and the driver no-show, never calls it. It journals the trip, calls `_rideLifecycle.cancel/noShow`, shows a SnackBar and then just `navigator.pop()`s (1439-1445). Nothing else ends the trip: Home's push of AcceptRide (home_offer_radar.dart:940, home.dart:567) has no `.then`, and AcceptRide.dispose does not touch the session. The DriverSessionController therefore keeps `_activeTripId = <cancelled trip>` and `_status = onTrip`. On Home, `_isOnline => _liveVisible && _recoveryResolved && _driverSession.availableForOffers` (home.dart:335) is false because `availableForOffers` needs `status == online`. Tapping Go online runs `_goOnline` (home.dart:884), which calls `beginGoingOnline()`. That returns at once when `_activeTripId != null` (driver_session_controller.dart:129). The 1.4 s timer's `completeGoingOnline()` then does nothing because the status is not goingOnline, yet the island still shows the 'online' notice. `setOnline` during a trip only flips `_offlineAfterTrip`. `DrivingTimeClock.sync(online: isOnline)` keeps counting driving time, because `isOnline` is true for onTrip. `didPopNext` skips restore because `activeTripId != null`. The same happens when the driver cancels with a secured next trip: the next AcceptRide's `beginTrip(next.id)` is ignored (driver_session_controller.dart:58-61), so the session keeps the cancelled trip's id until some later trip completes. No test confirms a driver cancel and then checks Home (integration_test/driver_lifecycle_test.dart:165 and test/widget_test.dart:2659 both tap 'Keep trip').
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver is online on Home and accepts a Radar trip. At pickup the wait passes the no-show time. The driver taps 'Rider didn't show' and confirms (or picks Cancel trip with any reason and confirms). The SnackBar 'Trip cancelled · …' appears and Home comes back, but the radar shows OFF and no offers ever arrive. Tapping OFF/Go online shows the 'online' island message, but the session stays onTrip and the driver never becomes available. The driving-time clock keeps running and can force a rest. Only an app restart recovers. Worked out by hand from the code; nothing was run.
confirmed.evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:1384 `if (!await (noShow ? _rideLifecycle.noShow(clearSnapshot: false) : _rideLifecycle.cancel(clearSnapshot: false))) { _cancellationInFlight=false; return; }` ... 1439-1445 `final navigator = Navigator.of(context); if (nextRide != null) { navigator.pushReplacement(...); return; } if (navigator.canPop()) { navigator.pop(); }` (no stayOnlineAfterTrip). Compare accept_ride_trip.dart:456 `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip(); home.pop();`. driver_session_controller.dart:129 `if (_disposed || _activeTripId != null || isSuspended) { return; }`; :34 `bool get availableForOffers => _status == DriverOnlineStatus.online;`; home.dart:335 `bool get _isOnline => _liveVisible && _recoveryResolved && _driverSession.availableForOffers;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: In `_submitTripCancellation`, call `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip()` after the lifecycle cancel/noShow succeeds and before `pushReplacement`/`pop`, as the rider-cancel and authoritative paths do. Add a widget test that confirms a driver cancel and a no-show from Home and expects LIVE/availableForOffers.

verdicts.reason: In `_submitTripCancellation` (accept_ride_trip.dart:1356-1446), the successful path journals the trip, runs lifecycle cancel/noShow (:1384), shows a SnackBar and then calls `pushReplacement` or `pop` (:1439-1445). It never calls `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip()`. The only callers of endTrip/stayOnlineAfterTrip in lib/ are accept_ride_trip.dart:379, 402, 456 and 469 and ride_completed.dart:71, and none of them is on this path. `ActiveRideController` gets no session (accept_ride.dart:492-496), so it cannot end the trip either, and AcceptRide.dispose (accept_ride.dart:675-710) never touches the session. That leaves `_activeTripId` set and `_status` stuck at onTrip. `availableForOffers` (driver_session_controller.dart:34) is then false. `beginGoingOnline` returns early because `_activeTripId != null` (:129), and `completeGoingOnline` does nothing because the status is not goingOnline (:141). `restore()` also returns early (:179), and Home's didPopNext skips its restore while activeTripId is non-null (home.dart:182). On the secured-next path, `beginTrip(next.id)` is rejected because a different trip id is still active (driver_session_controller.dart:58-61). DECISIONS.md:107-108 explains the status mapping but says nothing that would keep the driver occupied after their own cancel.
verdicts.repro: Read-only static trace; nothing was run. I read _submitTripCancellation and grepped lib/ for every caller of endTrip/stayOnlineAfterTrip and every use of sessionController in the accept-ride folder. I also read the full DriverSessionController (beginTrip, beginGoingOnline, completeGoingOnline, restore, endTrip) and Home's didPopNext at home.dart:176-186.

verdicts.reason: _submitTripCancellation (accept_ride_trip.dart:1360-1445) never calls sessionController.endTrip/stayOnlineAfterTrip. The only callers in lib are accept_ride_trip.dart:379/402/456/469 and ride_completed.dart:71. Nothing else clears the trip: AcceptRide.dispose does not touch the session, and the controller's only other clearing methods are reset(), called only from profile.dart:397, and endTrip. _yieldToAuthoritativeTerminal (897-902) returns false unless a terminal projection is pending. So after a driver cancel or no-show, _activeTripId stays set and _status stays onTrip. availableForOffers (driver_session_controller.dart:34) is false, beginGoingOnline returns early at :129, completeGoingOnline does nothing at :142, setOnline during a trip only flips _offlineAfterTrip (:108-113), and Home's didPopNext skips the restore because activeTripId != null (home.dart:182). With a secured next trip, the next AcceptRide's beginTrip(next.id) is ignored at :58-61, because a different id is already active.
verdicts.repro: Read-only, as the run required; nothing was run. I traced the cancel and no-show path through pop() and grepped every endTrip/stayOnlineAfterTrip/reset caller in lib, then followed the DriverSessionController state for a driver who was online before the trip: status onTrip, activeTripId set, and no transition back to online.

confirmed.title: Home passes translated text as matchedVia, so waiting rules for reservations and scheduled rides depend on the UI language and stored sources are no longer English
confirmed.description: _openOfferTrip passes matchedVia from tr.exclusiveReservation / tr.exclusiveOffer (line 837), ExclusiveReasons.text(assigned), which is tr.assignedByMovera (line 860), and tr.scheduledRide (home_scheduled.dart:236). AcceptRide builds its waiting terms from that string: _waitTerms = WaitingRules.current.termsFor(type: WaitingRules.typeOf(matchedVia: widget.matchedVia, ...)) (accept_ride.dart:988-995). typeOf only matches the English substrings 'scheduled' / 'reservation' (waiting_rules.dart:251). Swedish 'Exklusiv bokning' / 'Bokad resa' and French 'Réservation exclusive' (accented é) / 'Course planifiée' never match, so in sv/fr a reservation or scheduled ride falls back to WaitingRideType.normal. The same string is stored as WaybillRecord.source and as PersistedActiveRide.matchedVia. waybill.dart:46-47 documents that source values 'stay in English in storage', and sourceText only translates the English constants.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An XL reservation is accepted from its Exclusive card. In English, termsFor applies the scheduled rule (includedWaitingMinutes = 5) on top of the XL rule (3 free minutes, no-show at 3): 5 free minutes, no-show from 5:00. In Swedish the same trip gets 3 free minutes, the waiting fee starts 2 minutes earlier and 'Rider didn't show' unlocks at 3:00. The rider's charge and the driver's no-show right depend on the phone's language. If an admin raises includedWaitingMinutes (say to 10), every sv/fr reservation loses the extra free minutes. The 'Scheduled ride' rule line also disappears from the waiting sheet.
confirmed.evidence: home_offer_radar.dart:835-838 `_openOfferTrip(offer, offer.reservation ? tr.exclusiveReservation : tr.exclusiveOffer,);` ; home_scheduled.dart:236 `tr.scheduledRide,` ; waiting_rules.dart:250-252 `final via = matchedVia.toLowerCase(); if (via.contains('scheduled') || via.contains('reservation')) { return WaitingRideType.scheduled;` ; app_sv.arb:90 `"exclusiveReservation": "Exklusiv bokning"`, app_sv.arb:57 `"scheduledRide": "Bokad resa"`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass stable English source constants (as ride_requests.dart does with 'Movera Radar') or an enum, decide the waiting ride type from offer.reservation / scheduled flags rather than display text, and translate only for display through WaybillRecord.sourceText.

confirmed.title: Closing (×) the Radar card whose Match claim is in flight leaves Home permanently in "Matching": no other trip can be matched and the won claim is dropped
confirmed.description: RadarOfferCard always shows the corner × on Home (onClose is always passed; radar_offer_card.dart:589-616 draws it regardless of `state`, including `matching`). _closeRadarHomeOffer (home_offer_radar.dart:890-896) calls _dismissRadarHomeOffer, which removes the offer from _radarHomeOffers and _homeRadarMatchStates (479-492) but never clears _homeRadarMatchingOfferId or _claimedHomeOffer. From then on: every other card's onMatch is null (`blocked != null && blocked != id ? null : ...`, 1127-1129), the radar orb is `busy` ("Matching · please wait", home_map_sheet.dart:1753-1774), _canStartScheduled is false so a scheduled "Leave now" goes to the backup driver (home_scheduled.dart:166-170, 177-178). When the dispatch claim resolves successfully, _claimHomeRadarOffer passes its guard (`_homeRadarMatchingOfferId == offer.id`), _resolveHomeRadarMatchWon sets _claimedHomeOffer and _openClaimedHomeOffer → 850 ms → _acceptRadarHomeOffer returns because the offer is no longer in _radarHomeOffers (925-928). _claimedHomeOffer stays set, so every later _scheduleVisibleOffers (resume) returns early at 1167-1170. The only exit is going offline (which runs _cancelAllOfferTimers without preserveClaim). The same path is reachable through _setAcceptsCash/_onCategoriesChanged, which dismiss listed offers regardless of claim state (home_offer_rules.dart:31-35, 52-56). Reproduced with a throwaway widget test (two offers on the deck, Match on `first`, tap `radar-offer-close`, then complete the claim with ClaimResult.success): AcceptRide never opened, `radar-match-second` onPressed stayed null and the orb read "Matching" 30 s later. confirmed.title: "Leave now" removes the accepted scheduled ride from the store before a push that silently does nothing when Home is not the current route
confirmed.description: `_planScheduled` arms `Timer(_clock.realUntil(start), () => _leaveNow(ride))` (line 161). These timers live in `_scheduled.timers`, which `_pauseHomeUpdates` (home.dart 192-203) never cancels, and `_leaveNow`/`_canStartScheduled` (lines 166-170, 175-189) only check `mounted`, `_recoveryResolved`, `_driverSession.availableForOffers`, `_claimedHomeOffer` and `_homeRadarMatchingOfferId`; neither `_routeVisible` nor `ModalRoute.isCurrent` is consulted. `availableForOffers` is `_status == online` (driver_session_controller.dart 34), which stays true while the driver is on any non-trip screen pushed over Home (Scheduled rides, Notifications, Settings, Support, Wallet, Ride history, a modal sheet such as the destination details sheet or the queue sheet). When the timer fires in that state, `_startScheduledTrip` (218-239) first calls `ScheduledRideStore.start(ride)` which is `_removeAccepted(ride) != null` (scheduled_rides.dart 638-660) and permanently drops the ride from Accepted, posts the "Leave now" island message and notification, and only then calls `_HomeOfferRadar(this)._openOfferTrip(...)` (home_offer_radar.dart 931-981) whose `pushSingle(context, ActiveRideTransition(AcceptRide(...)))` returns `Future.value()` without pushing because `ModalRoute.of(context)?.isCurrent == false` (single_route_entry.dart 11-13). `_planScheduled()` then re-plans for the *next* ride. Nothing re-opens or restores the removed ride; `didPopNext` only re-runs `_restoreActiveRideIfNeeded`, and no AcceptRide/persisted trip was ever created.

confirmed.title: Same defect as driver-74: "Leave now" removes the accepted ride from Accepted, then pushSingle silently does nothing while any route or sheet covers Home, so the trip never opens and the ride is lost
confirmed.description: _leaveNow() fires from a Timer planned in _planScheduled(). Its only guard is _canStartScheduled (home_scheduled.dart:166-170: _recoveryResolved, availableForOffers, no claim in flight); it never checks that Home is the current route. _startScheduledTrip() first calls ScheduledRideStore.start(ride) (line 220), which removes the ride from Accepted (scheduled_rides.dart:638-639 / 652-660), posts "Leave now" and then calls _HomeOfferRadar._openOfferTrip (line 234). _openOfferTrip cancels every offer timer and calls pushSingle(context, ActiveRideTransition(AcceptRide(...))) confirmed.title: System Back on the Ride completed screen skips _finish(): the session stays on_trip and Home can never go online again (a secured next trip is dropped too)
confirmed.description: _completeCurrentTrip (accept_ride_trip.dart:965) uses pushReplacement to put DriverRideCompleted over Home. Only the Done button runs _finish(), and _finish() is the only code on this path that calls sessionController.stayOnlineAfterTrip() (-> endTrip(), which clears _activeTripId), promotes or clears the next waybill, and pushes the queued next ride. The screen's Scaffold has no PopScope (a grep of lib finds PopScope only in accept_ride, ride_check_card, profile, ride_history, emergency_contacts, app_update_sheet, home_back and support_inbox), and BottomToTopTransition is a plain ModalRoute. So Android Back pops straight to Home. After that, DriverSessionController keeps _activeTripId set to the completed trip with status onTrip. On Home, _isOnline needs availableForOffers (status == online), so it is false and the radar shows 'OFF · Tap to scan'. Tapping it runs _goOnline(), which calls _driverSession.beginGoingOnline(). That method returns at once because _activeTripId != null, yet Home still posts IslandMessages.show(HomeIslandNotices.online). completeGoingOnline() then does nothing because the status is not goingOnline. didPopNext only re-runs recovery when activeTripId == null, so nothing repairs this. DrivingTimeClock.sync(online: isOnline) also keeps counting driving time, because isOnline is true for onTrip.

confirmed.title: On web, every live-car marker push leaks a new Blob URL of the arrow PNG and reloads the car image, so memory grows for as long as a trip lasts
confirmed.description: The active-ride car marker (accept_ride.dart:1484-1498, `icon: widget.vehicleIcon`) uses `MoveraVehicleMarker.createIcon()` -> `arrowAt(1)`, which is `BitmapDescriptor.bytes(png, width, height)`, a BytesMapBitmap (movera_vehicle_marker.dart:128). `_ThrottledVehicleMap` sets `_car.value` every 33 ms whenever the pose changes (accept_ride.dart:1458). While following, `onFrame` snaps the vehicle to the camera target on every 16 ms camera frame (accept_ride.dart:1257-1260), so the pose changes on nearly every tick while driving. Each change goes through `_onLiveMarker` -> `_pushLiveMarker` -> `GoogleMapsFlutterPlatform.instance.updateMarkers(updates)` (custom_google_map.dart:241-242) with the 'driver' marker in markersToChange. In the pinned google_maps_flutter_web 0.5.14+2, `_changeMarker` rebuilds the full options, including the icon (`_markerOptionsFromMarker` -> `_gmIconFromBitmapDescriptor` -> `urlFromMapBitmap`). For a BytesMapBitmap that calls `URL.createObjectURL(Blob(bytes))` through `_bitmapBlobUrlCache`, and `updateMarkers` runs `_cleanUpBitmapConversionCaches()` after every batch, which clears that cache without `revokeObjectURL`. Every push therefore creates a new, never-revoked Blob URL that holds a copy of the PNG until the page unloads. Because the icon object is new each time, the Maps Marker also fires `icon_changed`. web/driver_map_camera.js:598 handles that by setting `image.src` to the new blob URL, so the browser fetches and decodes the car image on every push. The Home map leaks the same way, once per GPS fix (home_map_sheet.dart:95 rebuilds `_markers`) and once per pin on each RouteFade step. This is the same unbounded growth and per-frame map churn that DECISIONS.md says made Safari kill the tab. Even the documented 5 Hz throttle would not stop it, because the growth comes from the BytesMapBitmap icon being re-sent with each position update. On Android and iOS the same pushes send and decode the PNG bytes on every update, which causes GC and jank but no leak.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Web or PWA driver on Safari drives a 30-minute trip with the follow camera. About 30 pushes a second for 1800 s is roughly 54,000 Blob URLs (a few KB each, about 100+ MB), plus 30 image decodes a second, and it keeps growing over a shift. Safari's memory pressure reloads the tab ('A problem repeatedly occurred') mid-trip. Worked by hand from the plugin source; not run.
confirmed.evidence:
accept_ride.dart:1458 `_ticker = Timer.periodic(const Duration(milliseconds: 33), (_) { ... _car.value = _carMarker; });`
accept_ride.dart:1498 `icon: widget.vehicleIcon,`
movera_vehicle_marker.dart:128 `return cache[key] ??= BitmapDescriptor.bytes(png, width: ..., height: ...);`

confirmed.suggested_fix: On web, do not send the car as a bytes-icon marker on every move. Move only the JS car overlay (add a `driverMapCamera.vehiclePosition(id, lat, lng, heading)` call and keep the gmaps Marker static), or use an AssetMapBitmap/stable URL icon on web. At the least, add the 'driver' marker once and update only its position through the JS adapter. Cap the push rate to the documented 5 Hz as well.

verdicts.reason: On web `_shown` (lib/widgets/custom_google_map.dart:250) sends the marker as it is, so the 'driver' marker keeps `icon: widget.vehicleIcon`. That icon is a BytesMapBitmap built from the cached `_arrowPng` (lib/widgets/movera_vehicle_marker.dart:128). `_ThrottledVehicleMap` (accept_ride.dart:1457-1467; liveMapTicker defaults to true, driver_runtime_config.dart:15) sets `_car.value` on every 33 ms tick in which the pose moved. `_pushLiveMarker` (custom_google_map.dart:241) then sends 'driver' in markersToChange, at most once a frame. In google_maps_flutter_web 0.5.14+2, `_changeMarker` (markers.dart:113-115) rebuilds the full MarkerOptions, and that includes the icon (convert.dart:514). `urlFromMapBitmap` (convert.dart:754-760) calls `URL.createObjectURL(Blob(bytes))` through `_bitmapBlobUrlCache`. `updateMarkers` (google_maps_controller.dart:577) clears that cache after every batch (convert.dart:422-424), and nothing anywhere calls revokeObjectURL (the only revoke is in overlay.dart). So every push mints a new Blob URL that is never released, and each one holds a copy of the arrow PNG. web/driver_map_camera.js:598 reacts to the new icon object on `icon_changed` and sets `image.src` to the new URL each time, so the image is fetched and decoded again on every push. No guard stops this: the throttle only drops pushes when the pose did not change, and the follow-camera `onFrame` snap (accept_ride.dart:1257-1260) changes the pose on nearly every frame while driving. Web/PWA on Safari is a supported target (DECISIONS.md:79-85). That document records that the app moved to a 5 Hz throttle because Safari killed the tab; the code ticks at 33 ms instead, and the Blob URLs pile up whatever the rate.

Also traced custom_google_map.dart:213-243 and 249-250, accept_ride.dart:1444-1501 and 1257-1260, and web/driver_map_camera.js:569-598. I searched lib/ and web/ for revokeObjectURL and found none. Not run in a browser.

verdicts.reason: On web, `_shown` returns the markers unchanged (lib/widgets/custom_google_map.dart:250), so the 'driver' marker carries `_driverVehicleIcon`, the cached BytesMapBitmap from MoveraVehicleMarker.createIcon/arrowAt (lib/widgets/movera_vehicle_marker.dart:126-131). While the car moves, the 33 ms ticker sets `_car.value` (lib/presentation/driver/accept ride/accept_ride.dart:1490-1500, liveMapTicker defaults to true). `_onLiveMarker` passes that on once per frame to `_pushLiveMarker`, which sends the marker in markersToChange to `updateMarkers` (custom_google_map.dart:233-242). In the pinned google_maps_flutter_web 0.5.14+2, `_changeMarker` (markers.dart:114-115) runs `_markerOptionsFromMarker`, which always rebuilds the icon (convert.dart:514). That calls `urlFromMapBitmap`, which calls `URL.createObjectURL` through `_bitmapBlobUrlCache.putIfAbsent` (convert.dart:754-760). `updateMarkers` then runs `_cleanUpBitmapConversionCaches()` (google_maps_controller.dart:577), which clears the cache without `revokeObjectURL` (convert.dart:422-425). The only revoke in the plugin is in overlay.dart:64, for tile overlays. So every push while moving creates a new Blob URL that is never revoked and holds a copy of the PNG, and the JS overlay reloads the image on `icon_changed` (web/driver_map_camera.js:598). Nothing in the app avoids this: there is no AssetMapBitmap on web and no position-only path. The code also pushes at about 30 Hz, not the 5 Hz that DECISIONS.md:85 documents. The size of the growth depends on the PNG size and how often the pose changes, so the 100+ MB figure is an estimate, but the growth is unbounded for as long as the car moves.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand through the app and the pinned plugin source in ~/.pub-cache/hosted/pub.dev/google_maps_flutter_web-0.5.14+2 (pubspec.lock:418-424). I found createObjectURL at convert.dart:484 and :760, cache clear at convert.dart:422-425 called from google_maps_controller.dart:577, and the only revokeObjectURL at overlay.dart:64. Not run in a browser because no web test runner is available here. Worked out: at about 30 changed poses a second, a 30-minute moving trip creates about 54,000 Blob URLs, each holding the arrow PNG (38 logical px x maxScale x density 3 per side).

confirmed.title: Device-to-device transfer rules leave the 'root' domain (app_flutter) included, so Ride-check audio recordings move to a new phone despite 'saved only on this phone'
confirmed.description: For apps targeting Android 12+ (targetSdk = flutter.targetSdkVersion = 36), `android:allowBackup="false"` no longer turns off device-to-device migration. Only the `<device-transfer>` rules control it. Those rules exclude only `sharedpref`, `database` and `file` (getFilesDir()). NativeRideCheckRecorder writes recordings to `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()`, which on Android is `PathUtils.getDataDirectory` = `context.getDir("flutter")`, that is /data/data/se.movera.driver/app_flutter. That directory is in the `root` domain, which is not excluded. The recordings are therefore copied to a new device during setup. That contradicts the XML comment ('Driver data ... is excluded from cloud backup and device-to-device transfer'), the RECORD_AUDIO rationale in docs/ANDROID_PERMISSIONS.md ('saved only on this phone and never sent'), and the Ride-check UI copy. privacy_storage_test only checks that a `<device-transfer>` tag exists, so it cannot catch this. (The iOS Documents backup issue is already known; this is the Android counterpart, a different mechanism.)
confirmed.failure_scenario: A driver records audio in a Ride check on an Android 12+ phone, then sets up a new phone with Google's 'copy apps & data' cable or wireless transfer. The rider-incident recordings in app_flutter/ride_check_audio/*.m4a are copied to the new device, although the app promised they stay only on the original phone.

test/audit/privacy_storage_test.dart:60-62 only `contains('<device-transfer>')`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add `<exclude domain="root" path="." />` (and `external`) to both `<device-transfer>` and `<cloud-backup>`, or store recordings under noBackupFilesDir. Make the test assert the domains.

verdicts.reason: data_extraction_rules.xml:10-14 excludes only the sharedpref, database and file domains from device-transfer. For targetSdk 31 and later (build.gradle.kts:25 uses flutter.targetSdkVersion), AndroidManifest.xml:13 `allowBackup="false"` does not turn off device-to-device migration. NativeRideCheckRecorder.start (ride_check_recorder_native.dart:31-37) writes to getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/ride_check_audio. On Android that is context.getDir("flutter") = <dataDir>/app_flutter, which belongs to the 'root' domain, not 'file' (getFilesDir). The recordings are therefore copied by device-to-device transfer, against the file's own comment (:2-3) and docs/ANDROID_PERMISSIONS.md:10 ('saved only on this phone'). No document records this as intentional.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: read the rules XML, backup_rules.xml, the manifest flags, the targetSdk setting and the recorder's path. Searched docs for any decision allowing transfer and found none.

verdicts.reason: The manifest sets allowBackup=false together with dataExtractionRules (AndroidManifest.xml:13-15), and targetSdk = flutter.targetSdkVersion (build.gradle.kts:25, Android 12+). From Android 12 on, allowBackup=false does not turn off device-to-device transfer, and only <device-transfer> controls it. data_extraction_rules.xml:10-14 excludes only sharedpref, database and file. Everything not excluded is included. ride_check_recorder_native.dart:31-37 writes recordings to getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/ride_check_audio. With the locked path_provider_android 2.2.17, that is PathUtils.getDataDirectory(context) (PathProviderPlugin.java:57-58), which is context.getDir("flutter") = <dataDir>/app_flutter. That directory is in the 'root' domain, not in 'file' (getFilesDir), so no exclusion covers it. This contradicts the XML comment, docs/PRIVACY_SECURITY.md:13, docs/ANDROID_PERMISSIONS.md:10 ('saved only on this phone') and the UI string audioSavedOnlyOnThisPhone.

confirmed.title: iOS bundle identifier is still the template com.example.movera, while README and the 16-point record say the bundle id is se.movera.driver
confirmed.description: Android uses applicationId/namespace `se.movera.driver`. README.md:7 says 'Bundle id `se.movera.driver` is unchanged', and FRONTEND_16_POINT_RECORD.md (F04/F15) says the application and bundle id were kept. The Runner target's Debug, Release and Profile configurations all set PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER to the Flutter template value `com.example.movera`, and RunnerTests uses `com.example.movera.RunnerTests`. Flutter's own `build ipa` validation flags this ('Your application still contains the default "com.example" bundle identifier'). Apple does not register App IDs under the reserved example domain, so the iOS release cannot be signed or uploaded under the intended identity. The `ios-release-preflight` job uses `--no-codesign` and never sees this. release_metadata_test.dart checks only the Android gradle file for 'se.movera.driver', so the mismatch passes CI.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The owner archives the iOS release for TestFlight or the App Store. Signing fails because the com.example.movera App ID cannot be registered, or a build goes out under a throwaway identifier that does not match the Android/README identity, so later updates cannot carry over to the real se.movera.driver listing.

confirmed.title: Info.plist has no NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription (or NSAppleMusicUsageDescription) although the linked image_picker and file_picker reference those APIs; a test asserts the key stays absent
confirmed.description: image_picker's README (pubspec image_picker 1.2.0) says NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription must be in Info.plist even if the photo library is never requested: 'This permission will not be requested if you always pass false for requestFullMetadata, but App Store policy requires including the plist entry.' file_picker 10.3.2's iOS podspec builds by default with PICKER_MEDIA (DKImagePickerController/PhotoGallery, Photos framework) and PICKER_AUDIO (MPMediaPickerController, which needs NSAppleMusicUsageDescription). No Podfile sets `Pod::PICKER_MEDIA=false` or `PICKER_AUDIO=false`. App Store Connect's static scan rejects uploads that reference these APIs without the purpose strings (ITMS-90683). ios_camera_privacy_test.dart explicitly asserts the plist does NOT contain NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription, which locks the defect in.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The owner uploads the iOS archive to App Store Connect. Processing returns ITMS-90683 'Missing purpose string in Info.plist' for NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription (and NSAppleMusicUsageDescription), and the build cannot be submitted. verdicts.reason: ios/Runner/Info.plist:7-12 declares only the Camera, Microphone and LocationWhenInUse keys. image_picker 1.2.0's README (lines 30-32) says App Store policy requires NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription even when the library is never requested. file_picker 10.3.2 compiles PICKER_MEDIA (with the DKImagePickerController/PhotoGallery dependency) and PICKER_AUDIO by default, both in its podspec and, unconditionally, in its Package.swift. The repo has no ios/Podfile overriding those, so either build path links the Photos and MediaPlayer APIs. FilePicker is called for real at vehicle_document_upload.dart:238. App Store Connect flags missing purpose strings for linked APIs (ITMS-90683). test/audit/ios_camera_privacy_test.dart:33 asserts the key stays absent. confirmed.title: Pickup pay is added to the fare shown on offer cards but is dropped on accept, so the trip, waybill earnings and history show less than the card promised
confirmed.description: PickupPayQuote.totalOf(fare) returns fare + pickup pay and is what the cards display: the on-trip next-trip card shows `_NextTripRadarOffer.shownFare` (accept_ride.dart:333 `String get shownFare => pickupPay.totalOf(fare);`, rendered at accept_ride_panel.dart:309 and accept_ride_sheet.dart:132), the exclusive sheet shows `offer.shownFare(show)` and Home radar cards get a PickupPayQuote (home_offer_radar.dart:1069). PickupPayConfig.current defaults have every kind on with demo rates (pickup_pay_config.dart:188-209, demoRates), so for the default next-trip offer (Comfort, 1.6 km / 4 min: (1.6-1)*3 + (4-2)*1 = 3,80 kr) the card promises 132,20 kr. When the driver accepts, the trip is opened with the plain fare: _buildNextWaybill uses `offer.fare` (accept_ride_trip.dart:217), _snapshotForOffer uses `offer.fare` (:976), the next AcceptRide gets `fare: offer.fare` (:940, :1398), PersistedQueuedTrip.fare is the plain fare (:49), and Home's _openOfferTrip passes `fare: offer.fare` (home_offer_radar.dart:954). Nothing stores or adds the pickup pay afterwards, so the trip screen, completion journal, history and earnings all show the lower number the driver did not accept.
confirmed.failure_scenario: While driving, the next-trip card says 132,20 kr (incl. 3,80 kr pickup) and the driver accepts. The secured-next banner, the next trip's screen, its waybill 'Your earnings' and the history row all say 128,40 kr; the 3,80 kr the card promised is gone. Same on Home radar/exclusive cards whenever pickup pay is non-zero.

At minimum pass `offer.shownFare` (or a stored PickupPayQuote) through _buildNextWaybill/_snapshotForOffer/_openOfferTrip so the accepted amount matches what was shown.

confirmed.title: Strip leg identity ignores the stop index: every stop-to-stop leg carries the previous leg's best ETA and shows a false 'Traffic ahead · +N min'
confirmed.description: AdaptiveTripIsland maps pointKind to TripLeg (adaptive_trip_island.dart:262-267). On a trip with 2 or more stops, the leg from stop k to stop k+1 has the same TripLeg.stop. TripStripController.update decides whether a new leg has started only from `last.leg != next.leg`, so `_bestEta` and `_arrivingSaid` are not reset when the stop changes. At the end of the stop-1 leg, `_routeEtaText` (accept_ride.dart:927-929) has fallen to its floor of `max(1, ...)` = 1 min, so `_bestEta` = 1. It stays 1 during the paid stop wait, because the island keeps feeding the stale route's ETA. When the driver slides 'Go to second stop', `_stopCursor` becomes 1 and the stop-2 route arrives with an ETA such as 9 min. The check `eta - best >= 2` fires and `_say(tr.trafficAheadValueMin(8))` is queued. The '<stop> next' message for stop 2 is also skipped, because it is guarded by newLeg.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A trip with stops A and B. The driver reaches A (ETA shown as 1 min), waits, then slides 'Go to second stop'. The route to B is 9 min. The island strip shows 'Traffic ahead · +8 min' (in fr 'Trafic devant · +8 min') with no traffic involved, and never shows 'Stop 2 next'. This repeats at every intermediate stop.
confirmed.evidence:
trip_island_controller.dart:302 `final newLeg = last == null || last.leg != next.leg;`
:321 `if (newLeg && next.leg == TripLeg.stop && next.stopLabel != null) {`
:326-329 `if (best != null && eta - best >= 2) { _say(tr.trafficAheadValueMin(eta - best)); ...`
adaptive_trip_island.dart:262-271 `final leg = switch (widget.pointKind) { ArrivalPointKind.stop => TripLeg.stop, ...}; ... stopLabel: leg == TripLeg.stop ? widget.pointLabel : null, etaMinutes: int.tryParse(RegExp(r'^(\d+)\s*min').firstMatch(widget.eta)?.group(1) ?? '')`
accept_ride.dart:800-801 `if (_stopCursor < widget.stopAddresses.length) { return ArrivalPointKind.stop; }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Include the stop label/index in the leg identity, for example `newLeg = last == null || last.leg != next.leg || last.stopLabel != next.stopLabel`, so a new stop resets `_bestEta`/`_arrivingSaid` and plays its own announcement.

verdicts.reason: trip_island_controller.dart:302 decides a new leg only by `last.leg != next.leg`. adaptive_trip_island.dart:262-271 maps every stop to TripLeg.stop and sends the stop label separately. When the paid stop wait ends, accept_ride_trip.dart:889 runs `_stopCursor += 1`, so the leg stays TripLeg.stop and only stopLabel changes ('Stop 1' to 'Stop 2', accept_ride.dart:809). Because of that, `_bestEta` and `_arrivingSaid` are not reset and the '<stop> next' message at :321 is skipped. Until _refreshOnTripRoute replaces the route, the island keeps getting the old route's floored ETA (accept_ride.dart:923-929, max(1, ...)). The new, longer route then trips the `eta - best >= 2` check at :326 and shows a false 'Traffic ahead'. Hiding the strip does not help: the early return at :316 leaves `_bestEta` stale too.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test on TripStripController, now deleted. It fed: Stop 1 with ETA 5, then 1; Stop 2 with ETA 1, then 9. Printed output: 'A Stop 1 next', 'B ' (no 'Stop 2 next'), 'C Traffic ahead · +8 min'. Result: All tests passed.

verdicts.reason: trip_island_controller.dart:302 treats a leg as new only when `last.leg != next.leg`. adaptive_trip_island.dart:262-271 maps every stop to TripLeg.stop and passes widget.pointLabel (accept_ride.dart:842 `tr.stopNumber(_stopCursor + 1)`) as stopLabel, but stopLabel is not part of the leg check. When the driver slides on from a paid stop wait, accept_ride_trip.dart:896 does `_stopCursor += 1` and the stop-2 route comes in, yet _bestEta keeps the low value from the end of the stop-1 leg. Hidden updates return before the ETA logic (:316), so the tucked arrival phase never resets it either. The check at :326-329 then queues 'Traffic ahead · +N min', and the '<stop> next' message at :321 is skipped for stop 2 and every later stop.

confirmed.title: On web the 8 s GPS time limit is not enforced (geolocator_web 4.1.4 passes microseconds as ms, with no Dart timeout), so a browser that never answers blocks the one-shot fix and the GPS subscription on Home and the trip
confirmed.description: `DriverLocationService.getCurrentPosition()` relies on `LocationSettings(timeLimit: 8 s)` to bound the one-shot fix. Both screens subscribe to `watchPosition()` only after that call resolves: `accept_ride_trip.dart:598-606` (`final position = await _locationService.getCurrentPosition(); ... _positionSubscription = _locationService.watchPosition(distanceFilterMeters: 0).listen(...)`) and `home_map_sheet.dart:38-45` (the catch path also subscribes, but only if the call completes). On native the platform-interface applies `.timeout(timeLimit)`, so after 8 s the service falls back to the last known fix or throws and the screens show `Location updating…` and keep working. On web the pinned geolocator_web 4.1.4 overrides `getCurrentPosition` with no Dart-side timeout and converts the limit with `timeout?.inMicroseconds` into the browser's millisecond `PositionOptions.timeout` (8 s becomes 8,000 s, about 2.2 h). The app's own guard therefore does not hold on its primary (web/PWA) deployment: when the browser's geolocation does not answer (device has location permission but no fix, e.g. indoors, or a slow provider), the one-shot neither resolves nor errors, no stream is ever subscribed, no `Location updating…` status is set, and on the trip no route request is made (`_refreshRoadRoute(force: true)` sits in the catch).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver opens the PWA on a phone whose browser cannot obtain a fix right away: Home stays on the locating placeholder and the trip map shows no live car, no route and no status for as long as the browser withholds an answer (up to ~2.2 h) instead of falling back after 8 s as on native.
confirmed.evidence: driver_location_service.dart:21-26: `LocationSettings get _settings => LocationSettings(accuracy: kIsWeb ? LocationAccuracy.high : LocationAccuracy.bestForNavigation, timeLimit: const Duration(seconds: 8));` 29-36: `await _ensurePermission(); try { final position = await Geolocator.getCurrentPosition(locationSettings: _settings);`. accept_ride_trip.dart:598-606: `final position = await _locationService.getCurrentPosition(); ... _positionSubscription = _locationService.watchPosition(distanceFilterMeters: 0).listen(`. geolocator_web-4.1.4 lib/src/html_geolocation_manager.dart:34-37: `timeout: timeout?.inMicroseconds ?? const Duration(days: 1).inMilliseconds,`; geolocator_web.dart:74-85 awaits `_geolocation.getCurrentPosition(...)` with no `.timeout`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Wrap `Geolocator.getCurrentPosition` in a Dart-side `.timeout(_settings.timeLimit!)` in `DriverLocationService.getCurrentPosition` (and `requestPermission` if it can block), and/or subscribe to `watchPosition` before awaiting the one-shot so a hung one-shot cannot block the stream.

verdicts.corrected_title: On web the 8 s GPS time limit is not enforced (geolocator_web 4.1.4 passes microseconds as ms, with no Dart timeout), so a browser that never answers blocks the one-shot fix and the GPS subscription on Home and the trip
verdicts.reason: In the resolved geolocator_web 4.1.4 (~/.pub-cache/.../geolocator_web-4.1.4/lib/src/html_geolocation_manager.dart:34-37), the timeout is `timeout?.inMicroseconds` in a field the browser reads as milliseconds, so 8 s becomes 8,000 s. geolocator_web.dart:74-85 awaits the result with no `.timeout`. DriverLocationService.getCurrentPosition (driver_location_service.dart:21-36) relies only on `LocationSettings.timeLimit`. Both callers subscribe to `watchPosition` only after that await resolves or throws: accept_ride_trip.dart:597-606 subscribes after it, and its catch at 620-627 sets 'Location updating…' and requests the route; home_map_sheet.dart:38-55 calls `_listenToDriverLocation` only after it or in its catch. A hung one-shot therefore leaves no stream, no status and, on the trip, no route request. Both screens use the real DriverLocationService for normal trips (accept_ride.dart:584, home.dart:453-454), and web/PWA is a primary deployment (DECISIONS.md:81-87). Whether a browser hangs depends on the device (for example high accuracy indoors), but the documented guard is plainly broken on web.
verdicts.repro: Static trace through the pinned geolocator_web 4.1.4 source in the pub cache (confirmed against pubspec.lock) and both screens' start flows. I did not reproduce it in a browser.

verdicts.corrected_title: On web the 8 s one-shot GPS limit becomes 8,000 s (geolocator_web 4.1.4 passes microseconds as milliseconds and adds no Dart timeout), so a slow browser fix leaves Home and the trip with no position, no 'Location updating…' status and no route until the browser answers
verdicts.reason: driver_location_service.dart:21-26 relies on `LocationSettings.timeLimit: 8 s`. In the pinned geolocator_web 4.1.4 (pubspec.lock:354-361), geolocator_web.dart:74-85 forwards `timeLimit` without a Dart `.timeout`, and html_geolocation_manager.dart:35-36 sets `timeout: timeout?.inMicroseconds`. That is 8 s = 8,000,000, which the browser reads as 8,000,000 ms = 8,000 s, about 2 h 13 min. On native, geolocator_android.dart:122-123 (and the apple equivalent) apply `.timeout(timeLimit)`, so the 8 s fallback only works off the web. Both callers await the one-shot before doing anything else. accept_ride_trip.dart:597 subscribes to the stream and sets the status/route fallback only after the call resolves or throws (catch at 619-627). home_map_sheet.dart:38 only reaches `_listenToDriverLocation` or `_startLocationFailed` afterwards. No other Dart guard bounds the wait. The impact lasts as long as the browser withholds both an answer and an error, for example during a high-accuracy cold start indoors. It is not a fixed 2.2 h in every case, because a browser may still return POSITION_UNAVAILABLE earlier.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand in the pub cache sources: ~/.pub-cache/hosted/pub.dev/geolocator_web-4.1.4/lib/src/html_geolocation_manager.dart:35-36 `timeout: timeout?.inMicroseconds ?? const Duration(days: 1).inMilliseconds`. Duration(seconds: 8).inMicroseconds = 8,000,000, read as ms by PositionOptions.timeout, gives 8,000 s. geolocator_web.dart:78-85 awaits the completer with no timeout, while geolocator_android-5.0.3 geolocator_android.dart:122-123 does `positionFuture.timeout(timeLimit)`. I did not run anything in a browser.

confirmed.title: Approximate-only location passes the permission check but every fix fails the 50 m accuracy gate, so in release builds Home has no live position and Arrived is always refused, with no prompt asking for precise location
confirmed.description: The manifest declares both ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION and ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION, and geolocator requests both. On Android 12+ the system dialog therefore offers 'Approximate'. geolocator_android.checkPermissionStatus returns `whileInUse` when either declared permission is granted, coarse alone included. iOS 14+ similarly lets the user turn Precise off, and the status stays whenInUse. `_ensurePermission` checks only denied/deniedForever, so it passes. The fixes then have accuracy of about 1–3 km. `DriverLocation.isUsableAt` rejects anything with `accuracy > 50`, so Home sets `_hasLiveDriverLocation = false` on every fix, the trip never follows the car, and `_nearArrivalTarget` returns false in every release build (simulatedArrival is false there). The code never calls `Geolocator.getLocationAccuracy()` or `requestTemporaryFullAccuracy`, and Info.plist has no `NSLocationTemporaryUsageDescriptionDictionary`, so the reduced-accuracy state is never detected or explained. docs/ANDROID_PERMISSIONS.md says ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION is kept as a 'Coarse fallback for the same when-in-use location', but the code cannot use a coarse fix at all.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On an Android 13 phone the driver taps 'Approximate' in the location dialog (or turns 'Precise Location' off on iOS). Home stays on 'Finding your location' with no car marker. On an accepted trip, tapping Arrived at the pickup shows 'Location unavailable. Enable location to confirm arrival.' although location is enabled. The trip cannot progress in a release APK/IPA or the CI web release.
confirmed.evidence:
driver_location_service.dart:115-128 only checks `LocationPermission.denied` / `deniedForever`
driver_location_repository.dart:48-55 `accuracy > 50) { return false; }`
home_map_sheet.dart:93 `_hasLiveDriverLocation = location.isUsableAt(DateTime.now());`
accept_ride.dart:765-768 `if (_arrivalDemo) { return true; } if (!_hasLiveLocation || _lastLocation?.isUsableAt(DateTime.now()) != true) { return false; }`
AndroidManifest.xml:4-5 FINE + COARSE; docs/ANDROID_PERMISSIONS.md 'ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION | Coarse fallback for the same when-in-use location'
geolocator_android PermissionManager.checkPermissionStatus: any granted declared permission -> whileInUse
confirmed.suggested_fix: After the permission check, call Geolocator.getLocationAccuracy(). On reduced accuracy, show a 'Precise location required' state with a settings link. On iOS, add NSLocationTemporaryUsageDescriptionDictionary and call requestTemporaryFullAccuracy. Alternatively drop COARSE from the manifest and fix the doc.

verdicts.corrected_title: Approximate-only location passes the permission check but every fix fails the 50 m accuracy gate, so in release builds Home has no live position and Arrived is always refused, with no prompt asking for precise location
verdicts.reason: _ensurePermission (driver_location_service.dart:109-129) rejects only denied and deniedForever. Approximate on Android 12+ and Precise Off on iOS 14+ both come back as whileInUse, so the check passes. The manifest declares both FINE and COARSE (AndroidManifest.xml:4-5). Every fix carries the platform accuracy (1-3 km for approximate), and isUsableAt rejects accuracy > 50 (driver_location_repository.dart:48-55). isDisplayableAt delegates to isUsableAt for measured fixes, so Home's _applyDriverLocation sets _hasLiveDriverLocation=false and returns (home_map_sheet.dart:82-84). In accept_ride.dart:765-768 _nearArrivalTarget returns false unless _arrivalDemo is on, and simulatedArrivalFor turns that off for release builds (driver_runtime_config.dart:63-69). Nothing in lib calls getLocationAccuracy or requestTemporaryFullAccuracy. docs/ANDROID_PERMISSIONS.md:9 presents COARSE as a usable fallback, but the code cannot use a coarse fix.
verdicts.repro: Traced the permission check, the fix-to-DriverLocation mapping, isDisplayableAt/isUsableAt, the Home location handler, the arrival gate and the runtime config. Grepped lib for accuracy-status APIs and found none. No test was run (needs a device).

verdicts.reason: _ensurePermission (driver_location_service.dart:109-128) rejects only denied and deniedForever. A grant of 'Approximate' only (ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION, which AndroidManifest.xml:5 declares next to FINE), or iOS with Precise Off, therefore passes. The code never calls getLocationAccuracy or requestTemporaryFullAccuracy (grep finds neither in lib/). DriverLocation.isUsableAt (driver_location_repository.dart:48-55) rejects any fix with accuracy > 50, and coarse fixes report about 1-3 km. In a release build, simulatedArrivalFor (driver_runtime_config.dart:63-70) returns false, so _arrivalDemo is false. _nearArrivalTarget (accept_ride.dart:797-806) then always returns false, and the driver sees locationUnavailableEnableLocationToConfirm ('Enable location to confirm arrival'), even though location is enabled. Requiring a precise fix is reasonable. The defect is that reduced accuracy is never detected or explained, so the trip cannot progress and the message gives the wrong remedy. It is an edge path because the driver has to pick Approximate.
verdicts.repro: Traced the path from the permission check to the 50 m accuracy gate, then to _nearArrivalTarget and the release-build arrival config. Checked the manifest permissions and confirmed with grep that no accuracy-status API is called anywhere. Did not run a test: it needs a device or OS permission state that flutter test cannot simulate. The geolocator_android behaviour (a coarse-only grant is reported as whileInUse) is the plugin's documented contract.

confirmed.title: Trip auto-resume timer that fires while suspended is dropped and never re-armed; resume() does not reschedule it
confirmed.description: `_scheduleResume()` arms a one-shot Timer whose callback returns early when `_suspended` is true without rescheduling, and `resume()` (lines 693-696) only calls `_request(immediate: true)`, which is a no-op in browsing mode (`_canFollow` is false). The trip screen relies on this timer to bring the camera back to the car 12 s after the driver lets go of the map (`accept_ride.dart:488` sets `autoResumeAfter = tripAutoResume`, `accept_ride_trip.dart:794` sets `onAutoResume`). `suspend()` is called from `_pauseLiveUpdates` (`accept_ride_trip.dart:117`) on every lifecycle pause. On Android and on the web (PWA tab in background) Dart timers keep firing while the app is hidden, so the 12 s timer runs during the pause, hits the `_suspended` guard and dies. After `resume()` nothing re-arms it: `mapActivity()` only reschedules when `_resumeTimer != null`, and a later `update()` only calls `_scheduleResume()` on `enteringGuidance`, which is false mid-trip. Reproduced with a throwaway Flutter test (controller with `autoResumeAfter` 50 ms: userGesture, touching=false, suspend, wait 120 ms, resume, wait 300 ms): `Expected: <1> Actual: <0> after resume the camera should still auto-return`, mode stayed `browsing`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver on an active trip pans the map (camera enters Free), switches to another app for more than 12 s on Android, comes back: the trip map stays where it was panned indefinitely; the camera never returns to the car until the driver touches the map again or taps recenter.
confirmed.evidence: driver_camera_controller.dart:472-484: `_resumeTimer = Timer(after, () { _resumeTimer = null; if (_disposed || _touching || _suspended || !isGuidance || mode != DriverCameraMode.browsing) { return; } ...`; 693-696: `void resume() { _suspended = false; _request(immediate: true); }`; 460-462: `void mapActivity() { if (_resumeTimer != null) _scheduleResume(); }`. Test run: `00:00 +0 -1: auto-resume timer that fires while suspended is never rescheduled [E] Expected: <1> Actual: <0>`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In the timer callback, when `_suspended` is true, leave `_resumeTimer` unset but have `resume()` call `_scheduleResume()` (it already checks mode/guidance/touching); alternatively cancel the timer in `suspend()` and re-arm it in `resume()`.

verdicts.reason: When the 12 s one-shot timer fires while _suspended is set, its callback clears _resumeTimer and returns (driver_camera_controller.dart:472-477). resume() (:693-696) only calls _request(immediate:true), which does nothing in browsing mode. mapActivity re-arms only when _resumeTimer != null (:460-462), and update() calls _scheduleResume only on enteringGuidance (:576-578). The trip's resume path (accept_ride.dart:715-719 -> accept_ride_trip.dart:137-153 _resumeLiveUpdates, plus _resyncTrip) never recenters or re-arms. didChangeAppLifecycleState also pauses on 'inactive', for example when the notification shade is pulled down, so this is easy to reach. The recenter button is the only way back.

confirmed.title: Off-route fix makes routeFraction 0: the island ETA, remaining distance and leg progress reset to the full route (and can trigger a false 'traffic ahead' strip message) until the reroute lands
confirmed.description: _rebuildBanner sets _progressAlong = progress.offRoute ? null : progress.alongMeters (line 481), so the next projection starts from scratch. routeFraction then reads (_progressAlong ?? 0) / length, so off route the driven share becomes 0 instead of unknown or the last value. AcceptRide uses it directly: _remainingMeters = total * (1 - (routeFraction ?? 0)) and _routeEtaText = seconds * (1 - (routeFraction ?? 0)) (accept_ride.dart:920, 927). The leg progress derived from remaining also drops to 0%. This holds through the 2 s reroute debounce plus the network fetch, and on any single fix more than 50 m off (accuracy up to 50 m is accepted).
confirmed.failure_scenario: 9 km into a 10 km trip, the driver takes a wrong turn or GPS drifts 60 m. The ETA chip jumps from '2 min' to the full original '18 min', the remaining distance shows the whole route, and route progress falls to 0%. They stay that way until the reroute lands, then jump back.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep the last on-route along value for routeFraction (a separate _lastOnRouteAlong field), or return null while off route and let callers keep their previous ETA, instead of treating null as 0.

verdicts.reason: navigation_controller.dart:481 sets _progressAlong to null on an off-route fix (more than 50 m from the polyline, route_progress.dart:34/98). routeFraction (line 156) then returns (null ?? 0)/length = 0. accept_ride.dart:920 and :927 multiply by (1 - 0), so _remainingMeters and _routeEtaText fall back to the full route values. _legFraction (accept_ride.dart:899-911) gets remaining equal to the route total and shows about 0%. While recalculating the island face shows the status, but the strip still renders the ETA and percent: _stripBody uses widget.eta and widget.progress (adaptive_trip_island.dart:836-860), and the strip is tucked only for arrival or a raised sheet (_syncTuck, :233-246). TripStripController.update (trip_island_controller.dart:~325) also sees etaMinutes jump by 2 or more and queues a false 'Traffic ahead +N min' message. This lasts through the 2 s reroute debounce plus the route request.

confirmed.title: A single fix that projects onto a later leg moves the instruction hint forward for good: the banner skips the turns in between and the car snaps to the other street
confirmed.description: measure() first projects inside [previousAlong-60, previousAlong+400]. The tie rule that prefers forward-consistent progress only applies within 10 m, so any later part of the route that is more than 10 m closer than the current leg wins. This can be a parallel street on an around-the-block route, or the opposite carriageway after a U-turn. The instruction search then starts at instructionHint and only moves forward. NavigationController stores the result unconditionally (_instructionHint = progress.instructionIndex, navigation_controller.dart:480), and DriverCameraPolicy does the same (driver_camera_controller.dart:266). When the next fixes project back onto the real leg (the window misses it, so the global projection is used), along goes back but the hint does not. The maneuvers between the two passes are skipped until a new route object resets the hint: the silent refresh comes after 90 s, or a reroute. The camera policy snaps vehiclePoint to the wrong leg for that fix (driver_camera_controller.dart:269-270), so the car marker jumps to the other street. Fixes with accuracy up to 50 m are accepted, and the jump filter subtracts both accuracies, so a 15-50 m urban-canyon drift is enough.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The pickup is around the block, or across a divided road that needs a U-turn. One GPS sample drifts toward the return leg. From then on the banner shows the arrival ('Pickup in 500 m') instead of the two turns ahead, for up to 90 s. The camera's turn framing is lost, and the car icon jumps onto the parallel street for that fix.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Do not let the windowed projection jump forward past a maneuver unless it is clearly better (for example, require the forward candidate to be consistent with the elapsed distance or speed). Also recompute the instruction index from projection.along when along goes backwards (search from 0, or step the hint back while maneuverAlong[hint-1] > along).

verdicts.reason: The tie rule applies only within 10 m (route_progress.dart:213-219). A single fix that lands more than 10 m closer to a later leg inside the +400 m window therefore wins, and the instruction loop moves forward from the stored hint without ever going back (route_progress.dart:100-121). NavigationController keeps that index without a check (navigation_controller.dart:480). The hint resets only on a new route (lines 176, 373, 416). Afterwards the windowed projection [along-60, along+400] no longer covers the true leg. It snaps to the top segment instead, about 35 m away, which is within the 50 m off-route threshold, so the global projection is never consulted and the stale arrival index stays. The fix with the bad offset is accepted because it is under 50 m off the route and the jump filter subtracts both accuracies (navigation_controller.dart:290-299). Downgraded from high to medium: it needs a lateral GPS error of roughly 45 m or more toward a nearby later leg.

confirmed.title: Corrupt local JSON records leak rider name, pickup/dropoff addresses (and trusted-contact phones) into DriverLog via FormatException source excerpts
confirmed.description: DriverLog's own contract (lib/core/logging/driver_log.dart:5-6: 'Messages must not contain rider names, phone numbers or free text') is violated by every storage reader that logs a jsonDecode error. Dart's FormatException.toString() appends ~78 characters of the offending source around the error offset, and the stored records are JSON blobs holding rider names, phone numbers and addresses (active ride), trusted-contact phone numbers (settings sections) and completion journals. Paths: PrefsActiveRideRepository.read -> `DriverLog.error('Active-ride snapshot parse failed', error, stack)` (line 81) and again through `_enqueue`'s catchError (line 57); LocalQuarantine.store builds `reason: '$error'` from callers (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:125, completion_journal.dart:157, settings_repository.dart:84) and then logs it: `DriverLog.warn('Quarantined $source record as $key: $reason')` (local_quarantine.dart:62). The default sink prints with debugPrint (driver_log.dart:42-43), which is not stripped in release builds, so this lands in logcat / the browser console; the file also says a crash-reporting adapter will be attached to this sink later. Reproduced with a throwaway flutter test: a truncated active-ride snapshot produced a log line containing `"riderPhone":"+46701234567","pickup":"Sveavägen 12, Stockholm"`, and a truncated contacts section produced `"phone":"+46709998877"` in the quarantine warning.
confirmed.failure_scenario: localStorage/SharedPreferences holds a half-written movera_driver_active_ride (e.g. tab killed mid-write) -> next launch Home calls read() -> the rider's name, phone and pickup address are printed to the device/browser log in a release build and would be shipped to any future crash-reporting sink.
confirmed.evidence: prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:80-82 `} catch (error, stack) { DriverLog.error('Active-ride snapshot parse failed', error, stack); throw ActiveRideUnreadable(error); }`; local_quarantine.dart:62 `DriverLog.warn('Quarantined $source record as $key: $reason');`; settings_repository.dart:84 `reason: '$storageKey: $error',`; driver_log.dart:5-6 `/// Messages must not contain rider names, phone numbers or free text; trip IDs and status names are allowed.`; test output: `Active-ride snapshot parse failed: FormatException: Unexpected end of input (at character 123)\n...na Svensson","riderPhone":"+46701234567","pickup":"Sveavägen 12, Stockholm"`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Log only the exception type/message without the source excerpt (e.g. `error is FormatException ? error.message : error.runtimeType`), and pass a scrubbed `reason` to LocalQuarantine (the raw text is already stored in the quarantine payload, so the reason need not repeat it).

verdicts.reason: The default sink prints the source excerpt that FormatException.toString() carries. In driver_log.dart:39-42 it formats '${record.message}: ${record.error}' and sends it through debugPrint, which still prints in release builds (logcat / browser console). That breaks the contract in driver_log.dart:5-6 that log messages must not contain rider names. The leak happens at prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:81 (the parse error), again at :57 (the _enqueue catchError re-logs ActiveRideUnreadable), and in local_quarantine.dart:62 via reason '$error' (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:125). No scrubbing guard exists on any of these paths. The trigger is an edge path: the record has to be corrupt, and SharedPreferences/localStorage writes are atomic, so 'killed mid-write' is unlikely. The app does build explicit quarantine handling for this case, though. The exposure is the device's local log, plus any future sink.
verdicts.repro: Ran the throwaway test test/_audit_d25log_test.dart (deleted afterwards). It put a truncated snapshot containing riderName/pickup under PrefsActiveRideRepository.key, captured DriverLog.sink, then called read() and quarantineUnreadable(). Output: 'LOG>> Active-ride snapshot parse failed: FormatException: Unterminated string (at character 130) ...erName":"Anna Svensson","pickup":"Sveavagen 12, Stockholm"...', the same excerpt again in 'Active-ride storage operation failed' and in 'Quarantined active_ride record as movera_driver_quarantine_active_ride_...'. Result: +1 All tests passed.

confirmed.title: Scheduled-ride waiting rule is found by searching the localized 'Scheduled ride' label, so French and Swedish drivers get different wait and no-show terms
confirmed.original_title: Scheduled-ride waiting rule is found by searching the localized 'Scheduled ride' label, so French and Swedish drivers get different wait and no-show terms
confirmed.description: AcceptRide builds `_waitTerms` from `WaitingRules.typeOf(matchedVia: widget.matchedVia, ...)` (accept_ride.dart:989-996). `typeOf` sees a scheduled ride only if `matchedVia.toLowerCase()` contains 'scheduled' or 'reservation'. 'Leave now' opens the trip with `matchedVia: tr.scheduledRide` (home_scheduled.dart:236). That is 'Scheduled ride' in English, 'Course planifiée' in French and 'Bokad resa' in Swedish, so in fr/sv the type falls back to `WaitingRideType.normal`. The scheduled rule is skipped: its free wait (`ScheduledRideRules.current.includedWaitingMinutes`), any admin perMin/noShowFee for `rideTypes.scheduled` (driver_app_config.dart reads them), and its 'Scheduled ride' rule label. The matchedVia string is also saved in the snapshot, so a restored trip keeps the wrong type.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Take a scheduled Movera XL reservation (category rule free 3 / no-show 3) and press Leave now. In English, termsFor applies XL, then scheduled sets free to 5, and the final guard lifts no-show to 5: 5 free minutes, no-show at 5 min. With the app in Swedish or French the same trip gets 3 free minutes and no-show at 3 min. Paid waiting therefore starts 2 minutes earlier (12,26 kr/min) and the driver can mark a no-show 2 minutes earlier, only because of the UI language. The waiting sheet also loses its 'Rule for this pickup: Scheduled ride' line. Worked out by hand from termsFor; nothing was run.
