confirmed.title: Ride-check audio stops capturing when the app is backgrounded (no iOS background audio mode, no Android microphone foreground service), but the counter and the saved length keep counting wall-clock time
confirmed.description: The Ride-check main step offers 'Call 112' and 'Record audio' side by side. Tapping Call 112 hands off to the dialer, which backgrounds the app; so does locking the screen. Info.plist has no UIBackgroundModes `audio`, so iOS suspends the app and the record session stops or is interrupted. Android 9+ gives silence to apps in the background, and the manifest has no microphone-type foreground service. AcceptRide.didChangeAppLifecycleState (accept_ride.dart:715-727) persists the trip and pauses GPS but does nothing about the recording. The controller computes `audioSeconds` as `now - _audioStartedAt`. When the driver comes back and taps stop, that wall-clock duration is shown ('Audio saved 3:12') and written to the Ride-check record (`copyWith(audioSeconds: seconds)`), although the file holds only the foreground part or silence.
confirmed.failure_scenario: During a frightening ride the driver taps Record audio, then Call 112 (or locks the phone). After 3 minutes they return and stop the recording. The card says 'Audio saved 3:12' and the trip detail stores 192 s, but the .m4a holds about 5 s (iOS) or 3 minutes of silence (Android). That evidence is missing when it matters.
confirmed.evidence:
ride_check_controller.dart:90-92 `int get audioSeconds => _audio == RideCheckAudio.recording ? services.now().difference(_audioStartedAt!).inSeconds : ...`
ride_check_controller.dart:277-287 `final seconds = audioSeconds; ... _record = _record?.copyWith(audioSeconds: seconds);`
ride_check_card.dart:491-495 Call 112 and :512 `_RecordAudio` on the same main step
accept_ride.dart:720-726 paused/hidden only `persistNow()` + `_pauseLiveUpdates()`
ios/Runner/Info.plist: no UIBackgroundModes; AndroidManifest.xml: no FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE / service
confirmed.suggested_fix: Stop (or pause and mark) the recording on paused/hidden and tell the driver. Take the saved duration from the file or the recorder's own amplitude/duration, not the wall clock. If background capture is wanted, add UIBackgroundModes audio and an Android microphone foreground service, with product and store sign-off.

verdicts.reason: The saved duration comes from the wall clock: audioSeconds = now - _audioStartedAt (ride_check_controller.dart:90-92), and _stopRecording stores it with `_record?.copyWith(audioSeconds: seconds)` once stop() returns any non-empty file (ride_check_controller.dart:283-300; ride_check_recorder_native.dart stop only checks that the file exists and is not empty). AcceptRide.didChangeAppLifecycleState (accept_ride.dart:715-727) persists the trip and pauses GPS on paused/hidden but leaves the recorder alone. The Call 112 button sits on the same main step as Record audio (ride_check_card.dart: ride-check-call-112 and _RecordAudio), so tapping it hands off to the dialer while recording. ios/Runner/Info.plist has no UIBackgroundModes, and AndroidManifest.xml declares only RECORD_AUDIO, with no foreground service or FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE. iOS suspends or interrupts the session, and Android silences background or in-call capture by non-call apps. The file therefore holds only the foreground part or silence, while the card and the trip record show the full wall-clock length. No document records this as intended. confirmed.title: Ride-check audio that is still starting when the card closes keeps the microphone recording with no UI, and dispose() never stops it after a later check opens
confirmed.description: `toggleRecording()` sets `_audio = starting`, awaits `recorder.requestPermission()` and then `recorder.start(...)` (lines 240-251). On native that start awaits `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()`, `Directory.create` and the plugin. If the driver answers meanwhile (`imOk`/`done` → `_close()`), `_close()` calls `_stopRecording()` which returns immediately because `_audio != recording` (line 275), then marks the record answered and closes the card. When `start()` later completes, the only guard is `if (_disposed)` (line 260): `_audio` becomes `recording`, `_audioStartedAt` is set and a periodic 1 s ticker starts notifying listeners (lines 264-270) although the card is closed and `_answerable` is false, so nothing on screen shows a recording and no button can stop it. If a further Ride check opens later, `open()` resets `_audio = idle` (line 114) without touching the recorder or the ticker, after which `dispose()` skips the stop because `_audio != recording` (line 412) — the native recorder is never stopped for the rest of the process. Reproduced with a throwaway flutter test using a recorder whose `start()` awaits a Completer: after `imOk()` and completing start, `c.audio == RideCheckAudio.recording` and the fake recorder was still recording; after `open()` of a second event and `dispose()`, the recorder was still recording with `stops == 0` (test output: `after close: audio=RideCheckAudio.recording recorderRecording=true stops=0` / `after dispose: recorderRecording=true stops=0`). The test file was deleted afterwards.

confirmed.title: If the one-time prime() fails (play rejected), the radar player stays at volume 0 and is never primed again, so later offer alerts play silently
confirmed.description: `prime()` sets volume 0, plays, stops, then sets volume 1, with no try/finally. If `setSource` or `play` throws, `setVolume(1)` never runs. On web, audioplayers_web awaits `player.play().toDart`, which rejects with NotAllowedError outside user activation. Home calls `tap()` from `Listener.onPointerDown` (home.dart:707), and a touch pointerdown is not an activation-triggering event on mobile browsers. The failure is swallowed by `_then`'s queue (`_queue = next.catchError(...)`) and by `tap()`'s `.catchError((Object _) {})`. `_primed` is already true, so prime never runs again. `startLoop()` only sets the release mode and plays; it never restores the volume. Once a later tap gives the page sticky activation, the loop plays, but silently. Home's `RadarOfferSound` lives as long as Home.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On a phone browser the driver's first touch on Home starts prime. play() rejects (not yet a user activation), so the player stays at volume 0. For the rest of the session, new Radar offers start the looped alert at volume 0. The driver hears nothing and misses offers.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Wrap the body of prime in try/finally and always `setVolume(1)` in the finally; reset `_primed = false` on failure so a later tap retries, or pass `volume: 1` in `startLoop`'s play call.

confirmed.title: Saved Ride-preferences category choice is never restored at boot, so switched-off categories are offered again after every restart
confirmed.description: `DriverCategoryChoice.off` (ride_categories.dart:56) is the in-memory set that every offer filter reads (`DriverCategoryChoice.takes` in home_offer_rules.dart:13/21/30, home_reservation.dart:107/132, scheduled_rides.dart:545). The only writer is the Ride preferences screen: `_publishChoice()` runs after `_restoreSettings()` or a toggle (preferences.dart:118/172), i.e. only once that screen has been opened. The choice is persisted to the `categories` settings section (preferences.dart:140), but nothing reads it back at app start: `main.dart:41-49` restores `MapTrafficSetting` and `DriverLanguage` and nothing else, and `DriverCategoryChoice` has no restore method. After a cold start `off` is the empty const set, so `takes()` returns true for every allowed category. The class comment (`ride_categories.dart:51`, 'kept for the session') documents the in-memory nature but the persisted setting and the Q27 promise ('offers follow that choice') make the restart behaviour wrong. The same global is also not reset on logout (`main.dart:180-195` calls `MapTrafficSetting.reset()` / `DriverLanguage.reset()` but not `DriverCategoryChoice.reset()`), so after logout the cleared storage and the stale in-memory set disagree until Preferences is opened again.

confirmed.title: WaybillPayment.fromFare reads only the first digit group of a thousands-grouped fare label, so earnings/fee are wrong for fares >= 1 000 kr
confirmed.description: Money.formatted groups thousands with a space ("1 234,50 kr", lib/core/money/money.dart:187 via _group). RideOffer.fareLabel (dispatch_repository.dart:114) and WaitingTerms.addFee (waiting_rules.dart:77, used for _fareWithWaiting on completion) both produce this format, and it is what reaches WaybillRecord.fare. WaybillPayment.fromFare parses the label with `RegExp(r'\d+(?:[.,]\d{1,2})?').firstMatch(fare)` which matches only the leading "1" of "1 234,50 kr", so fareOre becomes 100 and _comma is false. Consumers: waybill_sheet.dart:70 (`WaybillPayment.fromFare(record.fare, bonus: record.driverBonus)` -> "Your earnings" row) and OfferCardDetails.fare (offer_rules.dart:157, the net-fare mode admin can switch on for offer cards). Money.parseSekLabel already accepts the grouped form (money.dart:73), so the producer and this consumer disagree. Reproduced with a throwaway flutter test: `Money(minorUnits:123450).formatted` = "1 234,50 kr"; `WaybillPayment.fromFare(that)` gave fare=1.00 kr, fee=0.25 kr, earnings=0.75 kr; `OfferCardDetails(netFare:true).fare(label)` = "0.75 kr".
confirmed.failure_scenario: A driver completes a 1 234,50 kr trip (any backend Offer.fare >= 100000 minor units, or a demo fare pushed over 1 000 kr by waiting fees). Opening the waybill shows "Your earnings 0.75 kr" and "Service fee 0.25 kr" instead of about 925,88 kr / 308,62 kr; with netFare on, the offer card shows a 0.75 kr net fare for a 1 234 kr trip.
confirmed.evidence: waybill.dart:296 `final match = RegExp(r'\d+(?:[.,]\d{1,2})?').firstMatch(fare);` ... :301 `final fareOre = (value * 100).round();`  |  money.dart:187 `return '$sign${_group(int.parse(parts[0]))},${parts[1]} $symbol';` (groups thousands with a space)  |  waybill_sheet.dart:70 `final payment = WaybillPayment.fromFare(record.fare, bonus: record.driverBonus);`  |  test output: `formatted = "1 234,50 kr"` / `fare=1.00 kr fee=0.25 kr earnings=0.75 kr` / `netFare card = 0.75 kr` / `parseSekLabel = 123450`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Parse the fare with Money.parseLabel/parseSekLabel (which understand grouped thousands and the currency suffix) instead of the ad-hoc regex, e.g. `final money = Money.parseLabel(fare); if (money == null) return null; fareOre = money.minorUnits;` and keep the comma flag from the label. Add a test for a >= 1 000 kr label.

verdicts.reason: WaybillPayment.fromFare (lib/core/waybill/waybill.dart:296) reads only the first digit group of `RegExp(r'\d+(?:[.,]\d{1,2})?')`. confirmed.title: Waybill sheet takes Movera's 25% fee on the paid waiting fee and shows it in 'Base price' / 'Paid by the passenger', contradicting 'You get 100% of the wait time'
confirmed.description: At completion `_paidWaybill()` folds the driver's waiting fee into the waybill fare (`fare: _fareWithWaiting`, accept_ride_trip.dart:72-80, 912-913). Meanwhile the waiting sheet says 'You get 100% of the wait time' (driverShareWaitPercent = 100), the completion screen says 'Includes X waiting fee', and the code comments say 'Q43: the waiting fee is the driver's, in the trip's earnings'. verdicts.reason: accept_ride_trip.dart:82-90 folds driverWaitingFee into the record fare, and _completeCurrentTrip (accept_ride_trip.dart:940) stores that record. The test driver_waiting_earnings_test.dart confirms the stored fare is '118,39 kr' with waitingFee '18,39 kr'. DriverRideCompleted opens showMoveraWaybillSheet (ride_completed.dart:225), which calls WaybillPayment.fromFare(record.fare, bonus: record.driverBonus) at waybill_sheet.dart:70 and never passes waitingFee. waybill.dart:317-325 then computes fee = round((fare - bonus) * 0.25) on 11839 = 2960, so earnings show 88,79 kr instead of 75,00 + 18,39 = 93,39 kr. Base price and 'Paid by the passenger' show 118,39 kr. Meanwhile waiting_rules.dart:31-33/60-65 defines driverShareWaitPercent=100 as the share of the waiting money that goes to the driver. The app tells the driver 'You get 100% of the wait time' (waiting_time_sheet.dart:251), and ride_completed.dart:174 says 'Q43: the waiting fee is all the driver's'. The bonus is deliberately kept out of the commission; the waiting fee has no such exclusion. Severity is medium rather than high because it occurs only when the paid wait goes past the free minutes, and the 25% rate is a documented placeholder (waybill.dart:284-286). The displayed earnings are still wrong relative to the app's own rule.

verdicts.reason: accept_ride_trip.dart:84-92 _paidWaybill() puts the driver's waiting fee into `fare` (WaitingTerms.addFee) and only records waitingFee as a label. waybill_sheet.dart:70 calls WaybillPayment.fromFare(record.fare, bonus: record.driverBonus). Only the bonus is taken out of the commission base (waybill.dart:317-319, _riderOre = fare - bonus; _feeOre = riderOre*0.25), so Movera's 25% is also taken on the waiting fee. The waiting fee also appears inside 'Base price · <service>' (waybill_sheet.dart:91). No document lists the waiting fee as commissionable. confirmed.title: Logout keeps the previous driver's notifications and document-renewal state (DriverNotificationFeed, DocumentExpiryStore)
confirmed.description: DriverNotificationFeed.instance and DocumentExpiryStore.instance are process singletons, and both have reset() methods ('Back to the demo list at the next reading'). No code in lib/ calls them, and _logout does not. Notifications that Home adds while driver A works stay in the feed for driver B: scheduled-ride reminders carrying the pickup address (home_scheduled.dart:271-282), Exclusive offers, rest-over notices. A's read/unread state stays too. A's document uploads ('in review' via uploadNew) and approvals stay in DocumentExpiryStore, so B's Documents screen, the going-online block and the island hold show A's document status. The test harness resets both before every test (flutter_test_config.dart:65-68) because they are per-driver state.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver A gets 'Head to your 08:15 pickup · Södermalm, Stockholm' and uploads a new insurance letter (now 'in review'), then logs out. Driver B opens Notifications and sees A's reminders with A's rider pickup addresses, already marked read. B's Documents screen shows A's insurance in review.
confirmed.evidence: driver_notifications.dart:170 `void reset() { _items = null; _read.clear(); _popups.clear(); arrivals = DriverNotices.demoArrivals; ...}`; document_expiry.dart:190 `void reset() { _documents = null; _warned.clear(); _changes.value++; }`; neither is called from lib/ (grep). home_scheduled.dart:272-280 adds `DriverNotices.scheduledReminder(at: feed.now, title: title, body: body /* ride.pickupAddress */ ...)`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Call DriverNotificationFeed.instance.reset() and DocumentExpiryStore.instance.reset() from _logout.

verdicts.reason: _logout (lib/main.dart:180-195) resets waybills, dispatch, safety alerts, session, language and traffic, and clearLocalUserData clears SharedPreferences. It never calls DriverNotificationFeed.instance.reset() (lib/core/notifications/driver_notifications.dart:170) or DocumentExpiryStore.instance.reset() (lib/core/documents/document_expiry.dart:190). A grep finds no caller of either in lib/. The Profile logout path (profile.dart:396-397) does not call them either. Both are in-memory process singletons (driver_notifications.dart:102, document_expiry.dart:70), so the feed items, read state, popups, and document uploads or 'in review' states survive logout and log-in in the same process. Only the test harness resets them (test/flutter_test_config.dart:65-68). The app only advertises clearing persisted data (docs/LOCAL_DATA.md), but these singletons hold per-driver state that leaks to the next account, so this is an edge-path leak.
verdicts.repro: Traced _logout and the Profile logout handler. Grepped lib/ for reset calls on both singletons (none). Confirmed both singletons keep their state only in memory and that only flutter_test_config resets them.

confirmed.title: A restored trip loses its pickup distance (and bags), so the waiting terms change after the app is killed and reopened: far-pickup free wait and no-show fee are replaced by the defaults
confirmed.description: _waitTerms is computed from widget.pickupKm (WaitingRules.termsFor applies the farPickup rule when pickupKm > 5: freeMinutes 1, noShowFee 85 kr). Home, Radar and Ride requests pass offer.pickupKm into AcceptRide. PersistedActiveRide has no pickupKm field, so _buildSnapshot cannot save it, and AcceptRide.fromPersisted does not pass it. After a crash, reload or PWA resume, the same trip gets base terms: 5 free minutes and a 65 kr no-show fee. The waiting clock, the paid seconds, the cash to collect, the driver's earnings and the no-show threshold all change in the middle of the trip. bags is also not saved or restored, so the island's bag notice disappears.

The island now shows those 4 minutes as included free wait, so the paid wait and the waiting fee drop to 0. The no-show fee the driver is promised falls from 85 kr to 65 kr.
confirmed.evidence:
accept_ride.dart:989-996 `late final WaitingTerms _waitTerms = WaitingRules.current.termsFor(category: widget.category, type: ..., pickupKm: widget.pickupKm);`
accept_ride.dart:253-291 fromPersisted passes no pickupKm and no bags.
waiting_rules.dart `if (pickupKm != null && pickupKm > farPickupKm) { ... terms = terms._with(farPickup, ...); }` with farPickup freeMinutes 1, noShowFee 8500 ore.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Save pickupKm (and bags) in PersistedActiveRide.toJson/fromJson/stamped, write them in _buildSnapshot, and pass them through AcceptRide.fromPersisted. Better still, save the resolved WaitingTerms so the trip keeps the terms it was accepted under.

verdicts.reason: PersistedActiveRide (lib/core/ride/active_ride_repository.dart:136-180) has no pickupKm field, and AcceptRide.fromPersisted (accept_ride.dart:240-291) passes no pickupKm. So after a restore, _waitTerms (accept_ride.dart:989-996) runs WaitingRules.termsFor with pickupKm == null and skips the farPickup rule (waiting_rules.dart:226-231: 1 free minute, 85 kr no-show fee). The trip falls back to base terms: 5 free minutes, 65 kr. On first accept the offer's pickupKm is passed in (home_offer_radar.dart:133/982/1064, ride_requests.dart:167). Nothing reachable sets pickupKm above 5 in demo mode, because every demo offer is under 5 km. But ApiDispatchRepository builds pickupKm from pickupMeters/1000 (api_dispatch_repository.dart:73), so live offers over 5 km reach this path. The no-show threshold, waiting fee and cash total then change mid-trip after a restore. Nothing in DECISIONS.md or LOCAL_DATA.md documents dropping these terms.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: PersistedActiveRide fields, then the fromPersisted argument list, then _waitTerms, then the termsFor farPickup branch. I grepped every pickupKm source; only the API adapter can exceed 5 km. No test run.

verdicts.reason: _waitTerms (accept_ride.dart:1018-1025) is computed from widget.pickupKm, and termsFor (waiting_rules.dart:226) applies farPickup (1 free minute, 85 kr no-show fee) when pickupKm > 5. PersistedActiveRide has no pickupKm field (active_ride_repository.dart:138-188), _buildSnapshot does not save one (accept_ride_trip.dart:23-73), and AcceptRide.fromPersisted (accept_ride.dart:253-291) does not pass one. A restored trip therefore gets null pickupKm and the base terms (5 free minutes, 65 kr). Real offers can be over 5 km because ApiDispatchRepository sets pickupKm = pickupMeters/1000 (api_dispatch_repository.dart:73), and the Home, Radar and Ride requests screens pass offer.pickupKm on. All demo offers are under 5 km, so the bug only shows with live dispatch.

confirmed.title: Resuming a stale (>6 h) waiting snapshot adds the whole gap to the pickup wait, putting thousands of kronor of waiting fee on the trip
confirmed.description: Home offers 'Resume trip' for a snapshot that fails isFresh (home.dart:530-535, the button is enabled whenever endpoints are verified). AcceptRide.initState then adds now - savedAt to _waitSeconds whenever the restored stage is waitingForRider or a stop wait. The free 6-hour window, which exists so 'an abandoned trip cannot revive days later' (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:16-17), is not respected for the wait clock, and WaitingTerms.waitingFee has no cap. When the driver slides to start, _paidWaitSeconds += paidWait, and the fee goes into the archived fare and the cash to collect.

At 12,26 kr/min that is about 5 088 kr of waiting fee, added to the fare and the cash to collect, for a trip the driver resumed after the app sat dead overnight.

home.dart:535 `FilledButton(onPressed: snapshot.hasVerifiedEndpoints ? () => popOwned(context, true) : null, child: Text(tr.resumeTrip))`
waiting_rules.dart:53-58 waitingFee is uncapped

confirmed.title: Next-trip ids are '<tripId>-next' for every offer during a trip, so a re-offered next trip collides in history and its completion is never archived
confirmed.description: _uniqueDemoNext (and _onTripRadarOfferForDestination at accept_ride_trip.dart:1038) gives every next-trip offer during trip A the same id: '${widget.tripId}-next' or '-next-destination'. trip_occurrence.dart says every accept path must use a per-occurrence id 'so a repeated demo ride is never hidden as an already-finished trip'; this path does not. Cancelling a secured next trip archives it in history with that id (accept_ride_sheet.dart:270-286). Radar then returns to scanning and the next offer reuses the same id. If the driver secures it, finishes A and completes B, the journal's non-authoritative archive finds an existing row with that tripId and returns without writing (prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:201-202).

The next onTrip location update calls _maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer (accept_ride_trip.dart:712-713), which shows a new offer with the same id; _onTripRadarDeclined is not set by the cancel. If the driver secures that offer and finishes A, trip B runs with tripId 'A-next'. The driver's own finish, _completeCurrentTrip, calls CompletionJournal.finish without authoritative (accept_ride_trip.dart:942-945). The history archive then finds the existing 'A-next' row and returns early (prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:201-202). The completed trip never reaches history and stays listed as a driver cancel.

verdicts.reason: Every demo next-trip offer during trip A gets id '${tripId}-next' (accept_ride.dart:996-998), or '-next-destination' (accept_ride_trip.dart:1073). _cancelNextTrip archives the queued waybill as a driver cancel and returns the radar to scanning (accept_ride_sheet.dart:256-287). It does not set _onTripRadarDeclined, so _maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer, called again on location updates (accept_ride_trip.dart:719, 1100-1140), offers a new trip with the same id. Once that trip is secured and then completed, the driver's completion goes through CompletionJournal.finish with authoritative false (accept_ride_trip.dart:949-952), then history.archive. The archive returns early when a row with that tripId already exists (prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:201-202). The completed trip and its earnings are lost, and History keeps showing it as cancelled by the driver.

confirmed.title: On any cash trip with a Movera bonus, the app tells the driver to collect the full fare, bonus included, from the rider (API offers never carry cashToCollect)
confirmed.description: RideOffer.driverBonus is 'Movera-paid extra… [fare] already includes it', and WaybillPayment says of the bonus 'the rider never pays it'. On a cash trip whose offer has no explicit cashToCollect (null means 'the fare'), `_cashToCollect` falls back to `widget.fare`, which includes the bonus. That amount (plus the waiting fee) is what the Collect cash sheet shows in the big 'Collect … in cash' tray, and it is journaled as cashCollected. api_dispatch_repository parses driverBonus and paymentMethod independently, so a cash + bonus offer is a valid input.

confirmed.evidence:

verdicts.reason: accept_ride.dart:1040-1042 `_cashToCollect => WaitingTerms.addFee(widget.cashToCollect ?? widget.fare, ...)` falls back to the full fare. confirmed.title: On-trip next-trip offer card floats over the web map without PointerInterceptor or the map-gesture block that every other overlay uses
confirmed.description: When `_incomingOfferOpen` is true, the sliding panel collapses to 0 height (minHeight 0 / maxHeight 1), so the full-screen map (an HtmlElementView on web) lies under the card. Every other overlay on this screen goes through `_mapOverlay` (PointerInterceptor plus `_setMapGesturesBlocked`): the sheet, the island, the map controls and the Ride check layer. Home's equivalent offer sheet is also wrapped in PointerInterceptor, with the comment 'Opaque to touches: nothing under the sheet (dock, map) gets them'. The incoming ride card is added bare, so on web the map's DOM element receives pointer events in the card's area, and `_blockMapGestures` is never set while the driver touches it.

confirmed.evidence:
accept_ride.dart:1347-1354
```
if (offerOpen)
  Positioned(
    key: const ValueKey<String>('on-trip-radar-layer'),
    ...
    child: _AcceptRidePanel(this)._buildIncomingRideCard(),
  ),
```
versus accept_ride.dart:1177/1279/1342/1359 `_AcceptRidePanel(this)._mapOverlay(...)`; accept_ride_panel.dart:13-22 `_mapOverlay` = `PointerInterceptor(child: Listener(onPointerDown: (_) => _setMapGesturesBlocked(true) ...))`; home_offer_sheet.dart:291-292 `// Opaque to touches: nothing under the sheet (dock, map) gets them. final sheet = PointerInterceptor(`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Wrap the card in `_AcceptRidePanel(this)._mapOverlay(child: ...)`, as the other overlays are.

verdicts.reason: The incoming next-trip card is placed directly in the outer Stack (accept_ride.dart:1347-1354), above the full-screen map. Unlike every other overlay on this screen (sheet 1177, map controls 1342, Ride check 1359), it is not wrapped in _mapOverlay, which is PointerInterceptor plus the map-gesture block (accept_ride_panel.dart:13-22). While offerOpen is true the panel is collapsed to height 0 (1148-1149), so the card sits only over the map. The map comes from google_maps_flutter (pubspec:50), which is an HtmlElementView on web. The pointer_interceptor README (0.10.1+2) documents this exact case: clicks over an HtmlElementView are taken by it and not relayed to Flutter, for example a FAB over a full-screen map. The app depends on that behaviour everywhere else, and home_offer_sheet.dart:291-292 wraps the equivalent Home offer sheet for that reason. The card's AbsorbPointer flag _blockMapGestures is also never set while it is touched.
verdicts.repro: I traced this statically: the Stack layout in accept_ride.dart:1144-1366, the _mapOverlay definition, the PointerInterceptor usages across lib/, and the pointer_interceptor README in the pub cache. Not reproduced in a browser: flutter test cannot exercise web platform-view hit-testing.

verdicts.reason: In accept_ride.dart:1380-1387 the on-trip offer card is placed as a bare `Positioned(... child: _AcceptRidePanel(this)._buildIncomingRideCard())`. _buildIncomingRideCard (accept_ride_panel.dart:192-200) returns a plain Material/Container with no PointerInterceptor. Every other overlay on this map goes through `_mapOverlay` (accept_ride_panel.dart:13-22: PointerInterceptor plus Listener for _setMapGesturesBlocked): the panel at 1210, the island at 1312, the controls at 1375 and Ride check at 1392. While the offer is open, the sliding panel collapses to 0/1 height (1181-1182), so only the full-screen map lies under the card. On web the map is google_maps_flutter's HtmlElementView (DECISIONS.md:79-81 names Safari/PWA as a supported target). Without PointerInterceptor, DOM pointer events over a platform view go to the map element, not to Flutter widgets drawn above it. AbsorbPointer(_blockMapGestures) at 1226 cannot help: it only blocks Flutter-side events, and the flag is never set by this card.

confirmed.title: A destination set on the trip screen is lost when the trip returns to Home, but it still counts against today's limit
confirmed.description: Destination mode lives in three places: Home's `_destinationModeActive/_destinationAddress/_destinationPosition`, AcceptRide's `_destinationActive/...` (copied from the widget at mount, accept_ride.dart:471-473), and the `DestinationModeSession.instance` singleton (daily count, `_activeSince`, route). Setting a destination during a trip (R13-18) calls `OnTripDestination.started()`, which adds one use for today and starts the time limit, and then updates only the trip screen's copy. Nothing writes it back to Home. After completion (popUntil first), a cancel (pop) or a rider cancel, Home still has `_destinationModeActive == false`. It never reads `DestinationModeSession` to restore it and never arms its `_destinationLimitTimer`. The next trip in the chain receives the destination, but Home never does.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Default rules allow 2 destinations per day. During a trip the driver sets destination 'Solna' from the island. On-trip offers follow it. After the trip ends, Home shows no destination: no route and no on-the-way filtering of Radar offers. If the driver sets it again on Home, that is the second use. A third attempt is refused with 'destinations used today', although only one was ever visible on Home.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make DestinationModeSession (or a shared notifier) the single owner of the active destination. Home and AcceptRide should read it and listen to it instead of keeping private copies, and Home should pick up a destination set during the trip when it becomes visible again.

verdicts.reason: accept_ride_panel.dart:183-189 calls OnTripDestination.started(), which counts a use in DestinationModeSession (next_trip_gate.dart:73, destination_mode_session.dart:41-48), and sets only the trip screen's private _destinationActive/_destinationAddress/_destinationPosition. Home writes _destinationModeActive only in home_map_sheet.dart:321/484 and home.dart:966, and never reads DestinationModeSession's active state on return (didPopNext, home.dart:178-186, only resumes updates and recovery). The value goes forward to the next chained trip (accept_ride_trip.dart:982) but never back to Home. After the trip ends the driver has used one of today's destinations, while Home shows no destination, no route and no on-the-way filter. A later set on Home counts as another use (home_map_sheet.dart:273/309).
verdicts.repro: Static trace: every writer of Home's _destinationModeActive (grep), the DestinationModeSession API, and Home's didPopNext.

verdicts.reason: _openDestinationPicker (accept_ride_panel.dart:183-189) calls OnTripDestination.started(), which counts toward today's limit in DestinationModeSession. It then sets only AcceptRide's local _destinationActive/_destinationAddress/_destinationPosition. Home pushes AcceptRide with pushSingle and ignores the result (home_offer_radar.dart:956-997). Home's _destinationModeActive is set only in home_map_sheet.dart:321 and cleared at 484 and home.dart:966. didPopNext (home.dart:176-186) never reads DestinationModeSession. So after the trip Home shows no destination while the daily count has gone up (default limit 2, trip_rules_admin_config.dart:41). None of the docs say a trip-set destination is meant to end with the trip.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand: Home push (home_offer_radar.dart:993-995 passes Home's copy) -> on-trip set (accept_ride_panel.dart:183) -> completion popUntil/pop (ride_completed.dart:79) -> Home didPopNext (home.dart:176), where no destination is restored. No test run.

confirmed.title: A terminal projection (admin/system cancel, rider cancel, completed) that arrives while an earlier projection is still draining is never applied
confirmed.description: _onRealtimeEvent stores each status event in _pendingProjection and calls _drainProjection(). If a drain is already running (_drainingProjection true, e.g. it is awaiting applyProjection's save for an earlier stage projection), the new call returns at line 300 without scheduling a retry. When the first drain finishes, the non-terminal branch (lines 340-348) leaves the newer event in _pendingProjection because it is not identical to the one it drained, and the finally block only clears _drainingProjection. Nothing calls _drainProjection again. DriverRealtimeSequenceGate has already recorded the trip as terminal, so every later status event for the trip is dropped as blockedAfterTerminal, and a resync re-delivers the same eventId, which the gate drops as a duplicate. The terminal outcome is only picked up if the driver later tries to finish or cancel (through _yieldToAuthoritativeTerminal).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Reproduced with a throwaway widget test. AcceptRide is at headingToPickup and the repository save is held. Emitting the projection `arrived` and then `cancelled_by_admin`, releasing the save and pumping 10 s leaves the active snapshot at waitingForRider and the trip history empty (output: `AUDIT snapshot=ActiveRideStage.waitingForRider history=[]`). The driver keeps navigating to a trip Movera cancelled. After a kill and reopen, Home restores the cancelled trip from the snapshot.
confirmed.evidence:
accept_ride_trip.dart:300 `if (!mounted || _drainingProjection || _pendingProjection == null) { return; }`
accept_ride_trip.dart:340-347 `if (!await _rideLifecycle.applyProjection(status)) { return; } ... if (identical(event, _pendingProjection)) { _pendingProjection = null; }`
driver_realtime.dart:296-298 `if (_terminalTrips.contains(event.tripId) && !event.kind.passesAfterTerminal) { return DriverRealtimeDisposition.blockedAfterTerminal; }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: When _drainProjection returns early because a drain is running, set a 'drain again' flag, or schedule _projectionRetry. At the end of a drain, run again whenever _pendingProjection is not the event just handled.

verdicts.reason: _onRealtimeEvent sets `_pendingProjection = event` and calls `_drainProjection` (accept_ride_trip.dart:263-264). While a drain is running, the new call returns at line 310 (`_drainingProjection`) and does NOT schedule a retry. The retry timer is armed only on the `saving`/in-flight branch at 311-316, which comes after this check. When the first drain finishes its non-terminal branch (357-368), `identical(event, _pendingProjection)` is false, so the newer event stays pending, and `finally` only clears the flag (375). Nothing else calls _drainProjection except the retry timer, the SnackBar action and `_yieldToAuthoritativeTerminal` (928), which runs only when the driver finishes or cancels. The sequence gate already marked the trip terminal, so later events are dropped (driver_realtime.dart blockedAfterTerminal). On resync, a terminal projection keeps its original identity (driver_realtime.dart:462-467), so it is dropped as a duplicate. The race window is only as long as the projection save (`applyProjection` → `_write`), but a back-to-back status burst (resync/gap) is realistic. I rate it medium rather than high because it needs that timing.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _drainProjection (accept_ride_trip.dart:309-376), _scheduleProjectionRetry (378-389), every caller of _drainProjection (grep: 264, 313, 373, 387, 928), ActiveRideController.applyProjection/_write (active_ride_controller.dart:111-158, 274-305) and MemoryDriverRealtime.reconnectAndResync (driver_realtime.dart:454-480). I did not re-run the finder's widget test.

verdicts.reason: accept_ride_trip.dart:310 returns early when `_drainingProjection` is true and does not schedule a retry. When the first drain takes the non-terminal branch (line 359), `identical(event, _pendingProjection)` at line 368 is false, so the newer terminal event stays pending. The finally block at line 375 only resets the flag. `_scheduleProjectionRetry` runs only from the catch and rider-cancel paths. Line 935 (`_yieldToAuthoritativeTerminal`) is the only other caller, and it runs only when the driver finishes or cancels. Every later status event for the trip is dropped by the realtime gate, either as blockedAfterTerminal or as a duplicate.

confirmed.title: An authoritative `completed` projection archives a cash trip without its payment method, cash collected or waiting fee
confirmed.description: The driver's own Finish (`_completeCurrentTrip`, lines 912-917) journals `_paidWaybill()` (fare incl. the driver's waiting fee) with `paymentMethod: 'Cash'` and `cashCollected` for a cash trip; `TripHistoryRecord.cashBalance` and the history 'Other earnings' cash accounting depend on `paymentMethod == 'cash'`. The realtime terminal path in `_drainProjection` (contract rows `complete` by admin from rider_onboard/in_trip/approaching_dropoff, or a server echo of `completed`) journals `_waybills.current ?? _buildCurrentWaybill()` with only `status` and `authoritative: true`. The archived row then has no `paymentMethod`/`cashCollected` and no waiting fee, so the driver's cash balance for that trip (what they owe or are owed) silently disappears from history, and with `authoritative: true` it also overwrites a correct local row if one was written first.

confirmed.title: A repeated same-stage (onTrip) projection restarts the next-trip radar: an accepted (matching) or shown Exclusive offer is dropped, and the route and camera are re-fitted
confirmed.description: `_drainProjection` treats a successful `applyProjection` as a stage change: `if (!await _rideLifecycle.applyProjection(status)) { return; } if (mounted) { _rebuild(() {}); _resumeStageSideEffects(); }` (lines 340-342). But `ActiveRideController.applyProjection` returns true without changing anything when `next == _stage` (active_ride_controller.dart: 'Realtime may repeat the same stage each poll ... if (next == _stage) { return true; }'). Same-stage projections are normal: `reconnectAndResync` (called on every app resume, accept_ride.dart:719, and on every sequence gap, accept_ride_trip.dart:248) re-emits the cached projection with a new sequence (driver_realtime.dart:468-482), and a poll/echo would do the same. For `onTrip`, `_resumeStageSideEffects` (100-115) then calls `_rideCheckDetector.startTrip(...)` (forgetting any long-stop/off-route progress), `_demoDrive?.startTrip()`, `_startOnTripRadar()` (995-1008) which cancels `_nextTripRadarMatchTimer` and sets `scanning` with `_nextTripRadarOffer = null` — so an offer the driver has just accepted (900 ms `matching` window, 1190-1208) is silently discarded after `ExclusiveAnswers.accepted()` was already counted, and an offer on screen disappears — and finally `_refreshOnTripRoute(fitCamera: true)` forces a route re-fetch and camera re-follow. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test: on-trip demo offer shown, tap 'match next', emit an `in_trip` projection: `securedCardPresent=false offerVisible=true` (the same offer is re-presented as a new one instead of being secured).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver on trip accepts the Exclusive next-trip offer; within a second the app is resumed or a projection echo arrives with status in_trip. The match timer is cancelled, the state goes back to scanning, the accepted trip is lost and the same offer pops up again (or is gone if declined before); the long-stop ride-check timer also restarts from zero.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Only run `_resumeStageSideEffects()` when the stage actually changed (compare `_stage` before/after `applyProjection`, or have `applyProjection` report 'unchanged' distinctly), and make `_startOnTripRadar` a no-op when state is `matching`/`offerAvailable`.

confirmed.title: When the first GPS fix fails, the trip asks for and draws a road route from the hard-coded Stockholm placeholder position
confirmed.description: `_driverPosition` starts as `_fallbackDriverPosition = LatLng(59.3262, 18.0595)` (accept_ride.dart:423 and 543) and changes only when a real fix is applied (`_applyDriverPosition`, line 660). When `getCurrentPosition` fails, the catch calls `_refreshRoadRoute(force: true)`. With external routing on, which is the build default (driver_runtime_config.dart:88-91), that calls `_navigation.ensureRoute(origin: GeoPointMaps.fromLatLng(_driverPosition), ...)` (line 704-709). It fetches a route from that placeholder to the pickup and draws it: `_roadGeoPoints`, `_routeDurationSeconds`, the turn banner and the ride-check plan all come from it. Combined with the missing stream subscription above, this route stays on screen.

DriverRideHistory)` at accept_ride.dart:1307, or Chat from the trip options), GPS keeps flowing into `_applyDriverPosition`, which calls `_maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer`. An offer is presented and its 15 s expiry runs. `_denyNextTripRadar` then counts it as missed through `ExclusiveAnswers.instance.missed()`; at the admin's limit that calls `setOnline(false)` and shows 'offline after missed'. confirmed.title: The 'offline after missed offers' notice posted during a trip is consumed by the hidden Home island, so the driver never sees it
confirmed.description: `IslandMessages` is a static queue meant for the Home island. Home subscribes in initState (home.dart:487) and never pauses that listener when another route covers it (`_pauseHomeUpdates` does not touch it). `_showNextIslandMessage` (home_map_sheet.dart:1257) takes the next message as soon as it is posted and starts its display timer. It checks only `mounted`, not `_routeVisible`. When the trip screen (pushed over Home) reaches the missed-Exclusive limit, it calls `setOnline(false)`, which during a trip only records offline-after-trip, and posts `HomeIslandNotices.offlineAfterMissed`. The trip screen's own island never reads IslandMessages, so Home, which is not visible, dequeues the message and drops it after 4.5 s.
confirmed.failure_scenario: During a trip the driver lets 3 next-trip Exclusive offers run out (the admin default auto-offline count). The session records offline-after-trip, but nothing appears on the trip screen. When the trip ends, Home is offline with no explanation, because the 'went offline after N missed offers' message was shown and expired on the covered Home island minutes earlier.

confirmed.title: Silent GPS (no fixes, no error) leaves _hasLiveLocation true, so the Ride-check tick reads a GPS outage as a long stop and safety alerts send a stale position as current
confirmed.description: _hasLiveLocation is cleared only by a stream error, an unusable fix or a pause. When the stream simply goes quiet (tunnel, garage), it stays true indefinitely. The 20 s ride-check ticker passes it as `gps:` to RideCheckDetector.tick. That method treats gps=true plus no new fix as 'the car stands still' and runs _longStop against the last fix's time. The admin default longStopMinutes is 2 (ride_check_admin_config.dart:10). Native streams use a 1 s interval with distanceFilter 0, so a parked car still gets fixes and 2 minutes of silence means lost GPS, not a stop. Elsewhere the screen treats a fix older than 30 s as unusable (_nearArrivalTarget, _approachDistanceMeters, _rideCheckFarDrop use isUsableAt). The tick and _safetyAlertTrip (line 1470) do not. During the silence nothing calls keepLastKnown either, so the island keeps showing the frozen 'Turn right in 120 m' and ETA with no location warning.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On a trip, the driver goes through a 4 km tunnel (about 3 minutes, no fixes). About 2 min 20 s in, the 'Long stop' Ride check opens. It covers and hides the navigation island (opacity 0 while covering) as the driver leaves the tunnel, and it uses up the one long-stop check for this trip. If the driver raises an alert, the position sent is the tunnel entrance from minutes earlier. Verified by reading the code; not run.

GeoPointMaps.fromLatLng(_driverPosition) : null` ; ride_check_detector.dart:81-82 `if (!gps) return _longer(at); return _longStop(at, place) ?? _longer(at);` ; 131-133 `final stopped = at.difference(since); if (stopped <= Duration(minutes: rules.longStopMinutes)) return null;` ; ride_check_admin_config.dart:10 `static const int defaultLongStopMinutes = 2;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass `gps: _lastLocation?.isUsableAt(now) == true` (fresh GPS) to tick. Send the alert position only when it is fresh, or with its timestamp. Start a staleness timer that calls keepLastKnown after 30 s without a fix.

The 20 s ticker (accept_ride.dart:697) calls _rideCheckTick (accept_ride_trip.dart:1525-1529) with `gps: _hasLiveLocation`. RideCheckDetector.tick (ride_check_detector.dart:72-83) then runs _longStop against _stillSince, which is the time of the last fix (ride_check_detector.dart:128-139). The default longStopMinutes is 2. The native navigation stream uses distanceFilter 0 with a 1 s interval (driver_location_service.dart:66-80), so a parked car keeps getting fixes and long silence means lost GPS. _safetyAlertTrip (accept_ride_trip.dart:1508) also sends the stale _driverPosition as the current position whenever _hasLiveLocation is true.

confirmed.title: Re-tapping Continue on Add vehicle after taking document photos silently deletes the saved photos
confirmed.description: `_save` always upserts the bare identity map `submitted` = {id, make, model, year, plate} (lines 76-85) using the fixed `_vehicleId`. `LocalVehicleStore._upsertSnapshot` replaces the whole row for that id (`rows.removeWhere((row) => row['id'] == vehicle['id']); rows.insert(..., Map.of(vehicle))`, local_vehicle_store.dart) and skips photo fields that are null (`if (value == null) continue;`). After the driver has taken a registration/insurance photo on VehicleDocuments (which upserts the row with `registrationPhoto`/`insurancePhoto`), pressing Back returns to the still-mounted AddVehicle whose `_ready` is still true; tapping Continue again writes the row without the photo keys and the photos are gone. The new VehicleDocuments then restores `_registrationDone = false` and shows 'Recommended next step' again with no message. Reproduced at store level with a throwaway test (upsert identity -> upsert with photo -> upsert identity -> list: `registrationPhoto` absent), test deleted afterwards.

confirmed.suggested_fix: In `_save`, merge onto the existing row (`{...previousRow, ...submitted}`) or have the store preserve photo fields when the incoming map omits them; alternatively navigate with pushReplacement / disable re-save once the draft exists.

verdicts.reason: AddVehicle._save always upserts only the identity fields {id, make, model, year, plate}, using the fixed _vehicleId (add_vehicle.dart:41-42, 76-85). confirmed.title: Home takes and plays island messages posted while a route covers Home (e.g. 'offline after N missed' during a trip), so the driver never sees them
confirmed.description: IslandMessages is documented as 'Messages waiting for the Home island. Any screen can post one'. Home's listener _onIslandMessagesChanged calls _showNextIslandMessage, which checks only mounted and whether a message is already showing, never whether Home is visible (_liveVisible / _routeVisible). didPushNext pauses GPS and offers but not the island queue. So a message posted while another route covers Home is taken from the queue, shown on the hidden island for 2 to 4.5 s, and dropped. Real posters during the journey: AcceptRide's offlineAfterMissed (accept_ride_trip.dart:1228, posted while the trip screen covers Home), demo arrival and document popups through _showNoticePopups (home_account.dart:237), and Scheduled rides' reservationAcceptedAt and reservationCancelled (scheduled_rides.dart:235, 678). The trip island (AdaptiveTripIsland) never reads IslandMessages.
confirmed.failure_scenario: During a trip the driver misses the Nth Exclusive offer. AcceptRide calls setOnline(false) and posts 'offline after N missed' (high priority). Home, under the trip route, consumes it at once and its 4.5 s timer ends it. After the trip the driver lands on Home, offline, with no explanation. In the same way, the 20 s 'High demand' and 50 s event popups and a 'Reservation accepted' confirmation play unseen under the trip or the Scheduled rides screen.
confirmed.evidence: home_map_sheet.dart:1257-1268 'void _showNextIslandMessage() { if (!mounted || _islandMessage != null) { return; } final next = IslandMessages.take(); ... _islandMessageTimer = Timer(next.priority.duration, _endIslandMessage);'; home.dart:174 'void didPushNext() { _routeVisible = false; _pauseHomeUpdates(); }' (_pauseHomeUpdates does not touch the island queue); island_messages.dart:57 '/// Messages waiting for the Home island. Any screen can post one'; accept_ride_trip.dart:1228 'IslandMessages.show(HomeIslandNotices.offlineAfterMissed(...))'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In _onIslandMessagesChanged and _showNextIslandMessage, return early while !_liveVisible, and call _showNextIslandMessage from _resumeHomeUpdates, so queued messages wait until Home is on screen.

confirmed.title: System Back on the 'Unresolved trip' dialog closes the saved trip and marks it terminal
confirmed.description: For a stale snapshot (older than 6 h) or one without verified endpoints, Home shows an AlertDialog with 'Close trip' and 'Resume trip'. barrierDismissible: false only blocks taps outside the dialog. The Android or browser Back button still pops the DialogRoute with a null result, because there is no PopScope in the builder. The code treats any result other than true as 'Close trip' (`if (resume != true)`). It then writes a terminal marker (driver cancel, or released to dispatch) and clears the saved ride. So Back, which the driver expects to dismiss the dialog, silently cancels a trip that could have been resumed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver's phone restarts during a long trip, and the saved ride is more than 6 h old or the app is reopened late. Home shows 'Unresolved trip' with Resume enabled. The driver presses Android Back (or browser Back on the PWA) to get rid of the dialog. The trip is marked cancelled by the driver or released to dispatch, and its recovery record is deleted, with no confirmation.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Wrap the AlertDialog in PopScope(canPop: false), or treat a null result as 'ask again' rather than 'close'.

verdicts.reason: home.dart:530-537 (now ~535-541 in the working tree) shows the 'Unresolved trip' AlertDialog with only barrierDismissible:false. No PopScope wraps the dialog builder. Home's own PopScope (home_back.dart:39-44) sits on Home's route, not on the DialogRoute, so system Back pops the dialog with a null result. The next line, `if (resume != true)`, treats null the same as 'Close trip'. It calls markTerminal(... cancelledByDriver / released) and then clearForTrip, so a trip the driver could have resumed (Resume is enabled when hasVerifiedEndpoints) is ended with no confirmation. The reachable case is a stale snapshot (isFresh false, older than 6 h) with verified endpoints, so this is an edge path. Nothing in DECISIONS.md makes Back mean 'close'.

confirmed.title: _hasRideOffers set from the Radar list on close is never cleared when those offers leave dispatch: the orb says 'Trip found', 'Finding trips' never shows and Exclusive offers are held back
confirmed.description: Closing the full Radar list sets `_hasRideOffers = hasOffers || _radarHomeOffers.isNotEmpty`, where hasOffers comes from the list's own dispatch offers. _hasRideOffers is reset only by _dismissRadarHomeOffer, _refreshRadarHomeOffers (which needs pending Home offers), _openOfferTrip, go online and go offline. Suppose the Home deck was emptied while the list was open, for example when a card was withdrawn or taken and removed after 2.8 s, and the list still had other trips. The flag then stays true after those trips expire. While it is true: _buildTripRadarButton shows 'Trip found / NEW / Tap for all' with zero trips (totalTrips = max(0, 0)); _waitingForTrips is false, so the island never says 'Finding trips'; and _showOutsideRadarOffer returns early for every non-reservation Exclusive offer (`!offer.reservation && (_pendingRadarHomeOffers.isNotEmpty || _hasRideOffers)`).

confirmed.title: Driving-limit auto-offline leaves the Radar list open, and Match there still claims and starts a trip
confirmed.description: `_drivingLimitReached` (not on a trip) calls `_goOffline()`. `_goOffline` cancels Home's own dispatch subscription and clears Home's offer lists, but never sets `showRideRequests = false`. While the full Radar page is open, Home's body is the `RideRequests` Stack (home.dart:717), so the SlidingUpPanel and its `_closeHomeFloatingPopupsForSheet` are not mounted, and `_closeDriverSheet()` cannot close the page. RideRequests has its own dispatch subscription and offer list. `_matchTrip`/`_claimTrip` never check the session's availability. On a won claim it pushes AcceptRide, whose post-frame `beginTrip` puts the offline, limit-blocked driver onto a trip with the driving clock running again.
confirmed.failure_scenario: At 11 h 59 m 50 s the driver opens the Radar list to compare trips. At 12 h 00 the limit fires: the island says 'Offline' and the session goes offline, but the Radar list stays on screen with live Match buttons. The driver taps Match and gets a new trip although they are supposed to be resting for 6 h.
confirmed.evidence: home.dart:939-971 `Future<void> _goOffline() async { ... setState(() { _driverSession.setOnline(false); _hasRideOffers = false; _outsideRadarOffer = null; _radarHomeOffers.clear(); ... }); ... await _HomeMapSheet(this)._closeDriverSheet(); }` (no `showRideRequests = false`); home.dart:717 `body: showRideRequests ? Stack(... RideRequests(...` ; ride_requests.dart:301-318 `_matchTrip` checks only visibility/state/_matchingOfferId; home_account.dart:137 `unawaited(_goOffline());`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Set `showRideRequests = false` in `_goOffline`. Also make RideRequests refuse to claim when `sessionController.availableForOffers` is false.

verdicts.reason: _drivingLimitReached (home_account.dart:137) calls _goOffline (home.dart:944-976). _goOffline cancels Home's own subscriptions and calls setOnline(false), but it never sets showRideRequests=false. Its only sheet action is _closeDriverSheet, which is just _springPanelTo(0) (home_map_sheet.dart:613-615). _onDriverSessionChanged (home.dart:664-676) resets showRideRequests only when consumeResumeHomeAfterTrip() is true. While showRideRequests is set, the body is the RideRequests Stack (home.dart:722-772). RideRequests has its own _dispatch and never reads sessionController.isOnline. _matchTrip (ride_requests.dart:311-329) checks only visibility, offer state and _matchingOfferId. Going offline does not touch the dispatch repository: the demo claimOffer (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:527-535) refuses only when disposed or after a generation bump, and only reset/dispose bump it. A won claim pushes AcceptRide (ride_requests.dart:366+), so the offline, rest-blocked driver gets a trip.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: home_account.dart:126-138 -> home.dart:944-976 (no showRideRequests write) -> home.dart:722 body stays RideRequests -> ride_requests.dart:311-420 claim with no availability check -> demo_dispatch_repository.dart:527-545 claim succeeds. Checked every showRideRequests writer (home.dart:671,767,984; home_back.dart:61; home_map_sheet.dart:1417); none runs on this path. No test run.

The only code that clears it is _closeHomeFloatingPopupsForSheet (home_map_sheet.dart:1409), which lives on the panel that is not mounted while the body is the RideRequests Stack (home.dart:722), and the post-trip resume (home.dart:669). `_closeDriverSheet` only springs the panel (home_map_sheet.dart:613). confirmed.title: With GPS unavailable, Destination mode measures distance and time from the hard-coded city-centre placeholder
confirmed.description: Home's `_driverPosition` starts at `_fallbackDriverPosition` (home.dart:394-395, Stockholm centre). It is replaced only by a saved or live position. When location is denied or GPS fails, `_startLocationFailed` opens the map 'without a car', but `_openDestinationModePicker` still passes `origin: _driverPosition` to the picker. The picker supports `origin == null` (destination_picker.dart:146-149, skipping the confirm step), but Home never passes null. DestinationConfirmScreen then puts the car at the placeholder, draws the arc from there, and computes `_meters`/`_seconds` from the straight-line distance or a road route from that point (destination_confirm.dart:80-83 and 127-131). It returns those figures. With no live GPS, `_fetchLatestDestinationRoadRoute` returns early (home_map_sheet.dart:356), so `_destinationFigures` falls back to the confirmed figures. The Home bar and details sheet keep showing the wrong 'NN min · NN km'. `_fitDestinationRoute` also frames `[_driverPosition, destination]`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A driver outside Stockholm with location blocked (and no saved start position) turns on Destination mode to 'Home, 3 km away'. The confirm screen shows the car in central Stockholm and '412.0 km · 290 min'. After confirming, Home's destination bar keeps showing '290 min · 412 km' for the whole session.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass `origin: _startPositionKnown || _hasLiveDriverLocation ? _driverPosition : null`, or refuse Destination mode until a real position is known, so the picker's no-origin path is used and no figures are invented.

The destination button (home_map_sheet.dart:1177) is not gated on a known position, and _openDestinationModePicker passes origin: _driverPosition (line 291), never null. The picker's no-origin path (destination_picker.dart:146-149) is therefore skipped. DestinationConfirmScreen then computes _meters/_seconds from the placeholder (destination_confirm.dart:80-83, plus the road route at 127-131). Back on Home, _fetchLatestDestinationRoadRoute returns early with no live GPS (home_map_sheet.dart:356), so _destinationFigures (414-416) keeps showing the invented confirm figures. _fitDestinationRoute (line 395) and _seedDemoDestinationTrips also use the placeholder.

confirmed.title: Home's time-limit timer for the old destination ends a destination the driver set later during a trip
confirmed.description: Home arms _destinationLimitTimer for its own destination, and the timer stays armed while AcceptRide covers Home. On the trip, the driver can set a new destination (accept_ride_panel.dart:184), which calls DestinationModeSession.started() and restarts the shared session's clock. When Home's old timer fires, Home is still mounted and _destinationModeActive is still true, so it calls _endDestinationMode() (which calls session.ended()) and then session.timedOut(). That ends the new on-trip destination long before its own limit. From then on OnTripDestination.follows returns true for every offer.
confirmed.failure_scenario: At 10:00 the driver sets Kista on Home, so the 2 h timer is due at 12:00. They accept a trip at 11:40 and, at 11:50 on the trip, set Södertälje from the trip menu (a daily use; it should last until 13:50). At 12:00 Home's timer fires: the session is marked timed out, the island announces that the destination ended, and next-trip offers are no longer filtered toward Södertälje, 1 h 50 min early. Worked out from the code.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep one timer, owned by the session and re-armed by started(), or have Home's callback check that the session's _activeSince is still the one it armed for before ending it.

verdicts.reason: Home pushes AcceptRide on top of itself with pushSingle (home_offer_radar.dart:948), so Home stays mounted, and _pauseHomeUpdates (home.dart:195-202) does not cancel _destinationLimitTimer. The timer callback (home_map_sheet.dart:313-318) checks only mounted and _destinationModeActive, both still true. On the trip, _openDestinationPicker calls OnTripDestination.started() (accept_ride_panel.dart:184), which restarts the shared DestinationModeSession clock (destination_mode_session.dart:43-50). When Home's old timer fires, it calls _endDestinationMode, which calls session.ended(), and then timedOut(), which sets _timedOut = true. From then on OnTripDestination.follows returns true (next_trip_gate.dart:54), so the newly set on-trip destination stops filtering offers before its own limit. It also shows HomeIslandNotices.destinationEnded.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: home_map_sheet.dart:303-319, home_offer_radar.dart:938-990, home.dart:195-202, accept_ride_panel.dart:165-190, accept_ride_trip.dart:1047-1058, next_trip_gate.dart:47-73, destination_mode_session.dart:43-73. No test run.

verdicts.reason: Home arms a one-shot Timer(left) whose length is fixed at arm time (home_map_sheet.dart:311-318). It is cancelled only by _endDestinationMode (476), going offline (home.dart:973) or dispose. AcceptRide is pushed over a still-mounted Home (home_offer_radar.dart:957 pushSingle), and Home keeps _destinationModeActive=true (it passes it in at 992). On the trip, the Destination row is shown even when a destination is already active (accept_ride_panel.dart:1076-1085). _openDestinationPicker then calls OnTripDestination.started() (184), which resets the shared session's _activeSince (destination_mode_session.dart:41-48). When Home's old timer fires, its guard (`!mounted || !_destinationModeActive`) passes. It calls _endDestinationMode() -> session.ended() and then session.timedOut() (_timedOut=true). OnTripDestination.follows then returns true for every offer (next_trip_gate.dart:54), which ends the trip's new destination filter early.
verdicts.repro: Hand computation: 10:00 started(), timeLeft=2h, Timer(2h) due at 12:00. At 11:50 on the trip, started() sets _activeSince=11:50, so the real limit is 13:50. At 12:00 Home's Timer fires (Timers do not pause under a pushed route), and timedOut() sets _timedOut, so expired() is true and follows() returns true, 1 h 50 min early. No test run.

confirmed.title: While online and waiting, the Home menu and destination search are hidden from screen readers with no other way to reach them
confirmed.description: When the driver is online with no offer (_waitingForTrips), the island shows the waiting face and `waiting` is true. That sets `tucked`, which wraps both side buttons (Menu, the only openDrawer call on Home, and Search destination) in IgnorePointer plus AnimatedOpacity(opacity: 0). An opacity-0 subtree is dropped from the semantics tree. Sighted drivers get the buttons back because the island Listener calls _islandWaiting.touch() on onPointerDown. A screen-reader double-tap sends SemanticsAction.tap, not a pointer event. The middle InkWell's tap goes to _onIslandEarningsTap, which only cycles the hidden money face, so the waiting state never ends. The Home dock and sheet have no menu or destination entry, and the drawer edge swipe has no semantics action. This is the steady online state, so it lasts as long as no offer arrives.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A TalkBack/VoiceOver driver goes online. The island now reads 'Finding trips', and Menu (Settings, Ride history, Documents, Log out, Safety) and Search destination are no longer in the accessibility tree. Double-tapping the island never brings them back. The driver must go offline to open the menu or start destination mode.
confirmed.evidence:
home_map_sheet.dart:1020-1036
  final tucked = _islandMessage != null || reservation != null ||
      exclusive != null || waiting;
  Widget side(Widget button, {bool tuck = false}) => AnimatedContainer(
      width: tucked || tuck ? 14 : 54,
      ... IgnorePointer(ignoring: tucked || tuck,
        child: AnimatedOpacity(opacity: tucked || tuck ? 0 : 1, child: button)
home_map_sheet.dart:1044 onPointerDown: (_) => _islandWaiting.touch(),
home_map_sheet.dart:1297-1299 _onIslandEarningsTap(){ if (_islandWaiting.takeSwallowedTap()) return; ... cycles _islandFace }
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep the side buttons in the semantics tree while tucked (for example AnimatedOpacity alwaysIncludeSemantics plus a semantics-only tap path), or call _islandWaiting.touch() from the island's semantic tap too. Another option is a Semantics customSemanticsActions entry for Menu and Search on the island.

verdicts.reason: home_map_sheet.dart:1020-1036 sets `tucked` whenever `waiting` is true and wraps both side buttons in IgnorePointer plus AnimatedOpacity(opacity: 0) without alwaysIncludeSemantics. The opacity render object leaves the child out of semantics at alpha 0, so Menu and Search destination drop out of the semantics tree. The only thing that untucks them is `_islandWaiting.touch()`, which runs from Listener.onPointerDown at :1044, and a semantics tap does not send a pointer event. The island InkWell's semantic tap goes to `_onIslandEarningsTap` (:1297). That handler only cycles `_islandFace` (`takeSwallowedTap` is false because touch() never ran), so the waiting face stays up. `IslandWaitingController.sync` (island_waiting.dart) keeps `showing` true for as long as `_waitingForTrips` (:1194) holds. A grep finds no other `openDrawer` call on Home (only :1071) and no other caller of `_openDestinationModePicker` (only :1177). The only way out is to go offline with the island long-press (:1110).
verdicts.repro: Static trace: home_map_sheet.dart:979-983 (waiting), :1020-1036 (side/tucked), :1044 (Listener touch), :1095-1106 (InkWell onTap routing), :1297-1311 (_onIslandEarningsTap), and island_waiting.dart sync/touch/takeSwallowedTap. Grepped openDrawer and _openDestinationModePicker across lib/. No test was run.

That wraps Menu and Search in IgnorePointer and AnimatedOpacity(opacity 0) without alwaysIncludeSemantics (1022-1036), so both drop out of the semantics tree. The only thing that brings them back is `_islandWaiting.touch()`, and that is called only from the Listener's onPointerDown (1044). A semantics tap on the island InkWell (1096-1106) goes to `_onIslandEarningsTap`. `takeSwallowedTap()` is false there, so the tap only cycles `_islandFace`. `IslandWaitingController.showing` (island_waiting.dart) stays true. `openDrawer` is called only at 1071 and `_openDestinationModePicker` only at 1177, so nothing else on Home opens them. confirmed.title: The island's TODAY earnings face always shows the hard-coded '183.25 kr', whatever the driver earned today
confirmed.description: Tapping the Home island cycles through hidden -> LAST TRIP -> TODAY -> history. The TODAY face always renders `DigitalIslandParts.sampleToday` ('183.25 kr'), and so does the trip screen's TripIsland. It has no demo label, although the app records every completed fare locally (PrefsTripHistoryRepository) and History computes a real 'Today' total from them. The constant is only marked as sample in a code comment. LAST TRIP likewise falls back to the sample '126 kr' before any trip has been driven. The figure also uses a '.' decimal, unlike Money's '183,25 kr'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: After 25 trips worth about 3 100 kr, the driver taps the island and sees 'TODAY 183.25 kr'. Opening Ride history -> Today shows the real recorded total. On the first launch of a shift, 'LAST TRIP 126 kr' is shown before any trip.

confirmed.suggested_fix: Compute today's total from the local history, as Ride history does, or label the face as sample/unavailable. Show '—' for the last trip when there is none.
