confirmed.title: Driving-limit and other island notices posted while a trip screen covers Home are taken by Home's hidden island and expire unseen
confirmed.description: The 30 and 10 minute warnings and the limit notice are Dart timers in Home (`_syncDrivingLimit` -> `_drivingWarning` / `_drivingLimitReached`). They post through `IslandMessages.show`. Home is the only consumer of that queue (grep: only home_map_sheet.dart:1247/1259 call peek/take). `_onIslandMessagesChanged`/`_showNextIslandMessage` check only `mounted`, not `_routeVisible`, and `_pauseHomeUpdates` does not stop them. While AcceptRide is pushed over Home (as it is for most of a shift with 25 trips), Home stays mounted underneath. It takes the message off the queue at once and plays it for 3 to 4.5 s on its own hidden island. The trip screen's AdaptiveTripIsland never reads IslandMessages. When the driver returns to Home the message is gone. `_drivingWarning` also adds the minutes to `warned`, so the warning is never shown again. The same applies to the 'Rest until' notice from `_drivingLimitReached` and to `offlineAfterMissed` posted by `_denyNextTripRadar` during a trip.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver is 11 h 25 min into the shift and driving a rider. At 11 h 30 and 11 h 50 the 30-minute and 10-minute warnings fire, each consumed by the Home island under the trip screen. At 12 h 'Rest until 04:30' is consumed the same way. The driver finishes the trip, lands on Home already offline and blocked, and was never warned.
confirmed.evidence: home_account.dart:120-123 `void _drivingWarning(int minutes) { if (!mounted || !_account.warned.add(minutes)) { return; } IslandMessages.show(HomeIslandNotices.drivingLeft(minutes)); }`; home_map_sheet.dart:1244-1268 `void _onIslandMessagesChanged() { if (!mounted) { return; } ... _showNextIslandMessage(); } void _showNextIslandMessage() { if (!mounted || _islandMessage != null) { return; } final next = IslandMessages.take(); ...`; home.dart:173 `void didPushNext() { _routeVisible = false; _pauseHomeUpdates(); }` (the pause does not touch the island message queue).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Do not take messages from the queue while Home is covered (`!_liveVisible`); drain the queue on didPopNext/resume. Alternatively, let the trip screen's island show driving-limit warnings while a trip is open.

verdicts.corrected_title: Driving-limit and other island notices posted while a trip screen covers Home are taken by Home's hidden island and expire unseen
verdicts.reason: Home subscribes to `IslandMessages.changes` at home.dart:491, and that subscription is removed only in dispose (:1144). `didPushNext` (:174) calls `_pauseHomeUpdates` (:192-203), which cancels location, radar and offer timers but not the island-message listener or the driving timers. `_onIslandMessagesChanged`/`_showNextIslandMessage` (home_map_sheet.dart:1244-1268) check only `mounted`, then `IslandMessages.take()` removes the message and a 3-4.5 s timer expires it. The trip screen is pushed over Home with `pushSingle(... AcceptRide)` (home_offer_radar.dart:948-951), so Home stays mounted underneath. The trip-screen island never reads IslandMessages: accept ride/ only calls `show`. `_syncDrivingLimit` timers (home_account.dart:89-117) fire during the trip. `_drivingWarning` (:120-123) also adds the minutes to `warned`, so the warning never comes back. `_drivingLimitReached` (:127-137) posts 'Rest until' and goes offline. I rate it medium, not high: only shifts that reach the configured limit while on a trip are affected.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: home.dart:160-215 (RouteAware pause/resume), :258-259 and :491 (listener), home_map_sheet.dart:1244-1275, home_account.dart:89-137, home_offer_radar.dart:948-951 (push over Home). Grepped IslandMessages under lib/presentation/driver/accept ride: show calls only (accept_ride_trip.dart:433/482/1256). No test was run.

verdicts.reason: Messages are lost because Home stays mounted under the trip screen. `_drivingWarning` and `_drivingLimitReached` (home_account.dart:120-137) post through `IslandMessages.show`. `IslandMessages` (components/island_messages.dart:60-110) is a global queue. Its only consumer is Home (`_onIslandMessagesChanged` / `_showNextIslandMessage`, home_map_sheet.dart:1244-1268), which checks only `mounted`, never `_liveVisible` (home.dart:165). `didPushNext` sets `_routeVisible = false` and calls `_pauseHomeUpdates` (home.dart:174, 192-203), which cancels location, radar and offer timers but neither the driving timers nor the island-message listener (home.dart:491). The trip is opened with pushSingle(... AcceptRide) over Home (home_offer_radar.dart:956-959), so Home stays mounted. It takes each message at once and shows it on its covered island for the priority duration. `_endIslandMessage` then takes the next one. Nothing in 'accept ride/' reads IslandMessages or DrivingTimeClock; it only posts to them (accept_ride_trip.dart:433, 482, 1256). `warned.add(minutes)` stops the warning from being posted again. `offlineAfterMissed`, posted during a trip, is consumed the same way.
verdicts.repro: Hand trace of the listener chain: IslandMessages.show -> _changes.value++ -> Home._islandMessagesListener (home.dart:259) -> _showNextIslandMessage -> IslandMessages.take() removes the message, with no visibility guard. Grep shows peek/take are called only at home_map_sheet.dart:1247/1259. No runnable test: that would need driving a full trip across the driving-limit timer.

confirmed.title: A Match claim that succeeds after the driver went offline is silently discarded although dispatch assigned the trip
confirmed.description: While a Radar claim is in flight the radar orb is still wrapped in _radarLongPressOff (home_map_sheet.dart:1689, 1716-1723) and the island long press also offers "Go offline?" (1110-1116). _goOffline() calls _HomeOfferRadar._cancelAllOfferTimers() without preserveClaim (home.dart:949), which sets _homeRadarMatchingOfferId = null (home_offer_radar.dart:796-800). When _dispatch.claimOffer later resolves with ClaimOutcome.success, _claimHomeRadarOffer returns at line 546 because `_homeRadarMatchingOfferId != offer.id`; nothing tells dispatch and nothing is shown. In the demo repository the offer was already removed from the feed by the claim (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:565-566), i.e. it is taken by this driver. The driver is offline, the rider is matched to a driver who is not coming.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver taps Match, then long-presses the radar and confirms "Go offline" before dispatch answers (slow network). Dispatch answers success → the trip is assigned to this driver server-side; the app shows nothing, stays offline, never opens the trip and never declines/cancels it.
confirmed.evidence: home_offer_radar.dart:542-546 `result = await _dispatch.claimOffer(offer.id); ... if (!mounted || _homeRadarMatchingOfferId != offer.id) { return; }` | home.dart:949 `_HomeOfferRadar(this)._cancelAllOfferTimers();` | home_offer_radar.dart:796-800 `if (!preserveClaim) { _homeRadarMatchingOfferId = null; _claimedHomeOffer = null; _homeRadarMatchStates.clear(); }` | home_map_sheet.dart:1689-1691 `_radarLongPressOff(front != null ? _acceptRadar(front) : _buildTripRadarButton())`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Either block going offline while a claim is in flight (disable the long press / show "please wait"), or keep the claim across _goOffline and, on a late success, open the trip or send dispatch a decline/cancel for that offer.

verdicts.reason: Nothing blocks going offline while a claim is in flight. _radarLongPressOff (home_map_sheet.dart:1716-1723) and the island long press (1110-1116) both call _confirmGoOffline, which does not check _homeRadarMatchingOfferId. The confirm dialog is a ModalRoute, so it pauses Home with preserveClaim:true and the claim survives. If the claim wins while the dialog is open, _resolveHomeRadarMatchWon sets _claimedHomeOffer, but _openClaimedHomeOffer returns because !_liveVisible (home_offer_radar.dart:659). Tapping Go offline pops the dialog and then calls _goOffline, whose _cancelAllOfferTimers() without preserveClaim (home.dart:949) cancels _homeRadarNoticeTimer and nulls _claimedHomeOffer and _homeRadarMatchingOfferId (home_offer_radar.dart:792, 796-800). If instead the claim resolves after going offline, the guard at 546 discards it. Either way the trip dispatch gave this driver is dropped. The demo repository has already removed it from the feed (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:565-566), nothing tells dispatch, and no AcceptRide opens. Because the dialog stays open as long as the driver reads it, the window is larger than the 1.45 s claim delay suggests.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test test/_audit_c2b1x_test.dart (now deleted). It is based on test/audit/home_claim_ownership_test.dart: mount with 'first' and 'second' on the deck, tap Match on 'first', long-press home-radar-long-press (the dialog showed), complete the claim with ClaimResult.success, tap go-offline-yes, pump about 7 s. Output: `d69 dialog: 1` / `d69 AcceptRide: 0 OFF visible: 1` / `All tests passed!`.

verdicts.reason: While a claim is in flight the radar is still wrapped in _radarLongPressOff (home_map_sheet.dart:1689-1691, 1716-1723), so the driver can still go offline. _goOffline calls _cancelAllOfferTimers() without preserveClaim (home.dart:949), which sets _homeRadarMatchingOfferId to null (home_offer_radar.dart:796-800). When the claim later succeeds, _claimHomeRadarOffer returns at the guard on home_offer_radar.dart:546 (`_homeRadarMatchingOfferId != offer.id`). Nothing calls declineOffer, nothing opens the trip and nothing is shown. In the demo, claimOffer already removed the offer from the feed (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:565-566), so dispatch counts the trip as taken by this driver.
verdicts.repro: I wrote a throwaway widget test using the harness from test/audit/home_claim_ownership_test.dart (a _Dispatch whose claims are completers). Steps: mount with 'first' and 'second' on the deck, tap radar-match-first, long-press home-radar-long-press, tap go-offline-yes, then complete the claim with ClaimResult.success. Output: `D69 dialog yes: 1`, `D69 OFF visible: 1`, `D69 AcceptRide: 0 claims=1`. All tests passed. The test file was deleted afterwards.

confirmed.title: Two Radar offers lost within 2.8 s share one _homeRadarLostMatchTimer: only the last is dismissed, and the other stays in _radarHomeOffers (hidden by the deck), which keeps the deck slot and "trips found" up and holds back every Exclusive offer
confirmed.description: _watchDispatchRadar's listener loops over every listed/pending offer missing from the new snapshot and calls _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost for each (604-611). _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost marks the offer claimedElsewhere and arms the single field _homeRadarLostMatchTimer after `_homeRadarLostMatchTimer?.cancel()` (691-702). The second call cancels the first offer's dismissal, so that offer keeps state claimedElsewhere, stays in _radarHomeOffers (shown blurred/"Taken"), keeps _hasRideOffers true (radar "trips found", island green ring) and is only removed by a manual ×, a pause/resume (_resumeOfferTimers) or going offline. _refreshRadarHomeOffers never drops claimedElsewhere offers. Concrete demo path: two destination-mode trips on the deck (home_map_sheet.dart:463-465), then "Turn off destination" → _clearDemoDestinationTrips → DemoDispatchRepository.clearDestinationTrips emits a snapshot without both (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:614-624) → both resolved lost in one loop. With a real feed any update that drops two listed offers at once does the same.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver has two deck cards from destination mode and turns destination mode off. Both cards are marked taken; after 2.8 s only the second disappears, the first stays as a greyed "Taken by another driver" card and the radar keeps saying trips are found until the driver taps × or goes offline.
confirmed.evidence: home_offer_radar.dart:604-611 `for (final offer in [..._radarHomeOffers, ..._pendingRadarHomeOffers]) { if (!ids.contains(offer.id) && _homeRadarStateFor(offer.id) == _HomeRadarMatchState.available) { _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost(offer, _RadarOfferGone.unavailable); } }` | home_offer_radar.dart:691-702 `_homeRadarLostMatchTimer?.cancel(); _homeRadarLostMatchTimer = Timer(const Duration(milliseconds: 2800), () { ... _dismissRadarHomeOffer(offer); });`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep one dismissal timer per offer id (a Map<String, Timer> like _radarOfferTimeoutTimers), or have the timer dismiss every offer currently in claimedElsewhere state.

verdicts.corrected_title: Two Radar offers lost within 2.8 s share one _homeRadarLostMatchTimer: only the last is dismissed, and the other stays in _radarHomeOffers (hidden by the deck), which keeps the deck slot and "trips found" up and holds back every Exclusive offer
verdicts.reason: _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost cancels and replaces the single field _homeRadarLostMatchTimer (home_offer_radar.dart:691-702), and the closure only dismisses the latest offer. When the snapshot loop (604-611) resolves two offers, or two withdrawals arrive within 2.8 s (_onOfferWithdrawn, 917-923), the first offer stays in state claimedElsewhere. Nothing else removes it on Home: _refreshRadarHomeOffers keeps it (386-399), the external-claim cleanup handles only its own offer, and only pause/resume (_resumeOfferTimers 765-784), × or going offline clear it. The finding's description of the result is wrong. RadarOfferDeck hides taken cards (radar_offer_deck.dart:126-139), so no "Taken" card stays visible. The real effect is that _radarHomeOffers stays non-empty: the deck slot stays up (home_map_sheet.dart:873-876), _hasRideOffers stays true, and _showOutsideRadarOffer refuses every Exclusive offer while `_radarHomeOffers.isNotEmpty` (home_offer_radar.dart:235). The demo path is real: destination-mode trips on the deck, then Turn off in the details sheet. That sheet pops first and then calls onTurnOff (destination_island.dart:187-188), so the live subscription receives a snapshot without both trips.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test (now deleted). With 'first' and 'second' on the deck, one update with [] then 33 s of pumps gave `d70 first: 0 second: 0`, `d70 deck slot: 1`: no card widgets, but the deck slot and the _radarHomeOffers entry remain. Control: drop 'second' first, wait 3 s, then drop 'first'. It gave `d70ctl deck slot: 0`. `All tests passed!`

verdicts.corrected_title: When two Radar offers leave in one dispatch update, they share one _homeRadarLostMatchTimer, so the first stays in _radarHomeOffers (hidden on the deck). It keeps _hasRideOffers true and blocks Exclusive offers until resume or going offline.
verdicts.reason: The listener at home_offer_radar.dart:604-611 calls _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost once for each missing offer. Each call cancels the single _homeRadarLostMatchTimer before re-arming it (691-702), so only the last offer is dismissed. The first offer keeps the claimedElsewhere state in _radarHomeOffers. The finding says the card stays visible as a 'Taken' card. That part is wrong: RadarOfferDeck._sync moves taken ids into _gone (radar_offer_deck.dart:126-139), so the card is hidden. The stuck entry still matters: _showOutsideRadarOffer refuses while `_radarHomeOffers.isNotEmpty` (home_offer_radar.dart:235), and _hasRideOffers is only recomputed in _dismissRadarHomeOffer.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test with the same harness. Mount with first and second, push an empty list on dispatch.updates, pump 3 s and then 30 s more. Output: `D70 after 3s: first=0 second=0` (no card widgets visible), but `D70 deck ids=[first] taken={first}` after 33 s. So 'second' was dismissed and 'first' stayed in _radarHomeOffers as claimedElsewhere. All tests passed. The file was deleted afterwards.

confirmed.title: A waiting Radar offer that left dispatch is stuck as a 'Taken' card when Home is paused during its 2.8 s removal
confirmed.description: The dispatch watcher (line 604-610) also resolves pending offers that left dispatch: they become claimedElsewhere, and the shared _homeRadarLostMatchTimer is meant to remove them 2.8 s later. A pause in that window (another route pushed, a dialog, app inactive) runs _cancelAllOfferTimers(preserveClaim: true), which cancels that timer but keeps the claimedElsewhere state. On resume, _resumeOfferTimers re-schedules removal only for claimedElsewhere offers in _radarHomeOffers, never for those in _pendingRadarHomeOffers. The pending offer stays forever. It counts in the radar button's homeTrips (home.dart:1053), and once the blocker clears, _refreshRadarHomeOffers moves it onto the deck as a 'Taken' card that no timer ever removes. The pick-window timer ignores non-available cards, and the external-claim demo picks only available ones.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A Ride check is open and a Radar trip waits as pending. Dispatch drops it from the feed. Within 2.8 s the driver opens another screen (any route push) and comes back. The Ride check is then answered. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test (with driverRouteObserver installed): after resume the radar still reads '1 trip / NEW'; 25 s later the deck holds ids=[audit-card] taken={audit-card} and the radar reads 'Trip found / Tap for all', though dispatch has had no offers for over 30 s.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In _resumeOfferTimers, include claimedElsewhere offers from _pendingRadarHomeOffers, or remove pending offers that left dispatch right away instead of giving them a Taken state and a timer.

verdicts.reason: The dispatch watcher (home_offer_radar.dart:604-610) marks a pending offer claimedElsewhere when it leaves the nearby feed without a withdrawal event, then arms a 2.8 s timer in _homeRadarLostMatchTimers (:691-703). Feed drops without a withdrawal do happen: ApiDispatchRepository._load replaces the whole list (api_dispatch_repository.dart:232-238), and the demo repo has _removeOffer at :540-575 and :707. A pause in that window (home.dart:174/190 -> _pauseHomeUpdates -> _cancelAllOfferTimers(preserveClaim: true)) cancels and clears the lost-match timers (:799-802) but keeps the claimedElsewhere state. _resumeOfferTimers (:762-787) re-schedules removal only for offers in _radarHomeOffers. The new watcher subscription skips the offer because it only resolves `available` offers. _refreshRadarHomeOffers (:391-415) later moves it onto the deck in the Taken state with no timer. Nothing removes it until another pause/resume or a manual close. While it waits, it also counts in homeTrips (home.dart:1053).
verdicts.repro: Traced the watcher, _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost, pause/resume (home.dart:192-213) and _resumeOfferTimers. Checked which repo paths drop an offer without emitting a withdrawal. When there is a withdrawal, _onOfferWithdrawn removes the pending offer first, so this needs a silent drop such as a list reload. I did not run a test.

verdicts.reason: The dispatch watcher (home_offer_radar.dart:604-610) marks a pending offer claimedElsewhere and arms a 2.8 s lost timer (_resolveHomeRadarMatchLost, 695-707). A pause runs _cancelAllOfferTimers(preserveClaim: true) (home.dart:198 and home_offer_radar.dart:1182). That clears _homeRadarLostMatchTimers (800-803) but keeps _homeRadarMatchStates (804-808). On resume, _resumeOfferTimers (762-789) only looks at _radarHomeOffers, so the pending claimedElsewhere offer gets no removal timer. When the blocker clears, _releasePendingRadarOffers calls _refreshRadarHomeOffers (390-418), which moves it onto the deck. After that nothing removes it automatically: the pick-window callback, the external-claim demo, the watcher and the withdrawal handler all act only on `available` offers. Only the driver's × removes it. This path needs the offer to leave the feed without a withdrawal arriving first. The API repo's _load() replace does that (api_dispatch_repository.dart:228-238), and so do the demo's _removeOffer paths. If a withdrawal arrives first, the pending offer is simply removed (916).
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand from the pause/resume code (home.dart:192-213, home_offer_radar.dart:762-818, 1180-1182) and the refresh path (390-418). No run: getting a pending offer, a feed drop and a route pause into the same 2.8 s window needed more harness than the time allowed. Each step in the chain is unconditional code with no guard.

confirmed.title: An admin direct-assign claim won after the driver goes offline mid-claim is silently discarded
confirmed.description: _claimAdminAssign awaits dispatch.claimOffer and then returns early when `_outsideRadarOffer?.id != offer.id`. _goOffline (home.dart:957) sets `_outsideRadarOffer = null`. The Exclusive sheet turns its down arrow and the Back button off while a claim runs, but the top-island long-press does not. home_map_sheet.dart:1110 checks only `reservation != null || exclusive != null`, and `exclusive` is non-null only when no island message is showing (line 969). _claimAdminAssign itself posts the 'Matching…' message (line 847), so while the claim runs the island long-press opens 'Go offline?'. When the driver confirms, the claim then resolves `success`, the early return fires, and no trip opens, no message shows and nothing is declined. Dispatch has already given the trip to this driver. The known finding at home_offer_radar.dart:546 covers the same pattern only for the Radar-card Match path, not for this Exclusive admin-assign path.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An admin direct assign is up. The driver taps the orb (Accept) and the island shows 'Matching…'. The driver long-presses the island and confirms Go offline. Dispatch answers success. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test (completer-controlled claim): island onLongPress enabled during claim: true; AcceptRide after the won claim: 0; island messages: [Radar online, Exclusive ride, Matching…, Radar offline]. The rider's trip is assigned to a driver who never sees it.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Turn the island (and any other) Go-offline entry off while `_HomeExclusive._exclusiveClaiming` is true, or have _goOffline wait for or decline the claim in flight. Alternatively, on success with the offer no longer on screen, show the trip or send dispatch a decline or release instead of returning silently.

verdicts.reason: _claimAdminAssign posts HomeIslandNotices.matching (home_offer_radar.dart:847). While that message shows, `exclusive` is null (home_map_sheet.dart:969-972), so the island long-press is enabled (:1110-1116). _confirmGoOffline (:1706-1718) only guards _homeRadarMatchingOfferId and _claimedHomeOffer. It does not check _HomeExclusive._exclusiveClaiming (home_exclusive.dart:58-61). After the driver confirms, _goOffline sets _outsideRadarOffer = null (home.dart:957). When the claim then succeeds, the early return at home_offer_radar.dart:856 drops it: no trip opens, nothing is declined and nothing is persisted. _restoreActiveRideIfNeeded (home.dart:505-532) only reads the local snapshot, so the trip dispatch assigned to this driver is never shown.
verdicts.repro: Traced the island gesture gating, _confirmGoOffline, _goOffline and _claimAdminAssign. No guard stops going offline while _exclusive.claimingId is set. Static trace only; the finding's widget-test numbers agree with the trace.

verdicts.reason: _claimAdminAssign posts HomeIslandNotices.matching (home_offer_radar.dart:847). That is an IslandPriority.low message, 2 s (island_messages.dart:10). While it shows, `message != null`, so `exclusive` is null (home_map_sheet.dart:969-971) and the island's onLongPress opens _confirmGoOffline (1110-1116). The guard in _confirmGoOffline (home_map_sheet.dart:1711-1714) checks only _homeRadarMatchingOfferId and _claimedHomeOffer, never _exclusive.claimingId. If the driver confirms before the claim resolves, _goOffline sets _outsideRadarOffer = null (home.dart:957-963). The `success` result then hits the early return at home_offer_radar.dart:856: no trip opens and no decline is sent, though dispatch has already given the trip to this driver.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand through the island build (home_map_sheet.dart:960-1120), _confirmGoOffline (1706-1717), _goOffline (home.dart:945-976) and _claimAdminAssign (843-870). No run. The race needs the claim to last longer than the long press plus the confirm tap, which is realistic on the API path with its retry of a stale version (api_dispatch_repository.dart:340+).

confirmed.title: A withdrawn waiting (pending) Radar offer leaves _hasRideOffers true: Home shows 'Trip found / NEW' with no trips and blocks later Exclusive offers
confirmed.description: _showRadarHomeOffer sets `_hasRideOffers = true` when it parks an offer in _pendingRadarHomeOffers, which happens while an Exclusive offer, a Ride check or a reservation request is up. _onOfferWithdrawn removes that pending offer but never recomputes `_hasRideOffers`. The same happens with _setAcceptsCash(false) (home_offer_rules.dart:53) and _onCategoriesChanged (line 32). When the blocker goes away, _releasePendingRadarOffers returns on an empty pending list (line 459), so nothing resets the flag. Everything that reads the flag is then wrong: the radar button shows the 'Trip found / NEW / Tap for all' face (home.dart:1055-1071), the island gets the green offers ring (home_map_sheet.dart:1061), 'Finding trips' never shows (_waitingForTrips at line 1197), non-reservation Exclusive offers are refused (line 239), and the later Exclusive demo (line 1228) never shows.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A Ride check is open (or an Exclusive offer is up) when a Radar trip arrives and waits as pending. Dispatch withdraws it (for example, a radar-group trip another driver took). The Ride check is answered. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test: with dispatch offers at 0, the radar orb reads title='Trip found' status=NEW subtitle='Tap for all' offer=true, and 'Finding trips' is not shown. The driver is told a trip was found when none exists, and no further Exclusive offer can appear until they tap the radar.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Wherever pending offers are removed (here, in _setAcceptsCash and in _onCategoriesChanged), recompute `_hasRideOffers = _radarHomeOffers.isNotEmpty || _pendingRadarHomeOffers.isNotEmpty`, as _dismissRadarHomeOffer already does.

verdicts.reason: _showRadarHomeOffer sets _hasRideOffers = true when it parks an offer as pending (home_offer_radar.dart:338-343). The pending offers come from dispatch, while an Exclusive offer, a reservation or a Ride check is up. _onOfferWithdrawn (:916) removes the pending offer without recomputing _hasRideOffers. Both repos emit the withdrawal before the list update (api_dispatch_repository.dart:316-323, demo :591-594), so the pending entry is already gone when the watcher runs. The watcher (:604-610) therefore never arms the lost-match timer whose _dismissRadarHomeOffer would recompute the flag. When the blocker clears, _releasePendingRadarOffers returns on an empty pending list (:459), and _refreshRadarHomeOffers also returns on an empty pending list (:396). The flag stays true until the driver taps the radar (_openRideOffers, home.dart:985) or goes offline. While it is true, the radar orb shows tripFound (home.dart:1061-1071), 'Finding trips' is suppressed (home_map_sheet.dart:1197), and non-reservation Exclusive offers are refused (home_offer_radar.dart:238-239, :1233-1238).
verdicts.repro: Traced the order in which the repos emit withdrawal and nearby events, every writer of _hasRideOffers (found by grep), and the gates that read it. Static trace only.

verdicts.reason: _showRadarHomeOffer sets _hasRideOffers = true when it parks an offer as pending (home_offer_radar.dart:337-343). _onOfferWithdrawn removes the pending offer (916) but never recomputes the flag. When the gate closes, _releasePendingRadarOffers returns on the empty pending list (459), and _refreshRadarHomeOffers also returns early (384). With the API repo, the withdrawal event is queued before the nearby list update (api_dispatch_repository.dart:312-323), so the offer is already gone from pending when the watcher runs. The watcher therefore never gives it a lost timer, and the recompute in _dismissRadarHomeOffer (493) never happens.
verdicts.repro: I wrote a throwaway widget test (same harness): go online, call RideCheckGate.set(true) so dispatch offers 'first' and 'second' park as pending, send withdrawals for both, then one pump later emit an empty nearby list, then call RideCheckGate.set(false) and pump about 45 s. Output: `withdrawn, gate open: Trip found | NEW | Tap for all`, then `g+9: Trip found | NEW | Tap for all`, then `after: ... texts=Trip found | NEW | Tap for all`, with no 'Finding trips'. So the button keeps saying a trip was found while dispatch has zero offers. When I emitted the nearby drop in the same tick in my fake, the 2.8 s lost-match path cleared the flag. That ordering differs from the API repo, where the withdrawal comes first. Test file deleted.

confirmed.title: Home Radar cards and the Exclusive sheet never show the CASH badge in Swedish or French
confirmed.description: _radarOfferView turns the offer's wire payment into the display word before building the RadarOfferView: `payment: offer.cash ? tr.cash : offer.payment`. RadarOfferView then works out the cash flag from that same string: `bool get cash => isCash(payment);` with `isCash(String payment) => payment.trim().toLowerCase() == 'cash'` (lib/widgets/radar_offer_card.dart:87-89). In sv tr.cash is 'Kontant' and in fr it is 'Espèces', so `offer.cash` comes out false. Both Home surfaces gate the badge on it: RadarOfferCard `if (show.badges && offer.cash) OfferBadge.cash(...)` (radar_offer_card.dart:224) and ExclusiveRequestSheet `if (show.badges && offer.cash)` (exclusive_request_sheet.dart:80). RadarOfferView.payment is used nowhere else, so swapping in tr.cash has no visible benefit. The Radar list screen passes the raw value (`payment: offer.payment`, ride_requests.dart:164/730) and keeps the badge, so the two lists disagree. The Swedish zone defaults to sv, so most drivers are affected.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The app is in Svenska (the Stockholm zone default) or the driver switches to Français. A cash offer reaches Home (demo dispatch offers have payment: 'Cash'). The Radar card and the Exclusive sheet show no CASH chip, so the driver accepts without knowing they must collect cash. In English the same offer shows the chip.
confirmed.evidence:
home_offer_radar.dart:1052  `payment: offer.cash ? tr.cash : offer.payment,`
radar_offer_card.dart:87-89  `bool get cash => isCash(payment);` / `static bool isCash(String payment) => payment.trim().toLowerCase() == 'cash';`
radar_offer_card.dart:224  `if (show.badges && offer.cash)`
exclusive_request_sheet.dart:80  `if (show.badges && offer.cash)`
app_sv.arb:94 `"cash": "Kontant"`, app_fr.arb:94 `"cash": "Espèces"`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass the raw `offer.payment` (or carry the bool) into RadarOfferView and translate only where a payment word is displayed.

verdicts.reason: home_offer_radar.dart:1060 builds RadarOfferView with `payment: offer.cash ? tr.cash : offer.payment`. RadarOfferView.cash is `isCash(payment)`, which is `payment.trim().toLowerCase() == 'cash'` (radar_offer_card.dart:87-89). With app_sv.arb:94 'Kontant' or app_fr.arb:94 'Espèces' it returns false. Both Home consumers of _radarOfferView gate the badge on it: the Radar deck card (radar_offer_card.dart:224, via home_offer_radar.dart:1127) and ExclusiveRequestSheet (components/exclusive_request_sheet.dart:80, via home_offer_radar.dart:1157). The Swedish zone maps to 'sv' (zone_settings.dart:110). I rate it medium rather than high: cash offers reach Home only when the driver has turned cash rides on (home_offer_rules.dart:11-12, 18-20), and AcceptRide still gets paidByCash: offer.cash (line 963), so the trip screen knows it is cash. The loss is the CASH chip on the offer.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the payment string through RadarOfferView.cash to both badge gates, plus the sv/fr arb values. No test run.

verdicts.reason: _radarOfferView sets `payment: offer.cash ? tr.cash : offer.payment` (home_offer_radar.dart:1070). RadarOfferView.cash is `isCash(payment)`, which compares with 'cash' (radar_offer_card.dart:87-89). The view built here feeds both the deck cards (line 1137) and the Exclusive sheet (line 1167). Both show the CASH badge only when offer.cash is true (radar_offer_card.dart:224, exclusive_request_sheet.dart:80). Neither widget displays RadarOfferView.payment as text, so in sv and fr a cash offer has no cash marker at all on Home.
verdicts.repro: Ran test/_audit_u135_test.dart (since deleted), which printed lookupAppLocalizations(locale).cash and RadarOfferView.isCash of it. Output: `en cash="Cash" isCash=true`, `sv cash="Kontant" isCash=false`, `fr cash="Espèces" isCash=false`. All tests passed.

confirmed.title: A reservation's Exclusive claim that wins while the driving-time limit forces Go offline (or a cash-rule change dismisses the offer) is dropped: dispatch has given it to this driver, but the app keeps no record of the win
confirmed.description: _claimExclusiveReservation stops the offer timer and awaits dispatch.claimOffer. If _outsideRadarOffer is cleared meanwhile, the function returns before looking at the result. _goOffline (home.dart:957) and going online (home.dart:918) both set _outsideRadarOffer = null directly; going offline can happen through the Go-offline confirm or _drivingLimitReached (home_account.dart:137). _claimReservation only updates ScheduledRideStore when the claim is lost, so a win is never recorded: no take(upcoming:true), no take(), no trip. The demo dispatch has already removed the reservation from its open set (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:536), so the next claim attempt returns unavailable. This is the same pattern as the known home_offer_radar.dart:856 bug, but on the reservation path.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The reservation's Exclusive offer is up and the driver taps Accept. While dispatch decides, the driving-time limit is reached (or the driver confirms Go offline). The claim comes back success, but the code returns early. Dispatch has given the reservation to this driver, yet the phone still lists it as Available in Scheduled rides and never starts it. Tapping Accept there later gets 'no longer available', and the rider's booking has a driver who has no record of it.
confirmed.suggested_fix: On success, always record it: take(id, upcoming: true) when the Exclusive window has not been reached, otherwise keep it as a won trip for when the driver is back online. Only skip the UI work when the offer is gone.

verdicts.reason: home_reservation.dart:488-489 awaits _claimReservation and then returns early if _outsideRadarOffer changed. _claimReservation (home_reservation.dart:353-370) only updates ScheduledRideStore on networkError or a loss, so a win is recorded nowhere. confirmed.title: After midnight, 'Today'/'Tomorrow' reservations are re-read against the new date: a 'Tomorrow 01:00' ride jumps 24 h ahead and never reaches its Exclusive step
confirmed.description: Reservations keep the relative words 'Today'/'Tomorrow' from when they were booked (DemoReservations._at). pickupAt reinterprets those words against whatever 'now' it is given (driver_home_admin_content.dart:240). The demo books relative to the real clock (main +2 h, clashing +2h25, airport +5 h), so any session opened after 22:00 has 'Tomorrow' rides. At 00:00 each of them silently moves to the day after. Scope code that reads it: _exclusiveStepReached/untilPickup here, _untilExclusiveStep:105, _planScheduled:131 (any re-plan after midnight, e.g. a store change or going online, schedules 'leave now' 24 h late), ReservationWhen.ofRequest (sheet and island labels), ScheduledRideStore.isLateCancel/freeCancelUntil (scheduled_rides.dart:510-519), ScheduledRideStore.upcoming ordering, and the fixed card text built in _ScheduledRide.request (scheduled_rides.dart:1134).
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver goes online at 23:00. The main reservation is 'Tomorrow 01:00'. At 00:40 the Exclusive timer fires, _exclusiveStepReached sees 24h20m left and returns false, so the ride never becomes Exclusive on this phone. The Home popup keeps offering it as 'Tomorrow 01:00' when it is 20 minutes away. An accepted 'Tomorrow 01:00' ride cancelled at 00:30 is treated as a free cancel ('Free cancel until tomorrow 00:00') and is not counted as late. A re-plan after midnight moves its 'leave now' to the next night.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store an absolute pickup DateTime (or a date plus wall time) when the ride is booked. Derive the 'Today'/'Tomorrow' words only for display.

Nothing re-anchors at a day change: no midnight or rollover handling exists anywhere in lib, and DemoReservations.reset is not called on a timer. After 00:00 a 'Tomorrow 01:00' ride resolves to the next day, 24 h late. _exclusiveStepReached (home_scheduled.dart:94-96) then returns false, and _untilExclusiveStep and _planScheduled (pickupAt at line ~131) compute times 24 h late. ScheduledClock is the real clock outside tests (scheduled_clock.dart). I rate it medium: it needs a session that runs across midnight with rides booked after about 22:00 (main +2 h). confirmed.title: Accepted and requested rides store a relative 'Today'/'Tomorrow' that is re-read against the current date, so after midnight a ride moves a day later
confirmed.description: Reservations carry pickupDay 'Today' or 'Tomorrow', fixed when they are built (DemoReservations books them once from the first clock reading; the seed accepted ride is 'Tomorrow'). Every consumer resolves them again with pickupAt(now) = today or tomorrow of the current `now`. Once the date changes, a 'Tomorrow 00:30' ride booked at 22:30 resolves to the day after. _planScheduled re-runs on every store change and every time Radar goes live (_onRadarLive). After midnight it recomputes pickupAt and cancels the correct Leave-now timer, replacing it with one 24 h later. The same shift reaches the late-cancel rule (isLateCancel calls a 20-minutes-to-pickup cancel free), the smart gap, the clash check and the cards, which still say 'Tomorrow'.

confirmed.title: Accepting a reservation whose pickup has already passed leaves it as the 'next' scheduled ride forever, and it then filters out every trip offer
confirmed.description: _nextScheduledRide is ScheduledRideStore.upcoming.first, and upcoming sorts accepted rides soonest first without dropping ones whose pickup has passed. When the next ride's pickup has passed and lateSince is null, _planScheduled returns at line 140 (`if (state.lateSince == null && !pickupAt.isAfter(now)) { return; }`), so no Leave-now, late warning or backup is ever planned and the ride never leaves Accepted. _fitsSchedule (305-320) then calls SmartGap.offerFits against that past pickup. offerFits returns `!now.add(needed).isAfter(at)`, which is always false for a past `at`, so every Radar deck trip, Live-list trip (_rideAllowed in home_offer_rules.dart:22) and Exclusive offer (home_offer_radar.dart:241/326) is rejected. _towardPickupTime also keeps saying 'Trips toward your HH:MM pickup'. There are several ways a past ride gets there. (1) Requests are never pruned when their time passes (see the next finding), so the driver can accept one from Scheduled rides. (2) The Home popup can raise a released request whose pickup has passed: _exclusiveStepReached returns false when untilPickup is null, so _waitsForHome is true. (3) An assignment that waited while the driver was offline can be accepted after its time (_maybeShowAssignment never checks the pickup time). (4) A won Exclusive claim whose pickup has just passed is saved 'for later' (home_reservation.dart:494-498).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Reproduced with a throwaway widget test on the fast test day. At 08:10 the 08:05 Lidingö request is still listed (openRequests=2). The driver accepts it, giving upcoming=[Today 08:05, Tomorrow 08:15], then goes online, and dispatch publishes a trip that ends near the driver. Control run without the stale accept: the Radar deck shows ['toward']. With the stale accept: no Radar deck at all (deck found=0). The driver gets no trips for the rest of the session, and the 08:05 ride sits in Accepted indefinitely.
confirmed.evidence:
home_scheduled.dart:113-116 `final upcoming = ScheduledRideStore.upcoming; return upcoming.isEmpty ? null : upcoming.first;`
home_scheduled.dart:140 `if (state.lateSince == null && !pickupAt.isAfter(now)) { return; }`
home_scheduled.dart:312-320 `final fits = SmartGap.offerFits(...); if (!fits) { return false; }`
smart_gap.dart:131 `return !now.add(Duration(minutes: needed)).isAfter(at);`
scheduled_rides.dart:626-633 upcoming keeps every ride with `route.pickupAt(now) != null`, past ones included
confirmed.suggested_fix: Leave rides whose pickup has passed out of `upcoming` and _nextScheduledRide, or move them out of Accepted (missed or backup) when they pass. Refuse to accept a request, popup or assignment whose pickup has passed.

verdicts.corrected_title: Accepting a reservation whose pickup has already passed leaves it as the 'next' scheduled ride forever, and it then filters out every trip offer
verdicts.reason: ScheduledRideStore.upcoming (scheduled_rides.dart:625-633) keeps every accepted ride whose pickupAt is non-null, past ones included. _nextScheduledRide takes upcoming.first (home_scheduled.dart:113-116). When a new ride is set there, lateSince is reset to null (124-128). The early return at home_scheduled.dart:140 then fires for a past pickup, so _leaveNow, _lateScheduled and _giveToBackup are never reached and the ride never leaves Accepted. _fitsSchedule (home_scheduled.dart:323-335) calls SmartGap.offerFits, which returns !now.add(needed).isAfter(at) (smart_gap.dart:131). That is always false for a past `at`. This filter is used for the Radar deck (home_offer_radar.dart:241,326) and for the Live list (home_offer_rules.dart:22). Reachable path: the seeded Lidingö request (scheduled_rides.dart:409-414) has no id, so _claim returns true without asking dispatch (scheduled_rides.dart:268). Requests are never pruned by time; _visibleRequests (541-547) filters only on block, category and clash. So the driver can open its details after 08:05 and accept it (scheduled_rides.dart:218-224). In normal use a ride accepted while still in the future is guarded, because the Leave-now timer sets lateSince or starts the trip before the pickup. I rate it medium rather than high because the trigger is an edge path: accepting an already-stale request.

The Accept path in _openRideDetails (scheduled_rides.dart:220-227) checks nothing about the time. DemoDispatchRepository.claimOffer (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:536-543) returns success for any reservation still in _reservations, and reservations are never expired. Once accepted, the past ride becomes _nextScheduledRide (home_scheduled.dart:113-116). _planScheduled then returns at line 140, so nothing is planned and the ride never leaves Accepted. _fitsSchedule (334-349) calls SmartGap.offerFits, which returns `!now.add(needed).isAfter(at)` (smart_gap.dart:149). That is always false for at < now, and needed >= 1 because driveMinutes is at least 1. Every non-assigned offer is therefore rejected. Reaching this needs the driver to accept an already-passed request, which is an edge path, so medium rather than high.

confirmed.title: When the estimated drive plus spare minutes exceeds the 'be online' window, Leave-now opens the trip at onlineBy, after the latest departure time, and the go-online reminder and the 15-min reminder are skipped
confirmed.description: SmartGap.leaveAt is documented as 'the latest moment to set off'. _planScheduled clamps the trip start to `leave.isBefore(onlineBy) ? onlineBy : leave`, so when leave < onlineBy the ride opens at onlineBy, after the latest moment to leave. The reminders and the online reminder are also only scheduled when they are `isBefore(leave)`, so in this case none fire between leave and the clamped start. For a normal ride (online 30 min before, spare 15 min) this happens whenever the estimated drive exceeds 15 min, roughly 6 km straight-line. A code comment says 'never before the be online window' is intended, but that rule directly contradicts leaveAt's meaning.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver is 12 km from a normal 10:00 pickup. The estimated drive is 31 min, so leave = 09:14 and onlineBy = 09:30. No 60-min reminder fires, because 09:00 is not before 09:14. The trip opens at 09:30, 16 minutes after the latest departure, and the driver arrives about 10:01 plus the spare time they no longer have.
confirmed.evidence:
home_scheduled.dart:146 `if (time.isAfter(now) && time.isBefore(leave)) {`
home_scheduled.dart:153 `if (onlineBy.isAfter(now) && onlineBy.isBefore(leave)) {`
home_scheduled.dart:157 `final start = leave.isBefore(onlineBy) ? onlineBy : leave;`
smart_gap.dart:94-95 `/// "Leave now": the latest moment to set off ...`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Open the trip at `leave` when it is earlier than onlineBy (or at least warn at `leave`), and schedule the reminders relative to the actual start.

verdicts.corrected_title: When the estimated drive plus spare minutes exceeds the 'be online' window, Leave-now opens the trip at onlineBy, after the latest departure time, and the go-online reminder and the 15-min reminder are skipped
verdicts.reason: SmartGap.leaveAt is documented as 'the latest moment to set off' (smart_gap.dart:94-108), computed as pickup - (drive + spare). home_scheduled.dart:157 sets `start = leave.isBefore(onlineBy) ? onlineBy : leave`. Whenever leave is earlier than onlineBy, the trip therefore opens later than the latest departure. For a normal ride, onlineBefore=30 and spare=15 (scheduled_ride_rules.dart:45,70), so this happens for any estimated drive over 15 min. The inline comment states the clamp is intended, but no document in docs/ defines it, and the result guarantees a late arrival. One part of the finding is wrong. The 60-min reminder does fire in its example: 09:00 is before leave 09:14 (home_scheduled.dart:146). What is lost is the online reminder (onlineBy 09:30 is not before 09:14, line 153) and the 15-min reminder.

verdicts.corrected_title: When the estimated drive plus spare time is longer than the 'be online' window, Leave now opens at onlineBy, after the latest departure, and the 'go online' and late reminders are skipped
verdicts.reason: home_scheduled.dart:157 `final start = leave.isBefore(onlineBy) ? onlineBy : leave;` opens the trip later than SmartGap.leaveAt, which smart_gap.dart:94-95 documents as 'the latest moment to set off'. The 'never before the be online window' comment (line 9, 156) explains why the trip does not open early. It does not justify opening after the departure deadline. No listed decision document covers this. The finding's reminder claim is partly wrong. A reminder is kept when `time.isBefore(leave)`, so the 60-min reminder at 09:00 does fire (09:00 < 09:14). The 15-min reminder (09:45) and the go-online reminder (onlineBy 09:30, line 153) are skipped. An offline driver therefore gets no 'go online' prompt, and at 09:30 the ride goes late and then to backup.
verdicts.repro: Worked by hand: 12 km x 1.35 = 16.2 km road; 16.2/32 x 60 = 30.375, ceil = 31 min drive; leave = 10:00 - (31+15) = 09:14; onlineBy = 10:00 - 30 = 09:30; start = 09:30; arrival = 10:01. In general this happens for normal rides whenever drive > 15 min. No test was run.

confirmed.title: Native: the map padding switches between the 75% driving anchor and the plain top inset the instant a pan is reported or recenter starts, which the SDK realizes as an immediate content shift under the finger and a snap at the start of the 'no snap' recenter flight
confirmed.description: On native the 75% vehicle anchor is realized through `GoogleMap.padding` (`drivingInsets(... following:)` returns a top inset of `2*desired - height + bottom`, roughly 520 px on an 800 px screen with a 260 px top and 120 px sheet, versus 260 px when not following). `accept_ride.dart:1227-1234` passes `following: _camera.isGuidance && _camera.mode == DriverCameraMode.following`. `onUserGesture` (`accept_ride.dart:1242`) runs `_rebuild(_camera.userGesture)`, so on the first 6 px of a drag the widget rebuilds with the smaller top padding; Android `setPadding` and iOS `GMSMapView.padding` keep the camera target lat/lng and re-centre it in the new padded region, i.e. the map content jumps by about (520-260)/2 = 130 px while the driver's finger is on it. On recenter the padding flips back before the eased 1 s flight (`google_driver_camera_port.dart:102-106` documents the flight as landing with no snap), so the flight starts with an instant jump. The web path is guarded (`drivingInsets` returns `edgeInsets` on web and the JS `configure` only pans when `state.anchored`, which `release()` has already cleared); the native path has no equivalent guard. Not executable here (needs a device), hence the modest confidence.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver in guidance on Android/iOS starts dragging the map: as soon as the drag registers (6 px) the whole map lurches ~130 px up under the finger; tapping recenter produces an equal downward jump before the smooth flight begins.
confirmed.evidence: map_overlay_insets.dart:25-47: `EdgeInsets drivingInsets(double height, {required bool following}) { if (kIsWeb) { return edgeInsets; } ... final desired = (height * .75).clamp(top + margin, height - bottom - margin); return EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(32, following ? math.max(top, 2 * desired - height + bottom) : top, 32, bottom);`. accept_ride.dart:1227-1234: `padding: MapOverlayInsets.forActiveRide(...).drivingInsets(MediaQuery.sizeOf(context).height, following: _camera.isGuidance && _camera.mode == DriverCameraMode.following), cameraAnchor: ... ? .75 : .5,`. accept_ride.dart:1242: `onUserGesture: () { _rebuild(_camera.userGesture); ...`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep the native padding constant across follow/browse (the anchor is only needed for follow frames, which the port can realize by offsetting the camera target instead), or defer the padding change until the gesture ends and apply it together with the first camera move.

verdicts.reason: On native, the 75% anchor exists only as GoogleMap.padding. drivingInsets (map_overlay_insets.dart:25-43) returns a top inset of max(top, 2*desired-height+bottom) while following and plain `top` otherwise. The web early return at line 26 is the only guard. accept_ride.dart:1230-1235 switches `following` on _camera.mode. onUserGesture (accept_ride.dart:1242) calls _rebuild(_camera.userGesture), which sets the mode to browsing (driver_camera_controller.dart:582-588). recenter (lines 599-607) sets it back to following before the flight starts. Each switch rebuilds CustomGoogleMap with new `padding: widget.padding` (custom_google_map.dart:429). The plugin forwards that straight to googleMap.setPadding (google_maps_flutter_android 2.18.2 GoogleMapController.java:576-578) with no camera compensation. On native, GoogleDriverCameraPort._move (google_driver_camera_port.dart:197-212) only calls moveCamera(target). The web bridge claim/configure does the anchor shift on web only. The Maps SDK keeps the camera target at the centre of the padded region. On an 800 px screen that region's centre moves by (520-260)/2, about 130 px, at drag start, and back at recenter before the 1 s eased flight. Only the visual effect is unconfirmed: it follows from documented SDK padding semantics, not from a device run.

confirmed.title: A ride-category choice saved in Ride preferences is not applied to offers after a cold start until the driver reopens Ride preferences

Nothing reads the `'categories'` settings section at startup: `main.dart` restores only `MapTrafficSetting.restore()` (line 41) and `DriverLanguage.restore()` (line 46); grep shows `read('categories')` exists only in preferences.dart. verdicts.reason: The only writer of DriverCategoryChoice.off is Preferences._publishChoice (preferences.dart:171-176). confirmed.title: System Back while a Radar claim is in flight unmounts Radar and drops a won trip (the on-screen Back is covered by the Matching banner)
confirmed.description: `_claimTrip` awaits `claimOffer` and then returns if `!mounted` (line 322) without handling the result. The Back button (`_closeRides`, line 270-282) stays enabled during Matching, and Home unmounts `RideRequests` on close (`showRideRequests = false`, home.dart:759-765, the whole Stack is replaced). `DemoDispatchRepository.claimOffer` removes the offer from the feed on success (line 565-566) and there is no other path that opens the accepted trip. So a Back tap during the ~1.45 s claim delay loses the trip: it is assigned (server side) but the driver never sees AcceptRide, and the card is gone from Radar when reopened.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver taps Match, changes their mind and taps Back within a second, then reopens Radar: the trip is no longer listed (claim succeeded and removed it) and no active trip exists on this phone, while dispatch considers it accepted.
confirmed.evidence: line 318 `result = await _dispatch.claimOffer(trip.id);` — line 322 `if (!mounted || _matchingOfferId != trip.id) { return; }` — line 567 (demo_dispatch_repository.dart) `_removeOffer(offerId); return ClaimResult.success(offer);` — home.dart:759-763 `onCloseRides: (hasOffers) { setState(() { showRideRequests = false; ...` (RideRequests is a child of the conditional Stack)
confirmed.suggested_fix: Disable Back while `_matchingOfferId != null`, or hand a successful claim result to Home (callback/repository) so the active trip opens even when the Radar sheet has been closed.

confirmed.title: The 'Could not match' banner after a network error on the Radar screen never clears and covers the Back and Refresh buttons
confirmed.description: On `ClaimOutcome.networkError` `_claimTrip` sets an error `_matchNotice` and schedules no timer to clear it. Every other notice path does: lost match at line 452 (2800 ms), success through `_matchNoticeTimer`. The notice is drawn as a `TripStatusBanner` in `Positioned(top: 0)` over the whole screen (lines 531-536). It is an elevated opaque Material, 10+pad.top+44+12 px tall, while the header (Back and Refresh) is pad.top+8+44+12 px. It therefore fully covers and absorbs taps on the Back button (`_closeRides`) and the Refresh control. It goes away only when the driver taps Match on another card and that claim resolves.

The notice is drawn as Positioned(top:0) over the SafeArea column (ride_requests.dart:548-553). confirmed.title: A withdrawal of another offer cancels the won-match timer: the claimed trip never opens and Radar is stuck in Matching
confirmed.description: `_resolveMatchWon` (line 351-418) keeps the AcceptRide push on `_matchNoticeTimer` (500 ms). `_resolveMatchLost` (line 435) unconditionally does `_matchNoticeTimer?.cancel()` for any trip, and `_onWithdrawn` (line 181-189) calls it for every `claimedElsewhere` withdrawal whose trip is still `available`. If dispatch withdraws trip B while trip A's win timer is pending, the timer is cancelled: `navigator.push(ActiveRideTransition(ride))` never runs, `_matchingOfferId` stays A (line 437 only clears it when it equals B), `_offerStates[A]` stays `resolving`, so A's card shows the spinner forever and every other card's Match is disabled (`blockOtherOffers`, line 724-725). The server already removed A from the feed (`DemoDispatchRepository.claimOffer` line 565-566), so the trip is lost. Reproduced: match A, complete claim with success, pump 100 ms, emit `OfferWithdrawal(offerId: 'b', reason: claimedElsewhere)`, pump 2 s → `AcceptRide mounted: false; matching text: 1`. The demo fires `withdrawOffer(radarGroupTaken)` on its own timer (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:710-714), so the window is real, and a backend's `offer_withdrawn` can arrive at any moment.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver taps Match on a Radar trip, dispatch answers success; within half a second another driver's accept withdraws a different card. The 'Matched' banner is replaced by 'Taken by another driver', no trip screen opens, the matched card spins forever, and no other trip can be matched until the driver closes and reopens Radar. The accepted trip is gone from the server feed.
confirmed.evidence: line 366-368 `_matchNoticeTimer = Timer(const Duration(milliseconds: 500), () { ... navigator.push(ActiveRideTransition(ride));` — line 435 `_matchNoticeTimer?.cancel();` in `_resolveMatchLost` — line 181-187 `void _onWithdrawn(OfferWithdrawal gone) { ... _resolveMatchLost(trip, _RadarGone.lostOwnMatch, notice: shown);` — test: `AcceptRide mounted: false; matching text: 1`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use a separate timer for the won-match navigation (or push immediately and keep only the banner on a timer), and never let `_resolveMatchLost` for another offer touch the win timer; also ignore withdrawals while `_matchingOfferId` names a won trip.

Nothing re-arms the push. _matchingOfferId stays on the won trip because line 437 only clears it for the lost id, so the other cards stay blocked (lines 724-725). confirmed.description: `_claim` awaits `dispatch.claimOffer(ride.id)` (line 273) with the list screen's Back button active (`_buildHeader`, line 310-313). confirmed.title: Late-cancel pause ends early: it is lifted as soon as the first counted cancel leaves the 7-day period, not at the announced date
confirmed.description: pausedUntil recomputes `recent`, the late cancels in the last lateCancelPeriodDays, at every call, and returns null when fewer than lateCancelLimit remain. The pause end is announced as recent.last + pauseDays (Notifications, island and the confirmation sheet). With the defaults (limit 2, period 7 days, pause 7 days), the pause actually ends 7 days after the earlier of the two cancels, which can be minutes after it began.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Reproduced: late cancels at 20 Oct 09:00 and 27 Oct 08:00. Right after the second cancel, pausedUntil gives 3 Nov 08:00 and the driver is told 'Scheduled rides paused until 3 Nov'. At 27 Oct 09:01, 61 minutes later, pausedUntil returns null and the requests are back.
confirmed.evidence: scheduled_rides.dart:494-500 `final since = now.subtract(Duration(days: rules.lateCancelPeriodDays)); final recent = _lateCancels.where((at) => at.isAfter(since)).toList(); if (recent.length < rules.lateCancelLimit) { return null; } final until = recent.last.add(Duration(days: rules.pauseDays));`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Record the pause (its start and end) when the limit is reached and honour that end date, instead of re-deriving it from a sliding window.

verdicts.reason: pausedUntil (scheduled_rides.dart:493-501) works the pause out again from a sliding window on every call: `recent` holds only the late cancels after now-lateCancelPeriodDays, and the method returns null once fewer than lateCancelLimit (default 2, scheduled_ride_rules.dart:81-83) are left. The end date it announces is recent.last + pauseDays, and _openRideDetails sends that date to Notifications (scheduled_rides.dart:244-250). With cancels at T1 and T2 (T2-T1 < 7 d), T1 leaves the window at T1+7d. From then on `recent` holds 1 cancel and the block is lifted, possibly minutes after T2. Nothing stores the pause once it starts: _lateCancels is the only state (addLateCancel :470, _cancelAccepted :697). The rules doc comment at scheduled_ride_rules.dart:121-122 says the cancels 'pause Scheduled rides for [pauseDays]', so the early end is not intentional.
verdicts.repro: Traced statically: pausedUntil, block(), _visibleRequests and _cancelAccepted, plus the default rules in scheduled_ride_rules.dart:80-83. Cancels at 20 Oct 09:00 and 27 Oct 08:00: at 27 Oct 08:00 the window starts 20 Oct 08:00, recent = 2, so the pause runs until 3 Nov 08:00. At 27 Oct 09:01 the window starts 20 Oct 09:01, recent = 1, so the result is null. No test was run; the arithmetic is deterministic.

verdicts.reason: scheduled_rides.dart:495-503 pausedUntil re-derives the pause every call from a sliding window (`recent = _lateCancels.where(at.isAfter(now - periodDays))`) and returns null once fewer than lateCancelLimit remain. The announced end is recent.last + pauseDays. No stored pause record or other guard exists, so the pause ends when the earliest counted cancel ages out of the window. With defaults 2/7/7 (scheduled_ride_rules.dart:166-168) that can be minutes after the announcement.

confirmed.title: Backup and device-transfer rules leave out the root domain, so ride-check audio under app_flutter is not excluded, and the test only checks that the tags exist
confirmed.description: The test 'Android excludes app data from backup and device transfer' only asserts that `<cloud-backup>` and `<device-transfer>` are present. It never checks what they exclude. The rules exclude the `sharedpref`, `database` and `file` domains only. Ride-check audio is written under `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()`, which on Android is `context.getDir("flutter")`, i.e. `<dataDir>/app_flutter`. That is in the `root` domain, not `file`. For apps targeting Android 12+, `allowBackup="false"` does not stop device-to-device migration, so the recordings leave the phone when the driver moves to a new device. The rules file's own comment says driver data stays on this device, and the ride-check UI says the recording is saved only on this phone. The test cannot catch this, or any rule that includes data.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A driver records audio in a Ride check, then sets up a new Android phone with device transfer. The .m4a files under app_flutter/ride_check_audio are copied to the new device. A rules file containing `<include domain="root" path="."/>` would also pass this test. confirmed.title: Web zoom-about-finger compensation uses the requested zoom, not the capped one: on the default raster map, a double tap or pinch at zoom 18 pans the map instead of zooming
confirmed.description: zoomAt clamps the next zoom to 3..21 and calls map.moveCamera({zoom: next}). Without a configured cloud map ID (the default; the meta tag holds the 'DRIVER_GOOGLE_MAP_ID' placeholder), the map is RASTER with maxZoom capped at 18 (lines 539-541 and zoomCap). Google Maps clamps the applied zoom to maxZoom, but the pan compensation is computed with scale = 2 ** (next - current) using the unclamped next, then applied with pan(). At or near the cap, the map pans by (1 - 2^Δ) × (finger offset from centre) although the zoom did not change, or changed less. The tapped road then moves away from the finger. Pinch does the same on every touchmove frame. The comment at google_driver_camera_port.dart:78 says the bridge caps pinch zoom on raster, but zoomAt uses 21.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On the web app (raster default), the driver has zoomed in to 18 and double-taps a street 120 px right of centre. The zoom stays 18, but the map scrolls about 120 px sideways. A pinch-out held at the cap makes the map slide away from the fingers on every frame.
confirmed.suggested_fix: After moveCamera, read the zoom actually applied (Number(map.getZoom())) and compute scale from that, or clamp next to the active maxZoom (zoomCap()) before moving.

confirmed.title: No release gate stops a keyless iOS build (MOVERA_REQUIRE_MAPS_KEY is Android-only), and that build skips GMSServices.provideAPIKey, so Home's map would crash on device
confirmed.description: Info.plist sets `GoogleMapsApiKey` to `$(GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY)`. No xcconfig or CI step defines that setting, so in the CI preflight and any local build without the env var it expands to empty. AppDelegate then deliberately skips `GMSServices.provideAPIKey`. The Google Maps SDK for iOS throws an uncaught GMSServicesException ('must be initialized via [GMSServices provideAPIKey:...] prior to use') when the first GMSMapView is created. That happens when Home's map mounts, so the app crashes rather than showing a blank map as Android does. Android has a `MOVERA_REQUIRE_MAPS_KEY` gate and a CI step that proves it, and FRONTEND_16_POINT_RECORD.md F04 says '`MOVERA_REQUIRE_MAPS_KEY=true` fails a native release when `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` is blank'. iOS has no such check: `ios-release-preflight` builds a keyless release and reports success.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The owner archives an iOS release from a shell where GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY is not exported (as in CI). The archive succeeds. On device, the driver signs in, Home mounts the GoogleMap, and the app terminates with GMSServicesException. CI stayed green because nothing checks the key for iOS.
confirmed.evidence:
ios/Runner/Info.plist:5-6 `<key>GoogleMapsApiKey</key><string>$(GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY)</string>`
AppDelegate.swift:11-15 `if let mapsKey = ..., !mapsKey.isEmpty, mapsKey != "$(GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY)" { GMSServices.provideAPIKey(mapsKey) }`
drider-ci.yml:148-149 `flutter build ios --release --no-codesign` (no key, no MOVERA_REQUIRE_MAPS_KEY check)
android/app/build.gradle.kts:85-91 Android-only `MOVERA_REQUIRE_MAPS_KEY` gate
docs/FRONTEND_16_POINT_RECORD.md:49 'fails a native release when GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY is blank'
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add an iOS Run Script build phase (or a CI step) that fails a Release build when MOVERA_REQUIRE_MAPS_KEY=true and GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY is empty. Have it exercised in ios-release-preflight like the Android step, and narrow the docs claim until then.

verdicts.reason: Info.plist:5-6 expands $(GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY) from the build environment. AppDelegate.swift:11-15 skips GMSServices.provideAPIKey when the key is empty, and no Dart-side guard checks for the key (grep of lib finds nothing). The Google Maps iOS SDK raises an exception when a GMSMapView is created without provideAPIKey, so a keyless iOS build crashes when Home's map mounts. CI runs only `flutter build ios --release --no-codesign` (REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:35), and nothing fails a keyless iOS release. The finding overstates the docs mismatch: F04 (FRONTEND_16_POINT_RECORD.md:49) and REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:34 both sit under the Android release, so no doc actually promises an iOS gate. The trigger is a misconfigured build rather than user input, which is why the severity is low.
verdicts.repro: Read AppDelegate.swift, Info.plist, drider-ci.yml:116-125 (the Android-only MOVERA_REQUIRE_MAPS_KEY check), android/app/build.gradle.kts:85-89 and the gate docs. No iOS build was possible here, so the SDK crash is from its documented behaviour, not reproduced.

No xcconfig defines it (ios/Flutter/Release.xcconfig only includes Generated.xcconfig, which has no key), so it is empty unless exported in the environment. AppDelegate.swift:11-15 then skips GMSServices.provideAPIKey. On native, CustomGoogleMap builds GoogleMap directly (custom_google_map.dart:407-410; the _mapsReady guard is the web loader). google_maps_flutter_ios 2.15.5 GoogleMapController.m:60 calls [GMSServices sharedServices] and never provides a key itself. The Google Maps iOS SDK raises the 'must be initialized via provideAPIKey' exception there, so Home crashes instead of showing a blank map. CI: drider-ci.yml:148-149 runs `flutter build ios --release --no-codesign` with no key check, while Android has the gate at build.gradle.kts:85-91 and the CI proof at drider-ci.yml:116-125. One point is overstated: FRONTEND_16_POINT_RECORD.md:49's 'native release' sentence sits inside the Android-only F04 item, and REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:34-35 scopes the maps-key gate to android-release. So the docs do not clearly claim an iOS gate; the gap is the missing iOS gate itself.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand; iOS cannot be built or run in this container. I read AppDelegate.swift, Info.plist, the ios/Flutter xcconfigs, the CI workflow, android build.gradle.kts, and the google_maps_flutter_ios 2.15.5 plugin source in the pub cache (grep for provideAPIKey/GMSServices: only `[GMSServices sharedServices]` at GoogleMapController.m:60). The crash on an uninitialized GMSServices is documented SDK behaviour and was not reproduced on a device.

confirmed.title: ReservationRequestPreview.pickupAt is one hour off on daylight-saving switch days (adds minutes as absolute Duration to local midnight)
confirmed.description: `pickupAt` builds the pickup instant as `DateTime(y, m, d + offset).add(Duration(minutes: minuteOfDay))`. `DateTime.add` adds absolute time, so when the 'Today'/'Tomorrow' date is a DST transition day in the zone (Sweden/France: last Sunday of March and October) the wall-clock result is shifted by an hour relative to the 'HH:mm' label. Reproduced with `TZ=Europe/Stockholm`: for 'Tomorrow 07:40' on 24 Oct 2026 the code yields 2026-10-25 06:40 (untilPickup 11h40 instead of 12h40); on 28 Mar 2026 it yields 08:40 (untilPickup 11h40 instead of 10h40). `untilPickup`, the 'leave now'/'go online for' island timers (home_scheduled.dart:94-131, 321-342), the Scheduled-rides sort (scheduled_rides.dart:630-632) and `SmartGap` clash detection (smart_gap.dart:67-68) all consume this value.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On Sunday 25 Oct 2026 (DST ends) a driver has a reservation 'Today 07:40'. The island says 'Leave now' and the reminder fires an hour early (06:40), and the countdown reads 1 h less than the clock; on 29 Mar it is an hour late, so 'leave now' appears after the pickup time.
confirmed.evidence: driver_home_admin_content.dart:244-245 `return DateTime(now.year, now.month, now.day + offset)\n        .add(Duration(minutes: minute));` · scratch run output: `Tomorrow 07:40 (DST ends 25 Oct): pickupAt()=2026-10-25 06:40:00.000 expected=2026-10-25 07:40:00.000` / `(DST starts 29 Mar): pickupAt()=2026-03-29 08:40:00.000 expected=07:40`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Construct the wall-clock time directly: `DateTime(now.year, now.month, now.day + offset, minute ~/ 60, minute % 60)`.

verdicts.reason: driver_home_admin_content.dart:244-245 builds DateTime(y,m,d+offset).add(Duration(minutes: minuteOfDay)), which adds absolute time to local midnight. On a DST switch day the wall-clock pickup is therefore an hour off. untilPickup (:226-233) and its consumers use this value. Nothing normalizes it.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_c4b2dst_test.dart run with TZ=Europe/Stockholm (now deleted). Output: '7: Oct24 Tomorrow 07:40 -> 2026-10-25 06:40:00.000', '7: Oct25 Today 07:40 -> 2026-10-25 06:40:00.000', '7: Mar28 Tomorrow 07:40 -> 2026-03-29 08:40:00.000'.

verdicts.reason: driver_home_admin_content.dart:244-245 builds the time as `DateTime(y,m,d+offset).add(Duration(minutes: minute))`. A local DateTime.add adds absolute time, so on a 23-hour or 25-hour day the wall-clock result is off by one hour. untilPickup (lines 225-232) and everything downstream use this value.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_dst78_test.dart, run with TZ=Europe/Stockholm (file deleted afterwards). Output: `Today 07:40 on 25 Oct: 2026-10-25 06:40:00.000 until=1:40` (expected 07:40 and 2:40 from 05:00) and `Today 07:40 on 29 Mar: 2026-03-29 08:40:00.000 until=3:40` (expected 07:40 and 2:40 from 05:00).

confirmed.title: _DemoReservationSet._at labels a next-day demo reservation 'Today' when the demo is booked on the spring-forward day itself (e.g. 29 Mar 2026), so its pickupAt is on the wrong day and untilPickup is null
confirmed.description: Same pattern as scheduled_rides_notes.dart: `DateTime(at.y,m,d).difference(DateTime(anchor.y,m,d)).inDays` is 0 across the 23-hour spring-forward day, so `days == 0 ? 'Today' : 'Tomorrow'` yields 'Today' for a ride that is actually tomorrow. The resulting pickupDay feeds `pickupAt` (offset 0 instead of 1), so the demo reservation's countdown and clash logic are a full day off on that day. Demo seed data only (DemoReservations), hence low.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Demo launched late on 28 March with a reservation lead that lands after midnight: Scheduled rides and the island show it as 'Today HH:mm' and its untilPickup is already negative, so it never becomes a 'Leave now' trip.
confirmed.evidence:
lib/core/admin/driver_home_admin_content.dart:492-495 `final days = DateTime(at.year, at.month, at.day)
        .difference(DateTime(anchor.year, anchor.month, anchor.day))
        .inDays;
    return build(clockLabel(at), days == 0 ? 'Today' : 'Tomorrow');`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Compare calendar dates (e.g. `DateTime.utc(at.year, at.month, at.day).difference(DateTime.utc(anchor.year, ...)).inDays`).

verdicts.corrected_title: _DemoReservationSet._at labels a next-day demo reservation 'Today' when the demo is booked on the spring-forward day itself (e.g. 29 Mar 2026), so its pickupAt is on the wrong day and untilPickup is null
verdicts.reason: The mechanism is right but the finding names the wrong date. On 28 March, midnight-to-midnight is 24h, so inDays is 1 and the label is correct. The 23-hour day is 29 March. A demo anchored that evening with a lead that crosses midnight gives DateTime(3,30).difference(DateTime(3,29)) = 23h, so inDays is 0 and the label is 'Today' (driver_home_admin_content.dart:492-495). pickupAt then uses offset 0 and points to the wrong day. Leads go up to 8h30 (DemoReservationPlan.app, :305-310), so any launch after about 15:30 on that day hits it. This affects demo seed data only.
verdicts.repro: Same throwaway TZ=Europe/Stockholm test, setting ScheduledClock.realNow and DemoReservations.reset(). Output: 'launch 2026-03-28 20:00 assigned Tomorrow 05:30 ... until=9:30:00' (correct), 'launch 2026-03-29 20:00 assigned Today 04:30 pickupAt=2026-03-29 05:30 until=null' (wrong), 'launch 2026-10-25 20:00 assigned Tomorrow 04:30 until=8:30:00' (correct).

verdicts.corrected_title: _DemoReservationSet._at labels a next-day demo reservation 'Today' when it is booked on the spring-forward day itself (29 March), so the reservation's pickupAt lands on the past day and untilPickup is null
verdicts.reason: driver_home_admin_content.dart:492-495 compares local midnights with .difference().inDays. Midnight 30 Mar minus midnight 29 Mar in CET/CEST is 23h, which gives inDays 0 and so 'Today'. pickupAt with offset 0 then puts the pickup on 29 Mar 00:30, which has already passed, and untilPickup returns null. The finding gave the wrong date: launching on 28 March is correct, because that day has 24 hours (my run shows 'Tomorrow 00:30' for an anchor of 28 Mar 22:30). The bug happens only on 29 March. Effect is limited to the demo seed data.
verdicts.repro: Same throwaway test, with TZ=Europe/Stockholm, ScheduledClock.realNow pinned and DemoReservations.plan = DemoReservationPlan.app. Output: `anchor 2026-03-28 22:30 main=Tomorrow 00:30 pickupAt=2026-03-29 00:30 until=2:00` (correct), `anchor 2026-03-29 22:30 main=Today 00:30 pickupAt=2026-03-29 00:30 until=null` (wrong), `anchor 2026-03-29 23:00 main=Today 01:00 ... until=null` (wrong).

confirmed.title: Eight admin-editable Driver app texts are never read by any screen, so admin's edits to them have no effect
confirmed.description: DriverTexts.all is 'Every key admin can change' (Content › Driver app texts, Q30). offerFare, offerHide, offerReservationRequest, offerYourNextRide, offerViewRoute, offerNewReservation, offerViewDetails and tripCompleteRide are listed and mapped in driver_text_l10n.dart, but nothing in lib calls driverText() with them, and the matching tr getters (tr.offerHide, tr.offerViewRoute, …) are not used either. verdicts.reason: DriverTexts.all (lib/core/content/driver_app_texts.dart:270-271, 'Every key, for admin's list') includes offerFare (:208), offerHide, offerReservationRequest, offerYourNextRide, offerViewRoute, offerNewReservation, offerViewDetails (:232-243) and tripCompleteRide (:262). driver_text_l10n.dart:62,72-77,86 maps them, but no widget in lib calls DriverTexts.<these> or the matching tr getters (tr.offerHide, tr.offerViewRoute, ...).
