confirmed.title: Demo document titles and demo notifications are localised once and cached, so they stay in the old language after the driver switches language
confirmed.description: `DocumentExpiryStore.documents` lazily builds the demo list with `tr.docInsuranceLetter` etc. and caches it in `_documents` (line 110); only `load()`/`reset()` replace it and neither is called on a language change (`DriverLanguage.choose` → `_apply()` only flips `DriverAppTexts.language` and the notifier; no caller resets the store — grep shows no `DocumentExpiryStore.instance.reset()` in lib). The cached `title`/`shortTitle` feed the island and notification text (`home_account.dart:153-160` → `DriverNotices.documentExpiring(title: document.title, shortTitle: document.shortTitle)`), the Documents list (`documents.dart:224`) and the renewal sheet (`document_renewal.dart:65,168,304`). Reproduced with a throwaway test: with language `en` the first title is 'Insurance letter'; after setting the language to `sv` it is still 'Insurance letter' while `tr.docInsuranceLetter` is 'Försäkringsbrev'. The same pattern exists in `DriverNotificationFeed.items` (`driver_notifications.dart:127-128` caches `demoReceived`, whose first title is `tr.noticeNewScheduledRide` and whose bodies 'Tomorrow 07:40 · 126 kr · Tap to view', 'Bonus progress', 'Payout sent' are English literals even though a localised `tr.noticeScheduledBody` template exists).
confirmed.failure_scenario: App starts in Swedish (zone default), the Home island already read the documents; the driver picks English in Settings. The island later says 'Försäkringsbrev expires in 7 days', the notification is 'Försäkringsbrev expires tomorrow' and the Documents screen keeps the Swedish names until the app is restarted. Conversely a Swedish driver always sees the three demo notifications in English.
confirmed.evidence: document_expiry.dart:109-110 `List<TrackedDocument> get documents =>\n      List.unmodifiable(_documents ??= _seed ?? demo(_now()));` · document_expiry.dart:88-92 `title: tr.docInsuranceLetter, shortTitle: tr.insurance,` · driver_language.dart:105-109 `_apply()` only sets `DriverAppTexts.language`/`current.value` · driver_notifications.dart:127-128 `_items ??= DriverNotices.demoReceived(_now())` and :333 `body: 'Tomorrow 07:40 · 126 kr · Tap to view',` :341 `title: 'Bonus progress',` :347 `title: 'Payout sent',` · test output: `en title=Insurance letter, after switch to sv title=Insurance letter, tr now=Försäkringsbrev`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep language-independent ids/keys in `TrackedDocument` and resolve the title through `tr` at read time (or rebuild the demo list when `DriverLanguage.current` changes); build the demo notifications with the existing `tr.noticeScheduledBody` and arb keys.

verdicts.reason: document_expiry.dart:109-110 caches `_documents ??= _seed ?? demo(_now())`, and demo() bakes `tr.docInsuranceLetter`/`tr.insurance` etc. into the titles (lines 85-107). DriverLanguage._apply (lib/core/l10n/driver_language.dart:105-109) only sets the language and the notifier. The main.dart:105-115 listener only marks elements for rebuild. Nothing resets or reloads DocumentExpiryStore.instance on a language change. In the same way, DriverNotificationFeed.items caches demoReceived (driver_notifications.dart:127-128), and its bodies and titles at 333/341/342/348/349 are English literals in every language.
verdicts.repro: Ran the throwaway test test/_audit_c1b4v_test.dart (since deleted). It builds a DocumentExpiryStore in English, reads documents, then calls DriverLanguage.choose('sv'). Output: `lang=sv before=Insurance letter after=Insurance letter tr=Försäkringsbrev`.

verdicts.reason: document_expiry.dart:109-110 caches `_documents ??= _seed ?? demo(_now())`, and the titles in it were resolved through `tr` when it was built (lines 88-103). A language change (driver_language.dart:74-80 choose, then _apply at 105-109) only flips DriverAppTexts.language and the notifier. main.dart:106-116 rebuilds the widgets in place, so the singleton DocumentExpiryStore.instance keeps its cached list, and nothing in lib calls DocumentExpiryStore.instance.load/reset on a language change. confirmed.title: Corrupt-record warnings log the raw stored JSON (rider names, addresses, free-text notes) through FormatException.toString()
confirmed.description: `DriverLogRecord` documents that messages 'must not contain rider names, phone numbers or free text' (driver_log.dart:5-6), and the default sink prints to the console in release builds too (`debugPrint`, driver_log.dart:42). Several readers interpolate the `FormatException` thrown by `jsonDecode` into the message. Dart's `FormatException.toString()` appends a window of the `source` string around the failing offset, so the log line carries whatever personal data sits near the corruption. Verified with a dart script: `jsonDecode` of a truncated history blob logged `...:"Angelica Holm","pickup":"Sveavägen 12, Stockholm","phone":"+46701234567"` under 'History JSON malformed:'. Affected in-scope sites: history (`prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:88`, rider names/addresses), ride-check log (`ride_check_log.dart:104`, includes the driver's 'What happened' free text and answers), and settings (`settings_repository.dart:84` builds `reason: '$storageKey: $error'` which `local_quarantine.dart:62` logs; settings sections hold trusted-contact phone numbers and vehicle drafts). The same pattern exists in `prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:81` (out of scope) via `DriverLog.error(..., error, stack)` which the sink prints verbatim.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A localStorage write is cut off mid-blob (web quota, process kill). On the next History open the console/crash log receives 'WARN History JSON malformed: FormatException: Unexpected end of input (at character N) ..."riderName":"Angelica Holm","pickup":"Sveavägen 12...' — rider PII in a log that is meant to be shippable to a crash reporter.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Log only `error.message` (and offset) for FormatException, never `$error`/`error.toString()`; in `DriverLog._debugSink` scrub `FormatException.source` before printing so no sink can leak stored blobs.

verdicts.reason: prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:88 logs '$error' for a jsonDecode FormatException. On the Dart VM (Android/iOS), FormatException.toString() includes the source text around the offset. DriverLog._debugSink (lib/core/logging/driver_log.dart) prints it through debugPrint, which also reaches the console and logcat in release builds. That breaks the class's own rule that log messages must not contain rider names or free text (driver_log.dart:5-6). The same pattern is at ride_check_log.dart:104 and settings_repository.dart:84, which feeds local_quarantine. It needs a corrupt stored blob to trigger, so it is an edge path. On web, dart2js builds the FormatException from the JS SyntaxError message, which may include less of the source.

It logged: 'History JSON malformed: FormatException: Unterminated string (at character 90) ...n":1,"rows":[{"riderName":"Angelica Holm","pickup":"Sveavagen 12","note":"x'. Result: All tests passed.

Nothing scrubs the text first. Limits: dart2js on web builds the FormatException without the source, and the default sink is only console or logcat, so for now this is a local-log privacy issue.

confirmed.title: Local history is capped at 500 rows (completed and cancelled), so for a driver with more than 500 rows in a month the Month view's total and ride count silently leave out the oldest trips
confirmed.description: Both `_decode` and `archive` keep only `rows.take(maxReceipts)` with maxReceipts = 500, counting completed and cancelled rows alike. Older rows are dropped from storage on the next archive. Ride history's 'Month' period sums `_periodRidesList`, filtered by calendar month from that truncated list, and labels it 'October 2026' with no hint that older trips were evicted. At the journey's 25 trips a day (plus cancels), 500 rows cover about 19 days, so from around the 20th of the month the month's 'Recorded fares' and ride count are too low, and the dropped receipts are gone for good.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver does 25 trips a day from 1 October. On 22 October, about 550 rows have been archived, so the 1-2 October trips are deleted from storage. History -> Month shows 'October 2026' earnings and ride count without them. The money shown for the month is wrong, and the old receipts cannot be recovered.
confirmed.evidence: prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:79 `static const maxReceipts = 500;` :150 `return _HistoryDecode(unique.take(maxReceipts).toList(), invalid: invalid);` :245 `'rows': rows.take(maxReceipts).toList(),`; ride_history.dart:108 `_HistoryPeriod.month => at.year == now.year && at.month == now.month,`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Evict by age (for example older than the period views need) rather than by count, or keep per-period aggregates. At minimum, mark a period total as partial when its oldest row may have been evicted.

verdicts.corrected_title: Local history is capped at 500 rows (completed and cancelled), so for a driver with more than 500 rows in a month the Month view's total and ride count silently leave out the oldest trips
verdicts.reason: prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:79 sets maxReceipts = 500. Both _decode (:150) and archive (:245) keep only the newest 500 rows sorted by completedAt, so older rows are dropped from storage on the next write. ride_history.dart:108 filters the Month period by calendar month from that truncated list and shows nothing to say it is partial. No document records the cap. LOCAL_DATA.md and the inventory say history is kept 'Until logout', which the cap contradicts. Low severity because this is local demo state (LOCAL_DATA.md: recoverable demo state, not a server) and it takes 500+ rows in one month to reach.
verdicts.repro: Traced _decode, archive and ride_history period filtering. Grepped docs for any record of the 500 cap and found none. No test was run.

verdicts.reason: The 500-row cap is a deliberate retention bound, not an accident. It is set at prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:79 and pinned by tests: test/audit/history_hardening_test.dart:10-12 expects exactly 500 with the newest kept, and test/core/next30_storage_regression_test.dart:147-157 does the same. docs/LOCAL_DATA.md says this store is 'recoverable demo state ... not a server' and that production storage moves to a server later. The local list was never meant to be the authoritative ledger of earnings. The failure needs 500 or more archived local trips inside one calendar month, about 25 trips a day for 20 days on one phone without a logout. In this frontend preview, trips come from demo or admin offers, so that state is not realistic. Eviction drops only the oldest rows, so the newest receipts and day and week totals stay correct. The worst that can be said is that the Month view has no 'partial' hint. That is a low-value polish item, not data loss on a reachable path.
verdicts.repro: Read _decode (line 150) and archive (line 245): both apply take(maxReceipts) after a newest-first sort. Found the existing tests that assert the cap as intended behaviour. Checked docs/LOCAL_DATA.md for the stated nature and retention of local history. Did not run a test: reaching the failure needs more than 500 archived trips in one month, and the existing tests already show that the cap works as designed.

verdicts.reason:
The 500-row cap is deliberate. prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:79 sets it, :150 (_decode) and :245 (archive) apply it after a newest-first sort, and two tests pin it (test/audit/history_hardening_test.dart and test/core/next30_storage_regression_test.dart R07). But those tests only fix the bound and which rows it keeps. Nothing covers or records what the cap does to the period views. ride_history.dart:100-108 filters the Month period by calendar month from the capped list. Then _periodEarnings (:124-131) and _periodRides (:145) total it under the label DriverDates.monthYear(now) (:120), as if the month were complete. No 'partial' flag exists, and the evicted receipts are deleted from storage for good on the next archive.

The reproducer's 'intended' argument covers the cap, not the wrong month total. The repo even shows how a cap is meant to be disclosed. lib/core/privacy/local_data.dart:70 states the ride-check cap as 'Newest ${PrefsRideCheckLog.maxRows} checks, until logout'. The history entry at :64 says only 'Until logout', so the history cap is undisclosed. DECISIONS.md, REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md and LOCAL_DATA.md say nothing about it either.

Severity is low, not medium. This is recoverable local demo state (LOCAL_DATA.md). It needs 500 or more archived rows, cancels included, in a single calendar month on one device without logging out. The newest receipts and the Today and Week totals stay correct until about 71 rows a day.
verdicts.repro: I wrote a throwaway test, test/_audit_u18_cap_test.dart, and deleted it afterwards. It seeded empty SharedPreferences, then called PrefsTripHistoryRepository().archive() 550 times with fare '100 kr' and completedAt = 2026-10-01 06:00 + 50 min * i, so every row falls in October. It then called list() and filtered for month == 10. Output: "archived=550 stored=500 october=500 oldestKept=2026-10-02 23:40:00.000 newest=2026-10-20 07:30:00.000 octSumMinor=5000000 hasT0=false". The test passed (00:48 +1: All tests passed!). So the Month view would show 500 rides and 50,000 kr for 'October 2026' instead of 550 rides and 55,000 kr, and the receipts t0-t49 from 1-2 October are gone from storage.

confirmed.title: Cash trips use two money models: History's cash balance treats the fare as the driver's money, while the waybill takes a 25 % Movera fee from the same fare
confirmed.description: The waybill sheet treats `fare` as what the rider pays: WaybillPayment takes a 25 % Movera fee and shows 'Your earnings' = fare − fee. History's cash balance treats the same `fare` as the driver's money: CashBalance.balance = fare − cashCollected. For a cash trip where the rider paid exactly the fare, History says 'Settled · cash matched your fare', but by the waybill the driver holds Movera's 25 % and owes it. The two screens give contradictory money for the same trip, and 'Other earnings' sums the History version.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Cash trip, fare 128,40 kr, the rider pays 128,40 kr in cash. The latest waybill shows Movera fee −32,10 kr, your earnings 96,30 kr. Ride history -> Other earnings shows +0,00 kr 'Settled' and does not show the 32,10 kr owed to Movera.
confirmed.evidence: waybill.dart:285 `static const double serviceFeeRate = 0.25;` :319 `int get _feeOre => (_riderOre * _feeRate).round();` :326 `String get earnings => _format(_fareOre - _feeOre);`; cash_balance.dart:86 `Money get balance => fare - cashCollected;`; trip_history.dart:172-174 `CashBalance? get cashBalance => paidByCash && status == TripStatus.completed ? CashBalance.fromLabels(fare: fare, cashCollected: cashCollected ?? fare) : null;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use one money model: either compute the cash balance from the driver's earnings (fare − fee) or drop the fee from the waybill for these trips. Until pricing comes from the backend, make both screens read the same definition.

verdicts.corrected_title: Cash trips use two money models: History's cash balance treats the fare as the driver's money, while the waybill takes a 25 % Movera fee from the same fare
verdicts.reason: WaybillPayment (waybill.dart:285, 319-326) treats `fare` as what the rider pays and takes serviceFeeRate 0.25 from it. TripHistoryRecord.cashBalance (trip_history.dart:63-64) builds CashBalance(fare, cashCollected ?? fare), and CashBalance.balance = fare - cashCollected (cash_balance.dart:32). Its comment calls `fare` 'the driver's fare'. _cashToCollect is widget.cashToCollect ?? widget.fare plus the waiting fee (accept_ride.dart:1007-1009). So a normal cash trip has balance 0 and History shows 'Settled'. By the waybill's model the driver holds Movera's 25 % fee in cash. The 25 % rate is a documented placeholder, but the two screens contradict each other for the same trip today, and the period total (ride_history.dart:141, cash_balance_sheet.dart:49) adds up the 'Settled' version. No document reconciles the two.

verdicts.corrected_title: Waybill takes a 25 % Movera fee from the fare, but History counts the full fare as earnings and as the cash-balance base, so a cash trip paid in full shows 'Settled'
verdicts.reason: The waybill sheet (waybill_sheet.dart:70) uses WaybillPayment (waybill.dart:285 serviceFeeRate 0.25, :319 fee, :326 earnings = fare - fee). History uses the same record.fare (completion_journal.dart:104 stores record.fare) as the driver's money. trip_history.dart:64 builds CashBalance(fare, cashCollected ?? fare), and cash_balance.dart:32 sets balance = fare - cash. ride_history.dart:125-130 adds up the full fares as period earnings. No document reconciles the two (DECISIONS.md, LOCAL_DATA.md and the gates say nothing about the fee or cash). The fee is a documented placeholder (waybill.dart:283-284), but the contradiction between the two screens is real. Severity is low because both figures are local placeholder pricing until the backend supplies amounts.
verdicts.repro: Worked by hand. Fare '128,40 kr' gives 12840 öre. Fee = round(12840*0.25) = 3210, so the waybill shows Movera fee 32,10 kr and earnings 96,30 kr. For the same trip with cashCollected = _cashToCollect = the fare (accept_ride.dart:1040, no promo and no wait), CashBalance.balance = 12840 - 12840 = 0, so it shows 'Settled'. Period earnings add 128,40 kr.

TripIslandController.release() refuses to show the default face while `_fault` is set, and `defaultFace` also returns false with a fault. A fault such as 'Location updating…' stays on screen for as long as GPS is unavailable (accept_ride_trip.dart:621-627 keeps `_locationStatus` set until a usable fix arrives). For that whole time, tapping the island does nothing and the driver cannot open the menu (support, history and the rest) for the rest of the trip.

trip_island_controller.dart:53 `bool get defaultFace => _defaultFace && !(_fault?.isNotEmpty ?? false);`
:123 `if (_fault?.isNotEmpty ?? false) return;`
accept_ride.dart:1120 `drawerEnableOpenDragGesture: false,`
accept_ride.dart:1305 `onMenu: () => _rideScaffoldKey.currentState?.openDrawer(),` (only via AdaptiveTripIsland -> TripIsland)

The only openDrawer call on the trip screen is that onMenu (accept_ride.dart:1305), and drawerEnableOpenDragGesture is false (:1120). TripTopReveal also has an onMenu, but nothing constructs it. The long-press tools sheet has no menu entry. A persistent 'Location updating…' fault is real: accept_ride_trip.dart:640-680 sets it on a stream error, a getCurrentPosition failure or a non-displayable fix, and clears it only on a usable fix. docs/driver-island-state-map.md gives faults the top display priority, but it never says the menu should become unreachable. The trip itself can still be completed from the sheet, so the impact is minor.
verdicts.repro: Traced every openDrawer call in lib (accept_ride.dart:1305 and home_map_sheet.dart only), the onMenu wiring through AdaptiveTripIsland, the fault guard in release(), and the writers of _locationStatus. Not run.

verdicts.reason: On the trip screen the drawer opens only through TripIsland's menu button. Swipe-open is turned off (accept_ride.dart:1153 `drawerEnableOpenDragGesture: false`), and onMenu (accept_ride.dart:1338) is shown only when `_controller.defaultFace` is true (adaptive_trip_island.dart, default-face branch near line 364). TripIslandController.release() returns early while a fault is set, and `defaultFace` is forced false (trip_island_controller.dart:53 and in release()). TripTopReveal is the other widget with a menu button, and nothing in lib uses it. When GPS keeps failing (a position error, or a fix that is not displayable), _locationStatus stays 'Location updating…' until a usable fix arrives (accept_ride_trip.dart:640-662, 680-686). For that whole time the side menu cannot be opened. The long-press tools sheet still gives route/options, safety and radar, but it has no menu (adaptive_trip_island.dart:1028-1060). The rule that a fault stays visible is intentional (docs/driver-island-state-map.md priority list, test S03), but no document says the menu should be blocked. The menu comes back once GPS recovers, so the effect is minor.
verdicts.repro: Ran the existing test/core/status_dispatch_followup_test.dart and all 6 tests passed. confirmed.title: The 'same fix reported again' guard compares the route by identity, so every route refresh/reroute resolves the same GPS fix twice and doubles the per-fix zoom, speed and bearing smoothing steps
confirmed.description: `update()` returns early only when `identical(location, _location) && identical(route, _route) && ...`. verdicts.reason: The guard at driver_camera_controller.dart:550-557 needs identical(route, _route). After _applyDriverPosition calls update (accept_ride_trip.dart:665), _refreshRoadRoute -> ensureRoute allocates a new RoadRoute whenever it fetches (navigation_controller.dart:404), and _followVehicle (accept_ride_trip.dart:728-731) calls update again with the same location. DriverCameraPolicy.resolve then re-runs speed smoothing, the cruise-zoom step and the 0.65 bearing damping (:320-323) for the same fix. This happens only on fetched refreshes and reroutes; an unchanged route stays identical and is caught by the guard.

verdicts.reason: The guard in update() (driver_camera_controller.dart:550-557) needs identical(route, _route). _applyDriverPosition (accept_ride_trip.dart:665) calls update(location, R0). confirmed.title: Native only: persistNow is silently dropped while another save is in flight (active_ride_controller.dart:276-278), so a stop arrival or departure, a secured next trip or a next-trip cancel stays unsaved until the next save. Not reachable on web/Safari.
confirmed.description: _write returns false at once when `_writing` is true. Several trip changes are persisted only through a single persistNow, and none of the callers check the result or retry: stop arrival (_onArrivedTap sets _paidStopWait, line 529), stop departure (_stopCursor += 1 and paid stop seconds folded in, line 862), a secured next trip (line 1206), and a next-trip cancel (accept_ride_sheet.dart:266). If a GPS snapshot save (every 2 minutes) or a lifecycle save is in flight at that moment, the change is not written until the next save. The documented Safari crash kills the tab with no pause event, so after a reload the trip restores from the older snapshot.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A driver leaves stop 1 at the moment a GPS snapshot save is in flight, and the tab crashes a minute later. Restore puts them back in 'waiting at stop 1' and adds the whole drive since the last save to the paid stop wait. A next trip the driver cancelled can likewise come back as secured, while history already records it as cancelled.
confirmed.evidence:
active_ride_controller.dart:276-278 `if (_disposed || _writing) { return false; }`
accept_ride_trip.dart:856-862 `_paidWaitSeconds += _paidWaitNow; _paidStopWait = false; _waitTimer?.cancel(); _stopCursor += 1; await _rideLifecycle.persistNow();` (result ignored)
accept_ride_sheet.dart:266 `unawaited(_rideLifecycle.persistNow());`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Give persistNow a 'dirty' flag: when a write is in flight, mark the state dirty and save again when that write finishes, instead of returning false.

verdicts.reason: active_ride_controller.dart:276-278 returns false at once when _writing is true. persistNow (310-320) runs with background:true, and the dirty/retry logic of D-09 (_afterBackgroundSave, 264-269) covers only driver commands, not persistNow. The in-flight save took its snapshot before the change. The stop-arrival (accept_ride_trip.dart:557), stop-departure (:874/890) and next-trip-cancel (accept_ride_sheet.dart:269) callers ignore the result, so the change stays unsaved until the next GPS snapshot (every 2 minutes or more, accept_ride_trip.dart:702) or a lifecycle save. The window is small, since local saves take milliseconds, and a crash is needed within the next save interval. Hence low severity.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_u32_test.dart (now deleted): ActiveRideController with a repository whose save waits on a Completer. A first persistNow is started, the snapshot state is changed, then a second persistNow is awaited. Output: 'second=false saved=[stop0]'. The second save was dropped and only the stale snapshot was written. '+1: All tests passed!'

verdicts.reason: The code mechanism is real: _write returns false while _writing (active_ride_controller.dart:276-278), and the in-flight save holds the snapshot built when it started. The failure needs a driver tap or timer callback to arrive while a background save is in flight, and the finding's scenario, the documented Safari tab crash (DECISIONS.md:79-88), is web-only. On web, PrefsActiveRideRepository.save (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:134-159) only awaits SharedPreferences.getInstance(), which is already completed, and shared_preferences_web setValue, which is `async { localStorage.setItem(...); return true; }`. The whole _write finishes in microtasks within the same event-loop task as the GPS callback that started it. Taps, Timers (next-trip secured, accept_ride_trip.dart:1238-1242) and the sheet cancel (accept_ride_sheet.dart:269) are separate macrotasks, so they cannot overlap an in-flight save on web. Each call sequence in one handler awaits the previous write, for example transitionTo then persistNow at accept_ride_trip.dart:575-584. Only on native, where the platform channel is truly async (a window of a few ms), could a collision happen. It would then also need the process to die without a pause/inactive lifecycle save (accept_ride.dart:757) before the next save, which is at most 2 minutes away. That is speculative.
verdicts.repro: Traced every persistNow caller with grep: accept_ride_trip.dart:521,563,584,710,881,897,1241; accept_ride.dart:658,757; accept_ride_sheet.dart:269. Read the repository save path and the shared_preferences_web setValue implementation in the pub cache, which completes synchronously inside an async function, so it holds no macrotask gap. No test was run, because the test SharedPreferences mock is also microtask-only and would not show the native timing.

verdicts.corrected_title: Native only: persistNow is silently dropped while another save is in flight (active_ride_controller.dart:276-278), so a stop arrival or departure, a secured next trip or a next-trip cancel stays unsaved until the next save. Not reachable on web/Safari.
verdicts.reason:
The bug is real, but only on native builds, and only in a narrow window.

**The mechanism.** `_write` returns false at once while `_writing` is true (active_ride_controller.dart:276-278). The D-09 wait in `_afterBackgroundSave` (lines 264-269) protects only `transitionTo`, `complete`, `cancel` and `noShow`, not `persistNow` (lines 310-320). Four callers make a state change and then persist it with a single `persistNow`, ignoring the result, with no retry and no error shown:
- stop arrival, accept_ride_trip.dart:557-563
- stop departure, accept_ride_trip.dart:891-897 (`_stopCursor += 1`)
- the secured-next-trip Timer, accept_ride_trip.dart:1238-1241
- the next-trip cancel, accept_ride_sheet.dart:269

**The reproducer is right about web.** shared_preferences_web 2.4.3 `setValue` is `async { localStorage.setItem(...); return true; }` with nothing awaited, and `PrefsActiveRideRepository.save` (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:134-159) awaits only prefs. So on web the whole write finishes inside the microtasks of the task that started it, and no tap or Timer can arrive during it. The finding's own scenario (a Safari tab crash, DECISIONS.md:79-88) is therefore unreachable.

**The tracer is right about native.** The app ships for Android: there is an android/ folder and docs/ANDROID_PERMISSIONS.md, and main.dart:93 creates `PrefsActiveRideRepository` on every platform. There, `setString` is a platform-channel round trip, so the write spans a real gap in the event loop. A tap or Timer in that gap is dropped, and the stored snapshot keeps the old state. Nothing is lost unless the process dies before the next save, and that save comes soon: the GPS snapshot at most 2 minutes later (accept_ride_trip.dart:706-710), the lifecycle save on inactive/paused (accept_ride.dart:750-757), or the next command. A native crash or a foreground kill can skip the lifecycle save.

So the defect is real on a shipped platform, but the trigger is a window of a few milliseconds every 2 minutes plus a crash. That is low severity.
verdicts.repro:
I wrote a throwaway test, test/_audit_u32_decide_test.dart (since deleted). It used the real `ActiveRideController` and the real `PrefsActiveRideRepository`, with a `snapshotBuilder` that writes `stopIndex` from a variable.

**Case 1, web-like store.** I used `SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues`, which only uses microtasks, the same as shared_preferences_web. I started the GPS save with `persistNow` without awaiting it, then awaited `Future.delayed(Duration.zero)` to stand in for a tap or Timer arriving as a new task. Then I set `stop = 1` and called `persistNow` again.

**Case 2, native-like store.** I used an `InMemorySharedPreferencesStore` subclass whose `setValue` first awaits a 5 ms delay, like a platform-channel round trip. I started the GPS save, and a 1 ms Timer set `stop = 1` and called `persistNow`.

Output:
```
WEB savingSync=true savingNextTask=false second=true stored=1
NATIVE first=true second=false stored=0 error=null
+2: All tests passed!
```
On web the in-flight window closes before the next task, so nothing is lost. On native the departure's save is dropped silently: no error, and the stored stop stays 0.

The run did not change any tracked file, and pubspec.lock and pubspec.yaml are unchanged.

The trip screen relies on persistNow to make non-stage progress durable. Examples: the stop wait starting (accept_ride_trip.dart:529), the stop wait ending with _stopCursor += 1 and _paidWaitSeconds (862), securing a next trip (1206), and cancelling the secured next trip (accept_ride_sheet.dart:269). A GPS snapshot (every 2 min, line 676) or a lifecycle save can be in flight at that moment. The newer state is then not written until the next 2-minute GPS save, no error SnackBar appears, and no retry runs. This is unlike driver commands, which wait for the background save (D-09).

After the first save completes, the stored snapshot still has stopIndex 0 ('F: second=false saved=[0] error=null'). If the tab or app dies within the next 2 minutes, the restore puts the driver back at the already-finished stop, or brings back a next trip the driver cancelled (already archived as cancelled), or loses a just-secured next trip.

accept_ride_trip.dart:858-862 `_paidWaitSeconds += _paidWaitNow; _paidStopWait = false; ... _stopCursor += 1; await _rideLifecycle.persistNow();`
accept_ride_trip.dart:1206 `_rideLifecycle.persistNow();`
confirmed.suggested_fix: When a background save is in flight, mark the snapshot dirty and re-run the save when it completes (coalesce), instead of returning false.

The D-09 helper _afterBackgroundSave (265-269) only covers driver commands. Callers that change state that is not a stage and then call persistNow are accept_ride_trip.dart:557 (stop wait starts), :874 (_stopCursor += 1, _paidWaitSeconds), :1234 (secured next trip) and accept_ride_sheet.dart:269 (cancelled next trip). None of them checks the bool. The fire-and-forget GPS snapshot (accept_ride_trip.dart:704) can be the save in flight at that moment. On mobile, PrefsActiveRideRepository.save is a platform-channel async write (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart _enqueue), so a tap can land inside that window. The in-flight write took its snapshot before the change, so the newer state is not written. Two things soften the impact. didChangeAppLifecycleState saves again on inactive/hidden/paused (accept_ride.dart:715-725), so a normal backgrounding re-saves. confirmed.title: Snapshot times are stored as local ISO strings with no offset, so on the autumn DST night a restore adds an extra hour of waiting (and the freshness check is off by 1 h)
confirmed.description: savedAt, arrivedAt, acceptedAt and startedAt are written with toIso8601String() on local DateTime values, which have no 'Z' or offset. They are parsed back with DateTime.tryParse as local time. During the repeated 02:00-03:00 hour in Europe/Stockholm, Dart resolves the ambiguous wall time to the first (CEST) instant. A snapshot saved in the second (CET) 02:xx therefore reads back one hour earlier than it was written. AcceptRide adds now - savedAt to the wait (accept_ride.dart:615), and isFreshAt uses the same difference.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Tested with the SDK's dart under TZ=Europe/Stockholm: a time saved at 2026-10-25 02:20 CET parses as 00:20Z instead of 01:20Z, and 10 real minutes later the computed age is 1:10:00. A driver waiting at a pickup whose app reloads in that hour gets 3 600 s of extra paid waiting, about 735 kr at 12,26 kr/min.
confirmed.evidence:
active_ride_repository.dart:251 `if (savedAt != null) 'savedAt': savedAt!.toIso8601String(),`
active_ride_repository.dart:387 `savedAt: DateTime.tryParse(json['savedAt'] as String? ?? ''),`
accept_ride.dart:615 `final elapsed = DateTime.now().difference(restored!.savedAt!).inSeconds;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store snapshot instants as UTC (toUtc().toIso8601String()), as the terminal markers already do.

On the autumn DST night in Europe/Stockholm, a time saved during the second 02:xx hour is read back as the first one, one hour too early. AcceptRide then adds DateTime.now() - savedAt to the pickup or stop wait (accept_ride.dart:613-617), so the wait gains an hour. isFreshAt (:195-201) is off by the same hour. Nothing normalises these times to UTC.

confirmed.title: Journal replay re-stamps the queued trip's savedAt to 'now', so an interrupted journal replayed days later restores the queued trip as fresh and skips the stale-trip prompt
confirmed.description: An interrupted CompletionJournal (app killed between writing the journal and finishing the handoff, or a storage failure) is replayed by Home on the next cold start (home.dart:508). handoff() writes next.stamped().toJson(), and stamped() sets savedAt = DateTime.now(). Neither handoff nor _replay compares the journal's completedAt with PersistedActiveRide.freshnessWindow. Home then reads a snapshot that is always isFresh and pushes AcceptRide.fromPersisted(B) directly, skipping the 'older than 6 hours' dialog that a normal snapshot of the same age would get.

active_ride_repository.dart:212 `savedAt: at ?? DateTime.now(),`
completion_journal.dart:226-227 `await (repository as RideHandoffRepository).handoff(id, next);` (completedAt never compared to the freshness window)

AcceptRide.fromPersisted after a reload or PWA resume therefore starts with no fired triggers, and checks the driver already answered on this trip can open again. The restore path also passes the restore time instead of the saved start (accept_ride_trip.dart:108 `startTrip(_rideCheckNow)`), although the detector's doc says 'Restored trips pass their saved start'.

accept_ride_trip.dart:107-108 `case ActiveRideStage.onTrip: _rideCheckDetector.startTrip(_rideCheckNow);`

confirmed.title: After a pause or an open card, a 20 s ride-check tick that lands before the first observe() uses the old stop clock and can fire a false long stop
confirmed.description: _stillSince is only refreshed by observe(). The trip screen stops calling observe while the app is paused (_pauseLiveUpdates) and while any card is open (_rideCheckWatching is false). After resume, the first fix sets _hasLiveLocation = true (accept_ride_trip.dart:661) but calls _rideCheckObserve only after `await _refreshRoadRoute(force: true)` (up to the 8 s routing timeout, line 683-686). A 20 s ticker tick in that window calls tick(gps: true), which computes `at - _stillSince` from the old timestamp and fires longStop. Nothing resets _stillSince when observation resumes.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver switches to another navigation app for 5 minutes while driving, then returns. On resume, the routing request takes a few seconds. A ride-check tick lands in that window and opens 'Your car has stopped for 5 min', even though the car has been moving the whole time. The longStop trigger is then used up for the rest of the trip.
confirmed.evidence:
ride_check_detector.dart:81-82 `if (!gps) return _longer(at); return _longStop(at, place) ?? _longer(at);`
ride_check_detector.dart:132-133 `final stopped = at.difference(since); if (stopped <= Duration(minutes: rules.longStopMinutes)) return null;`
accept_ride_trip.dart:661 `_hasLiveLocation = location.isUsableAt(DateTime.now());` ... 683 `await _refreshRoadRoute(force: forceRoute);` ... 686 `_rideCheckObserve();`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Reset the stop clock (_stillAt = null / _stillSince = now) whenever observation resumes after a pause or after a card closes, or call observe before the awaited route refresh.

verdicts.reason: _stillSince is only refreshed in observe() (ride_check_detector.dart:57-63) or by tick at a planned stop (:77-79). Nothing resets it when observation resumes. _pauseLiveUpdates (accept_ride_trip.dart:126-145) clears _hasLiveLocation, and _rideCheckTick returns early while paused (:1519). On resume the first fix sets _hasLiveLocation = true (:689) but reaches _rideCheckObserve (:714) only after `await _refreshRoadRoute(force: true)` (:708), which awaits a forced ensureRoute network request (navigation_controller.dart:302ff). The 20 s Timer.periodic ticker (accept_ride.dart:667) can fire inside that window and call tick(gps: true) -> _longStop with the pre-pause _stillSince (:129-138), and longStop then cannot fire again (_fired, :172). The same happens after a card closes, because observe is skipped while _rideCheck.active (:1482-1484). The window is narrow: the position stream is subscribed before routing (:633-645), and its next fix goes through ensureRoute's non-forced early return (_routeInFlight, navigation_controller.dart ~345) to observe. That resets _stillSince if the car has moved more than 30 m. So the window is about one GPS interval, unless GPS is sparse.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _startLiveLocation -> _applyDriverPosition -> _refreshRoadRoute -> ensureRoute, of _rideCheckTick and the ticker setup, and of every writer of _stillSince. The stream subscription is set up before routing (:636-641) at 1 s intervals (driver_location_service.dart:72). The next fix's ensureRoute(force:false) returns at once while _routeInFlight is set (navigation_controller.dart ~343-349), so its observe resets the clock about 1 s later because the car has moved past the still radius. Real window: about 1 s out of each 20 s tick, so roughly a 5% chance per resume after a pause longer than the admin long-stop time (default 2 min, ride_check_admin_config.dart:10). confirmed.title: Ride check reason is stored and sent to Movera in the driver's UI language, contrary to the 'record and alert keep English' rule

ride_check_detector.dart:163 `RideCheckReason(tr.rcLongerLead, tr.rcPercent(percent), tr.rcLongerTrail)`; :176-181 longStopReason uses tr.rcStoppedLead/tr.rcMinutes

confirmed.title: Ride-check recordings are written to the iOS Documents directory, which is included in iCloud/iTunes backups, contradicting the 'saved only on this phone' permission text
confirmed.description: `start()` saves audio under `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/ride_check_audio`. On iOS that is `NSDocumentDirectory`, which Apple backs up to iCloud/Finder by default unless the file is flagged `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` or stored under Application Support/Caches. `ios/Runner/Info.plist:9-10` tells the user 'The recording is saved only on this phone' and `safety_alert_repository.dart:36` repeats 'recordings stay on the phone'. Cabin audio of riders therefore leaves the device whenever the driver has iCloud backup on, which the stated promise and GDPR expectations do not cover.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver with iCloud Backup enabled records a Ride check conversation with a rider; the .m4a is uploaded to Apple's servers with the next device backup although the app told the driver it stays only on the phone.
confirmed.evidence: ride_check_recorder_native.dart:31-33 `final directory = Directory('${(await getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()).path}/ride_check_audio');` · ios/Runner/Info.plist:9-10 `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` … 'The recording is saved only on this phone.'
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store recordings under `getApplicationSupportDirectory()` and mark the folder excluded from backup (or set `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` on each file).

verdicts.reason: ride_check_recorder_native.dart:31-37 writes .m4a files to getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/ride_check_audio. On iOS that folder is included in iCloud/Finder backups by default. Nothing in ios/ or lib/ sets NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey (grep found nothing), yet Info.plist:9-10 and the UI ('saved only on this phone', app_en.arb:511/841; ride_check_card.dart:980 'The file never leaves it') say the file stays on the phone. The project clearly means local-only: Android sets allowBackup=false and excludes the whole file domain (AndroidManifest.xml:13-15, res/xml/backup_rules.xml). iOS has no equivalent, and an iOS release build is part of CI (drider-ci.yml:130-149). This does not affect the web/PWA build, where the recorder is a stub.
verdicts.repro: Static check of the recorder path, Info.plist, a grep for backup exclusion across ios/ and lib/, and a comparison with the Android backup rules.

verdicts.reason: ride_check_recorder_native.dart:31-37 writes `<Documents>/ride_check_audio/<id>.m4a`. On iOS this recorder is the one in use: ride_check_recorder.dart:3 picks it under dart.library.io, and `supported` is true when Platform.isIOS. Nothing sets NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey (grep of lib/ios finds none). iOS includes Documents in iCloud and Finder backups by default, so the recording leaves the device when the driver's backup is on. That contradicts Info.plist:9-10 ('The recording is saved only on this phone') and safety_alert_repository.dart:36. The effect is real but minor: it applies only to the iOS native build (on the web/PWA the recorder is the unsupported stub), and the copy goes into the driver's own encrypted device backup. The suggested fix is also partly wrong: Library/Application Support is backed up as well. Only setting the exclude-from-backup flag, or using Caches/tmp, keeps the file out.
verdicts.repro: Traced it statically: the conditional import (ride_check_recorder.dart:2-3) leads to NativeRideCheckRecorder.start (native.dart:30-38), which uses the path_provider Documents directory. A grep for excludedFromBackup/isExcludedFromBackup in lib and ios found nothing. Info.plist has no UIFileSharingEnabled. The backup behaviour follows Apple's documented iOS rule that Documents and Library (except Caches) are backed up. I could not run it on a device here.

confirmed.title: NativeRideCheckRecorder never disposes its AudioRecorder, so each trip leaks a native recorder; an empty capture's file is also left on disk
confirmed.description: `stop()` returns null for an empty capture but does not delete the file it just created in `ride_check_audio/` (line 48), so every failed/instant stop leaves an orphan `.m4a` under the app documents folder; nothing in the app ever lists or prunes that directory. Separately, `AudioRecorder` (record 7.1.1 exposes `Future<void> dispose()`, record.dart:173) is created per `RideCheckController` via `services.createRecorder()` (ride_check_controller.dart:234) and neither `NativeRideCheckRecorder` nor `RideCheckController.dispose()` releases it, so each trip in which the driver taps Record leaves a native recorder instance (method-channel/stream subscription) alive.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver taps Record then immediately Stop on several trips: each leaves an empty `ride-check-<trip>-<ms>.m4a` in Documents/ride_check_audio (grows forever) and one undisposed native recorder per trip for the life of the process.
confirmed.evidence: ride_check_recorder_native.dart:47-48 `final file = File(path);\n    if (!await file.exists() || await file.length() == 0) return null;` (no delete) · ride_check_recorder_native.dart:15-56 has no `dispose` · ride_check_controller.dart:406-423 `dispose()` never disposes `_recorder` · record-7.1.1/lib/src/record.dart:173 `Future<void> dispose()`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Delete the empty file before returning null; add `dispose()` to `RideCheckRecorder` that calls `AudioRecorder.dispose()` and invoke it from `RideCheckController.dispose()`.

verdicts.reason: lib/core/safety/ride_check_recorder_native.dart:20 lazily builds an AudioRecorder. Its constructor (record-7.1.1/lib/src/record.dart:32-33) registers a native recorder under a UUID, and only dispose() (record.dart:173) releases it. NativeRideCheckRecorder has no dispose, and the RideCheckController that owns it (ride_check_controller.dart:234, created per trip screen) does not release it in dispose() (ride_check_controller.dart:407-423), which only calls stop(). So each trip where the driver taps Record leaves one native recorder alive for the whole process. Also, stop() at ride_check_recorder_native.dart:48 returns null for a missing or zero-byte file without deleting it. Nothing else in lib/ touches ride_check_audio/, and clearLocalUserData (docs/LOCAL_DATA.md) only clears SharedPreferences, so empty .m4a files pile up. Keeping non-empty recordings on the phone is intended (comment at controller:413); the empty files and the never-disposed recorder are not.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: grepped lib/ and docs for ride_check_audio, AudioRecorder and dispose, and read the record 7.1.1 constructor and dispose(). No test was run because native audio is not available headless.

verdicts.corrected_title: NativeRideCheckRecorder never disposes its AudioRecorder, so each trip leaks a native recorder; an empty capture's file is also left on disk
verdicts.reason: The leak is real. RideCheckController creates one recorder per controller at ride_check_controller.dart:234 (`_recorder ??= services.createRecorder()`). Its dispose() at ride_check_controller.dart:407-422 only calls stop() if a recording is running and never releases the recorder. NativeRideCheckRecorder (ride_check_recorder_native.dart:15-56) has no dispose at all. The AudioRecorder constructor (record-7.1.1/lib/src/record.dart:32-40) calls `_platform.create(id)`. On Android that puts a RecorderWrapper, with its event channels, into the `recorders` map (record_android-2.2.0 MethodCallHandlerImpl.kt createRecorder). It only leaves the map through `disposeRecorder` (`recorders.remove`, MethodCallHandlerImpl.kt:98-100), which is reached only from AudioRecorder.dispose() (record.dart:173) or when the plugin detaches. So one native recorder stays alive per trip in which the driver taps Record (requestPermission alone is enough to create it). Second part: stop() at ride_check_recorder_native.dart:47-48 returns null for a zero-length file without deleting it. The plugin's own cleanup (Utils.deleteFile) runs only on cancel (delete=true), never on stop (RecorderController.kt:93). Nothing in lib lists or prunes ride_check_audio (grep finds only line 32), and LOCAL_DATA.md does not cover audio files. The effect is small and has no user-visible failure, so low.
verdicts.repro: I could not run this: it needs the native plugin on a device. I traced it instead: ride_check_controller.dart:234, :274-290 and :407-422; record.dart:32-40, :73-81 and :173-179; record_android MethodCallHandlerImpl.kt create/dispose and RecorderController.kt:93-98 (stop keeps the file, cancel deletes it). A grep for `dispose` and `ride_check_audio` across lib confirms no release path and no pruning. Whether a real device produces a 0-byte .m4a on an instant stop depends on the encoder/muxer. That part is plausible but not reproduced. The undisposed recorder is certain.

confirmed.title: French plurals written as =1{1 ...} render a literal '1 course' / '1 arrêt' for count 0 (gen-l10n maps =1 to the CLDR 'one' slot, which in fr covers 0)
confirmed.description: French grammar uses the singular for 0 and 1 (CLDR 'one' covers 0 and 1 for fr). The ARB strings tripsCount (713), stopsCount (714), riderBags (676), inDaysCount (861), schedRidesHidden (904) and ratingAndRides (1319) are written as `{count, plural, =1{...} other{...}}`, so count 0 selects the 'other' branch and the UI shows '0 courses', '0 arrêts', 'Le passager a 0 bagages', 'dans 0 jours', '0 courses masquées'. The gen-l10n plural rules would do the right thing if the `one` category were used instead of `=1`. The English and Swedish files are fine with =1/other.
confirmed.failure_scenario: French driver opens history with no rides or a reservation with zero stops; the counters read '0 courses' / '0 arrêts' instead of '0 course' / '0 arrêt'.
confirmed.evidence: lib/l10n/app_fr.arb:713 `"tripsCount": "{count, plural, =1{1 course} other{{count} courses}}"`; :714 stopsCount; :676 riderBags; :861 inDaysCount; :904 schedRidesHidden; :1319 ratingAndRides
confirmed.suggested_fix: In app_fr.arb use `one{...}` (CLDR category) instead of `=1{...}` for these keys, or add `=0{0 course}` branches.

verdicts.corrected_title: French plurals written as =1{1 ...} render a literal '1 course' / '1 arrêt' for count 0 (gen-l10n maps =1 to the CLDR 'one' slot, which in fr covers 0)
verdicts.reason: The diagnosis is wrong but the bug is real. gen-l10n compiles `=1{1 course}` to `Intl.pluralLogic(count, one: '1 course', other: ...)` (lib/l10n/app_localizations_fr.dart:2493-2499). The French CLDR rule puts 0 in ONE, so for count 0 the app shows the hard-coded text '1 course', not '0 courses'. Most call sites never pass 0: home.dart:1065 (totalTrips > 0), radar_offer_card.dart:106 (stops <= 0 gives ''), radar_offer_card.dart:236 (riderTrips > 0), document_expiry.dart:199-201 (<=0 and 1 are handled first), trip_island_controller.dart:318 (bags > 0), scheduled_rides.dart:100 (clashing.isNotEmpty). One site has no guard: accept_ride_panel.dart:985 `tr.ratingAndRides(..., widget.riderTrips)`. That value comes from home_offer_radar.dart:953 offer.riderTrips, which is `(json['riderTrips'] as num?)?.toInt() ?? 0` in api_dispatch_repository.dart:71. The contract makes riderTrips optional with minimum 0 (contracts/CONTRACT.md:60, openapi.yaml:5513). So a first-time rider, or an offer without the field, shows a French driver '4.9 ★ · 1 course', which is a wrong number. English and Swedish are fine because their 'one' covers only 1. Fix: use `one{{count} course}` in app_fr.arb instead of the literal '1'.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_frplural33_test.dart called AppLocalizationsFr().tripsCount, stopsCount, inDaysCount, schedRidesHidden and riderBags with 0, 1 and 2. Output: '0 -> 1 course | 1 arrêt | dans 1 jour | 1 course masquée | Le passager a 1 bagage', '1 -> (same)', '2 -> 2 courses | 2 arrêts | ...'. All tests passed; file deleted. I then traced every call site for count guards.

verdicts.corrected_title: French plurals written as =1{1 ...} make a count of 0 show '1 course' / '1 arrêt' (wrong number); the accept-ride panel can show it for a rider with 0 trips
verdicts.reason: gen-l10n turns `=1{...}` into the `one:` argument of Intl.pluralLogic (lib/l10n/app_localizations_fr.dart:2493-2512: `one: '1 course'`). In CLDR, French puts both 0 and 1 in the 'one' category, so count 0 picks the hard-coded literal '1 course'. The finding claims the result is '0 courses', but it is actually '1 course', which is worse because the number is wrong. Most callers guard against 0: home.dart:1065 (totalTrips > 0), radar_offer_card.dart:106 and :236, trip_island_controller.dart:318 (bags > 0), document_expiry.dart:199 (<=0 and 1 handled separately), and scheduled_rides.dart:100 (clashing.isNotEmpty). One caller has no guard: accept_ride_panel.dart:985 `tr.ratingAndRides(..., widget.riderTrips)`. riderTrips really can be 0: api_dispatch_repository.dart:71 sets `?? 0` when the field is missing, and dispatch_repository.dart:47 and home_offer_radar.dart:108 default to 0. Those values reach AcceptRide through ride_requests.dart:380 and home_offer_radar.dart:953. A brand-new rider shown to a French driver therefore reads '4.9 ★ · 1 course'.
verdicts.repro: Wrote a throwaway test, test/_audit_fr_plural_d33_test.dart, that calls AppLocalizationsFr directly. Output: `n=0 trips=1 course | 4.9 ★ · 1 course | stops=1 arrêt`, `n=1 trips=1 course | ...`, `n=2 trips=2 courses | ...`, then 'All tests passed!'. The test file was deleted afterwards. I traced callers with grep to check which ones guard against 0.

confirmed.title: A failed clearLocalUserData leaves the driver logged in with every long-lived storage repository invalidated (generation already bumped) and no recovery
confirmed.description: `clearLocalUserData()` calls `LocalWriteSession.beginCleanup()` (local_data.dart:114), which increments the generation before any key is removed; every repository instance created earlier (`_activeRide = PrefsActiveRideRepository()` in main.dart:93, the settings/vehicle stores held by open screens) now fails `LocalWriteSession.check` with 'Local session ended; reopen the screen before saving'. If a `prefs.remove` returns false the function throws (local_data.dart:135-137/148-150), `_logout` rethrows before reaching `_activeRide = PrefsActiveRideRepository()` (main.dart:187) and `_session.reset()`, and Profile just shows 'could not clear' and keeps the driver signed in (profile.dart:397-406). From then on active-ride snapshots and terminal markers can no longer be written (every enqueued op logs 'Active-ride storage operation failed'), so crash recovery of a trip silently stops working, and local data is half-cleared, until the process restarts.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On a device where SharedPreferences commit fails for one key (full disk, broken prefs file), the driver taps Log out, sees 'Could not clear local data', continues driving; the next accepted trip is not persisted, so a crash mid-trip comes back to an empty Home.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Recreate the composition-root repositories (and reset the session) in a `finally`, or bump the generation only after the removals succeeded / roll it back on failure.

verdicts.reason: lib/core/storage/local_write_session.dart:13-17: beginCleanup() increments _generation before any key is removed, and endCleanup() (local_data.dart:152-153) only clears _clearing. It never restores the generation. When prefs.remove returns false (local_data.dart:135-137/148-150), clearLocalUserData throws, so main.dart:184 rethrows before the line `_activeRide = PrefsActiveRideRepository()` (main.dart:187) and before `_session.reset()`. Profile catches the error, shows profCouldNotClear and keeps the driver on Profile, logged in (profile.dart:397-406). Every repository created earlier, such as the composition-root PrefsActiveRideRepository (main.dart:93, which DriverHome receives at main.dart:202), now fails LocalWriteSession.check (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:34, 72, 136 ...). _enqueue logs those failures (lines 52-57), so active-ride snapshots silently stop being saved. The precondition can happen: shared_preferences_android 2.4.11 LegacySharedPreferencesPlugin.java:103 returns `preferences.edit().remove(key).commit()`, which is false when the disk write fails. It is rare, so the severity is low. A later logout retry that succeeds does rebuild the repository.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_d34_test.dart: created a PrefsActiveRideRepository, called clearLocalUserData(load: a SharedPreferences fake whose remove returns false), then called repo.clear(). Output: 'repo.clear after failed logout: Bad state: Local session ended; reopen the screen before saving', then '+1: All tests passed!'. The file was deleted afterwards.

verdicts.reason: lib/core/storage/local_write_session.dart:13-17 beginCleanup() increments _generation before any key is removed. If a remove fails, lib/core/privacy/local_data.dart:135-137 and 148-150 throw, and the finally block (line 152-153) only resets _clearing; it never rolls the generation back. lib/main.dart:184 then rethrows before line 187 (`_activeRide = PrefsActiveRideRepository()`) and before _session.reset(). profile.dart:397-406 catches the error, shows profCouldNotClear and returns with the driver still signed in, and the existing DriverHome keeps the stale repository from main.dart:93/205. PrefsActiveRideRepository stores _generation at construction (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:34), and every read, save or clear calls LocalWriteSession.check(_generation), so they now throw. The trigger is real but rare: on Android, shared_preferences_android 2.4.11 LegacySharedPreferencesPlugin.java:103 is `preferences.edit().remove(key).commit()`, which returns false when the disk write fails. The existing test 006 expects this failure but only checks a retry, not instances made before it. A successful retry recreates the repository, so the effect lasts until the driver retries logout or restarts the app.
verdicts.repro: Wrote test/_audit_d34_test.dart: built PrefsActiveRideRepository() and read once, swapped SharedPreferencesStorePlatform.instance for a store whose remove returns false, and expected clearLocalUserData() to throw StateError, which it did. Then the same instance's clear() printed 'clear after failed cleanup: Bad state: Local session ended; reopen the screen before saving' (its read failed the same way). confirmed.title: Disposing AcceptRide while a Ride check is open makes Home call setState during finalizeTree: a debug-only 'widget tree was locked' error, and in debug the held radar offers are not released
confirmed.description: `_AcceptRideState.dispose` calls `_rideCheck.dispose()` (679). `RideCheckController.dispose` calls `_syncGate(false)` (ride_check_controller.dart 409), which, when the gate was held (a Ride check pill/card was open), sets `RideCheckGate.set(false)` → `ValueNotifier` notifies synchronously. Home is still mounted underneath and its listener `_rideCheckGateListener` → `_onRideCheckGate` (home_offer_radar.dart 473-478) runs `_rebuild(() {})`, i.e. `setState` (home.dart 338), from inside another State's `dispose`. State.dispose runs in `BuildOwner.finalizeTree` under `lockState`, where `markNeedsBuild` asserts "setState() or markNeedsBuild() called when widget tree was locked". In debug/profile builds the FlutterError is thrown out of `_rideCheck.dispose()`, so the remainder of `AcceptRide.dispose` (camera, realtime subscription/unsubscribe, timers, animation controllers at 680-700+) never runs, leaking the realtime subscription, the 20 s ride-check ticker already cancelled but `_waitTimer`, `_nextTrip*` timers and the two AnimationControllers (which then also report "disposed with an active Ticker"). Release builds only mark Home dirty and rebuild.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A Ride check card is open (long stop / off-route) when the rider cancels (or admin releases the trip); the trip screen pops. In a debug or profile build the framework reports "setState() or markNeedsBuild() called when widget tree was locked" during finalizeTree and AcceptRide's dispose is cut short, leaving its realtime subscription and timers alive.
confirmed.evidence:
accept_ride.dart 675-679: `void dispose() { RideCheckGate.listenable.removeListener(_onRideCheckGateListener); ... _rideCheck.dispose();`
ride_check_controller.dart 407-409: `void dispose() { _disposed = true; _syncGate(false);` and 400-404: `if (open == _holdsGate) return; _holdsGate = open; RideCheckGate.set(open);`
home_offer_radar.dart 473-475: `void _onRideCheckGate() { if (!mounted || RideCheckGate.open) { return; } _rebuild(() {});`
home.dart 338: `void _rebuild(VoidCallback update) => setState(update);`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Close the gate before the route is popped (e.g. in `_pauseLiveUpdates`/the exit paths) or defer the Home reaction with `WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback`/`scheduleMicrotask` in `_onRideCheckGate`; alternatively have `RideCheckController.dispose` schedule `RideCheckGate.set(false)` asynchronously.

verdicts.corrected_title: Disposing AcceptRide while a Ride check is open makes Home call setState during finalizeTree: a debug-only 'widget tree was locked' error, and in debug the held radar offers are not released
verdicts.reason: The mechanism is real. RideCheckController.dispose calls _syncGate(false), which calls RideCheckGate.set(false) (ride_check_controller.dart:400-409). Home is still mounted underneath (pushSingle, home_offer_radar.dart:940; home.dart:567). Its listener _onRideCheckGate then calls _rebuild(() {}), which is setState (home_offer_radar.dart:473-478), while finalizeTree holds lockState (flutter framework.dart:3357). Element.markNeedsBuild then throws 'called when widget tree was locked' (framework.dart:5387). A real path exists: _leaveAfterAuthoritativeOutcome and _leaveAfterRelease pop the route (accept_ride_trip.dart:371-410), and _pauseLiveUpdates does not close the Ride check. The claimed leak is wrong, though. ValueNotifier.notifyListeners catches the listener's exception and reports it, so the rest of AcceptRide.dispose still runs and nothing leaks. In debug the throw skips _releasePendingRadarOffers() and _maybeShowSoonReservation() for that gate change. Release builds have no assert and behave correctly.
verdicts.repro: Wrote a throwaway test, test/_audit_d36_test.dart (deleted afterwards), using the real RideCheckGate and RideCheckController: a Home whose RideCheckGate listener calls setState, a pushed route that opens a long-stop check (instant) and disposes the controller in dispose(), then pop. Result: takeException() returned 'setState() or markNeedsBuild() called when widget tree was locked. This Home widget cannot be marked as needing to build because the framework is locked.', and the code after c.dispose() still ran (trailingRan=true, gate=false). The test passed.

verdicts.corrected_title: Disposing the trip screen while a Ride check is open makes Home call setState in a locked tree: debug builds report a FlutterError and skip releasing held offers (dispose itself is not cut short)
verdicts.reason: The chain is real. AcceptRide.dispose (accept_ride.dart:679) calls RideCheckController.dispose, which calls _syncGate(false) (ride_check_controller.dart:409). That runs RideCheckGate.set(false), so the ValueNotifier fires Home's listener synchronously (home.dart:261 -> home_offer_radar.dart:473-475), and its _rebuild calls setState while finalizeTree holds the lock. Home is still mounted under the trip route (it pushes AcceptRide with pushSingle, home_offer_radar.dart:941), and the exit paths (accept_ride_trip.dart:389/406/457/1445) pop without closing the Ride check. The claimed leak is wrong, though. ChangeNotifier.notifyListeners catches errors thrown by listeners and reports them, so nothing propagates out of _rideCheck.dispose() and the rest of AcceptRide.dispose still runs. What actually goes wrong: (a) in debug builds the framework reports 'setState() or markNeedsBuild() called when widget tree was locked'; (b) the listener throws at _rebuild, before _releasePendingRadarOffers() and _maybeShowSoonReservation() (home_offer_radar.dart:476-477), so in debug, offers held back during the check are not released at that moment. The lock assert exists only in debug builds, so profile and release builds are unaffected.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_d36gate_test.dart (deleted). A Home stand-in had the same listener body as home_offer_radar.dart:473-475. It pushed a route whose State owns a real RideCheckController, opened it (instant), then popped the route. Output: 'EXCEPTION: setState() or markNeedsBuild() called when widget tree was locked. This FakeHome widget cannot be marked as needing to build because the framework is locked.' and 'afterRideCheckDispose=true gateOpen=false'. The second line shows the code after _rideCheck.dispose() did run, so there is no leak.

confirmed.title: Trip camera approach loop and 33 ms car-marker ticker keep updating the hidden trip map while another route covers AcceptRide
confirmed.description: AcceptRide pauses live updates only on app lifecycle changes (didChangeAppLifecycleState -> `_pauseLiveUpdates` -> `_camera.suspend()`). Unlike Home (didPushNext -> `_pauseHomeUpdates`), it is not RouteAware. When the driver opens a full-screen route from the trip, for example `onHistory: () => pushSingle(context, MaterialPageRoute(builder: (_) => const DriverRideHistory()))` (accept_ride.dart:1307), the chat, destination picker or safety screens, GPS keeps arriving and `_camera.update` keeps retargeting. GoogleDriverCameraPort's loop paces itself with `Timer`-based `_sleep(16 ms)`, not vsync, so it keeps calling `controller.moveCamera` about 60 times a second on the hidden map. Each frame's `onFrame` snaps the vehicle pose, so the 33 ms `_ThrottledVehicleMap` timer keeps pushing marker updates. On web each of those pushes also leaks a Blob URL (see the first finding).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Mid-trip, the driver opens Ride history from the island and reads it for 2 minutes while driving. The invisible trip map gets about 7,200 camera moves and about 3,600 marker pushes, which wastes CPU and battery on native and grows memory on web. Worked out from the code; not run.
confirmed.evidence:
accept_ride.dart:715-724 only lifecycle states call `_rideLifecycle.persistNow(); _AcceptRideTrip(this)._pauseLiveUpdates();`
google_driver_camera_port.dart:328-329 `await _sleep(Duration(milliseconds: settled ? 50 : 16));` (Timer-based, lines 557-563)
accept_ride.dart:1257-1260 `onFrame: (position) { ... _vehicle.snapTo(position.target, _camera.vehicleCourse); }`
home.dart:174 `void didPushNext() { _routeVisible = false; _pauseHomeUpdates(); }` (Home has the guard, AcceptRide does not)
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make AcceptRide RouteAware (or check TickerMode/ModalRoute.isCurrent). On didPushNext suspend the camera and stop the 33 ms ticker, keeping GPS and the trip logic running. On didPopNext resume and recenter.

verdicts.corrected_title: Trip camera approach loop and 33 ms car-marker ticker keep updating the hidden trip map while another route covers AcceptRide
verdicts.reason: AcceptRide pauses only on app lifecycle changes (accept_ride.dart:715-727, which calls _pauseLiveUpdates and then _camera.suspend at accept_ride_trip.dart:126-127). It has no RouteAware/didPushNext hook, unlike Home. Routes pushed over the trip, such as onHistory pushSingle(DriverRideHistory) at accept_ride.dart:1307, leave GPS, the camera and the ticker running. Two details in the finding are overstated. The camera loop in google_driver_camera_port.dart:276-335 is not a constant 60 Hz: it runs 16 ms steps only until the pose settles, then breaks. And the _ThrottledVehicleMap ticker (accept_ride.dart:1458-1467) pushes a marker only when the pose changed. While driving, GPS updates keep both busy on an invisible map. That wastes CPU and battery but breaks nothing functionally.

confirmed.title: A radar the driver held off comes back on after a crash or reload restore
confirmed.description: Holding the trip radar sets `_OnTripRadarState.stopped`, but the persisted snapshot (`_buildSnapshot`) does not save the radar state. On restore the state starts as `off`, and `_resumeStageSideEffects` calls `_startOnTripRadar`, whose only guard is `stopped`. The radar therefore scans again, and the driver gets Exclusive next-trip offers they turned off; letting them run out counts as misses.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On the last leg the driver holds the radar to stop next-trip offers. Safari reloads the PWA and the trip is restored. A few seconds later an Exclusive next-trip offer pops up, and ignoring it counts toward the auto-offline limit.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Persist whether next-trip offers were stopped in PersistedActiveRide and restore `stopped` from it.

verdicts.reason: _buildSnapshot (accept_ride_trip.dart:18-60) saves only a *secured* next offer; neither the `stopped` radar state nor `_onTripRadarDeclined` is saved in PersistedActiveRide. When the trip is restored, `_onTripRadarState` starts as `off` (accept_ride.dart:536). `_restoreQueuedNextFromSnapshot` changes that only when there is a secured next trip (accept_ride_trip.dart:92-95). Then `_resumeStageSideEffects` (accept_ride_trip.dart:118-120, called from accept_ride.dart:625) calls `_startOnTripRadar`, whose only guard is `stopped` (accept_ride_trip.dart:1024). That sets the radar to `scanning`, and `_maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer` sets a 2.2 s timer that brings up an offer (1100-1145). If the offer runs out, `_denyNextTripRadar` calls `ExclusiveAnswers.instance.missed()`, which can take the driver offline (1252-1258). No document says this is intended.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: restore path in initState (accept_ride.dart:603-625), then _resumeStageSideEffects, _startOnTripRadar, the demo offer timer, _armOnTripOfferExpiry and _denyNextTripRadar. Checked every write of _onTripRadarState with grep. No test run.

verdicts.reason: `_stopOnTripRadar` (accept_ride_trip.dart:1089) sets `_OnTripRadarState.stopped`, but `_buildSnapshot` (lines 18-60) persists only a secured next offer. On restore the state starts as `off` (accept_ride.dart), and initState calls `_resumeStageSideEffects` after the first frame (accept_ride.dart:653). At the onTrip stage that calls `_startOnTripRadar` (line 121), whose only guard is `stopped` (line 1024), so scanning starts again. By default `exclusiveWhileDriving` is true and the count is 1 (offer_rules.dart:16-17), so `_maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer` presents an offer after 2.2 s. If it runs out, `_armOnTripOfferExpiry` calls `_denyNextTripRadar`, which counts `ExclusiveAnswers.instance.missed()` (line 1261).
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand: restore path accept_ride.dart:631-653, then `_resumeStageSideEffects` (accept_ride_trip.dart:112-124), then `_startOnTripRadar`, the demo offer timer, the expiry timer and `missed()`. There is no persisted field for the stopped state in PersistedActiveRide (`_buildSnapshot`). I did not run a test.

confirmed.title: The trip-save error SnackBar fires again on later state changes, and its Retry does not retry the failed slide
confirmed.description: `_onPersistenceChanged` is an `ActiveRideController` listener that shows 'Trip progress could not be saved' whenever `persistenceError != null`. `persistenceError` is cleared only at the start of a new `_write`. `_end(clearSnapshot: false)` (active_ride_controller.dart:228-231), which completion, cancel and no-show use, notifies listeners without writing. So an old background-save failure re-shows the error SnackBar while the trip is being finished successfully, and the SnackBar is carried to the next route on the root messenger. Separately, when `transitionTo` (Arrive or Start trip) fails its save, the SnackBar's Retry calls `persistNow()`. That re-saves the current stage, not the stage change. It succeeds silently and leaves the trip where it was, so Retry looks like it did something when it did not.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A 2-minute GPS snapshot save fails once (web storage quota), and the error SnackBar shows. Later the driver finishes the trip and the journal saves fine, but the Ride completed screen shows 'Trip progress could not be saved · Retry'. Or: the 'Start trip' slide's save fails, the driver taps Retry, nothing visible happens, and the trip is still 'Waiting'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Show the SnackBar only on the notify that ends a failed write (track the write revision), clear `persistenceError` in `_end`, and make Retry repeat the failed command rather than calling `persistNow`.

verdicts.reason: _onPersistenceChanged (accept_ride_trip.dart:511-517) shows the SnackBar on every notify while `persistenceError != null`. The error is cleared only at the start of `_write` (active_ride_controller.dart:283). `_end(clearSnapshot:false)` notifies without writing (228-231), and completion, cancel and no-show use it (accept_ride_trip.dart:948, 1412). So if the last background save failed and no later save succeeded, finishing the trip re-shows 'Trip progress could not be saved'. Retry calls `persistNow()`, which saves the current `_stage` (active_ride_controller.dart:309-319), not a failed `transitionTo`. After a failed Arrive/Start slide, Retry therefore succeeds silently and the stage does not change. The harm is limited: the slide is reset (`_stageTransitioning=false`, 570-573, 861-863), so the driver can slide again, and the stale re-show needs a failed save with no successful write before the finish.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of ActiveRideController._write/_end/persistNow (active_ride_controller.dart:221-320), the listener registration (accept_ride.dart:600), the completion path (accept_ride_trip.dart:935-950) and the slide failure paths (561-578, 855-865). No test run.

verdicts.reason: `persistenceError` is reset only at the start of `_write` (active_ride_controller.dart:~284). `_end(clearSnapshot:false)` (lines 228-231) notifies listeners without writing, so `_onPersistenceChanged` (accept_ride_trip.dart:511) shows 'Trip progress could not be saved' again when a trip finishes successfully. Completion (line 955), cancel and no-show (line 1419) all use clearSnapshot:false. After the trip is terminal, Retry's `persistNow` returns true without writing and the error stays set. When `transitionTo` fails, Retry calls `persistNow`, which saves the current stage and does not repeat the stage change (accept_ride_trip.dart:576-579 and 868-871 only reset `_stageTransitioning`).

Output: `persistNow=false`, then `complete=true notifiesWithError=[Bad state: quota]`, then `retry persistNow=true err=Bad state: quota`. For a failed transition: `transition=false`, then `retry=true stage=ActiveRideStage.headingToPickup saved=ActiveRideStage.headingToPickup`. Ran on the HEAD snapshot copy; the file was deleted afterwards.

confirmed.title: After 'I've arrived', the pickup route line stays on the map during the wait until the car moves at least 0.4 m (or a GPS snapshot persist fires), because the route-cleared notification is dropped while _stageTransitioning is set
confirmed.description: `_confirmPickupArrival` sets `_stageTransitioning = true` (541) and awaits `transitionTo(waitingForRider)`; the controller's commit notifies `_syncNavigationStage` → `NavigationController.setStage` which clears `_route` and notifies (navigation_controller.dart:163-188). `_onNavigationChanged` returns at once because `_stageTransitioning` is still true (562), so `_roadGeoPoints`/`_routeDurationSeconds` keep the pickup route; the following `_rebuild(() {})` (558) calls `_syncRouteLines()` which redraws that stale route. During waiting `ensureRoute` returns early and `setVehicle` does not notify while the car is parked (moved < 0.4 m, navigation_controller.dart:242-246), so nothing clears it until the car moves. `_routeEtaText` likewise keeps the old duration (`routeFraction` is null → full duration) while waiting.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver taps 'I've arrived' at the pickup. The waiting stage starts but the black route line to the pickup (and the old ETA value) remain on the map for the whole wait.
confirmed.evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:561-562 `void _onNavigationChanged() {\n      if (!mounted || _stageTransitioning) { return; }` ; 547-559 `_waitSeconds = 0; ... if (mounted) { _rebuild(() {}); }\n      _unlockStageAfterFrame();` ; navigation_controller.dart:168 `_route = null;` inside setStage
confirmed.suggested_fix: Do not skip `_onNavigationChanged` during a stage transition (or re-run it in `_unlockStageAfterFrame`), and clear `_roadGeoPoints`/`_routeDurationSeconds` explicitly when entering waiting.

verdicts.reason: _confirmPickupArrival sets _stageTransitioning=true (accept_ride_trip.dart:541). The navigation controller clears the route and notifies on every lifecycle notify: setStage -> _rebuildBanner -> notifyListeners (navigation_controller.dart:163-188, 448-468). Every one of those notifications arrives while the flag is still true: the transition commit, then both notifies of persistNow at :550. _onNavigationChanged drops them (:562). The flag is only cleared in a post-frame callback (:980-983), and nothing replays the cleared route afterwards. TripRouteLines draws whatever _roadGeoPoints holds, whatever the stage (trip_route_lines.dart:23-56; accept_ride.dart:1545). So the pickup route stays on the map until something makes the navigation controller notify again. That is either a fix that moves at least 0.4 m or turns at least 1 degree (navigation_controller.dart:242-246), or the GPS-driven snapshot persist that runs at most every 2 minutes (accept_ride_trip.dart:672-676). With a parked car, or with no GPS callbacks at all, the route stays drawn. The ETA part is overstated: the island receives _routeEtaText, but while waiting it shows the wait clock, and _legFraction returns null when _countingWait (accept_ride.dart:900).
verdicts.repro: I wrote and ran a throwaway widget test, test/_audit_d42route_test.dart (deleted afterwards). Setup: simulatedArrival and externalRouting on, a stub route repository, a fix 50 m from pickup, then a tap on active-ride-arrived-button after expanding the panel. Output: 'before arrive lines=2', 'after arrive lines=2', 'after 10 identical fixes lines=2', 'after 2m jitter fix lines=0', then 'All tests passed!'. The stale polylines survive arrival and identical fixes, and clear only once a fix moves.
