confirmed.title: After a timer-driven reroute, the new route is drawn split at the old route's progress until the next GPS fix (usually about a second)
confirmed.description: _onNavigationChanged puts the new route into _roadGeoPoints and _rebuild calls _syncRouteLines(_roadGeoPoints, _camera.alongMeters, ...). _camera.alongMeters is DriverCameraPolicy._along, which still refers to the old route: it resets only in the next camera.update, which needs a new usable fix. The reroute timer and 'Retry route' deliver routes outside any fix. Their new polyline (starting at the car) is drawn with its first N metres (N = old route progress) faded as already driven, and the remaining line starts far ahead of the car. This lasts until a fix arrives, which can be a long time when GPS is silent.
confirmed.failure_scenario: 4 km into the leg the driver leaves the route and the reroute arrives from the timer. The first 4 km of the new route draw grey 'travelled' and the blue route starts 4 km ahead of the car until the next fix, which never comes while GPS is silent. Verified by reading the code; not run.
confirmed.evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:572-580 `_rebuild(() { if (pointsChanged && mappedRoute != null) { _roadGeoPoints = mappedRoute.points; ...` ; accept_ride.dart:499 `void _rebuild(VoidCallback update) { setState(update); _AcceptRideTrip(this)._syncRouteLines(); }` ; accept_ride_trip.dart:637-638 `_routeLines.sync(_roadGeoPoints, _camera.alongMeters, _routeZoomStep);` ; driver_camera_controller.dart:87 `double get alongMeters => _along ?? 0;` (reset only inside resolve at 221-222)
confirmed.suggested_fix: Reset the split to 0 when the polyline identity changes (or have the camera policy take the new route at once), and sync the lines after _followVehicle.

verdicts.corrected_title: After a timer-driven reroute, the new route is drawn split at the old route's progress until the next GPS fix (usually about a second)
verdicts.reason: _onNavigationChanged (accept_ride_trip.dart:589-607) stores the new route and calls _rebuild, which calls _syncRouteLines -> _routeLines.sync(_roadGeoPoints, _camera.alongMeters, ...) (line 666). DriverCameraPolicy._along resets only inside resolve() when the polyline changes (driver_camera_controller.dart:221-222), and resolve runs only from _camera.update on a fix. The reroute arrives from _rerouteDebounce (navigation_controller.dart:641), not from a fix, so for that frame the first N metres of the new route (N = old progress) are drawn as already driven. The 'Retry route' case does not happen: after a failed route, the next fix calls camera.update with route null, which clears _along. The finding also overstates how long it lasts. A reroute is scheduled from an off-route fix, so GPS is live, and watchPosition(distanceFilterMeters: 0) (line 629) delivers the next fix, which resets the split. The glitch is real but short.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: _onNavigationChanged -> _rebuild (accept_ride.dart:499) -> _syncRouteLines (accept_ride_trip.dart:665-666) -> DriverCameraController.alongMeters (driver_camera_controller.dart:426) -> policy _along, reset only at :221-222 inside resolve. Checked that the retry path clears _along through camera.update(route: null). No test run.

verdicts.corrected_title: After a reroute, the new route is drawn split at the old route's progress until the next GPS fix (normally about a second)
verdicts.reason: _onNavigationChanged sets _roadGeoPoints to the new route, and _rebuild (accept_ride.dart:499) calls _syncRouteLines, which passes _camera.alongMeters (driver_camera_controller.dart:87, `_along ?? 0`). _along is reset only inside DriverCameraPolicy.resolve when the polyline changes (driver_camera_controller.dart:221-222). resolve runs only from _camera.update, which is called from a fix (accept_ride_trip.dart:693) or from _followVehicle. The reroute debounce timer (navigation_controller.dart:641-656) calls ensureRoute outside any fix, so nothing calls the camera when its route arrives. TripRouteLines.sync then draws traveled(oldAlong) and remaining(oldAlong) on the new polyline (trip_route_lines.dart:41-53). This does not apply to the retry path: a failed route sets _route to null, and the following _followVehicle resets _along to 0. The 90 s silent refresh is not affected either, because _applyDriverPosition calls _followVehicle right after it. The bad split lasts only until the next fix. The stream runs with distanceFilterMeters: 0, so that is normally about a second; it only stays longer if GPS goes silent right after the reroute.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand: the reroute timer, then ensureRoute, then the notifyListeners in _onNavigationChanged, then _rebuild, then _syncRouteLines with the unchanged _camera._along. I checked every caller of _camera.update (accept_ride_trip.dart:693 and 759) and DriverCameraController._request (it uses the controller's own stored _route, which only update sets). Not run.

confirmed.title: DECISIONS.md's '20 m web GPS filter' is not applied: the active ride passes distanceFilter 0 on web, so every browser fix is processed (the per-fix rebuild cost is already handled by D-07)
confirmed.description: DECISIONS.md ('Active ride crash recovery (Safari / PWA)', line 85) states the Safari tab-kill fix included 'web GPS filter is 20m'. The active ride subscribes with `watchPosition(distanceFilterMeters: 0)` and DriverLocationService._streamSettings builds `LocationSettings(accuracy: high, distanceFilter: distanceFilterMeters)` for web, so on web every browser geolocation callback (typically ~1 Hz, more on some devices) reaches _applyDriverPosition. There is no kIsWeb branch anywhere in accept_ride*.dart (grep shows none) and no constant 20 in the location code. The documented decision and the shipped behaviour differ; the task rules treat that as a defect to report.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Safari PWA on an active trip: each raw geolocation fix (no distance gating) drives _applyDriverPosition, route-refresh checks and island updates, the very load pattern the recorded decision says was limited by a 20 m filter.
confirmed.evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md:85 `GPS setState is gone; web GPS filter is 20m.`; accept_ride_trip.dart:604-606 `_positionSubscription = _locationService.watchPosition(distanceFilterMeters: 0)`; driver_location_service.dart:58-67 `if (kIsWeb || !navigation) { return LocationSettings(accuracy: kIsWeb ? LocationAccuracy.high : LocationAccuracy.bestForNavigation, distanceFilter: distanceFilterMeters); }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Either pass `distanceFilterMeters: kIsWeb ? 20 : 0` from the active ride (or apply the web filter inside DriverLocationService) or correct DECISIONS.md so the record matches the code.

What remains is per-fix map and route-line work on web at the raw geolocation rate.

confirmed.title: The GPS-lost status keeps the old language after a switch, and the 'GPS restored' notice is then skipped
confirmed.description: When the GPS stream errors, the trip saves the rendered text both in `_locationStatus = tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis` and in NavigationController `_locationWarning` (keepLastKnown, navigation_controller.dart:298). Both stay until a usable fix arrives. Covering the trip with Settings does not pause GPS (live updates pause only on app lifecycle, accept_ride.dart:713-726), so returning does not refresh the text, and the island keeps showing the old-language warning. When GPS comes back, TripIslandController decides whether to say 'GPS restored' by comparing the stored old-language text with the new language: `fault == tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis || fault.contains('Location')`. Neither test matches a Swedish string while the app is in French, so the notice is never shown.
confirmed.failure_scenario: In Swedish, GPS drops during the trip and the island shows 'Platsen uppdateras…'. The driver switches to French via the side menu and returns. The island still shows Swedish, and when the fix returns the island goes straight back to guidance without 'GPS rétabli'.

accept_ride_trip.dart:614-617  `_navigation.keepLastKnown(status: tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis); _rebuild(() { _hasLiveLocation = false; _locationStatus = tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis; });`
navigation_controller.dart:298  `_locationWarning = status ?? tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis;`
trip_island_controller.dart:96-97  `static bool _isLocationFault(String fault) => fault == tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis || fault.contains('Location');`

verdicts.reason: The GPS-error handler stores already-translated text in two places: _locationStatus and NavigationController._locationWarning (accept_ride_trip.dart:634-639, navigation_controller.dart:298). Nothing translates the stored strings again. When a usable fix clears the warning, TripIslandController checks the old text with fault == tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis || fault.contains('Location') (trip_island_controller.dart:96-97). confirmed.title: After the trip ends (outcome sheet up), a GPS fix after an app resume can still schedule an on-trip Exclusive offer; when it expires unseen it counts as a missed offer
confirmed.description: _leaveAfterAuthoritativeOutcome pauses live updates and then awaits showTripOutcomeSheet. If the app is backgrounded and resumed while that sheet is open, _resumeLiveUpdates restarts GPS. _resumeOnTripOffer checks `_rideLifecycle.terminal`, but _applyDriverPosition calls _maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer when `_stage == onTrip`, and that function has no terminal check. An offer is then shown under the modal, its expiry timer runs, and _denyNextTripRadar calls ExclusiveAnswers.instance.missed(), which can switch the driver offline after the trip.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Movera cancels a trip while the driver is on board, and the outcome sheet is shown. The driver switches apps and comes back without closing the sheet. 2.2 s later a hidden next-trip offer appears and then expires, and it counts toward the auto-offline missed-offer streak.
confirmed.evidence:
accept_ride_trip.dart:684-686 `if (_stage == ActiveRideStage.onTrip) { _maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer(); _rideCheckObserve(); }`
accept_ride_trip.dart:1072-1078 the guard checks mounted/paused/stage/scanning only.
accept_ride_trip.dart:1226-1227 `if (ExclusiveAnswers.instance.missed()) { widget.sessionController?.setOnline(false);`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Return early from _maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer, _presentOnTripOffer and _resumeLiveUpdates when _rideLifecycle.terminal is true.

verdicts.reason: A terminal projection calls _leaveAfterAuthoritativeOutcome (accept_ride_trip.dart:340, 393-411). It pauses updates and awaits the outcome sheet. applyProjection marks the ride terminal but leaves _stage at onTrip, because ActiveRideStage has no terminal value. On app resume, didChangeAppLifecycleState calls _resumeLiveUpdates (accept_ride.dart:718), which has no terminal guard (accept_ride_trip.dart:147-163) and restarts GPS. Only _resumeOnTripOffer checks terminal. The next fix reaches _maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer (line 684-686). Its guards (1093-1146) check mounted, paused, stage, scanning and declined, but not _rideLifecycle.terminal. The offer appears under the modal sheet (barrierDismissible: false), its expiry calls _denyNextTripRadar, and that calls ExclusiveAnswers.missed() and possibly setOnline(false) (line 1254). This needs the radar to still be scanning and not declined at the terminal outcome. That is likely in production, where NextTripGate only allows offers near the final drop-off (next_trip_gate allows:27-37), when the driver reaches the window after the cancel. It also needs the expiry to come before the driver taps the sheet. This is an edge path, but no guard stops it.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _drainProjection -> applyProjection (no stage change) -> _leaveAfterAuthoritativeOutcome, lifecycle resume -> _resumeLiveUpdates -> _startLiveLocation -> _applyDriverPosition -> _maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer -> _presentOnTripOffer -> _armOnTripOfferExpiry -> _denyNextTripRadar. Also checked the OfferRules defaults (exclusiveWhileDriving=true). No test run.

verdicts.reason: After an authoritative terminal status, applyProjection sets only _terminalStatus, and the stage stays onTrip (active_ride_controller.dart:111-124). _leaveAfterAuthoritativeOutcome pauses updates and awaits showTripOutcomeSheet, which cannot be dismissed by tapping outside (accept_ride_trip.dart:393-407). On resume, _resumeLiveUpdates (accept_ride_trip.dart:147-163) restarts GPS with no terminal check. _applyDriverPosition then calls _maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer when _stage==onTrip (line 711-713). That function, its timer callback and _presentOnTripOffer check only mounted, paused, stage, radar state and declined, never _rideLifecycle.terminal (lines 1093-1160). The expiry then calls _denyNextTripRadar, which calls ExclusiveAnswers.instance.missed() (line 1253). The guard in _resumeOnTripOffer does not cover the fix path. It is reachable when the terminal event arrives while radar is still scanning, for example within 2.2 s of a fix or before any offer appeared.
verdicts.repro: Ran a throwaway widget test on a git-archive copy of HEAD. AcceptRide started onTrip with MemoryDriverRealtime. I sent a cancelledByAdmin tripProjection after 400 ms, pumped 3 s, then sent paused and resumed lifecycle events, and pumped past exclusiveAcceptTime. Output: `sheet: 1`, `offer before resume: 0`, `offer after resume: 1`, `sheet: 1`, `missedInRow: 1, online=true autoOff=3`, then `All tests passed!`. So the hidden offer appeared under the outcome sheet and counted as one miss (the auto-offline threshold is 3).

confirmed.title: A next-trip offer hidden for a Ride check comes back with a new full exclusiveAcceptTime, ignoring the time it was already on screen
confirmed.description: `_onRideCheckGate` (1137-1162) hides an open offer while the Ride check is up and records `_nextTripOfferHeldAt`. After the answer it checks only whether the full lifetime has elapsed since `heldAt` and then calls `_presentOnTripOffer()`, which calls `_armOnTripOfferExpiry()` with `left == null` → `_nextTripOfferDeadline = now + lifetime` (1163-1173). Time already spent before the check (and `_nextTripOfferDeadline`) is ignored, so the rider's offer is held open longer than Dispatch's time to accept; the comment and D-05 say a surviving offer counts down the rest.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Offer shown with 20 s left; a Ride check opens and is answered after 10 s; the offer returns with the full exclusiveAcceptTime again instead of ~10 s.
confirmed.evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:1157-1161 `if (DateTime.now().difference(heldAt) >= _AcceptRideState._onTripOfferLifetime) { _maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer(); return; }\n      _presentOnTripOffer();` ; 1166-1167 `final time = left ?? _AcceptRideState._onTripOfferLifetime;\n      if (left == null) { _nextTripOfferDeadline = _offerNow().add(time); }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep `_nextTripOfferDeadline` when holding and re-arm with `left: deadline - now` (drop the offer when it is <= 0), as `_resumeOnTripOffer` does.

verdicts.reason: _onRideCheckGate (accept_ride_trip.dart:1137-1162) cancels the expiry and stores _nextTripOfferHeldAt=now when a Ride check opens over a visible offer. On the answer, it compares only the time spent held against the full lifetime (:1157), then calls _presentOnTripOffer (:1161). That calls _armOnTripOfferExpiry() with left==null, which resets _nextTripOfferDeadline to now plus the full exclusiveAcceptTime (:1166-1167). The offer is the same one: the same id comes from _uniqueDemoNext (accept_ride.dart:963) or the '-next-destination' id. So the time it was already shown is discarded, and the window can run to about twice Dispatch's accept time plus the check. This contradicts the method's own doc ('comes back if its time has not passed') and the D-05 handling in _resumeOnTripOffer (:158-167), which re-arms with the remaining time. Dispatch is a mock, so the effect is a wrong local countdown, not a server-side acceptance.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _onRideCheckGate, _presentOnTripOffer and _armOnTripOfferExpiry (accept_ride_trip.dart:1122-1175), compared with _resumeOnTripOffer (:158-167). No test covers this timing: test/widget/ride_check_test.dart is the only test that references RideCheckGate, and it has no lifetime or remaining-time assertions.

verdicts.corrected_title: A next-trip offer hidden for a Ride check comes back with a new full exclusiveAcceptTime, ignoring the time it was already on screen
verdicts.reason: _onRideCheckGate (accept_ride_trip.dart:1137-1162): when the gate opens it cancels _nextTripOfferExpiry and sets _nextTripOfferHeldAt = now (:1144-1145). It does not use _nextTripOfferDeadline. When the gate closes, the only check is now - heldAt >= lifetime (:1157). After that, _presentOnTripOffer (:1161 -> :1131) calls _armOnTripOfferExpiry() with left == null, which sets _nextTripOfferDeadline = now + lifetime and starts a full-length Timer (:1166-1168). The panel countdown is also a fresh TweenAnimationBuilder over the full lifetime (accept_ride_panel.dart:350-353), because the offer widget was removed while scanning. Compare _resumeOnTripOffer (:158-167), which re-arms with deadline - now. The D-05 comment there says 'one with time left counts down the rest', and this path does not do that.
verdicts.repro: Worked by hand from the code. Let L = exclusiveAcceptTime and suppose the offer is shown at t0. A Ride check opens at t0+10 s, so heldAt = t0+10 and the expiry timer is cancelled. It is answered at t0+15 s: 5 s < L, so the offer is shown again and the deadline becomes t0+15+L. Total exposure is L+15 s instead of L. In the worst case the hold lasts just under L, and exposure approaches about 2L plus the time shown before the hold. No guard uses the original deadline.

confirmed.title: Cancelling the current trip with a secured next trip starts the next AcceptRide without destination mode, unlike completion and the journal snapshot
confirmed.description: `_submitTripCancellation` builds the next `AcceptRide` (1394-1414) without `destinationModeActive`, `destinationAddress` or `destinationPosition`, whereas `_completeCurrentTrip` (954-956) passes them and the journal's `next` snapshot (`_snapshotForOffer`, 971-979) stores them. After a driver cancel the next trip therefore runs with destination mode off (no on-the-way filter for next-trip offers, the trip options row shows 'next trips on your way' as off), while a crash restore of that same trip from the journal snapshot would restore destination mode on — the two paths disagree.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver has destination mode on, secures a next trip, then ends the current trip early. The next trip's screen has destination mode off; Exclusive offers no longer follow the destination.
confirmed.evidence:
accept_ride_trip.dart:1394-1414 `AcceptRide(
              tripId: offer.id, ... dispatchRepository: widget.dispatchRepository,
            )` (no destination fields) vs 954-956 `destinationModeActive: _destinationActive,
              destinationAddress: _destinationAddress,
              destinationPosition: _destinationPosition,`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass the three destination fields (or use `AcceptRide.fromPersisted(_snapshotForOffer(offer))` as the rider-cancel path does).

verdicts.reason: _submitTripCancellation builds the next AcceptRide (accept_ride_trip.dart:1394-1414) without destinationModeActive, destinationAddress or destinationPosition. The constructor defaults destinationModeActive to false (accept_ride.dart:138), and the state reads it only from the widget (accept_ride.dart:471-473), so destination mode is off on the next trip. _completeCurrentTrip passes all three (:954-956). The journal handoff snapshot from the same cancel call, _snapshotForOffer (:971-979 via :1374), stores them, so a crash restore would bring destination mode back on. The two paths disagree. With the mode off, _dropoffFollowsDestination and _onTripRadarOfferForDestination (:1023, :1033) stop filtering next-trip offers to the destination.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the AcceptRide construction at accept_ride_trip.dart:1394-1414 against 935-957 and 971-979, plus the state initialisation at accept_ride.dart:471-473. No other source sets _destinationActive except the panel toggle (accept_ride_panel.dart:186).

verdicts.reason: _submitTripCancellation builds the next AcceptRide (accept_ride_trip.dart:1394-1414) without destinationModeActive, destinationAddress or destinationPosition. The constructor defaults destinationModeActive to false (accept_ride.dart:138), and the next screen reads it at accept_ride.dart:471 (late bool _destinationActive = widget.destinationModeActive). It controls the on-the-way filter for next-trip offers (accept_ride_trip.dart:1023, :1033) and the options row (accept_ride_panel.dart:1080). Completion passes all three fields (:954-956). The rider-cancel paths use AcceptRide.fromPersisted(next) (:382, :472), and the journal snapshot _snapshotForOffer stores them (:971-974). So only a driver cancel with a secured next trip loses destination mode. One correction to the description: once the new screen persists its own snapshot, it saves the mode as off, so a later crash restore would also have it off.
verdicts.repro: Traced the constructors and state initialisation (accept_ride.dart:138, 206, 288, 471) and compared the three handoff paths (accept_ride_trip.dart:935-957 completion, :1394-1414 driver cancel, :382/:472 rider cancel via fromPersisted). Path: the driver turns destination mode on, accepts an Exclusive offer (state secured, :1196-1199), then cancels the current trip. The secured offer is promoted (:1415-1416) and the next AcceptRide starts with _destinationActive = false.

verdicts.reason: adaptive_trip_island.dart:387-390 clamps the status/waiting-message island to `available` (screen width minus 24), not to TripIslandGeometry.maximumWidth (trip_island.dart:16, 224.48). docs/driver-island-state-map.md:3 documents a 224.48 maximum, and the existing test (adaptive_trip_island_test.dart:559) expects width <= maximumWidth for normal islands. verdicts.corrected_title: Trip status and waiting-message island is capped only by screen width, not by the documented 224.48 maximum (+15%)
verdicts.reason:
Confirmed. adaptive_trip_island.dart:387-390 sets the status and waiting-message width with `desired.clamp(home.width, available)`. `available` is the screen width minus 24, so the only upper limit is the screen.

Two sources set a lower limit:
- docs/driver-island-state-map.md:3 says this renderer uses a default height of 40.32, a default width of 195.2 and a maximum of 224.48 (+15%). The height (40.32) and the 24 px slots (adaptive_trip_island.dart:404, 446) match what that line describes, which shows it refers to these compact faces.
- The same maximum exists in code as TripIslandGeometry.maximumWidth (trip_island.dart:16), and adaptive_trip_island_test.dart:559 asserts it for a waiting face.

The tracer read the comment at adaptive_trip_island.dart:378, "A message sizes the island to its words", as proof that the growth is deliberate. That does not hold. Home has the same comment at home_map_sheet.dart:984-986 and still caps message width at exactly this +15%: `.clamp(math.min(244.0, maxWidth), math.min(244.0 * 1.15, maxWidth))` at home_map_sheet.dart:993-996. 244 × 1.15 × 0.8 = 224.48. So in this codebase, growing with the text and capping at +15% go together. None of DECISIONS.md, REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md or LOCAL_DATA.md records an exception for trip faces.

The real status strings that exceed the cap are French location and route faults:
- tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis, set at accept_ride_trip.dart:647-684 and navigation_controller.dart:298, shown through trip_island_controller.dart:148-151.
- tr.navRouteUpdating.

A cap would not lose text: the title already has maxLines: 1 and an ellipsis (`_message`, adaptive_trip_island.dart:~951-961).

Impact is layout only: no overflow exception, no money or data effect. Typical English strings stay under the cap (198.97 and 207.21 px). This is the documented spec not being enforced on an edge path, hence low.

Side note: the Home-style TripIsland message on the trip screen (trip_island.dart:115-117) also clamps only to the screen. It is a separate code path and outside this finding.
verdicts.repro:
Wrote a throwaway test, /home/user/Movera-driver-app/test/_audit_u88dec_test.dart. It reuses `surface()` from test/widget/adaptive_trip_island_test.dart and loads the real Roboto fonts from /opt/flutter/bin/cache/artifacts/material_fonts, so the widths are not Ahem widths. Each case was rendered at screen width 390 with `NavigationBanner(primary: 'Turn right', distanceLabel: '100 m', status: s)`, then the width of the 'island-morph-shell' widget was measured.

Output (`PATH=/opt/flutter/bin:$PATH flutter test test/_audit_u88dec_test.dart`):

verdicts.reason:
The defect is real, and I reproduced it on the current code. It only shows up in an opt-in build, so I rate it low rather than medium.

Mechanism: in "lib/presentation/driver/auth/additional detail/navigation.dart", line 117 returns a bare Scaffold. There is no PopScope and no onPopInvoked handler. The step-aware back exists only in the on-screen IconButton (line 126, which calls moveToPreviousStep). That method moves back one page and pops the route only on page 0 (lines 71-73). The wizard is pushed from "lib/presentation/driver/auth/sign in/sign_in.dart" lines 83 and 102 as BottomToTopTransition. That is a plain ModalRoute (lib/widgets/navigation_transition.dart:10), so a system back pops the whole wizard from any step. The page states in the PageView are disposed with it, so whatever the driver entered on earlier steps is lost.

The iOS edge-swipe part of the finding is wrong. A custom ModalRoute has no Cupertino back-swipe gesture, so only Android back and predictive back are affected.

Why it still counts despite the tracer's point: the tracer is right that the screen is only reachable behind a compile-time flag. The path is DriverStarter, then starter.dart:74-91, then DriverSignIn, and that path needs MOVERA_ENABLE_LEGACY_AUTH (lib/core/session/demo_features.dart:2, defaultValue false; docs/ROUTES.md marks the screen 'legacy gated'). That limits the severity. It does not make the bug false:
- Legacy auth is a documented, supported opt-in (docs/BASELINE.md:16).
- This exact screen has maintained regression tests (test/widget/onboarding_route_regression_test.dart:85-152).
- This audit already confirmed bugs on legacy-gated screens at low severity (docs/audit-2026-10-21/AUDIT.md L40, phone_verify.dart:122; and L41).
- Nothing in DECISIONS.md, REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md or LOCAL_DATA.md says this behaviour was chosen on purpose.

Severity is low because the screen cannot be reached in the default build. It would be medium if legacy auth were turned on.

confirmed.title: feeSuffix hardcodes 'kr' and a /100 divisor for whole cancel fees, ignoring the Money currency and exponent (latent until a non-SEK cancelFee arrives)
confirmed.description: `feeSuffix(Money? fee)` prints `'${fee.minorUnits ~/ 100} kr'` whenever the amount is a whole number of minor-hundreds, ignoring `fee.currency` and its exponent (Money supports SEK/EUR with exponent 2 and TND with exponent 3; zone_settings maps EUR->FR and TND->TN). Only the non-whole branch uses `fee.formatted`. Callers: reservationCancelled island message (line 60-66), RiderCancelledSheet status line (rider_cancelled_sheet.dart:59-62), ScheduledRideStore.riderCancelled (scheduled_rides.dart:678). The fee is the backend's decision (R15-7) in the zone currency.
confirmed.failure_scenario: In a French zone the backend sends cancelFee {amountMinor: 500, currency: 'EUR'}: the island and the rider-cancelled sheet say '· +5 kr' instead of '· +5,00 €'; for TND 5000 millimes they say '+50 kr' instead of '5,000 DT'.
confirmed.evidence: lib/presentation/driver/home/components/home_island_notices.dart:72-74 `final amount = fee.minorUnits % 100 == 0\n        ? '${fee.minorUnits ~/ 100} kr'\n        : fee.formatted;`

verdicts.reason: home_island_notices.dart:72-74: when `minorUnits % 100 == 0` the code returns `'${fee.minorUnits ~/ 100} kr'` and ignores `fee.currency` and its exponent. The fee comes off the wire: driver_realtime.dart:179-201 reads `cancelFee` with `Money.fromJson`, and that accepts EUR and TND (money.dart:43, exponents SEK/EUR 2, TND 3). The app is built for more than one zone: driver_app_config.dart:112-116 takes the zone currency from config, and zone_settings.dart:66-67 and 104-105 handle EUR and TND. accept_ride_trip.dart:278/312 passes event.cancelFee to rider_cancelled_sheet.dart:62, which calls feeSuffix. A EUR 500 fee shows as '+5 kr'. A TND 5000-millime fee shows as '+50 kr' (correct is '5,000 DT'), so both the currency and the size are wrong. Money.formattedShort (money.dart) already handles every currency correctly. Severity is low because the main market is SEK (DECISIONS.md P2) and SEK output is correct.
verdicts.repro: Traced feeSuffix's callers (rider_cancelled_sheet.dart:62, home_island_notices.dart:52/61, scheduled_rides.dart:678) back to the realtime wire parsing and the zone currency config. Worked through the integer arithmetic by hand for EUR 500 and TND 5000.

verdicts.reason: The code defect is real but no runtime path reaches it. Every fee that reaches feeSuffix (home_island_notices.dart:67-76) comes from DriverRealtimeEvent.cancelFee or ScheduledRideStore.riderCancelled(fee:). driver_realtime.dart:11 says there is no transport yet. The only event source in the app is MemoryDriverRealtime (accept_ride.dart:592), and no code in lib calls emit(cancelFee: ...). DriverRealtimeEvent.tryParse/fromJson is called only from tests. ScheduledRideStore.riderCancelled (scheduled_rides.dart:674) is also called only from tests, with Money.sek(105). So no fee, and certainly no EUR or TND fee, reaches the island or the RiderCancelledSheet today. It becomes a real bug once a transport delivers a non-SEK cancelFee, and the suggested fix (fee.formattedShort) is right.
verdicts.repro: Ran throwaway test test/_audit_d73_test.dart (since deleted) calling HomeIslandNotices.feeSuffix. EUR 500 gave ' · +5 kr', TND 5000 gave ' · +50 kr' and SEK 10500 gave ' · +105 kr'. So the function ignores the currency, but tracing found no caller in lib that produces a fee (grep of `cancelFee:` and `.riderCancelled(` hits only definitions and tests).

verdicts.reason:
The defect is in the code. lib/presentation/driver/home/components/home_island_notices.dart:72-74 hardcodes `' kr'` and divides by 100 whenever `minorUnits % 100 == 0`. It ignores `fee.currency` and `fee.exponent`, but the other branch uses the currency-aware `fee.formatted`, so the function contradicts itself. The input type allows other currencies. Contract v0.3 (docs/DECISIONS.md, "Contract v0.3": Money JSON with exponents SEK/EUR 2, TND 3) and money.dart:43 accept EUR and TND. DriverRealtimeEvent.fromJson (driver_realtime.dart:179-201) parses them from the wire. The app also ships a French locale and test fixtures for the FR-PC and TN-TC zones.

The code sits on a live chain in lib, not dead code. accept_ride.dart:594 subscribes the realtime stream. accept_ride_trip.dart:278 and :312 pass `event.cancelFee` to `_handleRiderCancelled`. From there it goes to `riderCancelledWithFee` (:455) and `showRiderCancelledSheet` (:461 to rider_cancelled_sheet.dart:62), and both call feeSuffix.

The reproducer is right that nothing in lib produces a fee today. There is no transport (driver_realtime.dart:11), MemoryDriverRealtime is the only source, and nothing calls `emit(cancelFee:)` or `ScheduledRideStore.riderCancelled`. That is true of every backend-fed path in this demo frontend (REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:45), so it does not make a wrong consumer of a contract-typed value correct. No decision document records SEK-only formatting for Money values. The "Other trip models still carry SEK labels (follow-up)" note covers string-typed trip fields, not Money values. DECISIONS P2 (SEK market) explains why the severity is low, not why this would be intended. The bug is latent and only shows for non-SEK fees, while SEK output is correct, so severity is low.
verdicts.repro:
Ran a throwaway test, test/_audit_d62_decide_test.dart, since deleted. It confirmed DriverRealtimeEvent.tryParse accepts `cancelFee: {amountMinor: 500, currency: 'EUR'}`, giving parsed fee EUR 500. It then called HomeIslandNotices.feeSuffix and compared the result with Money.formattedShort:
EUR 500: feeSuffix=" · +5 kr", formattedShort="5 €"
TND 5000: feeSuffix=" · +50 kr", formattedShort="5 DT"
SEK 10500: feeSuffix=" · +105 kr", formattedShort="105 kr"
SEK 10550: feeSuffix=" · +105,50 kr", formattedShort="105,50 kr"
Result: "All tests passed!" The wire accepts the non-SEK fee and feeSuffix gets both the currency and the amount wrong for it. Using `fee.formattedShort` in both branches gives the correct output.

confirmed.title: When browser storage is blocked outright, recovery never resolves, so the driver can never go online and is told about a saved trip that does not exist
confirmed.description: _restoreActiveRideIfNeeded runs CompletionJournal.reconcile() and repo.read(). Both call SharedPreferences.getInstance(), which throws when the browser blocks localStorage (Safari 'Block all cookies', some private modes). Any non-ActiveRideUnreadable error lands in the generic catch, which shows 'The saved trip could not be opened' and leaves _recoveryResolved false. _goOnline refuses while !_recoveryResolved and shows 'Finish or close the saved trip before going online' with 'Open saved trip', which only retries the same failing read. On a first launch with no storage there is no saved trip, yet the driver is blocked from going online for the whole session.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Fresh install opened in a browser with site storage blocked: Home shows 'The saved trip could not be opened'. Every radar tap answers 'Finish or close the saved trip before going online', and 'Open saved trip' fails again. The driver can never go online.
confirmed.evidence: home.dart:519-525 `} catch (_) { _didAttemptActiveRideRestore = false; if(mounted) { _HomeMapSheet(this)._tripProblem(HomeIslandNotices.recoveryFailed, tr.savedTripCouldNotBeOpened); } return; }`; home.dart:890-895 `if(!_recoveryResolved) { _HomeMapSheet(this)._tripProblem(HomeIslandNotices.recoveryPending, tr.finishOrCloseSavedTripBefore, action: tr.openSavedTrip); return; }`; prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:71 `final prefs = await _load();`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Tell 'storage unavailable' apart from 'a saved trip exists but failed'. When the store cannot be opened, nothing can be recovered: resolve recovery (with a warning) instead of blocking going online.

verdicts.reason: PrefsActiveRideRepository.read (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:69-72) lets SharedPreferences.getInstance errors propagate on purpose ('A failing storage plugin is transient: let it propagate for Retry'). home.dart:519-525 catches them, shows savedTripCouldNotBeOpened and leaves _recoveryResolved false, and _goOnline (home.dart:890-895) then refuses to go online. Failing closed is intentional for transient faults. However, when storage is permanently unavailable, the getter itself throws SecurityError: on web, Chrome with site data blocked or Safari with 'Block all cookies'. In that case every retry fails the same way. Startup does not stop the app before Home (main.dart:46-50 catches errors, and the session store is in memory), so the driver reaches Home and is blocked for the whole session, told about a 'saved trip' that does not exist. The path is real but needs a non-default browser setting, hence low.
verdicts.repro: I traced this statically: main.dart startup, which tolerates storage errors -> DriverHome post-frame _restoreActiveRideIfNeeded -> CompletionJournal.reconcile / repo.read -> _load() throws -> generic catch at home.dart:519 -> _goOnline gate at home.dart:890. I found no doc entry covering permanently unavailable storage (LOCAL_DATA.md, DECISIONS.md). Not reproduced in a browser.
verdicts.corrected_title: When browser storage is blocked outright, recovery never resolves, so the driver can never go online and is told about a saved trip that does not exist

verdicts.reason: In home.dart:505-528, _restoreActiveRideIfNeeded calls CompletionJournal.reconcile() and repo.read(), and both load SharedPreferences.getInstance (completion_journal.dart:39, prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:71, which has the comment 'A failing storage plugin is transient: let it propagate for Retry'). On web, shared_preferences_web 2.4.3 reads html.window.localStorage with no guard. That access throws SecurityError when site data is blocked, and shared_preferences resets _completer on error, so every retry throws again. The generic catch at home.dart:519-526 shows savedTripCouldNotBeOpened and leaves _recoveryResolved false. _goOnline (home.dart:896-900) then refuses with 'finish or close saved trip', and its 'Open saved trip' action (home_map_sheet.dart:1286) only reruns the same failing restore. Home is reachable without storage, because the session store is MemoryDriverSessionRepository (main.dart:86) and DriverLanguage.restore is in a try/catch (main.dart:46-47). The driver is therefore locked offline for the whole session, and is told about a saved trip that does not exist.
verdicts.repro: Static trace through home.dart restore, the _goOnline guard, the _tripProblem retry action and the shared_preferences_web/legacy getInstance source in the pub cache (completeError, then _completer = null; no catch around localStorage). Not run, since a browser with storage blocked cannot be simulated in flutter test. The premise is that the browser throws on window.localStorage access when site data is blocked, which is standard Chrome/Firefox/Safari behaviour. No document in docs/ makes the storage-unavailable case intentional.

verdicts.corrected_title: An Exclusive offer that arrives while the side menu is open is shown under the drawer, keeps its timeout and counts as missed (Q16)
verdicts.reason: The finding's exact path, opening the menu from the island while the Exclusive is up, is blocked. While _exclusiveOnIsland is true the island is `tucked`, and the menu button sits under IgnorePointer(ignoring: tucked) (home_map_sheet.dart:969-1030). The bug is still reachable two ways. First, an offer can arrive while the drawer is already open: _showOutsideRadarOffer (home_offer_radar.dart:209-248) has no isDrawerOpen or visibility gate, and the drawer is not a route, so _routeVisible stays true and didPushNext never fires. Second, the Scaffold's default edge-swipe can open the drawer over a live offer. In both cases _outsideOfferTimeoutTimer (home_offer_radar.dart:275-281) fires _dismissOutsideRadarOffer(missed:true). A pause behind a hidden tab or route, by contrast, does not count as a miss (home_exclusive.dart:110-112). Effect: a false miss that feeds the auto-offline count.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: the island tuck and IgnorePointer, the show-gate conditions (no drawer check), the only isDrawerOpen use (home_back.dart:53), and the timeout callback. No test was run.

verdicts.corrected_title: An Exclusive offer that rises while the side menu is already open (or the menu is edge-swiped open) counts down under the drawer and is counted as missed
verdicts.reason: The finding's own trigger is blocked: while an Exclusive is on the island, the island's menu button is tucked and wrapped in IgnorePointer (home_map_sheet.dart:1019-1031, `tucked = ... || exclusive != null`). Other paths still reach the failure. _showOutsideRadarOffer (home_offer_radar.dart:228-247) never checks whether the drawer is open, so an offer can arrive while the driver is already reading the menu. Home's Scaffold also leaves the default edge-swipe drawer gesture on, unlike accept_ride.dart:1153 which disables it. The drawer is not a route, so didPushNext/_pauseHomeUpdates (home.dart:174) never runs, and nothing uses onDrawerChanged. The timer at home_offer_radar.dart:275-281 fires _dismissOutsideRadarOffer(missed: true), which reaches _exclusiveMissed (line 320). The hidden-by-route case in home_exclusive.dart:110-112 is treated as not a miss.
verdicts.repro: Traced callers: grep finds no onDrawerChanged/isDrawerOpen handling apart from Back (home_back.dart:53), no drawer check in _showOutsideRadarOffer, and no drawerEnableOpenDragGesture:false on Home. No widget test was run, because Home needs the full dependency graph.

confirmed.title: Matching from the full Radar list leaves Home's copy of the card live: it is marked 'unavailable' at match time and the driven trip briefly reappears as 'Taken' after the trip
confirmed.description: When the driver matches from the Home deck, _openOfferTrip clears all Home offer state in a post-frame callback (_outsideRadarOffer, _radarHomeOffers, _pendingRadarHomeOffers, _hasRideOffers = false). When the driver matches from the embedded RideRequests list (shown when showRideRequests is true), Home only receives onCloseRides and the session callbacks, and nothing clears Home's deck. The sequence is as follows. (1) RideRequests claims the offer. The demo dispatch _removeOffer emits the new offer list to Home's still-live _watchDispatchRadar listener, which calls _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost(offer, unavailable) on Home's copy of the same trip and marks it claimedElsewhere. (2) Within 500 ms AcceptRide is pushed, and didPushNext -> _cancelAllOfferTimers(preserveClaim: true) cancels the 2.8 s cleanup but keeps every list and deadline. (3) After the trip, endTrip sets resumeHomeAfterTrip, and _onDriverSessionChanged only sets showRideRequests = false. didPopNext -> _resumeOfferTimers shows the driven trip as a 'Taken' card for 1.2 s. Other cards have old deadlines and come back already expired (Match faded), and _hasRideOffers stays true.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver is online with three Radar cards on Home, taps the orb to open the full Radar list, and taps Match on the first trip. They drive it and complete it 20 minutes later. Back on Home, the deck still holds the pre-trip cards: the trip just completed is shown as 'Taken', and the rest have Match faded. If that card was the expanded front card, the island also posted 'Trip unavailable' at the moment of the match.
confirmed.evidence:
home.dart:746-766 `RideRequests(... onCloseRides: (hasOffers) { setState(() { showRideRequests = false; _hasRideOffers = hasOffers || _radarHomeOffers.isNotEmpty; }); }, )`. No match callback exists.
home.dart:664-668 `if (_driverSession.consumeResumeHomeAfterTrip()) { setState(() { showRideRequests = false; }); return; }`
Compare home_offer_radar.dart:983-990 (Home-deck accept): `_rebuild(() { _outsideRadarOffer = null; _radarHomeOffers.clear(); _pendingRadarHomeOffers.clear(); _hasRideOffers = false; ...`
home_offer_radar.dart:604-610 `if (!ids.contains(offer.id) && _homeRadarStateFor(offer.id) == available) { _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost(offer, _RadarOfferGone.unavailable); }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Give RideRequests an onMatched callback, or clear Home's deck in _onDriverSessionChanged when a trip begins, in the same way as the Home-deck accept path.

verdicts.reason: _openRideOffers (home.dart:979-986) keeps Home's deck while the full list is open. On a list Match, DemoDispatchRepository.claimOffer calls _removeOffer (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:565), which emits to Home's still-live watcher. The watcher calls _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost(unavailable) (home_offer_radar.dart:604-610, 672-707). That sets claimedElsewhere, posts 'Trip unavailable' if the card was the front card, and starts a 2.8 s cleanup. AcceptRide is pushed about 520 ms later, and didPushNext calls _pauseHomeUpdates, which calls _cancelAllOfferTimers(preserveClaim:true) (home.dart:192-203, home_offer_radar.dart:791-818). That cancels the cleanup but keeps the deck, the match states and the deadlines. No RideRequests callback clears the deck; only onCloseRides exists. _onDriverSessionChanged only sets showRideRequests=false (home.dart:664-668). RideCompleted uses popUntil(isFirst) (ride_completed.dart:79), which brings back the same Home State. didPopNext then calls _resumeOfferTimers, which shows the driven trip as 'Taken' for 1.2 s and restarts pick windows against old deadlines, so those cards come back expired. The re-subscribed watcher replays a snapshot (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:505) that marks the others unavailable. The Home-deck accept path clears all of this (home_offer_radar.dart:1005-1007).
verdicts.repro: Static trace of claimOffer, _removeOffer, the Home watcher, didPushNext/didPopNext, and popUntil(isFirst). I tried a widget test that matched from the list, ended the trip and popped back. It would not compile because files were being edited at the same time (home_offer_radar.dart:995 passed scheduledPickupAt, which AcceptRide does not accept). I deleted the test, so this verdict rests on static tracing.

verdicts.corrected_title: Matching from the full Radar list leaves Home's copy of the card live: it is marked 'unavailable' at match time and the driven trip briefly reappears as 'Taken' after the trip
verdicts.reason: RideRequests has no match callback (home.dart:751-771), so Home's deck is not cleared the way the Home-deck accept does it (home_offer_radar.dart ~1000-1007). Home's dispatch listener is still live when the claim removes the offer. It calls _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost(unavailable) (home_offer_radar.dart:604-610), which marks the card claimedElsewhere and, if it was the front card, shows 'Trip unavailable' (line 689). The pause cancels the 2.8 s cleanup (_cancelAllOfferTimers, preserveClaim keeps the states). After the trip, _resumeOfferTimers (762-789) shows the driven trip as Taken for 1.2 s before removing it. The effect is short-lived, not a lasting stale deck: _resumeHomeUpdates calls _scheduleVisibleOffers, then _watchDispatchRadar. The demo stream replays a snapshot on listen (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:504-505), so any card gone from dispatch is resolved and removed after 2.8 s. Cards still in dispatch with a used-up pick window keep Match faded, which matches the D-04 pause rule for any covering route.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand: claim, then the watcher marks the card claimedElsewhere, then the AcceptRide push pauses Home with states kept. On pop: _scheduleVisibleOffers resubscribes and the snapshot resolves gone cards (2.8 s), and _resumeOfferTimers removes the Taken card after 1.2 s. No test was run.

confirmed.title: Go online / Locate / resume mute Home's running GPS stream until a fresh one-shot fix returns
confirmed.description: _startDriverLocation bumps _locationEpoch before it awaits getCurrentPosition(). The existing _driverLocationSubscription stays subscribed, but its listener drops every update because `epoch != _locationEpoch`. It is replaced only after the one-shot fix returns or throws. _goOnline (home.dart:924) and the locate button call this while a working stream is already running, so the car marker and camera freeze for the whole one-shot wait: up to the 8 s time limit natively, and without a limit on web (the time limit is not enforced there).
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver is moving with live GPS on Home and taps the radar to go online while the GPS signal is weak. The car marker stops updating until getCurrentPosition returns or times out (several seconds, longer on web), although the stream was already delivering fixes.
confirmed.evidence:
home_map_sheet.dart:35-38 `final epoch = ++_locationEpoch; if (!_liveVisible) { return; } try { final position = await _driverLocationService.getCurrentPosition();`
home_map_sheet.dart:65 `if (!mounted || !_liveVisible || epoch != _locationEpoch) { return; }`
home.dart:924 `unawaited(_HomeMapSheet(this)._startDriverLocation(moveCamera: true));`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep the old stream active until the new subscription is in place: bump the epoch only when replacing the subscription, or skip the one-shot when a subscription is already live.

verdicts.reason: home_map_sheet.dart:35 bumps _locationEpoch before awaiting getCurrentPosition() (line 38). The live subscription's listener (line 65) drops every fix because epoch != _locationEpoch, and it is replaced only at line 44 or 55 after the one-shot returns. Nothing cancels or keeps the old stream meanwhile. Callers that run this while a stream is already live: _goOnline (home.dart:930), Locate (_zoomToDriverLocation, home_map_sheet.dart:126) and every lifecycle resume (home.dart:207). On native the wait is capped by the 8 s timeLimit (driver_location_service.dart:25), plus a getLastKnownPosition fallback. On web, geolocator_web 4.1.4 passes timeout?.inMicroseconds where the browser expects milliseconds (html_geolocation_manager.dart:36), so 8 s becomes about 2.2 h. The web freeze is therefore effectively unbounded until the browser answers. With good GPS the one-shot returns fast and the freeze is short, so this is low.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: home_map_sheet.dart:34-80 epoch logic, callers at home.dart:207/488/930 and home_map_sheet.dart:126, driver_location_service.dart:29-49, and the pub-cache geolocator_web-4.1.4 html_geolocation_manager.dart:35-36. No test run.

verdicts.reason: home_map_sheet.dart:35 bumps _locationEpoch before awaiting getCurrentPosition() (line 38). The existing subscription made in _listenToDriverLocation captured the old epoch (line 57) and drops every fix at line 65 (`epoch != _locationEpoch`). It is replaced only after the one-shot returns or throws (lines 44 and 54). _goOnline calls it while a stream may already be live (home.dart:930), and so do the resume path (home.dart:488) and home_map_sheet.dart:126. On native, getCurrentPosition has an 8 s timeLimit (driver_location_service.dart:25), followed by a last-known fallback. So the marker and camera can freeze for up to about 8 s even though the stream is still delivering fixes. Nothing guards against it. The effect is cosmetic and short.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand: old listener epoch N, the call sets epoch N+1, and every stream event in the meantime returns early at line 65 until line 44 re-subscribes. I did not run a test, because it needs a fake location repository with a delayed one-shot and a live stream. The web timeout claim is not verified.

The mode actually stays on, and keeps filtering offers, until 12:00. If the admin sets a 0.25 h limit, it ends at 10:15 while the sheet still says 10:25. Worked out by hand from the code.

verdicts.reason: home_map_sheet.dart:325-326 sets _destinationUntil = now + result.durationSeconds, which is the route travel time. _openDestinationDetails passes it as `until` (430), and destination_island.dart:153 renders it as tr.destinationModeUntilUntil -> 'Destination mode until {until}' (app_en.arb:70). confirmed.title: _activateDestinationMode calls _goOnline() after its awaits without re-checking that destination mode is still active, so a driver who went offline or turned the destination off during the route fetch is put online
confirmed.description: After the synchronous setup, `_activateDestinationMode` awaits `_refreshDestinationRoadRoute()` (a network road-route request) and `_fitDestinationRoute()` (341-342) and then unconditionally runs `_seedDemoDestinationTrips()`, `_maybeShowSoonReservation()` and `if (!_isOnline && !_isGoingOnline) { _goOnline(); }` (343-348). The inner helpers guard themselves, but `_goOnline` (home.dart 884-930) has no `mounted` check and calls `showDriverSuspendedSheet(context)`, `setState(...)`, `_startDriverLocation` and arms timers. If the driver turned the destination off during the fetch (island → details sheet → "Turn off destination" → `_endDestinationMode`, or the admin time limit timer at 313-318 fired) the driver is still switched online because of a destination that no longer exists; if Home was disposed during the await, `setState`/`context` are used after dispose.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver confirms a destination, the road-route request is slow, and within those seconds they open the island sheet and tap "Turn off destination". The route request returns, and `_goOnline()` flips the driver online (radar starts, offers arrive) although destination mode is off and they never asked to go online.
confirmed.evidence:
home_map_sheet.dart 341-348: `await _refreshDestinationRoadRoute(); await _fitDestinationRoute(); _seedDemoDestinationTrips(); _HomeOfferRadar(this)._maybeShowSoonReservation(); if (!_isOnline && !_isGoingOnline) { _goOnline(); }`
home.dart 884-887: `void _goOnline() { if (_driverSession.isSuspended) { IslandMessages.show(...); unawaited(showDriverSuspendedSheet(context)); return; }` (no mounted guard)
confirmed.suggested_fix: After the awaits add `if (!mounted || !_destinationModeActive || _destinationPosition != destination) { return; }` before seeding/going online (the same guard `_fitDestinationRoute` already uses at 404-406).

verdicts.corrected_title: _activateDestinationMode calls _goOnline() after its awaits without re-checking that destination mode is still active, so a driver who went offline or turned the destination off during the route fetch is put online
verdicts.reason: In home_map_sheet.dart:341-347, after `await _refreshDestinationRoadRoute(); await _fitDestinationRoute();` the function runs `if (!_isOnline && !_isGoingOnline) { _goOnline(); }` with no check of mounted or _destinationModeActive. The OSRM request has an 8 s timeout (road_route_service.dart:29,96). CoalescingMapRouteRefresh.cancelPending (coalescing_map_route_refresh.dart:41-43) only drops queued work, so the running await still completes. Path 1: an online driver sets a destination and taps Go offline during the fetch. _goOffline (home.dart:939-964) sets online false and clears destination mode. When the fetch returns, the inner helpers bail out on their own guards, but _goOnline() (home.dart:884+, no mounted or destination guard) switches the driver back online and offers start. Path 2: an offline driver turns the destination off (_endDestinationMode, home_map_sheet.dart:473-490) during the fetch and is still put online. Only _seedDemoDestinationTrips guards itself (440-443). The window is the length of the network request, so this is an edge path, but the result is that the driver is put online against their action.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: _activateDestinationMode (301-348), _fetchLatestDestinationRoadRoute and its ownership guards (352-393), _fitDestinationRoute early return (395-408), CoalescingMapRouteRefresh.request and cancelPending, _goOffline (home.dart:939-964) and _goOnline (home.dart:884-930).

verdicts.reason: After the awaits in _activateDestinationMode (home_map_sheet.dart:341-348), nothing checks again whether destination mode is still on before calling _goOnline(). _endDestinationMode (home_map_sheet.dart:473-490) cancels only the queued refresh (cancelPending), not the fetch already running (coalescing_map_route_refresh.dart:38-42). So request() still completes, up to the 8 s RoadRouteService timeout (road_route_service.dart:29). _fitDestinationRoute and _seedDemoDestinationTrips return early on their own guards, but `if (!_isOnline && !_isGoingOnline) _goOnline();` runs anyway, and _goOnline (home.dart:884-935) has no destination or mounted guard. While offline, the island middle opens the destination details sheet during that window (home_map_sheet.dart:1105), and its 'Turn off destination' button calls _endDestinationMode (destination_island.dart:186-189). Result: a driver who started destination mode while offline and then turned it off during the route request is switched online anyway. The 'Home disposed' variant is speculative, because Home is the root screen.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test test/_audit_d66dest_test.dart (deleted), built from test/widget/destination_mode_route_refresh_test.dart with a fake route repository that takes 3 s. Steps: real DriverHome, driver offline, open the picker, pick Solna, confirm. After 0.6 s, tap 'last-trip-launcher' (destination details) and then 'destination-mode-end'. Output: 'after turn off posted=[]' and then 'after fetch posted=[Radar online]'. The HomeIslandNotices.online message comes from _goOnline after destination mode had been turned off.

confirmed.title: A pick window that ends during a Match claim is never re-armed: after a network error the card keeps Match enabled indefinitely
confirmed.description: _startRadarPickWindow stores a Timer in _radarOfferTimeoutTimers and refuses to start another while that key exists (line 425). When the timer fires while the card is `resolving` (a Match claim in flight), the callback returns without adding the id to _radarOfferExpired and leaves the dead timer in the map. If the claim then ends with ClaimOutcome.networkError, _claimHomeRadarOffer only removes the match state (line 560-563), which puts the card back to `available`. It never re-checks the deadline, and no later _startRadarPickWindow call can re-arm, because the stale key is still there. The D-04 rule ('the window has one deadline… Match fades at once when the window ran out') is broken: Match stays live past the deadline until the next pause/resume clears the map. This is a different path from the known :425 finding, which is about expired offers dropped by refresh and listed again.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A Radar card has about 2 s left in its 15 s pick window. The driver taps Match, the claim takes longer than 2 s and fails with a network error. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test: 30 s after the deadline, 'radar-match-audit-card' onPressed is still enabled. The radar sound also keeps treating the card as live.
confirmed.suggested_fix: On networkError, compare _radarOfferDeadlines[offer.id] with now: mark the card expired if the deadline has passed, otherwise remove the stale timer entry and call _startRadarPickWindow. Alternatively, have the timer callback remove its own map entry.

verdicts.reason: home_offer_radar.dart:436-440: the pick-window timer callback returns early when the card is `resolving` and does not add the id to _radarOfferExpired. It also leaves its own entry in _radarOfferTimeoutTimers. On ClaimOutcome.networkError (:558-563), only _homeRadarMatchStates[id] is removed, so the card goes back to `available`. The deadline is never checked again. Every later re-arm, from _refreshRadarHomeOffers (:405-407) or _resumeOfferTimers, goes through _startRadarPickWindow, and that returns at :425-428 because the stale key is still in the map. The card builder (:1126-1133) shows RadarOfferCardState.available with onMatch live, and _radarFrontOffer (:1024-1025) and home_offer_sound.dart:24 also treat the card as open. Only a pause, which runs _cancelAllOfferTimers and clears the map (:811-814), lets the next resume mark it expired. I rated it low because dispatch still decides the claim, so a late Match cannot win a trip dispatch already expired. What breaks is the client-side D-04 window, not a money or ownership rule.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _startRadarPickWindow (:424-443), _claimHomeRadarOffer (:540-565), _refreshRadarHomeOffers and _resumeOfferTimers/_cancelAllOfferTimers (:762-818). No code path removes the stale timer key or checks _radarOfferDeadlines after a networkError. I did not run a test; the trace is enough.

verdicts.reason: _startRadarPickWindow (home_offer_radar.dart:425-428) refuses to start when a key is already in _radarOfferTimeoutTimers. The timer callback (436-441) returns without marking the card expired when the card is `resolving`, and it never removes its own map entry. On ClaimOutcome.networkError, _claimHomeRadarOffer (558-563) only removes the match state, so the card goes back to `available`. Nothing checks _radarOfferDeadlines again. The only places that clear the stale entry are _cancelAllOfferTimers (809-812) on a pause or going offline, and _dismissRadarHomeOffer (483). Output: `during claim after 20s: first=matching second=expired` and `after neterr +30s: first=RadarOfferCardState.available enabled=true second=RadarOfferCardState.expired false`. The sibling card expired on time, but 'first' kept Match enabled more than 30 s after its window ended. The api_dispatch_repository.dart:353/385 claim path can really return networkError.

confirmed.title: Re-showing the Exclusive offer already on screen restarts its countdown; the demo _directOfferTimer re-fires on every resume, so returning from any route resets the offer's time to the full lifetime (contradicts the D-04/R13-3 "time left" rule)
confirmed.description: _showOutsideRadarOffer lets an offer whose id equals the current _outsideRadarOffer through its guard (232) and then cancels _outsideOfferTimeoutTimer and calls _raiseExclusive → _startExclusiveClock, which resets the clock to 1 and the deadline to now+lifetime (251-259, home_exclusive.dart:89-93). _resumeHomeUpdates (home.dart:204-213) first restores the time left via _resumeOfferTimers → _resumeExclusiveTimeout, but it also calls _scheduleVisibleOffers, which re-arms _directOfferTimer (2.2 s) to show the demo Exclusive again (1175-1189). If the same offer is still up (e.g. the driver dismissed the Go-offline dialog, or came back from Ride history inside the 15 s), 2.2 s later its ring and pill jump back to 15 s. _seedDemoDestinationTrips (home_map_sheet.dart:458-466) and _releasePendingRadarOffers → _pendingAdminAssign have the same re-show shape.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Exclusive offer shows 9 s left; driver long-presses the radar, gets "Go offline?", taps "Stay online". The offer resumes at ~8 s, then 2.2 s later jumps back to 15 s and the Q16 miss clock runs again from scratch.
confirmed.evidence: home_offer_radar.dart:232 `(_outsideRadarOffer != null && _outsideRadarOffer!.id != offer.id) ||` | home_offer_radar.dart:251-259 `_outsideOfferTimeoutTimer?.cancel(); final arriving = _outsideRadarOffer?.id != offer.id; _rebuild(() { _outsideRadarOffer = offer; }); ... _HomeExclusive(this)._raiseExclusive(offer, lifetime);` | home_exclusive.dart:89-93 `_exclusive.clock.duration = lifetime; _exclusive.deadline = ScheduledClock.realNow().add(lifetime); unawaited(_exclusive.clock.reverse(from: 1));` | home.dart:208-209 `_HomeOfferRadar(this)._scheduleVisibleOffers(); _HomeOfferRadar(this)._resumeOfferTimers();`
confirmed.suggested_fix: In _showOutsideRadarOffer return early when `_outsideRadarOffer?.id == offer.id` (the offer is already up), so only a new offer starts a clock.

verdicts.reason: _showOutsideRadarOffer lets the offer already on screen through its guard (`_outsideRadarOffer!.id != offer.id`, home_offer_radar.dart:232). It then cancels the timeout and calls _raiseExclusive -> _startExclusiveClock, which resets the clock and deadline to the full lifetime (251-259, home_exclusive.dart:89-93), and it arms a full-lifetime miss timer (275-282). _resumeHomeUpdates first restores the time left (_resumeOfferTimers -> _resumeExclusiveTimeout, home_exclusive.dart:98-120). But _scheduleVisibleOffers (home.dart:208) has already re-armed the 2.2 s demo _directOfferTimer (home_offer_radar.dart:1175-1189), and that timer re-shows the same _veryCloseDirectOffer. So every resume while the Exclusive offer is up resets its countdown to 15 s.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test (now deleted). Go online, let the Exclusive offer show, pump 6 s, send AppLifecycleState.paused then resumed, and read ExclusiveRequestSheet.secondsLeft. Output: `shown left=15`, `after 6s left=9`, `resumed left=8`, `resumed+3s left=14`, `resumed+11s left=6`. The offer was still up about 20 s after it first appeared. `All tests passed!`

verdicts.reason: On resume, _resumeHomeUpdates (home.dart:204-213) calls _scheduleVisibleOffers. That re-arms the 2.2 s demo _directOfferTimer (home_offer_radar.dart:1175-1189), which calls _showOutsideRadarOffer again with the same _veryCloseDirectOffer. The guard at 232 only blocks a different id, so the same offer passes. The code at 251-259 then cancels the timeout and calls _raiseExclusive, and _startExclusiveClock (home_exclusive.dart:89-93) resets the clock to the full lifetime with a new deadline. This undoes the time-left restore that _resumeExclusiveTimeout had just applied (home_exclusive.dart:97-121).
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test with the same harness. confirmed.title: Dragging across the rating stars queues one 'Rating not sent' SnackBar per drag update, so SnackBars keep showing for minutes
confirmed.description: The RatingBar has updateOnDrag: true, and onRatingUpdate calls ScaffoldMessenger.of(context).showSnackBar on every call. In flutter_rating_bar 4.0.1, _onDragUpdate calls widget.onRatingUpdate on every drag update (each pointer move) and _onDragEnd calls it once more. Each call adds another SnackBar to the root ScaffoldMessenger queue (default 4 s each). The queue survives Done and popUntil and keeps showing over Home's bottom dock.

confirmed.title: Overview counts and empty-state disagree about what a 'ride' is (cancelled trips counted in some places, not others)
confirmed.description: `_periodRidesList` (line 100-111) contains every record with a `completedAt`, cancelled ones included. The overview's 'Rides' metric uses `_periodRides` (completed only, line 145), but the empty state `tr.noCompletedRidesInThisPeriod` is shown only when the whole list is empty (line 390), 'Latest rides' takes the first two of all records (line 392) and the button says `viewAllVisibleRideCountRides(_periodRidesList.length)` (line 306, 403). The All-rides summary row then says '{_periodRides} rides in {period}' while listing more cards.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A week with 0 completed and 3 cancelled trips: Rides metric '0', no 'No completed rides in this period' text, two cancelled cards under Latest rides, button 'View all 3 rides', and the All rides header '0 rides in Last 7 days' above three cards.
confirmed.evidence: line 145 `String get _periodRides => _periodRidesList.where((ride)=>ride.status==TripStatus.completed).length.toString();` — line 390 `if (_periodRidesList.isEmpty) Padding(..., child: Text(tr.noCompletedRidesInThisPeriod)),` — line 403 `label: Text(tr.viewAllVisibleRideCountRides(visibleRideCount)),` — line 448 `tr.periodRidesRidesInPeriodLabel(_periodRides, _periodLabel),`

verdicts.reason: Cancelled and no-show trips do go into history with a completedAt. Both archive callers set one: PrefsTripHistoryRepository.archive defaults `completedAt ?? DateTime.now()` (prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:188), and they are called from accept_ride_sheet.dart:273 (the next trip is cancelled and sent back to dispatch) and completion_journal.dart:170 (any terminal status). So _periodRidesList (ride_history.dart:99-111) includes them. But _periodRides (line 145) counts only TripStatus.completed, and that number feeds the Rides metric (line 330) and the All rides header (line 448, '{n} rides in {period}'). Meanwhile the 'View all N rides' button (line 403) uses _periodRidesList.length, the Latest rides cards (392) show any status, and the 'No completed rides' text (390) appears only when the whole list is empty. A period with only cancelled trips therefore shows 'Rides 0', two cancelled cards, 'View all 3 rides', and '0 rides in Last 7 days' above three cards. No document records this split as intended.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of ride_history.dart:60-160 and 304-460, the archive callers and their completedAt default, and the app_en.arb strings (lines 875-885).

verdicts.reason: _periodRidesList (ride_history.dart:99-111) contains every record with a completedAt. confirmed.title: Trips hidden with × in the Live list come back immediately when the list is reopened (hidden state is destroyed with the widget)
confirmed.description: Q17 says a trip hidden with × comes back only after `hiddenComesBackAfter` (2 min by default), and only if it is still open. The hidden set `_dismissed` and its `_comeBackTimers` live in `_RideRequestsState`. Home mounts RideRequests only while `showRideRequests` is true (home.dart:717/746) and unmounts it when the driver closes the list. Reopening creates a fresh state with an empty `_dismissed` and a new first dispatch snapshot, so every hidden trip is listed again at once. The widget test for Q17 never closes and reopens the list, so it cannot catch this.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver hides 'Hantverkargatan → Bandhagen' with × in the Live list, closes the list and taps the radar orb again 10 s later. The hidden trip is back at the top with Match enabled, instead of staying away for the admin's 2 minutes.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep the hidden-until deadlines outside the widget (on Home's state or a small static store keyed by offer id with its come-back time), and apply them when the list is rebuilt.

verdicts.reason: `_dismissed` and `_comeBackTimers` are fields of _RideRequestsState (ride_requests.dart:114-119), and dispose cancels the timers (lines 213-215). Home builds RideRequests only inside `showRideRequests ? Stack(...RideRequests(...))` (home.dart:722-751), and onCloseRides sets showRideRequests=false (home.dart:767). Reopening therefore mounts a fresh state, whose first dispatch snapshot adds every offer back with no dismissed filter (ride_requests.dart:229-237). Only radar-group trips also call declineOffer (line 125). Ordinary hidden trips come back at once, which goes against the Q17 come-back delay.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the Home mount and unmount condition and the RideRequests state lifecycle. No key, no AutomaticKeepAlive and no external store keeps the hidden set.

verdicts.reason: _dismissed and _comeBackTimers live in _RideRequestsState (ride_requests.dart:116-120), and dispose cancels the timers. Home mounts RideRequests only while `showRideRequests` is true (home.dart:722) and sets it to false in onCloseRides (home.dart:767). Home has no store of hidden trips. For a normal nearby trip, _hide only adds the id to the local set; declineOffer runs only for radar-group trips (:124-126). So when the list is reopened, the dispatch snapshot brings the trip straight back.
verdicts.repro: Ran a throwaway widget test (test/_audit_u161_test.dart, now deleted) with a shared DemoDispatchRepository: tap 'radar-offer-dismiss-nearby-1', unmount RideRequests, wait 10 s, mount a new RideRequests. Output: 'after hide: 0', 'after reopen: 1'. The test passed, so the hidden trip came back after 10 s instead of 2 min.

confirmed.title: Radar's 'N new' refresh pill counts trips that the driver's filter will never show, so Refresh adds nothing
confirmed.description: `hasNew` lights the refresh pill for any new nearby offer that is not an admin direct assign. It ignores `widget.offerFilter` (Home's `_rideAllowed`: cash rides off, ride categories, the window before an accepted scheduled ride) and ignores destination mode. The pill text `fresh` in `_header` applies the destination filter but not `offerFilter` or admin direct assigns. `_visibleOffers` applies all of them, so after the driver taps Refresh the promised trips do not appear.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A driver with cash rides switched off has Radar open. The demo or the server releases cash trips, the pill says '7 new', and tapping it adds no cards. The same happens in destination mode with off-route trips: the pill says 'New' and nothing is added.
confirmed.evidence:
ride_requests.dart:229-233 `final hasNew = offers.any((offer) => offer.isNearby && !offer.isAdminDirectAssign && !displayedIds.contains(offer.id));`
ride_requests.dart:548-553 `final fresh = _latestDispatchOffers.where((offer) => offer.isNearby && !shown.contains(offer.id) && (!widget.destinationModeActive || _follows(offer))).length;`
ride_requests.dart:135 `if (!(widget.offerFilter?.call(offer.source) ?? true)) { return false; }`
Reproduced with a throwaway test: with `offerFilter` allowing only nearby-1..3, the pill read '9 new' after the demo released its later offers, and tapping it showed none of them (nearby-4 not found).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Compute `hasNew` and `fresh` with the same predicate as `_visibleOffers`: offerFilter, admin direct assign, destination and dismissed.

verdicts.reason: `hasNew` (ride_requests.dart:243-247) checks only isNearby, !isAdminDirectAssign and not-displayed. The header count `fresh` (lines 564-569) checks isNearby, not-shown and destination, but not offerFilter or admin direct assign. `_visibleOffers` (lines 142-150) also applies `widget.offerFilter`, which Home wires to `_HomeOfferRules._rideAllowed` (home.dart:762), and destination mode. Offers that the filter rejects therefore light the pill and add to its count, while Refresh (lines 261-281) adds nothing visible.
verdicts.repro: Static comparison of the three predicates (hasNew, fresh, _visibleOffers) and of the Home wiring of offerFilter. The reporter's throwaway test result is consistent with this trace. I did not re-run it.

verdicts.reason: The pill's `hasNew` check (ride_requests.dart:240-244) and the `fresh` count in _header (:560-565) both ignore widget.offerFilter. _visibleOffers (:147) applies it. Home passes `_HomeOfferRules(this)._rideAllowed` as offerFilter (home.dart:759), so a driver with a real filter (for example cash rides off) sees a 'N new' pill, and tapping Refresh adds no cards.
verdicts.repro: Ran a throwaway widget test (test/_audit_u160_test.dart, now deleted): RideRequests with a DemoDispatchRepository (newOfferDelay 2 s) and an offerFilter that allows only nearby-1..3, then pumped 6 s. Output: 'cards before=3 pill=1 text=[9 new]', and after tapping 'radar-refresh-new': 'cards after=3'. The test passed, so the pill promised 9 trips and none appeared.

confirmed.title: On web builds without a tel: handler (desktop or non-telephony tablet browsers), the Safety toolkit says 'Emergency dialer opened' because url_launcher_web always returns true
confirmed.description: handoffEmergencyDial maps `launch()` true to EmergencyDialResult.opened, and the Safety toolkit then shows tr.safetyDialerOpened; RideCheckController.callEmergency likewise sets `_dialOpened = true` and moves the card to the 'called' state. The default launcher is `launchUrl(Uri.parse('tel:112'))`. url_launcher_web (2.4.3, url_launcher_web.dart:66-69, 112-115) documents that launchUrl 'Always returns true, except for disallowed schemes' because window.open with noopener cannot report success; on a desktop browser (or a mobile browser with no tel handler) nothing opens, yet the UI confirms the dialer opened. REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md's product-truth gate forbids claiming an action succeeded when it did not.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver using the PWA on a laptop/desktop (or a tablet without telephony) taps Call 112 -> browser does nothing or shows a silent protocol prompt -> app shows 'Dialer opened' / ride-check card advances to 'Called 112' with alertSent, though no call path exists.
confirmed.evidence: safety_toolkits.dart:87-97 `final result = await handoffEmergencyDial(widget.launchEmergencyDial ?? () => launchUrl(Uri.parse('tel:112'))); ... _showMessage(result == EmergencyDialResult.opened ? tr.safetyDialerOpened : tr.couldNotOpenDialerDial112);`; ride_check_controller.dart:166-171 `final result = await handoffEmergencyDial(() => services.launch(RideCheckServices.emergencyNumber)); ... _dialOpened = result == EmergencyDialResult.opened;`; url_launcher_web.dart:66-69 `/// Always returns true, except for disallowed schemes. Because noopener ... opened successfully.`
confirmed.suggested_fix: On web, phrase the confirmation neutrally ('Opening 112…' / show the number to dial) instead of asserting the dialer opened, or gate the success copy on `!kIsWeb`.

verdicts.reason: handoffEmergencyDial (lib/core/safety/emergency_dial.dart:2-4) maps launch()==true to opened, and safety_toolkits.dart:87-97 then shows tr.safetyDialerOpened ('Emergency dialer opened — confirm the call on your device.'). In url_launcher_web 2.4.3, launchUrl calls openNewWindow, which returns true for every non-disallowed scheme (url_launcher_web.dart:66-90, '_window.open(...); return true;'). The app ships as a web/PWA build (DECISIONS.md:79-86, REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:33). On a browser with no tel: handler the confirmation is therefore unconditional, against the product-truth gate (REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:45). The impact is small: on the main mobile Safari/Chrome path tel: does open the dialer, and the copy is hedged. RideCheckController.callEmergency (ride_check_controller.dart:150-170) records 'Called 112' before launching whatever the result, so for ride check only the _dialOpened/_dialFailed flag is affected.
verdicts.repro: Read url_launcher_web-2.4.3/lib/url_launcher_web.dart in the pub cache (openNewWindow/launchUrl), emergency_dial.dart, safety_toolkits.dart:85-97, and ride_check_services.dart:18-44 (no kIsWeb guard anywhere in lib/core/safety or the safety toolkit).

verdicts.reason: In url_launcher_web 2.4.3, openNewWindow (lib/url_launcher_web.dart:66-90) calls window.open(url, target, 'noopener,noreferrer') and returns true for every scheme that is not disallowed, and tel: is allowed. handoffEmergencyDial (lib/core/safety/emergency_dial.dart:3) turns true into EmergencyDialResult.opened. safety_toolkits.dart:93-96 then shows safetyDialerOpened ('Emergency dialer opened — confirm the call on your device.', app_en.arb:2626), and ride_check_controller.dart:170 sets _dialOpened=true. The app ships a web/PWA build (web/ directory; DECISIONS.md:79 'Safari / PWA'). There is no kIsWeb guard in the safety code, and no doc excuses this. On a phone browser, tel: does open the dialer, so only desktop and non-telephony web hit this. That is an edge path, hence low. Correction: the ride-check card moves to 'Called 112' before launch regardless of the result (ride_check_controller.dart:154-157), so that part is not caused by the true return.

Not run in a browser.
