Dial 112 manually.') into the same banner when `handoffEmergencyDial` returns `unavailable`, and `_toggleRecording`/`_shareTrip` put 'Audio recording is unavailable in this demo.' there. The failure of the only real action in the sheet (112 dial) is thus visually confirmed as success.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On a device/browser where `launchUrl(Uri.parse('tel:112'))` returns false (web, tablet without telephony), tap Contact 112 > Call 112: a green check banner appears reading 'Could not open the dialer...'.
confirmed.evidence: safety_toolkits.dart:93-97 `_showMessage(result == EmergencyDialResult.opened ? tr.safetyDialerOpened : tr.couldNotOpenDialerDial112);` and :452-455 `const Icon(Icons.check_circle_outline_rounded, color: _green, size: 17,)`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Carry a severity with `_status` (info/error) and style the banner/icon accordingly.

verdicts.reason: The banner has one fixed success style, a green 0xFFE7F4EE background and a green Icons.check_circle_outline_rounded (safety_toolkits.dart:438-456). Failure and unavailable messages are put into the same _status: couldNotOpenDialerDial112 when handoffEmergencyDial returns unavailable (safety_toolkits.dart:93-97). emergency_dial.dart:3-4 returns unavailable when launch() is false or throws. The 'Audio recording is unavailable' and 'Trip sharing is unavailable' messages also land there (:104-110). No guard or variant styling exists. REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:45 says the UI must not claim success it did not achieve. The wording is honest but the green check contradicts it.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: _confirmEmergencyCall -> handoffEmergencyDial(launchUrl tel:112) -> unavailable -> _showMessage -> setState(_status) -> the single green-check banner build at :438-470. I also read emergency_dial.dart.

verdicts.reason: _showMessage (safety_toolkits.dart:40-42) only sets the String _status. The banner at lines 438-466 always draws a green 0xFFE7F4EE background with a green Icons.check_circle_outline_rounded and has no severity variant. _confirmEmergencyCall (lines 93-97) sends tr.couldNotOpenDialerDial112 ('Could not open the dialer. Dial 112 manually.') into that same banner when handoffEmergencyDial does not return opened. _toggleRecording and _shareTrip (lines 104-110) also put their 'unavailable' messages there. A failed 112 handoff is therefore shown with a success check. The text is still correct and the user is told to dial by hand, so this is low severity.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand: confirmEmergencyCall -> handoffEmergencyDial(launchUrl('tel:112')) returns not-opened -> _showMessage(couldNotOpenDialerDial112) -> the banner build at lines 438-466 draws a const green check icon whatever the message. Checked the en arb strings.

confirmed.title: Sample accepted ride is seeded with a localized pickupDay, so its time logic silently differs by language
confirmed.description: `_seedAccepted` sets `pickupDay: tr.tomorrow` on the `ReservationRequestPreview` (line 445). `pickupAt` only recognises the English keys 'today'/'tomorrow' (driver_home_admin_content.dart:246-251), so in Swedish ('Imorgon') or French the sample ride has `pickupAt == null`. Consequences inside this screen: `_clashWith` never treats it as clashing (smart_gap.dart:88-90 returns false), so the clash filter and the 'rides hidden' note behave differently from English; `freeCancelUntil` returns null so the cancel sheet shows the generic 'free X hours before' line instead of the real time and `isLateCancel` is never true; `upcoming` (line 626-634) excludes it so Home's reminders/leave-now never fire for it. The existing test (scheduled_rides_rules_test.dart:112) only asserts the English behaviour.
confirmed.failure_scenario: In Swedish, a request whose time clashes with the sample 08:15 ride is still listed and can be accepted, and cancelling the sample ride 30 minutes before pickup is not counted as late; in English the same actions are blocked/counted.
confirmed.evidence: line 445 `pickupDay: tr.tomorrow,` — driver_home_admin_content.dart:247-249 `final day = pickupDay.trim().toLowerCase(); final offset = day == 'today' ? 0 : day == 'tomorrow' ? 1 : null;` — smart_gap.dart:88-90 `if (a.pickupAt(now) == null || b.pickupAt(now) == null) { return false; }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Seed the model with the English key ('Tomorrow') and localize only for display (`ReservationWhen.dayWord`).

verdicts.reason: scheduled_rides.dart:445 seeds the sample accepted ride with `pickupDay: tr.tomorrow`, which is 'Imorgon' in sv and 'Demain' in fr (app_localizations_sv.dart:2358, _fr.dart:2384). `pickupAt` (lib/core/admin/driver_home_admin_content.dart:237-246) only maps 'today'/'tomorrow', so in sv/fr it returns null. Then `SmartGap.clash` returns false (smart_gap.dart:88-90), so `_clashWith` (scheduled_rides.dart:522-535) never hides clashing requests; `freeCancelUntil`/`isLateCancel` (lines 510-519) return null/false; and `upcoming` (lines 626-634) leaves the ride out, so Home never schedules reminders or leave-now for it. Every other model in the app uses the English keys (driver_home_admin_content.dart:495 `'Today' : 'Tomorrow'`), so this seed is the only one that breaks. It is demo seed data, but which rules apply depends on the language the app was in when the seed was first built.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_drv95_test.dart called ScheduledRideStore.reset() after setting DriverAppTexts.language to 'en', then to 'sv'. Output: `en upcoming=1 day=Tomorrow free=2015-01-02 07:15:00.000` and `sv upcoming=0`, then `All tests passed!`. I deleted the file afterwards and `git status` was clean.

verdicts.reason: scheduled_rides.dart:445 seeds the sample accepted ride with `pickupDay: tr.tomorrow`, which is 'Imorgon' in sv and 'Demain' in fr (app_sv.arb:680, app_fr.arb:680). `pickupAt` (driver_home_admin_content.dart:237-246) only matches the English keys 'today'/'tomorrow', so in sv/fr it returns null. As a result `upcoming` (scheduled_rides.dart:626-634) drops the ride, `freeCancelUntil` and `isLateCancel` (510-518) return null/false, and `SmartGap.clash` (smart_gap.dart:87-89) never reports a clash with it. No guard normalises the day. The other rides are built with English keys (driver_home_admin_content.dart:495), so only this seed is affected. Low because it is the demo's sample ride.

Output: `95 [en] lang=en upcoming=1 [Tomorrow]`, `95 [sv] lang=sv upcoming=0 []`, `95 [fr] lang=fr upcoming=0 []`. All passed; file deleted.

confirmed.title: 'N rides hidden: clashes with your pickup' counts requests the driver would not see anyway because of their categories
confirmed.description: _clashing iterates all _requests without the DriverCategoryChoice.takes filter that _visibleRequests applies. The note at 100-107 therefore says rides were hidden by a clash when they were actually filtered out by category, and its count can exceed what is really hidden.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver drives only Comfort and accepts the 07:40 Comfort ride. The Premium 08:05 Lidingö request (never shown to them) still produces '1 ride hidden · It clashes with your 07:40 pickup'.
confirmed.evidence:
scheduled_rides.dart:553-556 `for (final ride in _requests) if (_clashWith(ride) case final taken?) (ride, taken)`
scheduled_rides.dart:544-546 `DriverCategoryChoice.takes(ride.category) && _clashWith(ride) == null`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Apply the same category filter in _clashing.

verdicts.reason: _clashing (scheduled_rides.dart:553-556) goes through every _requests item and keeps only those with _clashWith(ride) != null. It never applies the DriverCategoryChoice.takes filter that _visibleRequests uses (:544-546). _notes (:100-107) shows schedRidesHidden(clashing.length) on the Requests tab when block()==null. A Comfort-only driver (DriverCategoryChoice.off holds Premium, ride_categories.dart:61-63) who has accepted the 07:40 main ride is told that the Premium Lidingö request was hidden because it clashes. In fact it was filtered out by category, and the count can be higher than the number of rides hidden for clashing.
verdicts.repro: Traced statically: _clashing vs _visibleRequests and the _notes rendering condition. No test was run.

verdicts.reason: scheduled_rides.dart:555-558 _clashing iterates every _requests entry with no DriverCategoryChoice.takes filter, unlike _visibleRequests at 545-547. The note at 100-107 counts it as 'N rides hidden: clashes with your pickup'. When the driver has Premium off and accepts the 07:40 Comfort ride, the Premium 08:05 Lidingö request (which they would never see) still produces the clash note.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test showed the clash is real: on the testDay plan, take(demoReservationId, upcoming: true) gives `before open=2` then `after take open=0`, meaning the Premium Lidingö request is hidden by the clash. With Premium off (DriverCategoryChoice.off) openRequests is 0 (`premiumTaken=false`), while _clashing, which has no category filter, still lists it. That is read from the code at 555-558; the getter is private, so the test cannot call it.

confirmed.title: Scheduled ride cards show English 'Today'/'Tomorrow' in the Swedish and French UI
confirmed.description: `_ScheduledRide.request` (line 1134) and `_ScheduledRide.fromRoute` (line 1117) format the card time with `tr.schedSeedTime(route.pickupDay, route.pickupTime)` using the model's raw English day key ('Today'/'Tomorrow', see `_DemoReservationSet._at` and `pickupAt`'s parsing of 'today'/'tomorrow'). The app has a localizer for exactly this (`ReservationWhen.dayWord`, reservation_when.dart:89-93, used by reservation_route_map.dart:427) but these two constructors do not use it. Every real request and every accepted ride in the list therefore reads 'Today, 07:40–07:45' / 'Tomorrow, 08:15' under Swedish or French.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver language is Swedish. Scheduled rides lists 'Today, 07:40–07:45' and 'Tomorrow, 08:15' while the header, tabs and notes are Swedish; the same label is used in the details hero (line 1518).
confirmed.evidence: line 1117 `time: tr.schedSeedTime(route.pickupDay, route.pickupTime),` — line 1134 `var time = tr.schedSeedTime(route.pickupDay, route.pickupTime);` — reservation_when.dart:89-91 `static String dayWord(String day) => switch (day.trim().toLowerCase()) { 'today' => tr.today, 'tomorrow' => tr.tomorrow, ...`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass `ReservationWhen.dayWord(route.pickupDay)` to `schedSeedTime` in both constructors.

verdicts.reason: `_ScheduledRide.fromRoute` (scheduled_rides.dart:1117) and `_ScheduledRide.request` (line 1134) pass the raw model key `route.pickupDay` to `tr.schedSeedTime`. That key is always English 'Today'/'Tomorrow' (driver_home_admin_content.dart:495). The sv/fr `schedSeedTime` only fills in `{day} {time}` (app_sv.arb:916), so the card (line 832) and the details hero (line 1518) show 'Today 07:40–07:45' in Swedish and French. `ReservationWhen.dayWord` (reservation_when.dart:89-93) exists to translate exactly this and is used at reservation_route_map.dart:427, but not here. Nothing else translates `ride.time`.
verdicts.repro: Static trace from the model's day keys (driver_home_admin_content.dart:495) through schedSeedTime in app_localizations_sv.dart and app_sv.arb:916 to the Text(ride.time) widgets at scheduled_rides.dart:832 and :1518.

verdicts.reason: `_ScheduledRide.request` (scheduled_rides.dart:1134) and `_ScheduledRide.fromRoute` (1117) pass the model's raw English day key straight to `tr.schedSeedTime(route.pickupDay, ...)`. Real requests come from `_DemoReservationSet._at`, which always writes 'Today'/'Tomorrow' in English (driver_home_admin_content.dart:495). The localiser `ReservationWhen.dayWord` (reservation_when.dart:89-93) exists but these two constructors do not call it. The string is shown on the card (line 832) and in the details hero (line 1518). Rides accepted through take()/acceptAssigned() go through fromRoute, so they show the English day too.
verdicts.repro: Same throwaway widget test: pumped ScheduledRidesScreen inside a localized MaterialApp for each zone and collected the Text widgets that contain a time. Output: `96 [en] [Today, 07:40–07:45, Today, 08:05–08:15]`, `96 [sv] [Today 07:40–07:45, Today 08:05–08:15]`, `96 [fr] [Today, 07:40–07:45, Today, 08:05–08:15]`. The Swedish and French screens show 'Today' instead of 'Idag'/'Aujourd’hui'. File deleted.

confirmed.title: 'tomorrow' is dropped from the free-cancel time on the spring DST day
confirmed.description: `_timeFrom` computes the day gap as `DateTime(y,m,d).difference(DateTime(y,m,d)).inDays`. On the day DST starts, local midnight to next local midnight is 23 h, so `inDays` is 0 and a time that is tomorrow is rendered as a bare clock ('07:15') instead of 'tomorrow 07:15'. Used by `_freeCancelLine` for `schedFreeCancelUntil` in the details plan card (scheduled_rides.dart:1705) and the cancel sheet (`_CancelRulesBox`). Reproduced in TZ=Europe/Stockholm: now 28 Mar 2027 12:00, until 29 Mar 07:00 → `inDays=0`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On the last Sunday of March the driver opens an accepted ride for tomorrow 08:15. The plan card says 'Free cancel until 07:15.' with no day, which reads as today 07:15 (already passed), so the driver believes any cancel is now late.
confirmed.evidence: scheduled_rides_notes.dart:11-13 `final days = DateTime(time.year, time.month, time.day).difference(DateTime(now.year, now.month, now.day)).inDays;` — line 15-19 `return days == 0 ? clock : days == 1 ? tr.tomorrowAtClock(clock) : ...` — test: `spring: offsets now=2:00 until=2:00 inDays=0`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Compare calendar dates (`DateUtils.dateOnly` and compute the day number difference in UTC), e.g. `DateTime.utc(time.year, time.month, time.day).difference(DateTime.utc(now.year, now.month, now.day)).inDays`.

verdicts.reason: scheduled_rides_notes.dart:11-13 gets the day gap from DateTime(y,m,d) differences in local time. On the spring DST day, local midnight to the next midnight is 23 h, so .inDays is 0 and line 15 prints the bare clock instead of tr.tomorrowAtClock. freeCancelUntil (scheduled_rides.dart:516-519) is a local DateTime computed from pickupAt(_now). The wrong text reaches the plan card (scheduled_rides.dart:1705) and the cancel rules box (notes:165). It only happens on one day a year, hence low.
verdicts.repro: Ran a standalone dart script with TZ=Europe/Stockholm: now=DateTime(2027,3,28,12,0), time=DateTime(2027,3,29,7,15), using the same expression. Output: 'days=0 tz=CEST'.

verdicts.reason: scheduled_rides_notes.dart:11-13 computes the day gap as local-midnight difference .inDays. On the spring DST day the gap is 23h, so inDays is 0 and _timeFrom drops 'tomorrow' (returns the bare clock). The time source is the real local clock (scheduled_clock.dart:27 realNow = DateTime.now). _freeCancelLine (notes:32) feeds the plan card (scheduled_rides.dart:1705) and the cancel box (notes:165).
verdicts.repro: Ran a Dart script with TZ=Europe/Stockholm: now=DateTime(2027,3,28,12), time=DateTime(2027,3,29,7,15) gave 'diff=23:00:00.000000 inDays=0'. The autumn case (31 Oct -> 1 Nov) gave inDays=1, so only spring is affected.

confirmed.title: A failed 'Show traffic on map' save is dropped as an unhandled future: the switch shows the new value, nothing tells the driver, and it reverts on the next start
confirmed.description: `toggle` calls `MapTrafficSetting.set(value, _settings)` and throws the returned Future away. `set` updates `enabled.value` immediately, then returns `SettingsRepository.save`. That save throws (`StateError('Settings save failed')` or a `LocalWriteSession` StateError) when storage refuses the write. The error is never awaited or caught, so it becomes an uncaught async error (logged by `installGlobalErrorHooks`). The switch shows the unsaved value and no failure message or retry appears, unlike Sound & voice, Accessibility and Preferences, which show `_saveFailed` with Retry. On the next cold start `MapTrafficSetting.restore()` (main.dart:41) loads the old value.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On web with localStorage full (vehicle photos fill most of the ~5 MB quota), the driver turns traffic off. The switch shows Off and the trip map hides traffic for this run. No error is shown. After the next app start traffic is back on.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Await the save in the Settings row; on failure revert `enabled.value` and show a SnackBar or retry like the other settings screens.

verdicts.reason: settings.dart:270 `void toggle(bool value) => MapTrafficSetting.set(value, _settings);` drops the Future. map_traffic_setting.dart:30-33 sets `enabled.value` first and then returns `SettingsRepository.save`. settings_repository.dart:107-115 throws `StateError('Settings save failed')` when `prefs.setString` returns false, or a LocalWriteSession error from `check`. `_enqueue` gives the caller its `result` future, not the error-swallowing `tail`, so the error comes back to toggle, where nothing awaits or catches it. The switch keeps the unsaved value and nothing tells the driver. Sound & voice (sound_voice.dart:94) and Accessibility (accessibility.dart:81) show `_saveFailed`; the language row in the same file wraps its save in try/catch with a SnackBar. On the next start `restore()` loads the old saved value. The failing write only happens when storage refuses it, so this is an edge path.
verdicts.repro: Traced settings.dart:270 through MapTrafficSetting.set and SettingsRepository.save/_enqueue (settings_repository.dart:95-127), and compared with the save-failure handling in sound_voice.dart:94 and accessibility.dart:81. No test run.

verdicts.reason: settings.dart:270 `void toggle(bool value) => MapTrafficSetting.set(value, _settings);` drops the Future. map_traffic_setting.dart:30-33 sets `enabled.value` first and then returns `SettingsRepository.save`. That save rejects with `StateError('Settings save failed')` when setString returns false (settings_repository.dart:110-111), or with the LocalWriteSession StateError (line 109). Nothing awaits or catches it, so the error escapes as an uncaught async error. The switch keeps showing the unsaved value with no failure message. The language row a few lines above (settings.dart:255-262) does catch its save error and shows a SnackBar. On the next start, restore() loads the old value. No document in docs/ records this as intentional.
verdicts.repro: Traced the caller chain: toggle -> MapTrafficSetting.set -> SettingsRepository.save -> _enqueue(write). save is the Future that toggle drops. It fails whenever prefs.setString fails. No test was run because the code path is direct and has no guard.

The _Ticket built on save has no category field, toJson writes none, and the draft (including the category) is then reset to 'Trip & rider' (line 394-398). The driver's choice is lost as soon as the ticket is created and is never shown again.

confirmed.evidence:
support_inbox.dart:335-340 `final ticket = _Ticket(subject.text.trim(), message.text.trim(), 'LOCAL DRAFT', false);`
support_inbox.dart:826-834 toJson writes subject, preview, status, unread, messages only

confirmed.title: On web, if the Maps JavaScript script is blocked or fails to load, every CustomGoogleMap stays a plain land-colour box with no 'map unavailable' message (the poll is cancelled on dispose)
confirmed.description: On web `_mapsReady` starts as `web.ready`, which is false until `google.maps` is installed by driver_map_camera.js. If the Maps script never arrives (ad/privacy blocker, key referrer rejection returning an error script, captive portal, offline PWA start) the widget keeps a `Timer.periodic(50 ms)` running for its whole lifetime and renders `ColoredBox(color: MoveraMapPalette.land)` indefinitely. Nothing surfaces the failure to the driver: Home's own 8 s `_startWaitLimit` only covers the start position, not the SDK, and no caller of CustomGoogleMap can observe the not-ready state. The driver sees a flat colour where the map should be, with markers, routes and offer previews silently missing, and the DemoModeBanner/offer flow continue as if the map existed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver opens the PWA with a content blocker that blocks maps.googleapis.com -> Home shows the beige placeholder forever, 'Finding your location' resolves, offers arrive, but no map, route or car is ever drawn and no message explains why; the 50 ms timer keeps polling until the screen is disposed.
confirmed.evidence: custom_google_map.dart:273-286 `bool _mapsReady = web.ready; Timer? _mapsReadyPoll; ... _mapsReadyPoll = Timer.periodic(const Duration(milliseconds: 50), (timer) { if (!web.ready) return; timer.cancel(); if (mounted) setState(() => _mapsReady = true); });`; custom_google_map.dart:407-408 `if (!_mapsReady) const ColoredBox(color: MoveraMapPalette.land) else GoogleMap(`; driver_map_web_bridge.dart:11-17 `bool get ready { final adapter = _adapter; if (adapter == null) return false; ...}`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Bound the wait (e.g. 10-15 s) and then show a 'Map unavailable' state / retry, or expose an onUnavailable callback so Home and AcceptRide can tell the driver.

verdicts.corrected_title: On web, if the Maps JavaScript script is blocked or fails to load, every CustomGoogleMap stays a plain land-colour box with no 'map unavailable' message (the poll is cancelled on dispose)
verdicts.reason: web/index.html:40 loads https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/js with a plain script tag and has no onerror handling. web/driver_map_camera.js:615-626 polls for google.maps.Map every 25 ms with no limit, and ready() stays false while sdk is null. lib/widgets/custom_google_map.dart:273-286 polls web.ready every 50 ms with no limit, and :407-408 draws only ColoredBox(MoveraMapPalette.land) until it turns true. No caller in lib/ (accept_ride.dart:1535, home_map_sheet.dart:678/752, destination_confirm.dart:255, reservation_route_map.dart:288, history_detail.dart:78) can see that state, and nothing in lib/ or web/ shows a map-unavailable message. So when a content blocker, firewall or offline start stops the SDK, the driver gets a blank box and no explanation. Parts of the finding are overstated. The timer does not run past the widget's life: dispose cancels it at custom_google_map.dart:477. A rejected or referrer-restricted key still installs google.maps, so ready() becomes true and Google draws its own error inside the map; that sub-case does not reach this path. The waiting is intentional (code comment at :268-272, to avoid ErrorWidget over Home's overlays). What is missing is only a bound or notice. The app does not claim a success it did not get: offers still work and no map is presented as drawn. That makes it a low-severity edge-path UX gap.
verdicts.repro: Static trace only: index.html script tags, then driver_map_camera.js sdkLoaded/setInterval/ready, then driver_map_web_bridge.dart ready getter, then custom_google_map.dart initState poll, build branch and dispose cancel, then grep of all CustomGoogleMap callers and of gm_authFailure / 'unavailable' in lib and web (no matches). No test run, because the web-only path cannot be exercised under flutter test, which uses the bridge stub (custom_google_map.dart:16).

verdicts.corrected_title: Web: if the Maps JavaScript script is blocked or fails to load, CustomGoogleMap shows a plain land-coloured box with no error or retry, and a 50 ms poll runs until the widget is disposed
verdicts.reason: lib/widgets/custom_google_map.dart:273-286 sets `_mapsReady = web.ready` and, when it is false, starts a `Timer.periodic(50ms)` that only stops once `web.ready` turns true. Nothing limits how long it waits. Lines 407-408 draw `ColoredBox(MoveraMapPalette.land)` for as long as `_mapsReady` is false. `ready` (lib/widgets/driver_map_web_bridge.dart:11-17) calls `driverMapCamera.ready()`, and that returns `sdk !== null` (web/driver_map_camera.js ~624). `sdk` is only set by installSdk(), which only runs once `google.maps.Map` and `OverlayView` exist (js:614-622, its own 25 ms setInterval, also unbounded). web/index.html:40 loads the Maps script with a plain `<script src=https://maps.googleapis.com/...>` tag and has no onerror handler. So if that request is blocked (content blocker, captive portal, network failure), google.maps never appears, both polls run indefinitely, and the box stays blank. No caller can see the not-ready state: grep finds no use of web.ready outside the widget. The only related message, `mapCameraUnavailable`, comes from google_driver_camera_port.dart and needs a built map. dispose (custom_google_map.dart:477) does cancel the Dart timer, so this is not a leak past the widget's life. Part of the finding is misdescribed: a rejected API key still loads google.maps, and Google draws its own error overlay, so that case does not produce the blank box. The offline case would have no map tiles anyway. The real trigger is the script being blocked or failing to load. This is web-only and an edge path, there is no crash or data loss, and the offer flow keeps working, so severity is low.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand. No run was possible: `flutter test` runs on the Dart VM, where the conditional import resolves to driver_map_web_bridge_stub.dart, so the web branch is never exercised. Path traced: web/index.html:40 script tag (no onerror) -> driver_map_camera.js:614-622 sdkLoaded() stays false, so sdk stays null -> driverMapCamera.ready() is false -> driver_map_web_bridge.dart:15-16 `ready` is false -> custom_google_map.dart:283 poll returns early every 50 ms -> lines 407-408 draw the ColoredBox. Checked dispose at custom_google_map.dart:477 (cancels the timer). Grepped lib/ for web.ready, mapsReady and map-unavailable messages: none tied to SDK loading. None of DECISIONS.md, REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md or LOCAL_DATA.md documents this as intended.

confirmed.title: With reduced motion (and on the far-cut path) a GPS retarget that arrives during the single moveCamera await is dropped: retarget() requires _looping but _run has already captured the goal, and the controller nulls its pending pose after calling retarget
confirmed.description: `animate()` marks `_looping = true` and starts `_run`. In the `reducedMotion || _logical == null` branch `_run` reads `initial = _goal`, awaits one `_move(...)` and returns; the same happens on the `_far` cut (`await _move(destination ...); break;`). While that `moveCamera` platform call is in flight the controller still sees `_busy == true`, so a new fix goes through `_request` → `_port?.retarget(pending); _pending = null;` (driver_camera_controller.dart:732-737). `retarget` stores the pose in `_goal` (it passes the `_looping` check), but nobody reads `_goal` again: `_run` returns, `finally` clears `_looping`, the session completes, the controller sets `_busy = false` and arms a 16 ms throttle with `_pending` already null. The fix is lost until the next one, so under reduced motion the car/camera skip fixes whenever a platform round-trip overlaps a GPS event. Narrow window (a few ms per fix) but a real contract break of `DriverCameraPort.retarget` ('the in-flight animation steers toward this pose').
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver with 'reduce motion' enabled on a 1 Hz GPS trip: occasionally a fix lands while the previous moveCamera is awaiting acknowledgement; that fix never reaches the map and the camera holds the previous position for an extra second.
confirmed.evidence: google_driver_camera_port.dart:259-263: `if (reducedMotion || _logical == null) { await _move(_at(initial, initial.target), trackVehicle: true, generation: generation); return; }`; :283-287: `if (_far(from, destination)) { _flightPending = false; await _move(destination, trackVehicle: true, generation: generation); break; }`; :223-229: `void retarget(DriverCameraPose pose) { if (_disposed || !_looping) { return; } _goal = pose; ...`. driver_camera_controller.dart:732-737: `if (_busy && pending != null) { _port?.retarget(pending); _pending = null; }`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: After the single move / far cut, re-check `_goal` and issue one more `_move` if it changed during the await (or keep `_pending` in the controller until the port confirms it consumed the retarget).

verdicts.reason: I traced this and it holds. animate() sets _looping=true and calls _run (lib/widgets/google_driver_camera_port.dart:241-249). On the reduced-motion branch (:259-262), _run awaits a single _move and returns. On the far-cut branch (:283-287), it awaits _move and then breaks. The settled+first case (:310-320) also breaks right after its await. In none of these paths does _run read _goal again after the await. During that await, retarget() (:223-229) still passes the _looping check and writes _goal. Meanwhile the controller, which is still _busy, has already cleared its copy: DriverCameraController._request calls _port.retarget(pending) and then sets _pending=null (lib/core/navigation/driver_camera_controller.dart:732-737). After the await, finally (:340-345) clears _looping and the session completes. _flush then sets _busy=false and arms a 16 ms throttle (:765-770), but _pending is null so nothing is replayed. The fix is lost until the next GPS event. This is a real path for users: reducedMotion is wired to MediaQuery.disableAnimationsOf at home_map_sheet.dart:713/791, accept_ride.dart:1266 and adaptive_trip_island.dart:493. It also breaks the port contract at driver_camera_controller.dart:43-45, which says the in-flight animation steers toward the retargeted pose. The impact is small: the window is one platform round-trip, and the next fix (about 1 s later) corrects the camera. So severity is low.
verdicts.repro: Static trace only, no test run. GoogleMapController.moveCamera needs a platform map to fake. I read _run, retarget, animate and the finally block in google_driver_camera_port.dart:223-350, and _request/_flush/_invalidate in driver_camera_controller.dart:705-770. Nothing re-checks _goal after the single or far-cut _move, and the controller does not keep _pending after calling retarget. I grepped every caller of reducedMotion: and retarget in lib/ to confirm the path is live.

verdicts.reason: lib/widgets/google_driver_camera_port.dart:259-263: with reducedMotion, _run reads `initial = _goal` once, awaits a single _move and returns. retarget() (:223-229) passes the `_looping` check during that await and writes _goal, but nothing reads _goal again. The finally block (:340-349) clears _looping and completes the session. The controller (lib/core/navigation/driver_camera_controller.dart:732-737) has already set `_pending = null` after calling retarget, and _flush (:760-769) only arms a 16 ms throttle that flushes a null _pending, so the fix is lost until the next _request. The far-cut branch (:283-287, `await _move(destination); break;`) has the same gap, and so does the first-and-settled frame in the damped loop.

Output: `moves=1 lastFrame=LatLng(59.0001, 18.0)`, then `All tests passed!` (it asserted one move and the last frame at the stale target). The retargeted pose never reached moveCamera or onFrame. confirmed.title: The camera's coasted chase point reaches the car marker through onFrame, so between fixes the car icon moves in a straight line along the camera bearing (up to 21° off course) and overshoots by up to 22 m when the driver brakes
confirmed.description: Each loop frame aims at _at(goal, _coasted(goal)). _coasted extrapolates up to 1.1 s / 22 m along goal.bearing, which is the smoothed camera heading blended up to 21° toward the route ahead, not the car's course. _move calls onFrame(logical) whenever _trackCar is true (target within 25 m of goal.target, which a 22 m coast always is). AcceptRide's onFrame calls _vehicle.snapTo(position.target, …) every frame while following, which overrides the route-snapped _vehicle.moveTo(camera.vehiclePoint). The car marker is therefore drawn at the damped, coasted camera target. DriverCameraPose.speedMetersPerSecond is documented as 'Used only to coast the chase point between GPS fixes. Never the car marker.'
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver brakes hard for a light, or makes a turn while the camera bearing lags. Between fixes, the car icon keeps sliding up to 22 m along the old or look-ahead bearing, beyond the stop line or off the road at the corner, then rubber-bands back when the next fix arrives.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Publish the un-coasted vehicle point (goal.target, or the policy's vehiclePoint) to onFrame, and keep the coasted target only for the camera.

verdicts.reason: google_driver_camera_port.dart:281 aims each frame at `_at(goal, _coasted(goal))`. _coasted (:118-139) moves the point up to 1.1 s / 22 m along goal.bearing. During guidance that bearing is the course blended up to 21 degrees toward the road ahead and then smoothed (driver_camera_controller.dart:276-310), so it is not the road. _move publishes that logical frame through onFrame whenever _trackCar holds (:217-219, :184-193: follow durations of 450 ms are 600 ms or less, and the target is within 25 m). accept_ride.dart:1257-1260 then calls `_vehicle.snapTo(position.target, ...)` every frame while following in guidance. That replaces the route-snapped moveTo(camera.vehiclePoint) from accept_ride_trip.dart:696. The car marker therefore coasts off the snapped polyline between fixes, which contradicts 'Never the car marker' (driver_camera_controller.dart:33) and the 'on-route snapped' car in docs/driver-camera-architecture.md. The effect is visual: a few metres of overshoot or off-road drift, corrected at the next fix.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: the coast path (:118-139, :281), the onFrame publish in _move (:217-219), the _trackCar guard (:184-193), the snapTo consumer (accept_ride.dart:1257-1260), and how the policy builds bearing and the coast flag (driver_camera_controller.dart:276-337). No guard leaves the coast offset out of the marker.

verdicts.corrected_title: The camera's coasted chase point reaches the car marker through onFrame, so between fixes the car icon moves in a straight line along the camera bearing (up to 21° off course) and overshoots by up to 22 m when the driver brakes
verdicts.reason: During following guidance, the policy sets coast: onRoute && speed>=1 (driver_camera_controller.dart:337). On-route, the pose bearing is course + clamp(roadDelta,±30)*0.7, then smoothed (lines 279-317), so it can sit up to 21° off the car's course. In the port, _coasted moves the target up to min(v*1.1 s, 22 m) along goal.bearing (google_driver_camera_port.dart:117-139). The loop aims at _at(goal, _coasted(goal)) (line 281). For a 450 ms pose, _trackCar returns true because the frame is under 25 m from goal.target (lines 183-193). _move then calls onFrame(logical) (line 218). accept_ride.dart:1290-1293 calls _vehicle.snapTo(position.target, ...) on every frame while following in guidance. snapTo stops the animator (live_vehicle_animator.dart:47-48), so the coasted, damped camera target replaces the route-snapped moveTo(vehiclePoint) (accept_ride_trip.dart:702). This contradicts the doc comment at driver_camera_controller.dart:33 ('Never the car marker'). No guard drops the coast for the marker.
verdicts.repro: Worked by hand. Last fix at 15 m/s, then the driver brakes to a stop: the coast runs 15*1.1 = 16.5 m past the real position before the next fix pulls it back. Bearing 21° off the road direction with a 22 m cap: lateral offset 22*sin(21°) ≈ 7.9 m off the polyline at a curve. On the next fix, _goalAt resets, the coast drops to 0 and the damped approach pulls the car back. No test run, because the effect depends on real DateTime between fixes.

confirmed.title: The recenter/locate flight clock advances only by the 16 ms sleep. Time spent awaiting moveCamera is never counted, so on native platforms the 1 s flight runs longer by about (moveCamera latency / 16 ms) × 100%
confirmed.description: In the flight branch, flown advances by dt, and dt is measured from a stamp taken after `await _move(...)` returns, around the 16 ms _sleep only. The time spent awaiting controller.moveCamera (a platform-channel round trip on Android/iOS) is never added. The flight therefore lasts flightDuration × (frame time / sleep time) instead of the documented 1 s ('runs on the clock … start to rest'). The #325 measurement was taken on a release web build, where moveCamera resolves almost at once. frame() and tiltTo() in the same class use absolute elapsed time from start, so the inconsistency is only here and in the damped loop (line 333).
confirmed.failure_scenario: On a phone where each moveCamera await takes about 10-16 ms, a Recenter/Locate tap flies for about 1.6-2 s instead of 1 s, which brings back part of the slow glide #325 removed.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Measure dt from the previous frame's stamp, taken before _move, or compute the flight progress from a start timestamp like frame() does.

verdicts.reason: In the flight branch, google_driver_camera_port.dart:312-317 takes `stamp` after `await _move(...)` returns and only times the 16 ms _sleep. Time spent awaiting controller.moveCamera inside _move (:207-209) is never added to `flown`. The flight therefore lasts flightDuration multiplied by (frame time / sleep time), longer than the documented 1 s ('runs on the clock... start to rest', :102-106). The damped branch (:333-337) has the same omission, but its time constants are approximate there. How much longer depends on the platform-channel round trip (a few ms on a typical Android or iOS device, more under load), so the slowdown is real but usually small.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the _run loop (:259-338): dt is set only from `DateTime.now().difference(stamp)` where stamp comes after _move, and _move awaits moveCamera.

verdicts.corrected_title: The recenter/locate flight clock advances only by the 16 ms sleep. Time spent awaiting moveCamera is never counted, so on native platforms the 1 s flight runs longer by about (moveCamera latency / 16 ms) × 100%
verdicts.reason: In the flight branch, flown += dt (google_driver_camera_port.dart:296). dt is measured from a stamp taken after `await _move(...)` returns, and it covers only `_sleep(16ms)` (lines 308-313). The moveCamera round trip awaited inside _move (line 208) is left out. frame() measures from a fixed start (lines 437-440), so this is inconsistent within the same class. The landing frame count stays about 1e6/dt ≈ 60, but each frame takes 16 + m ms of wall time. The finding's figure of 1.6-2 s needs m of about 10-16 ms. That happens only when the platform-channel reply waits for a busy main thread or vsync. A typical Pigeon round trip of 1-5 ms gives about 1.06-1.3 s.
verdicts.repro: Worked by hand. In the existing test (test/widget/driver_camera_port_test.dart:100 'a locate flight lands in about 1 s'), the fake moveCamera returns at once and DateTime.now() is not faked, so dt = max(16000, ~0) = 16000 and the test counts frames, not wall time. It cannot see this. Wall time = 60 frames × (16 ms + m): m=0 gives 0.96 s, m=5 gives 1.26 s, m=12 gives 1.68 s.

confirmed.title: Radar sweep wedge never fades: SweepGradient with a negative startAngle clamps the whole arc to the end colour
confirmed.description: RadarWedgePainter draws the arc from -tail to 0 rad with SweepGradient(startAngle: -tail, endAngle: 0). Both Skia and Impeller compute a pixel's sweep parameter from its angle in [0, 2π), then remap it with (t - start) / (end - start). Pixels in the drawn arc (-60°..0°) have t in [5/6, 1), which remaps to [6, 7) and is clamped by the default TileMode.clamp to stop 1.0 (white at 0.6 alpha). The documented 'light wedge that fades behind its leading edge' therefore renders as a solid 60° white fan with a hard trailing edge. Worked by hand: a pixel at -30° has t_raw = 11/12, so (11/12 + 1/6) * 6 = 6.5, which clamps to 1.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver goes online. Home's radar orb shows a uniform bright 60° slice rotating around the ring instead of a soft sweep that fades out behind its leading edge.
confirmed.evidence: movera_radar_orb.dart:487-499 `canvas.translate(center.dx, center.dy); canvas.rotate(lead); ... ..shader = SweepGradient(startAngle: -tail, endAngle: 0, colors: [Colors.white.withValues(alpha: 0), Colors.white.withValues(alpha: 0.6)]).createShader(rect); canvas.drawArc(rect, -tail, tail, true, paint);`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use startAngle: 2*math.pi - tail and endAngle: 2*math.pi (the same position as -tail..0 in the gradient's [0, 2π) domain), or draw from 0 to tail and rotate by lead - tail.

verdicts.reason: RadarWedgePainter (movera_radar_orb.dart:487-499) uses SweepGradient(startAngle: -tail, endAngle: 0) and draws the arc from -tail to 0. The sweep parameter is computed in [0, 2π), so every pixel of the arc maps past stop 1 and is clamped to the end colour. The documented fading tail (:462-463) renders as a uniform 0.6-alpha 60° fan with a hard trailing edge.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_wedge_u180_test.dart painted RadarWedgePainter(turn: 0.25, inner: 10) to a 200x200 image and sampled alpha at radius 70. Output: 'deg -2 alpha 153', 'deg -10 alpha 153', 'deg -30 alpha 153', 'deg -50 alpha 153', 'deg -58 alpha 153', 'deg 10 alpha 0'; All tests passed. So alpha is a constant 153 (0.6) with no fade. The file was deleted afterwards.

verdicts.reason: RadarWedgePainter (movera_radar_orb.dart:487-499) uses SweepGradient(startAngle: -pi/3, endAngle: 0). The engine computes a pixel's sweep t in [0,1), so a pixel at -30 deg gets t = 11/12. The remap (t+1/6)*6 = 6.5 is then clamped to stop 1.0, so the whole 60 deg arc is painted the end colour (white at 0.6 alpha) with no fade. The code comment 'so the gradient never wraps' gets this backwards.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test drew RadarWedgePainter(turn:0.25, inner:20) on black into a 200x200 image and sampled the red channel at radius 70 along the arc. Output: 'deg=-2 r=153, deg=-10 r=153, deg=-30 r=153, deg=-50 r=153, deg=-58 r=153'. 153 = 0.6*255 at every angle, so the wedge is uniform and does not fade. Test deleted afterwards.

confirmed.description: The test says an on-trip Exclusive offer that is hidden and then shown again 'counts down the rest' (it resumes with the time it had left). The new timer would fire at resume + L, and the test has pumped to resume + 0.3 s + L by then, so the offer still disappears and still counts as a miss. It does `await store.save(...)` and only then `await store.clear()`, which is fully sequential. Any repository that removes the key passes, including one with no write queue at all. The ordering is actually provided by the static `_enqueue` queue in PrefsActiveRideRepository, and this test does not exercise it.

This test stays green because the save already finished before clear started. Verified by reading the code; no tests were run.

verdicts.repro: Read the test body and PrefsActiveRideRepository._enqueue, save and clear. Ran no tests.

verdicts.reason: test/core/active_ride_persistence_test.dart:134-145 awaits `store.save(...)` to completion and only then awaits `store.clear()`, so no save is in flight when clear starts. refuted.title: Paid pickup wait is added to _paidWaitSeconds only after the Waiting->OnTrip snapshot was persisted, so a crash between the two writes drops the waiting fee
refuted.description: `_advanceRide` captures `paidWait = _paidWaitNow`, then awaits `_rideLifecycle.transitionTo(onTrip)`, which immediately writes the snapshot built by `_buildSnapshot` (`paidWaitSeconds: _paidWaitSeconds`, line 39) — still the pre-increment value — and commits stage=onTrip. Only afterwards `_paidWaitSeconds += paidWait` runs and a second `persistNow()` (line 846) writes it. On restore `_paidWaitSeconds = restored?.paidWaitSeconds ?? 0` (accept_ride.dart:609) and the wait clock is no longer running, so `_paidWaitTotal`, `_fareWithWaiting` and the finish journal's `paid` amount lose the pickup waiting fee if the app is killed between the two saves (the second save can also be delayed by a pending background save, active_ride_controller.dart:73-75).
refuted.failure_scenario: Driver waited 9 minutes at pickup (4 paid minutes), slides 'Start trip'; the first snapshot (stage onTrip, paidWaitSeconds 0) lands, the process is killed before the second persistNow; after restart the trip resumes on-trip with no paid wait and the completed fare/earnings omit the 4 paid minutes.
refuted.suggested_fix: Fold the paid wait into `_paidWaitSeconds` (or into the snapshot builder) before calling `transitionTo`, rolling it back if the transition is refused, so the single stage write already carries the fee.

verdicts.reason: The two writes are not atomic, but the gap between them cannot realistically be hit. After transitionTo's write commits (active_ride_controller.dart:255-260), its future resolves through microtasks. Lines 837-845 of accept_ride_trip.dart are synchronous, and persistNow at :846 starts at once, without yielding to the event loop. So no GPS event, timer or lifecycle callback can slip a background save in between. The finding's claim that the second save 'can be delayed by a pending background save' is therefore wrong: _write would only drop it if _writing were true (:241-243), and nothing can set that here. The only losing case is the process dying during the single prefs.setString of that second save (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:155), a window of milliseconds. Any app pause also persists the corrected value (accept_ride.dart:724). That is a speculative crash timing, not a realistic path.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _advanceRide (accept_ride_trip.dart:830-846), ActiveRideController.transitionTo, _write and persistNow (active_ride_controller.dart:72-108, 236-279), and PrefsActiveRideRepository.save (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:134-158). I confirmed _buildSnapshot reads _paidWaitSeconds before the increment (:39), and that on restore _countingWait is false for an on-trip stage (accept_ride.dart:775-776). So the loss happens only if the second write never lands, and it starts with no interleaving.

But the far-pickup rule only applies when pickupKm > farPickupKm (5 km) (waiting_rules.dart:226), and no reachable offer is that far. Every RideOffer the app builds comes from demo_dispatch_repository.dart (0.5 to 3.6 km), demo_destination_trips.dart:40 (0.8), dispatch_repository.dart:67 (2.1), home.dart:410/428 (0.9, 3.3) or the next-trip demo (1.6). ApiDispatchRepository, the only source that could give pickupMeters over 5000, is never instantiated in lib/ (`grep 'ApiDispatchRepository(' lib` finds only its own constructor). A null pickupKm and any reachable pickupKm both give the same base terms, so the waiting fee and no-show terms are the same before and after a restore. This is a latent gap to fix when a real dispatch backend is wired, not a failure that can happen today.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: grep of every `pickupKm:` literal and RideOffer( construction site in lib/, the termsFor branch at waiting_rules.dart:194-238, the fromPersisted argument list, and a check that ApiDispatchRepository is never constructed.

DriverStartPosition.key ];`

verdicts.corrected_title: localDataInventory omits the home_island_hint_seen SharedPreferences key, so the 'inventory of keys' is incomplete (non-personal device flag, no privacy exposure)
verdicts.reason: local_data.dart:38-41 says localDataInventory is the inventory of Driver keys written through SharedPreferences. A grep of every prefs.set* call in lib/ shows home_map_sheet.dart:1339 (`prefs.setBool(_islandHintSeenKey, true)`) is the only writer missing from it, and clearLocalUserData's exact list (local_data.dart:123-132) does not include it. That is a real completeness gap in the record. The privacy framing does not hold: the key is a boolean holding no personal data. LOCAL_DATA.md explicitly says 'Keys that are not in localDataInventory are not removed'. The code comment at home_map_sheet.dart:1334 ('First launch only') makes this a per-device hint, so it surviving logout is arguably intended. The real defect is only the incomplete inventory.
verdicts.repro: grep of all SharedPreferences writes in lib/ compared against localDataInventory and the clear list. Read docs/LOCAL_DATA.md, test/core/local_data_test.dart and test/widget_test.dart:1804, which asserts the flag is set.

verdicts.reason: The key is written outside the inventory (home_map_sheet.dart:26, 1337-1339) and survives logout, but that is documented and harmless. LOCAL_DATA.md states 'Keys that are not in `localDataInventory` are not removed.', and clearLocalUserData's doc says keys outside the inventory are left untouched (local_data.dart:105-108). The value is a single non-personal boolean with no rider or driver data, so there is no privacy exposure. The method is commented 'First launch only' (home_map_sheet.dart:1334), meaning first launch on the device. Driver B not seeing a one-time UI hint on a device where it was already shown fits that intent, and the hint is gated by DriverRuntimeConfig.islandHint anyway. The only real gap is that the inventory's doc comment ('Inventory of Driver keys written through SharedPreferences', local_data.dart:38) is incomplete. That is a documentation nit, not a privacy or behaviour bug.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand. The only writer of home_island_hint_seen is _showIslandHintOnce (home_map_sheet.dart:1335-1341), called once from _startIslandWake. clearLocalUserData's exact list and its prefix sweep (local_data.dart:123-152) do not match the key, which is consistent with the stated policy in docs/LOCAL_DATA.md. No test run was needed.

verdicts.reason: The two facts in the finding are correct, but the defect it describes is not. The privacy issue, the claim that logout should clear the key, and the driver-B harm all contradict the documented design. (1) clearLocalUserData only removes "classified personal and recovery keys" and leaves keys outside the Movera inventory alone (lib/core/privacy/local_data.dart:106-110). docs/LOCAL_DATA.md:17-18 says the same: "Keys that are not in `localDataInventory` are not removed". The existing test pins that behaviour by asserting that a non-personal `unrelated_preview_flag` is kept after logout (test/core/local_data_test.dart:19,34). (2) `home_island_hint_seen` is a single non-personal boolean. If it were inventoried it would be class `preference` ("Non-personal preview preferences", local_data.dart:20-21), and that class is not personal or recovery, so logout would still leave it. The proposed fix of adding it to the logout clear list therefore goes against the design. (3) The hint is meant to show once per device. Its comments say "Set once the first-launch hint has been shown" (home_map_sheet.dart:25) and "First launch only" (home_map_sheet.dart:1334). Driver B on a phone that has already launched the app is not on a first launch, so not seeing the hint matches the design, and DriverRuntimeConfig.islandHint gates it anyway (home_map_sheet.dart:1336). (4) LOCAL_DATA.md's "settings" means the SettingsRepository blob and sections (local_data.dart:79-91), not this UI flag. One real gap remains. The doc comment "Inventory of Driver keys written through SharedPreferences" (local_data.dart:38) is incomplete: a grep of every prefs.set* in lib/ shows home_map_sheet.dart:1339 is the only writer missing, and the `preference` class has no records. But nothing reads localDataInventory at runtime except the test, so this is a documentation nit with no behaviour, privacy or data effect. It is not the privacy bug that was filed.
verdicts.repro: I wrote a throwaway test, test/_audit_driver67_test.dart, deleted it afterwards and confirmed it was gone. It seeded mock prefs with {'home_island_hint_seen': true, 'movera_driver_settings_section_contacts': '{}'}, called clearLocalUserData(), and printed the state. Output: "after logout: hint=true contacts=null inInventory=false preferenceRecords=0", then "00:00 +1: All tests passed!". The personal settings section is cleared and the hint flag survives. That matches the stated policy at local_data.dart:106-110 and docs/LOCAL_DATA.md:17-18, and the kept `unrelated_preview_flag` in test/core/local_data_test.dart:34. A grep of prefs.set* in lib/ confirms home_map_sheet.dart:1339 is the only uninventoried writer.
verdicts.corrected_title: localDataInventory doc comment (local_data.dart:38) omits the non-personal home_island_hint_seen preference; documentation nit, no privacy or logout defect

refuted.title: Expired Radar offers dropped by _refreshRadarHomeOffers keep their entry in _radarOfferTimeoutTimers, so the same offer re-listed later never gets a pick window
refuted.description: _refreshRadarHomeOffers removes offers in _radarOfferExpired from the list and clears _radarOfferExpired and their _radarOfferDeadlines (400-404), but leaves the fired Timer objects in _radarOfferTimeoutTimers (only _dismissRadarHomeOffer and _cancelAllOfferTimers remove them). _startRadarPickWindow returns early whenever `_radarOfferTimeoutTimers.containsKey(offer.id)` (425-428). An offer with the same id that comes back onto the deck (the demo's _showDispatchOfferAt(0..2) re-run on every _resumeHomeUpdates for nearby-1..3 which stay in the feed; a reservation re-joining via _reservationToDeck) is listed with no deadline and no timer, so its Match never fades.
refuted.failure_scenario: nearby-1's 15 s window runs out, a pending trip triggers a refresh (nearby-1 leaves). Driver opens and closes a side-menu screen; _scheduleVisibleOffers re-lists nearby-1. Its card now shows an active Match indefinitely instead of expiring after the radar time.
refuted.evidence: home_offer_radar.dart:400-404 `next.removeWhere((offer) => _radarOfferExpired.contains(offer.id)); _radarOfferExpired.clear(); _radarOfferDeadlines.removeWhere((id, _) => !next.any((offer) => offer.id == id));` | home_offer_radar.dart:424-428 `void _startRadarPickWindow(_HomeDirectOffer offer) { if (_radarOfferTimeoutTimers.containsKey(offer.id) || _radarOfferExpired.contains(offer.id)) { return; }`
refuted.suggested_fix: Remove (and cancel) the _radarOfferTimeoutTimers entry for every offer dropped in _refreshRadarHomeOffers, or key the early-return on an active (not yet fired) timer.

verdicts.reason: The cited path cannot reach the stale entry. An expired offer can only come back onto the deck through _scheduleVisibleOffers (the demo _showDispatchOfferAt timers). That function first calls _cancelAllOfferTimers(preserveClaim: true) at home_offer_radar.dart:1163, which cancels and clears every _radarOfferTimeoutTimers entry (801-804). Opening any screen from the side menu also pauses Home first (didPushNext -> _pauseHomeUpdates, home.dart:174/198), and that clears the map too. So when nearby-1 is listed again, _startRadarPickWindow finds no entry. Its _radarOfferExpired and _radarOfferDeadlines entries were already removed by the refresh (401-404), so it gets a fresh deadline. One residual path exists: a reservation that was dropped as expired, then left the dispatch feed and came back via _reservationToDeck (590-594) with no pause, offline or trip in between. That path is speculative, and the only harm would be a Match that does not fade; dispatch still decides the claim.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of every writer of _radarOfferTimeoutTimers (home_offer_radar.dart:433, 480, 801-804) and every caller of _activateRadarHomeOffer/_startRadarPickWindow (350, 372, 406, 762). Re-listing goes through _scheduleVisibleOffers (1161-1205) or _reservationToDeck (home_reservation.dart:534-544), and the first of these clears the map before re-listing.

refuted.title: A fresh Idempotency-Key is generated on every request, so a retry after a lost response is a new mutation instead of a replay
refuted.description: The contract (contract.json#headers, openapi IdempotencyKey: 'the same key replays the committed response', DriverCommand doc 'Reuse it on retry') makes the key the only way to recover from a committed-but-unanswered mutation. `_headers(mutation: true)` calls `_key()` (a random 32-hex string) each time it is invoked, and `claimOffer`/`declineOffer` call `_headers` per HTTP request with no key kept per offer/attempt. On a transport exception `claimOffer` returns `networkError`; Home/Ride requests then let the driver tap Match again (home_offer_radar.dart:559-564, ride_requests.dart:338-341), which sends the same body under a new key. If the first POST had been committed server-side (response lost), the second accept is a separate command against an offer this driver already holds; the server answers 409 (invalid_transition/conflict with the offer, status != open/claimed_elsewhere), and the 409 branch (lines 364-380) withdraws the offer locally and reports `unavailable`/`alreadyClaimed`, so the UI tells the driver the trip is gone while the server has assigned it to them.
refuted.failure_scenario: Flaky mobile network: POST /offers/{id}/accept commits on the server but the response times out -> app shows 'No connection', driver taps Match again -> new Idempotency-Key -> 409 -> island 'Trip no longer available' / 'Taken by another driver'; the trip never opens on this phone although dispatch locked it to this driver.
refuted.evidence: api_dispatch_repository.dart:178-187 `Future<Map<String, String>> _headers({bool mutation = false}) async { ... if (mutation) 'Idempotency-Key': _key(), }`; :347-351 `response = await _client.post(_uri('/offers/.../accept'), headers: await _headers(mutation: true), body: jsonEncode({'expectedVersion': version}));`; :352-353 `} catch (_) { return const ClaimResult.networkError(); }`; driver_trip_gateway.dart:101-102 `/// 16–128 characters (contract.json#headers). Reuse it on retry.`
refuted.suggested_fix: Derive/keep one key per (offerId, body) attempt (e.g. store it in a map until a definitive 2xx/4xx arrives) and reuse it on the network-error retry; only mint a new key when the body changes (the version_mismatch retry).

verdicts.reason: No runtime path reaches this. ApiDispatchRepository is never constructed in lib/; its class doc says 'nothing installs this class in the app; the demo builds use the in-process demo dispatch' (api_dispatch_repository.dart:134-135). Grep finds it only in test/round3/driver_admin_offers_dispatch_test.dart:55. The Home/Ride request screens therefore never reach claimOffer's per-request _key() (line 185) over HTTP. The scenario also depends on an unspecified server reply: what a re-accept by the same driver under a new key returns is not defined for a backend that does not exist. The missing key reuse is a valid hardening note for when the adapter is wired, but it is dormant code today.
verdicts.repro: Grepped lib/ and test/ for 'ApiDispatchRepository': no production callers, test only. Read api_dispatch_repository.dart:130-187 and 337-389, and checked contract.json:868-872 and openapi.yaml:4499-4504 for the idempotency semantics.

refuted.title: The SSE offer feed subscription has no onError/onDone handling, so a dropped stream raises an unhandled error and the feed silently dies with no resync
refuted.description: connect() subscribes with `.listen((line) {...})` only. A transport error on the body stream (connection reset, TLS error) has no onError handler, so it is forwarded to the zone's uncaught-error handler, and onDone (server closed the stream) is ignored: `_feed` keeps pointing at a finished subscription, nothing reconnects from `lastSequence` or reloads `GET /driver/offers`, and the driver's offer list stays frozen with stale open offers. The contract's realtime rules require resync after gaps/disconnects. ApiDispatchRepository is not installed by the app today (class doc: 'nothing installs this class in the app'), so this is dormant.
refuted.failure_scenario: With the API dispatch adapter in use, the phone loses connectivity for a minute; the SSE stream errors. The error surfaces as an uncaught exception (debug) and the offer list never updates again until the app restarts; offers that were withdrawn server-side remain tappable and accept returns 404/409.
refuted.evidence: api_dispatch_repository.dart:255-271 `_feed = response.stream.transform(utf8.decoder).transform(const LineSplitter()).listen((line) { ... });` (no onError, no onDone, no reconnect)
refuted.suggested_fix: Pass onError/onDone to listen; on either, clear `_feed`, schedule a reconnect with backoff using `after=$_lastSequence`, and call `_load()` to resync the open-offer list.

verdicts.reason: The code is unreachable. connect() at api_dispatch_repository.dart:245-272 is called by nothing in lib/ (grep for ApiDispatchRepository and .connect() finds only the test file). The class doc says nothing installs it (lines 134-135), and the finding itself calls it dormant. No real caller opens the SSE feed, so neither the missing onError nor the missing onDone/resync can affect the app as built.
verdicts.repro: Grepped lib/ and test/ for ApiDispatchRepository and connect(): only test/round3/driver_admin_offers_dispatch_test.dart constructs it. Read connect() at lines 244-272.

refuted.title: clearForTrip/save/handoff call jsonDecode on the raw snapshot without tolerating an undecodable value, so a corrupt snapshot makes the completion journal unrepayable and Home recovery permanently fails
refuted.description: read() and quarantineUnreadable() go through _decodeSnapshot and convert a decode failure into ActiveRideUnreadable (lines 77-83, 117-127), matching LOCAL_DATA.md ("A corrupt value is treated as missing by the readers"). The three writers do not: clearForTrip (line 290 `final data = jsonDecode(raw);`), save (line 143) and handoff (line 168) let a FormatException from invalid JSON propagate (save also does `ActiveRideStage.values.byName(current['stage'] as String)` at 151, which throws on a valid-JSON map with a bad stage). CompletionJournal._replay runs history.archive -> markTerminal -> clearForTrip(id) (completion_journal.dart:259) with no guard, so the thrown FormatException leaves the journal in prefs and makes finish() throw; every retry replays the same journal and fails at the same step. On the next Home, _restoreActiveRideIfNeeded awaits CompletionJournal.reconcile() BEFORE repo.read() (home.dart:508-514); reconcile throws the FormatException, which is caught by the generic `catch (_)` (home.dart:519) and shown as recoveryFailed, so the ActiveRideUnreadable path that offers 'Close unreadable trip' (home.dart:515-517) is never reached, _recoveryResolved stays false and the driver cannot go online (home.dart:335). Only logout (clearLocalUserData) clears it. Reproduced with a throwaway flutter test: prefs key set to '{not json'; read() -> ActiveRideUnreadable (handled), clearForTrip('T1') -> FormatException, CompletionJournal.finish(...) -> FormatException with the journal left in prefs, reconcile() -> FormatException.
refuted.failure_scenario: The movera_driver_active_ride value becomes undecodable mid-trip (truncated localStorage write on the PWA, storage corruption). The driver taps Finish: the trip is archived to history and marked terminal, then clearForTrip throws -> 'Could not finish saving this trip'; every retry fails the same way and the driver cannot leave the trip. After a restart, Home shows 'saved trip could not be opened' on every launch, never offers the unreadable-trip closure dialog, and the driver cannot go online until they log out.
refuted.evidence: prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:283-297 `Future<void> clearForTrip(String tripId) => _enqueue(() async { ... final raw = prefs.getString(key); if (raw == null) { return; } final data = jsonDecode(raw); if (data is! Map || data['tripId'] != tripId) { return; } ...`  |  :141-151 `final raw = prefs.getString(key); if (raw != null) { final current = jsonDecode(raw); ... final stage = ActiveRideStage.values.byName(current['stage'] as String);`  |  completion_journal.dart:258-259 `if (repository is TerminalRideRepository) { await (repository as TerminalRideRepository).clearForTrip(id); }` (no try/catch; journal removed only afterwards at :268)  |  home.dart:508 `final journal = await CompletionJournal(active: repo).reconcile();` precedes :514 `snapshot = await repo.read();`  |  test output: `clearForTrip() -> FormatException: Unexpected character (at character 2)` / `finish() -> FormatException; journal left = true` / `reconcile() -> FormatException`
refuted.suggested_fix: In clearForTrip/save/handoff decode the raw value with a guarded helper (try jsonDecode, treat non-Map/invalid JSON as 'not owned by any trip'); for clearForTrip that means returning without error, for save/handoff it means treating the slot as free (or quarantining it first). Alternatively have Home call repo.read() (or a cheap decode probe) before reconcile() so ActiveRideUnreadable is surfaced and the closure dialog still appears.

verdicts.reason: The mismatch is real: clearForTrip (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:290), save (:143) and handoff (:168) call jsonDecode without a guard, while read() and quarantineUnreadable() turn the same failure into ActiveRideUnreadable (:77-83, :117-127). No realistic path reaches it, though. The app writes this key in only two places, and both write jsonEncode output with one atomic setString (:156, :184). No code writes a truncated value or an empty string to it. localStorage.setItem and Android/iOS SharedPreferences writes are atomic, so a 'truncated write' does not happen. A snapshot already corrupt at startup is handled: reconcile() finds no journal (a journal exists only while finish() is running, completion_journal.dart:128-132), then repo.read() throws ActiveRideUnreadable and Home offers the closure dialog (home.dart:515-517). Traced CompletionJournal.finish/_replay (completion_journal.dart:91-133, 144-273) and Home._restoreActiveRideIfNeeded (home.dart:500-525). Read the existing tests test/audit/recovery_ownership_test.dart:27-32 and storage_integrity_test.dart N04, which show the startup corruption path is handled. No new test needed: the failure only happens after storage is corrupted from outside the app.

refuted.title: On web the last-known-position fallback throws UnsupportedError from inside the catch block, replacing the original GPS error and skipping the error log
refuted.description: `getCurrentPosition()` catches the live-fix error and calls `Geolocator.getLastKnownPosition()`. geolocator_web 4.1.4 implements that method as `throw _unsupported('getLastKnownPosition')` (geolocator_web.dart:68-71). The throw happens inside the `catch` clause, so it propagates out of the method before `vetCachedFix`, `DriverLog.error('No recent accurate GPS fix available', error, stack)` and `rethrow` run. Callers catch everything, so the screen outcome (`Location updating…`) is unchanged, but the diagnostic record of why GPS failed on web is lost and an unrelated `UnsupportedError` is what surfaces.
refuted.failure_scenario: On the PWA a timeout/permission error from the browser is reported as 'Unsupported operation: getLastKnownPosition is not supported on the web platform' with no 'No recent accurate GPS fix available' log, making field diagnosis of web GPS failures misleading.
refuted.evidence: driver_location_service.dart:37-49: `} catch (error, stack) { DriverLog.warn('Current GPS failed, trying last known: $error'); final last = await Geolocator.getLastKnownPosition(); ... DriverLog.error('No recent accurate GPS fix available', error, stack); rethrow; }`. geolocator_web-4.1.4/lib/geolocator_web.dart:68-71: `Future<Position> getLastKnownPosition({...}) { throw _unsupported('getLastKnownPosition'); }`.
refuted.suggested_fix: Skip the fallback on web (`if (kIsWeb) rethrow;`) or wrap `getLastKnownPosition()` in its own try/catch so the original error is logged and rethrown.

verdicts.reason: geolocator_web.dart:68-71 does make `getLastKnownPosition` throw UnsupportedError inside the catch, but the effect is harmless. The original GPS error has already been logged with its text at driver_location_service.dart:38 (`DriverLog.warn('Current GPS failed, trying last known: $error')`), so the diagnostic is not lost; only the duplicate error-level record is skipped. Both callers catch every error without looking at its type (accept_ride_trip.dart:620 `catch (_)`, home_map_sheet.dart:50 `catch (_)`) and show the same 'Location updating…' or failed state either way. DriverLog.sink is only a console print (driver_log.dart), with no crash reporter that would mis-classify the error. Users see no difference.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the catch block, the DriverLog sink and both callers' catch clauses.

refuted.title: DriverRealtimeEvent.tryParse throws TypeError on a non-string `kind` although it is documented to skip broken envelopes

The kind check `DriverRealtimeKind.tryParse(map['kind'] as String?)` is executed outside the try block, so an envelope whose kind is not a String (e.g. a number or an object) throws TypeError from the cast instead of returning null; only exceptions raised inside fromJson are caught. No transport calls tryParse in lib yet (only test/core/realtime_unknown_kind_test.dart), so this is dormant until an SSE/WebSocket adapter uses it.
refuted.failure_scenario: A future adapter does `DriverRealtimeEvent.tryParse(jsonDecode(frame))` on `{"kind": 7, ...}`; the call throws instead of returning null and, in a stream map/listen without onError, kills the subscription the contract expects to survive unknown envelopes.
refuted.evidence: driver_realtime.dart:147-162 `static DriverRealtimeEvent? tryParse(Object? json) { if (json is! Map) return null; final map = Map<String, dynamic>.from(json); if (DriverRealtimeKind.tryParse(map['kind'] as String?) == null) { return null; } try { return DriverRealtimeEvent.fromJson(map); } on FormatException { return null; } on TypeError { return null; } on ArgumentError { return null; } }`
refuted.suggested_fix: Read the kind defensively: `final kind = map['kind']; if (kind is! String || DriverRealtimeKind.tryParse(kind) == null) return null;` or move the check inside the try.

verdicts.reason: The code does throw: driver_realtime.dart:150 does `map['kind'] as String?` outside the try. But nothing in the app calls DriverRealtimeEvent.tryParse. The only callers are in test/core/realtime_unknown_kind_test.dart, and DECISIONS.md:75 says 'Screens do not subscribe yet'. No real input can reach the throw today, so there is no runtime path. It is a latent defect to fix before a transport adapter is written.

It printed `result=null err=_TypeError`, so the call throws instead of returning null. The file was deleted afterwards.

refuted.title: 37 bare tester.takeException() calls silently discard flow exceptions in widget tests
refuted.description: Across 15 widget test files (account_flow_test.dart x10, offer_rules_flow_test.dart x7, reservation_near_pickup_test.dart x5, radar_offer_gone_test.dart x3, d3_trip_options_test.dart x2, and one each in round3/driver_admin_offers_home_test, offer_rules_cards_test, d3_home_back_test, radar_offer_close_test, d11_home_map_keep_test, home_offer_route_test, reservation_request_popup_test, exclusive_sheet_test, home_scheduled_test, adaptive_trip_island_test) a bare `tester.takeException();` is placed before tear-down or before the real assertions. In d3_trip_options_test.dart:100-101 the comment even states the trip screen itself overflows at the tested sizes ('Layout of the trip screen itself is not what this test covers.').

Every test still passed. No exception is pending at any of those points today, including the d3_trip_options overflow the comment mentions, which no longer happens. Tests that actually cover layout still assert strictly, for example d3_trip_options_test.dart:104 `expect(tester.takeException(), isNull, reason: 'the options sheet overflows')`. So no current bug or regression is hidden. The only remaining point is that a future regression at those exact spots could go unnoticed. That is a speculative test-hygiene concern, not a failure reachable today. At most it is a cleanup: replace the bare calls with asserting ones and delete the stale comment at d3_trip_options_test.dart:100.
