verdicts.reason:
The 4.9 fallback at lib/presentation/driver/ride requests/ride_requests.dart:379 (`double.tryParse(rider.rating) ?? 4.9`) only matters if a RideOffer reaches Radar with an empty or non-numeric rating, and nothing the app runs can produce one. `RideOffer.rating` is a required String (lib/core/dispatch/dispatch_repository.dart:32). It is built from only four places:
(1) DemoDispatchRepository literals, all '4.8x' or '4.9x' (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:25-355).
(2) demo_destination_trips.dart:38, which is '4.95'.
(3) RideOffer.reservation (dispatch_repository.dart:65). This copies ReservationRequestPreview.rating, and every preview built in lib sets one: driver_home_admin_content.dart:389 '4.94', :417 '4.97', :443 '4.91', :464 '4.88', and scheduled_rides.dart:438 '4.90'. The `this.rating = ''` default at driver_home_admin_content.dart:144 is never relied on. There is no admin feed or deserializer: DriverHomeAdminConfig.load() always gives DemoReservations (driver_home_admin_content.dart:647-648), and DemoDispatchRepository seeds from DemoReservations.dispatchReservations (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:193).
(4) ApiDispatchRepository, which maps a missing riderRating to '—' (api_dispatch_repository.dart:70). The doc comment on that class (api_dispatch_repository.dart:133-134) says "No backend exists yet and nothing installs this class in the app". The only dispatch the app builds is DemoDispatchRepository (main.dart:91, home.dart:459, ride_requests.dart:174).
So the finding's scenario, an admin-created reservation with no rating, has no source in the code, and the tracer's API path is not wired in. The fallback is a latent problem for when a real backend lands, not a reachable bug. The same reasoning covers home_offer_radar.dart:952.
verdicts.repro:
Static trace, no test run, because the question is whether any source can produce an empty rating, and a test cannot show that none exists. Steps:
- grep -rn "RideOffer(" lib finds only the demo repo, RideOffer.reservation, demo_destination_trips.dart:32 and api_dispatch_repository.dart:59.
- grep -rn "rating:" lib shows every reservation and offer literal is numeric.
- grep -rn "ApiDispatchRepository(" lib finds only the class definition. It is constructed only under test/.
- grep -rn "DemoDispatchRepository(" lib finds the construction sites main.dart:91, home.dart:459 and ride_requests.dart:174.
- DriverHomeAdminConfig.load() (driver_home_admin_content.dart:630-650) always returns DemoReservations.
verdicts.corrected_title: Latent: ride panel would show an invented 4.9 rating when an offer has no rider rating, once a real dispatch backend is wired in (unreachable today)

refuted.title: Toggling the last category off is persisted and published immediately although the Save button refuses a zero selection
refuted.description: `_toggle` has no minimum-selection guard: it flips `_selected[index]`, calls `_publishChoice()` and `_persistSettings()` on every tap. Only the explicit Save button is disabled when `_selectedCount == 0` (line 465) and its border goes grey, suggesting that state is not accepted. But the auto-save has already written `selected: [false, ...]` to storage and set `DriverCategoryChoice.off` to every visible category, so `_rideAllowed`/`_offerAllowed` reject every offer: the driver can go online and never receive a ride, with the screen implying the zero state was never saved.
refuted.failure_scenario: Open Ride preferences, tap every card off (header '0 of 6 active', Save greyed), press Back, go online: no offers arrive at all; relaunching Preferences restores the all-off state from storage.
refuted.evidence: preferences.dart:178-185 `void _toggle(int index) { if (!_canEdit) return; setState(() { _selected[index] = !_selected[index]; }); _publishChoice(); _persistSettings(); }`; :465-467 `onPressed: !_canEdit || _explicitSaving || _selectedCount == 0 ? null : _save,`
refuted.suggested_fix: Either refuse the toggle that would leave zero visible categories (keep at least one on, as the Save guard implies) or make the Save state honest (allow saving zero, or show that nothing is saved).

verdicts.reason: An all-off state can be reached, but nothing in it is false. The header shows tr.prefActiveOfTotal(0, n), i.e. '0 of 6 active' (preferences.dart:317-318), and every card is drawn as off. Auto-save on each toggle (preferences.dart:178-185) persists exactly what the driver chose, and a failed write shows 'Changes not saved — Retry'. Getting no offers after switching every category off is the behaviour the driver asked for. The disabled Save button (:465-467, guard at :188) only means there is no '0 ride categories saved' announcement. It does not claim the state was discarded, and the UI never reports success it did not achieve, so the product-truth gate (REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:43-45) is not violated. The 'screen implies zero was never saved' reading is the finding's inference, not something the UI says.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _toggle, _persistSettings, _save, _buildSaveArea and the header in preferences.dart; checked test/widget/preferences_explicit_save_test.dart for the intended Save semantics.

refuted.title: The web verifier stubs MutationObserver as a no-op, so the documented 'listeners and overlays are released when their map is disposed' path in driver_map_camera.js is never executed
refuted.description: docs/driver-camera-architecture.md:77-78 and :87-89 claim the adapter releases Flutter listeners and the vehicle overlay when the map is disposed and that `tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs` covers 'listener removal'. The adapter implements disposal with a `MutationObserver` on `document.body` (`driver_map_camera.js:501-510`: `state.car?.setMap(null); overlay.setMap(null); state.callbacks.clear(); ... states.delete(id); observer.disconnect();`). The verifier's context defines `MutationObserver: class {observe() {} disconnect() {}}` and never toggles `div.isConnected`, so that callback cannot run; the only 'removal' asserted is the explicit unsubscribe returned by `listen()` (`cjs:477-479`). A regression in the disconnect cleanup (e.g. a stale `states` entry keeping a disposed map and its gesture callbacks alive across a map re-create) would pass CI.
refuted.failure_scenario: A change that breaks the disconnect cleanup in driver_map_camera.js ships green; after a Home map re-create the old map's JS state keeps calling the previous Flutter gesture callback and holding the old overlay.
refuted.evidence: tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs:72: `MutationObserver: class {observe() {} disconnect() {}}};`; :477-479: `remove(); const count = gestures; div.fire('pointerdown', [], mouse(100,100)); ... assert.equal(gestures,count,'Disposed Flutter listener released');`. web/driver_map_camera.js:503-509: `const observer = new MutationObserver(() => { wasConnected ||= div.isConnected; if (wasConnected && !div.isConnected) { state.car?.setMap(null); overlay.setMap(null); state.callbacks.clear(); ... states.delete(id); observer.disconnect(); } });`. docs/driver-camera-architecture.md:87-89: `tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs (CI): ... vehicle overlay and listener removal.`
refuted.suggested_fix: Give the verifier a MutationObserver double that captures the callback, set `div.isConnected = false`, invoke it, and assert `states` no longer serves the id (configure/listen become no-ops) and that the overlay/car `setMap(null)` ran.

verdicts.reason: This is a test-coverage observation with no runtime defect. The disconnect cleanup in web/driver_map_camera.js:502-510 is correct as written: it sets car and overlay setMap(null), clears callbacks, removes the renderer listener, runs states.delete(id) and disconnects the observer. The failure scenario is a hypothetical future regression, not a path that fails today. The document's claim of 'listener removal' (docs/driver-camera-architecture.md:87-89) is in fact exercised by the explicit unsubscribe assertion at tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs:477-479. Doc line :77-78 describes adapter behaviour, not verifier coverage. The no-op MutationObserver stub (cjs:72) is a deliberate SDK and DOM double; the doc states 'Uses SDK doubles'.
verdicts.repro: Static read of tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs:7, 60-80, 440-479 and web/driver_map_camera.js:495-510, with grep of the states.get/delete use sites (:168, :507, :628-672).

refuted.title: Final anchor/look-ahead/sheet-glide contract assertions run only inside nested queueMicrotask callbacks; script exits 0 if the chain never runs
refuted.description: Lines 607-649 wrap the last group of assertions (claim/anchor, look-ahead, sheet glide, locate view) in five nested queueMicrotask callbacks, and the only 'PASS: ...' log is at the innermost level (line 644). Nothing at top level records that the callbacks executed (no counter, no process.on('exit') check, no explicit process.exitCode set when the PASS line is not reached). If a future adapter change causes an earlier await/microtask to never resolve, or an exception inside the mocks is caught by the adapter, the script finishes with exit 0 and the CI step `node tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs` (drider-ci.yml:58) stays green with those contracts unverified.
refuted.failure_scenario: driver_map_camera.js changes so that the claim() path returns before scheduling the pan; the nested callbacks' assertions never execute; CI reports success and the look-ahead/sheet-glide regression ships to Pages.
refuted.evidence: tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs:607 `queueMicrotask(() => {` ... :619, :626, :633, :641 nested `queueMicrotask(() => {`; :644 `console.log('PASS: vector palette, ... locate view');` (only completion marker)
refuted.suggested_fix: Set a `done = false` flag, flip it after the innermost assertions, and add `process.on('exit', () => { if (!done) { console.error('FAIL: async contracts did not run'); process.exitCode = 1; } })`.

verdicts.reason: The nested callbacks cannot be skipped silently. Each queueMicrotask at tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs:607, 619, 626, 633 and 641 is scheduled by the test itself, unconditionally and synchronously from its parent (the first one at top level). None of them is scheduled by the adapter. Node always drains the microtask queue before it exits, so all five run. The finding's scenario (claim() returns before scheduling the pan) only means the pan assertion inside the callback sees the wrong camera; the AssertionError is then uncaught and Node exits 1. The assertions are test code, so the adapter cannot catch them. The script has no uncaughtException handler or exitCode override (grep count 0) and no await or promise that could hang the chain.
verdicts.repro: Read tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs:600-649 and grepped it for process.on, uncaughtException and exitCode (0 hits). In node v22.22.0, `queueMicrotask(()=>{queueMicrotask(()=>{assert.equal(1,2)})})` exits with exit=1 and an AssertionError, and the same nesting with a console.log prints 'ran'.

refuted.title: applyProjection refuses while a background save is in flight instead of waiting (unlike every driver command), and its terminal caller does not retry after the journal step, leaving an authoritative terminal unapplied
refuted.description: D-09 (comment at lines 261-264) makes transitionTo/complete/cancel/noShow `await _afterBackgroundSave()` so a command that lands during a GPS/lifecycle persistNow waits instead of being dropped. applyProjection does not: `if (saving || _disposed || ...) return false;` (line 115). Its caller _drainProjection checks `_rideLifecycle.saving` only before the journal step (accept_ride_trip.dart:301-306, 100 ms retry); in the terminal branch it then `await`s CompletionJournal.finish (archive + markTerminal + handoff, :316) and only afterwards calls applyProjection (:319). If a persistNow started during that await (GPS snapshot every 2 min at :672-677, lifecycle pause at accept_ride.dart:724, secured-next at :1206), applyProjection returns false and _drainProjection returns without clearing _pendingProjection and without _scheduleProjectionRetry (no retry is scheduled in that branch). The trip is already archived and marked terminal on disk, but the controller is not terminal: subsequent Arrive/Start slides call transitionTo -> save, which throws 'Cannot revive a terminal trip' (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:139) and the driver sees 'Trip progress could not be saved' with a Retry that also fails, until a Finish/Cancel tap reaches _yieldToAuthoritativeTerminal.
refuted.failure_scenario: With a realtime transport delivering an authoritative cancelled_by_rider / cancelled_by_admin projection: the event arrives just as a throttled GPS snapshot save begins; the journal archives the trip, but the screen stays on the live trip, every Arrive/Start slide is rejected with a 'could not be saved' snackbar, and the outcome sheet only appears after the driver taps Finish or Cancel. Only reachable with a real transport (MemoryDriverRealtime is per-screen today).
refuted.evidence: active_ride_controller.dart:111-119 `Future<bool> applyProjection(TripStatus status) async { ... if (saving || _disposed || (terminal && (!status.isTerminal || _terminalStatus == status))) { return false; }`  vs :72-76 `Future<bool> transitionTo(ActiveRideStage next) async { if (_backgroundSave != null) { await _afterBackgroundSave(); } if (_disposed || terminal || saving) { return false; }`  |  accept_ride_trip.dart:316-319 `await CompletionJournal(...).finish(... authoritative:true, next:next); if (!mounted) { return; } if (!await _rideLifecycle.applyProjection(status)) { return; }` (no _scheduleProjectionRetry on this return)
refuted.suggested_fix: Have applyProjection `await _afterBackgroundSave()` like the driver commands before checking `saving`, and/or make _drainProjection call _scheduleProjectionRetry() whenever applyProjection returns false for a terminal/released status.

verdicts.reason: The race is real in the code but cannot be reached today. The terminal branch of _drainProjection (accept_ride_trip.dart:316-319) does return without retrying when applyProjection rejects it while saving (active_ride_controller.dart:115). But it only runs for a status event from realtime. AcceptRide uses `widget.realtime ?? MemoryDriverRealtime()` (accept_ride.dart:592), and no code under lib/ calls emit or publish on it: grep for `.emit(` in lib returns nothing, and only tests inject a realtime. Without a transport, no authoritative cancelled_by_admin, completed or no_show projection reaches the screen, and the finding itself says so. Rider cancels go through _handleRiderCancelled, and when that fails the drain path calls _scheduleProjectionRetry (accept_ride_trip.dart:340-345). It is a latent hardening item for when a real transport lands, not a reachable defect now.
verdicts.repro: Traced the _drainProjection callers (accept_ride_trip.dart:254, 303, 352, 366, 900), the persistNow callers, and the MemoryDriverRealtime construction. `grep -rn "\.emit(" lib` returned no hits, so in the shipped app no event source produces status projections.

refuted.title: Settings re-runs MapTrafficSetting.restore on open; a quick toggle of 'Show traffic' is reverted in the UI while the opposite value is saved
refuted.description: `MapTrafficSetting.restore(_settings)` is fired unawaited in `initState` although main.dart:41 already restored it at startup. The restore enqueues a read; if the driver flips the switch before that read resolves, `MapTrafficSetting.set` sets `enabled.value` immediately and enqueues the save behind the read. When the read completes it overwrites `enabled.value` with the old stored value, so the switch snaps back, while the queued save then writes the driver's new value. UI and storage disagree until the next restore.
refuted.failure_scenario: Open Settings and immediately tap 'Show traffic on map' off: the switch flips back to ON; relaunch the app and it is OFF.
refuted.evidence: settings.dart:33-36 `void initState() { super.initState(); MapTrafficSetting.restore(_settings); }`; map_traffic_setting.dart `restore`: `enabled.value = saved is bool ? saved : defaultValue;` after the await; `set`: `enabled.value = value; return ... .save(section, {key: value});`
refuted.suggested_fix: Drop the restore in Settings (startup already restores) or have `restore` skip applying when a `set` happened after it started.

verdicts.reason: The race needs a tap on the switch before the Settings initState restore finishes, and in practice that does not happen. The restore is a SharedPreferences read (settings_repository.dart read(), with the getInstance result already cached after the restore in main.dart:41). It resolves within a few microtasks, long before the Settings route's push transition ends and a person can tap. The only delay is the static _enqueue queue, which waits only on settings writes already in flight, and those also finish in milliseconds. If the read did finish late, it would also report the value already stored, which matches the value already in `enabled` from startup. Divergence would need a tap in the gap of a few milliseconds before the read returns. The redundant restore is harmless.
verdicts.repro: Read map_traffic_setting.dart (restore/set), settings.dart:33-36, main.dart:41, and SettingsRepository.read/_enqueue. No caller holds the queue long enough for someone to tap first.

refuted.title: Evidence-matrix test forbids any PASS row, so recording real evidence breaks CI
refuted.description: The test asserts `expect(matrix, isNot(contains('| PASS |')))` on docs/certification/RELEASE_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md. That freezes the current all-PENDING state as a rule: the first legitimately PASSed check (with an artifact, which tool/check_evidence_matrix.py explicitly supports) makes `flutter test` fail in the verify job. The test does not verify the matrix's correctness; it verifies that no progress has been made.
refuted.failure_scenario: The team completes the layout certification, records `| PASS |` with an artifact path; drider-ci verify job fails on evidence_matrix_test and the only ways out are deleting the test or lying in the matrix.
refuted.evidence: test/audit/evidence_matrix_test.dart:17 `expect(matrix, isNot(contains('| PASS |')));`
refuted.suggested_fix: Replace with 'PASS rows must have an artifact' (or delegate to check_evidence_matrix.py) instead of forbidding PASS.

verdicts.reason: The no-PASS assertion at test/audit/evidence_matrix_test.dart:17 is a deliberate tripwire. The test is named 'release evidence matrix does not claim unproven certification' (line 6). docs/REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:49 says the matrix "stays PENDING. Device, browser, visual, accessibility, and performance PASS is not claimed." docs/FRONTEND_16_POINT_RECORD.md (F06) says "Rows were left PENDING on purpose." The matrix itself (RELEASE_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md, closing paragraph) says physical/browser/visual/performance rows stay PENDING until a human records the artifact for the shipped candidate. When the team records real evidence, it is expected to update this documented gate in the same reviewed change. That is an ordinary edit to a test that encodes a documented policy, not "lying or deleting". The test also runs tool/check_evidence_matrix.py (lines 7-10), which separately enforces that a PASS row carries an artifact (check_evidence_matrix.py:25-27). No runtime or user path is affected.
verdicts.repro: Static trace. Read test/audit/evidence_matrix_test.dart:6-17, tool/check_evidence_matrix.py:18-28 and docs/certification/RELEASE_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md (all 15 rows are PENDING). Cross-checked docs/REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:49 and docs/FRONTEND_16_POINT_RECORD.md F06, which record that the PENDING state is intentional. No test was run, since the behaviour (any '| PASS |' fails) is not in dispute; only its intent is.

refuted.title: PASS evidence accepted with any non-empty artifact string; artifact path existence is never checked
refuted.description: A PASS row only has to carry a non-empty `artifact` string; the script never verifies that the path exists in the repository or is a URL. A typo'd or deleted artifact path therefore still counts as evidence, and with --require-complete the release would be declared complete on the strength of a string. The companion script tool/check_evidence_matrix.py has the same shape (PASS requires a non-empty artifact cell only).
refuted.failure_scenario: Someone records status PASS with artifact 'docs/evidence/layout.png' that was never committed; both gates stay green and the release is signed off on missing evidence.
refuted.evidence: tool/check_frontend_release.py:46-48 `artifact = row.get("artifact")\nif not isinstance(artifact, str) or not artifact.strip():\n    raise ValueError(f"{check}: PASS requires an artifact")`
refuted.suggested_fix: Resolve `artifact` relative to the repo root (or accept http(s) URLs) and fail when the file does not exist.

verdicts.reason: Accepting any non-empty artifact string is the documented scope of the checker. tool/check_frontend_release.py:2 says "Validate candidate evidence metadata; never substitute for running checks." Even on full success it prints "review artifacts before release sign-off" (line 74). docs/frontend-completion/09-release-verification.md says "The checker cannot prove an artifact is truthful, so review the linked logs/screenshots/traces." It also says final sign-off is a human review step. Artifacts are explicitly allowed to be workflow runs (RELEASE_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md header: "a log, screenshot, or workflow run"), so they are often external URLs. The suggested repo-path existence check would therefore wrongly reject valid evidence, and an existing file still would not prove the evidence is true. The --require-complete gate is never treated as the sign-off. CI (drider-ci.yml:53-55) runs it only without --require-complete, against the all-PENDING template.
verdicts.repro: Static trace. Read tool/check_frontend_release.py:15-75, tool/check_evidence_matrix.py:25-27, .github/workflows/drider-ci.yml:53-55 (no --require-complete), docs/frontend-completion/09-release-candidate.json (all PENDING) and docs/frontend-completion/09-release-verification.md ("cannot prove an artifact is truthful"). No test was run.

refuted.title: Trip island route strip (ETA · arrival time, progress bar, percent) overflows at 320 dp wide with text scale 1.2 or more; the guidance Row at line 564 is not the culprit
refuted.description: The guidance face of AdaptiveTripIsland (the face the island opens on while a navigation banner is shown; key 'trip-guidance-island') lays out a fixed 74 px route cue plus the guidance text in a Row inside a width clamped to the available 320 dp. With the platform text scale at 1.3 the Row overflows and Flutter raises 'A RenderFlex overflowed by 22 pixels on the right'. The project's own test test/widget/adaptive_trip_island_test.dart:470-472 acknowledges this ('The route face it opens on overflows at 320 wide, text 130 %, on main too (a separate finding)') and swallows the exception with a bare tester.takeException(), so the defect is known, untested and shipped. I reproduced it with a throwaway test (since deleted) that pumped the default surface at (320, 1.3), (390, 1.3), (320, 1.0), (360, 1.3): only 320/1.3 raised, output 'AUDIT width=320.0 scale=1.3 exception=A RenderFlex overflowed by 22 pixels on the right.' then 'All tests passed!'. Drivers on a 320 dp phone (e.g. small Android, iPhone SE class) with Large text accessibility setting see a clipped banner with the yellow/black overflow stripes in debug and truncated/overlapping guidance text in release.
refuted.failure_scenario: Driver on a 320 dp wide device sets system font size to Large (1.3x). The app opens the trip island on the guidance face during an active trip; the instruction row overflows, guidance text/distance is cut off on the right, and in debug builds the overflow error is thrown every frame.
refuted.evidence: lib/presentation/driver/accept ride/adaptive_trip_island.dart:564 `child: Row(` with `SizedBox(width: 74, ...)` cue at ~574; test/widget/adaptive_trip_island_test.dart:470-472 `// The route face it opens on overflows at 320 wide, text 130 %, on\n// main too (a separate finding); this test is about the default face.\ntester.takeException();`; throwaway run: `AUDIT width=320.0 scale=1.3 exception=A RenderFlex overflowed by 22 pixels on the right.`
refuted.suggested_fix: Make the guidance Row's cue column shrinkable (Flexible/FittedBox) or wrap the text in Expanded + FittedBox(scaleDown)/maxLines with ellipsis so the face fits 320 dp at 1.3x; then change the test at line 472 to `expect(tester.takeException(), isNull)` and add a 320/1.3 guidance-face layout test.

verdicts.corrected_title: Trip island route strip (ETA · arrival time, progress bar, percent) overflows at 320 dp wide with text scale 1.2 or more; the guidance Row at line 564 is not the culprit
verdicts.reason: The overflow is real but sits in a different place than the finding says. The error points at the strip-eta Row in adaptive_trip_island.dart:837, not the guidance Row at :564. The guidance text at :634-637 is already wrapped in Expanded plus MediaQuery.withClampedTextScaling(maxScaleFactor: 1.2), so it fits. The strip Row (:837-861) has an unscaled-clamp Text for _arrivalLine() at 13 pt, then SizedBox(12), Expanded(progress bar), SizedBox(8) and Text('$percent%'). Nothing in it is clamped, ellipsized or flexible. The island's own Padding of 12+12 (:300-306) and the strip's 16+16 padding leave 264 px at a 320 dp screen width. AcceptRide places the island Positioned left 0 / right 0 (accept_ride.dart:1275-1284), so the test geometry is the real one. No global textScaler clamp exists in lib/. In release the result is clipping: the progress bar collapses and the right end of the strip (the percent) is cut off.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_c4b3_island_test.dart (deleted afterwards) pumped the existing surface() helper from test/widget/adaptive_trip_island_test.dart and captured FlutterError output. Results: 'AUDIT w=320.0 s=1.3 guidance=true errors=1 {A RenderFlex overflowed by 22 pixels on the right.}' with 'The relevant error-causing widget was: Row:.../adaptive_trip_island.dart:837:15'; 'w=320.0 s=1.2 ... overflowed by 2.3 pixels' at the same :837 Row; no errors at 320/1.0, 360/1.3 or 390/1.3. '00:01 +5: All tests passed!'

verdicts.reason: The finding points at the wrong widget. The top Row at adaptive_trip_island.dart:564 cannot overflow: it holds a 74 px cue, an 8 px gap and an Expanded, and the Expanded's text is clamped to 1.2x (line 636). The 22 px overflow the test reports comes from the strip Row `strip-eta` at adaptive_trip_island.dart:837. It shows up only with the flutter_test default font, whose glyphs are square, 1 em wide. With a real proportional font (Roboto, the Android default; the app sets no fontFamily in main.dart:151) the same surface lays out cleanly at 320/1.3 and also at 1.5, 1.75 and 2.0. Drivers on real devices do not see the overflow. The test comment at test/widget/adaptive_trip_island_test.dart:470-472 records a test-font artifact, not a shipped defect.
verdicts.repro: Wrote test/_audit_d47_test.dart, which pumps the existing `surface()` helper from test/widget/adaptive_trip_island_test.dart and captures FlutterError. With the test font: `AUDIT roboto=false 320.0/1.3 errors=1` and 'A RenderFlex overflowed by 22 pixels on the right. ... Row-[<'strip-eta'>] adaptive_trip_island.dart:837'. At 320/1.0, 390/1.3 and 320/1.15: errors=0. With Roboto loaded via FontLoader from /opt/flutter/bin/cache/artifacts/material_fonts/Roboto-Regular.ttf: `320.0/1.3 errors=0`, `320.0/1.5 errors=0`, `320.0/1.75 errors=0`, `320.0/2.0 errors=0`, `360.0/2.0 errors=0`. Result: All tests passed. File deleted.

verdicts.reason:
Two things are wrong with the finding. First, it names the wrong line. The guidance Row at adaptive_trip_island.dart:564 cannot overflow. It holds a fixed 74 px cue, an 8 px gap and an Expanded. The text inside the Expanded is clamped by MediaQuery.withClampedTextScaling(maxScaleFactor: 1.2) at :636-637. Every overflow I captured points at the strip-eta Row at :837, which both checkers also found.

Second, the 320 dp / 1.3x overflow comes from the flutter_test font, whose glyphs are 1 em wide. The real devices are not affected. The strip line is `_arrivalLine()` (:893-901), built from `_routeEtaText` (accept_ride.dart:923-929), so it reads 'N min · HH:MM'. The app sets no fontFamily (main.dart:151, ThemeData.light), so it uses the platform font. At 320/1.3 with the test font that text is 222.8 px wide, which does not fit the 264 px strip. With Roboto (Regular, Medium and Bold loaded) it is 102.7 px and lays out with no error. Roboto also gave no errors with a '125 min' ETA and with 100%, at 320 and 360 dp and at scales 1.0, 1.15, 1.3, 1.5 and 2.0. refuted.description: `_drainProjection` holds back a pending projection while `_stageTransitioning` or `_rideLifecycle.saving` is set (line 301). Unlike Finish (line 919) and driver cancel (line 1382), it never calls `_yieldToAuthoritativeTerminal`, even though `_pendingTerminal` already holds a rider cancel. When the held event is finally drained, `_handleRiderCancelled` works out `wasOnTrip = _stage == ActiveRideStage.onTrip` from the stage the app just set locally, not from when the cancel happened. Per contract.json transitions (`trip_transitions.dart:144-145`), a cancel from `arrived` is a pickup cancel, not an `end_early`. The driver gets the end-early copy for a pickup cancel: island 'Rider ended trip', or the sheet 'Rider ended the trip / {rider} cancelled while the trip was active / Keep control of the vehicle… / I have stopped safely'. The cancel event's own `occurredAt` is never compared with `_onTripStartedAt`, so a cancel delivered late over the network is mislabelled in the same way. Reachable whenever a DriverRealtime is injected (the widget's public seam; `test/audit/pending_terminal_event_test.dart` drives exactly this sequence).

refuted.description: `_submitTripCancellation` sets `_cancellationInFlight` and awaits `CompletionJournal.finish`. Afterwards `_rideLifecycle.cancel/noShow` runs. `_advanceRide` (820) only checks `_stageTransitioning || !mounted || _rideLifecycle.terminal`, not `_cancellationInFlight`. The confirm sheet has already closed, so the slide is live during the journal await. If the driver slides Start during that window, `transitionTo(onTrip)` takes the controller write lock. `ActiveRideController.cancel` then sees `saving` from a non-background write and returns false (active_ride_controller.dart:186). `_submitTripCancellation` resets the flag and returns with no message (1384). If instead the transition lands first, `cancel()` recomputes the target from in_trip, gives `cancelled_by_driver`, and disagrees with the `searching` already journalled.
refuted.failure_scenario: At pickup the driver confirms 'Cancel trip' and right away slides 'Start trip' while the journal write is pending. History and the terminal marker now say the trip was cancelled ('Cancelled by driver · reassigned'), but the trip screen stays open and goes on trip. Every later snapshot save fails with 'Cannot revive a terminal trip', and no error tells the driver the cancel did not take effect. Traced by hand through the code; nothing was run.
refuted.evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:821 `if (_stageTransitioning || !mounted || _rideLifecycle.terminal) { return; }`; :1357-1358 `if(_cancellationInFlight || _completionInFlight || _handlingRiderCancellation) { return; } _cancellationInFlight=true;`; :1384 `if (!await (noShow ? _rideLifecycle.noShow(clearSnapshot: false) : _rideLifecycle.cancel(clearSnapshot: false))) { _cancellationInFlight=false; return; }`; active_ride_controller.dart:186 `if (_disposed || terminal || saving) { return false; }`
refuted.suggested_fix: Make `_advanceRide` (and the arrive path) return while `_cancellationInFlight`/`_completionInFlight`. In `_submitTripCancellation`, set `_stageTransitioning` for the duration and pass the precomputed `outcome` to `cancel(status: outcome)`. If the lifecycle refuses after the journal has run, tell the driver and leave the screen instead of returning silently.

But the window is not realistically reachable. `_submitTripCancellation` starts only when the modal confirm sheet's future completes (line 1354). The journal step then takes a few SharedPreferences reads and writes, the history archive and the terminal marker (completion_journal.dart:91-133), which is milliseconds. To land inside that window, the driver would need a full 320px slide gesture that began while the modal sheet still covered the screen. If the slide's save does run after the terminal marker, prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:138-139 throws 'Cannot revive a terminal trip', so transitionTo returns false. In the other order, cancel() just resolves cancelled_by_driver and the screen leaves normally. The fully silent case needs both writes to overlap inside a millisecond window, so it is speculative.

Driver completion and driver cancel do the same. The released-to-dispatch branch (lines 324-338) only calls _rideLifecycle.applyProjection(status). That runs _finish: markTerminal(A) plus clearForTrip(A), with no journal and no next. _leaveAfterRelease then calls _waybills.clearNext() and pops. Dispatch still has B assigned to this driver, but B's snapshot, waybill and screen are gone, and nothing tells dispatch or the rider.

Emitting a trip_projection with status searching for A leaves storage with no active snapshot ('A: snapshot after release = null') and no history. The accepted next trip 'A-next' never opens and is not recoverable after a restart.

accept_ride_trip.dart:324-336 `} else if (status.isReleasedToDispatch) { ... if (!await _rideLifecycle.applyProjection(status)) {...} ... await _leaveAfterRelease(status);`

verdicts.reason: The failure state cannot be reached under the wire contract. A release to dispatch (`searching`/`requested`) is only legal from pre-trip stages: contracts/contract.json transitions 16/17/18 (driver cancel from accepted/driver_to_pickup/arrived) and 22 (admin `reassign` from offered/accepted/driver_to_pickup/arrived). No row releases a trip from rider_onboard/in_trip/approaching_dropoff. A secured next trip exists only while the stage is onTrip: _acceptNextTripRadar and the match timer require `_stage == ActiveRideStage.onTrip` (accept_ride_trip.dart:1219-1233), the radar only runs onTrip (1024-1028), and stages only move forward (active_ride_controller.dart:146 `next.index < _stage.index` → false). So `isReleasedToDispatch` with a secured next trip needs a backend to send a contract-violating `searching` for an in-progress trip. The finder's repro injected exactly that (A at onTrip + `searching`).

Listed contract.json transitions into searching/requested with a python script: only rows 4, 16, 17, 18 and 22, none from on-trip statuses. refuted.title: After one declined or expired next-trip offer, the trip radar still shows ON and sweeping but never offers again
refuted.description: `_denyNextTripRadar` (used by Deny and by expiry) sets `_onTripRadarDeclined = true` and puts the state back to `scanning`. `_maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer` and `_onRideCheckGate` return early while `_onTripRadarDeclined` is true, and only `_toggleOnTripRadar` clears it. The dock and island get `on: _onTripRadarOn`, which is true for `scanning`, so they keep showing the active sweeping orb with 'Stop radar' and 'Turn Exclusive offers off'. The D-05 comment says that after an offer leaves, 'Radar then looks for the next one'.

refuted.suggested_fix: Either show the radar as paused while declined, or clear the latch and keep scanning after a decline or expiry, as the D-05 resume path does.

verdicts.reason: The latch after Deny or expiry is deliberate. `_onTripRadarDeclined` is set only in _denyNextTripRadar (accept_ride_trip.dart:1247), and the existing test test/widget/trip_sheet_test.dart:176-183 taps Deny to 'let the first demo offer go by so none pops up', then asserts 'Stop radar' is still shown. The behaviour is tested as designed. The cited D-05 sentence 'Radar then looks for the next one' (trip.dart:165-167) is about the resume path, where an offer that expired while hidden does not count and does not latch. It is not about declines. The offers themselves come only from the simulated demo source (trip.dart:1108), so the dock that keeps sweeping is a cosmetic detail of a mock and not a false claim on a real path.

refuted.title: A driver cancel or no-show never ends the trip in DriverSessionController, so Home stays 'onTrip' and the driver can never go online again
refuted.description: Every other way a trip ends calls `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip()` (= `endTrip()`): authoritative outcome (line 379), release (402), rider cancel (456/469) and RideCompleted Done (ride_completed.dart:71). `_submitTripCancellation`, which runs for every driver cancel and for the no-show reason (accept_ride_panel.dart:532/1126 -> `_confirmCancellationReason` -> line 1354), never calls it. It journals the cancel, marks the trip terminal, discards the waybill and then `navigator.pop()` (1444-1446) or `pushReplacement(nextRide)` (1441). DriverSessionController keeps `_activeTripId` = the cancelled trip and `_status = onTrip`. Back on Home, `_isOnline` = `availableForOffers` (status == online) is false. `_goOnline` (home.dart:883) gets past every guard, but `beginGoingOnline()` returns early because `_activeTripId != null` (driver_session_controller.dart:129), and so does `completeGoingOnline()` (status is not goingOnline). Nothing else clears it: `didPopNext` only re-runs recovery when `activeTripId == null` (home.dart:182), and `_islandHold` returns null while `activeTripId != null` (home_account.dart:207). With a secured next trip, B's `beginTrip(B)` is refused because `_activeTripId` is still A (driver_session_controller.dart:58-61), so the session names the wrong trip until B completes.
refuted.failure_scenario: The driver goes online, accepts a trip and slides 'Cancel trip' with any reason (or 'Rider no-show' after the wait). The trip screen pops to Home. Home shows the offline dock. Tapping Go online shows the island 'online' message (home.dart:924), but after 1.4 s nothing happens: no radar, no offers, no reservation 'Leave now' (`_canStartScheduled` needs availableForOffers, so accepted rides go to the backup driver). `DrivingTimeClock` keeps counting (isOnline is true for onTrip), so after 12 h the driver is forced to rest without ever having been available. Only logout clears it.
refuted.suggested_fix: Call `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip()` in `_submitTripCancellation` after the lifecycle cancel/noShow succeeds and before pushing the next ride or popping, the same way the other terminal exits do. Add a widget test that cancels a trip and asserts `session.activeTripId == null` and `availableForOffers`.

verdicts.reason: Already fixed in the current tree. _submitTripCancellation now calls `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip();` at accept_ride_trip.dart:1469, after the lifecycle cancel/noShow succeeds and before both `navigator.pushReplacement(nextRide)` and `navigator.pop()` (1470-1476). Its comment reads 'Like every other trip exit: the session is free again, so Home takes offers and the queued trip can begin.' endTrip clears _activeTripId, so beginGoingOnline and the next beginTrip(B) are no longer blocked.
verdicts.repro: Read accept_ride_trip.dart:1383-1477 (the function has shifted from the cited 1356-1447). grep finds stayOnlineAfterTrip at lines 407, 430, 484, 497 and 1469. git status is clean, so the fix is committed (HEAD ae81ccf).

refuted.title: Driver cancel / end-trip-early / no-show never ends the trip in DriverSessionController, so Home is left permanently 'on trip' and the driver cannot go online

refuted.title: Waiting fee is dropped from the completion journal and history, so History cannot show or break down a fee the trip earned
refuted.description: The completed waybill carries `waitingFee` (the 'Includes X waiting fee' line on Ride completed). The journal record only copies tripId, riderName, fare, service, pickup, dropoff, paymentMethod, cashCollected and driverBonus. archive() has no waiting-fee parameter, and TripHistoryRecord has no field for it. After completion the fee survives only folded into the fare string. History detail shows 'Ride Cost' with the fee hidden inside it and no 'includes waiting fee' note. The earnings breakdown says 'Tips and fees: Not available' for a trip that earned a waiting fee. Once archived the split cannot be recovered.

History detail for the same trip shows 'Ride Cost 142,91 kr' with no waiting line. Earnings history shows 'Tips and fees: Not available'. Worked by hand: round(1226 x 210 / 60) = 4291.

completion_journal.dart:105-119: record map has no 'waitingFee' key
completion_journal.dart:170-188: archive(WaybillRecord(... fare: row['fare'] ...)) with no waitingFee
ride_completed.dart:175-179: `if (record?.waitingFee case final fee?) ... tr.includesFeeWaitingFee(fee)`

verdicts.reason: No money or data is lost. The waiting fee is added into the fare before the journal is written: accept_ride_trip.dart:84-90 `_paidWaybill()` sets `fare: _fareWithWaiting` (WaitingTerms.addFee). So History and earnings show the correct total. The only thing missing is a separate 'includes waiting fee' line. 'Tips and fees: Not available' at ride_history.dart:615 is a fixed placeholder that appears for every period, whether or not a trip had a fee. It does not claim a wrong value. No contract or document asks local History to show the fee split (contracts mention a waiting fare-line code only for the backend). This is a missing feature, not a defect.

refuted.title: A journal whose cancellation fields have the wrong type is never quarantined; replay fails forever and blocks every later trip finish and Home recovery
refuted.description: `_DecodedJournal.parse` is documented as 'Any type or schema problem throws before a single side effect is applied', and only parse errors are quarantined (lines 150-163). But parse never checks the types of `cancellation.actor` or `cancellation.reasonCode`. `_replay` then casts them: `(data['cancellation'] as Map)['actor'] as String?`, `['reasonCode'] as String?` (199, 202) and `cancellationMap?['reasonCode'] as String?` (216-217). A non-string value throws TypeError outside the quarantine try, so the journal stays stored. Every `finish()` first replays an existing journal (lines 94-96) and throws, so every later completion or cancel fails ('Could not finish saving this trip'). Home's `reconcile()` throws as well, so `_restoreActiveRideIfNeeded` lands in its catch, `_recoveryResolved` stays false and `_goOnline` refuses with 'finish or close saved trip'. This contradicts LOCAL_DATA.md: 'A corrupt value is treated as missing by the readers'.
refuted.failure_scenario: A stored journal has `"cancellation":{"actor":"driver","reasonCode":7}` (hand-edited localStorage, or a writer bug). On every start Home shows 'Saved trip could not be opened · Retry', Retry fails the same way, and the driver can never go online. Every trip already in progress also fails to finish or cancel.
refuted.evidence:
completion_journal.dart:150-163  try { entry = _DecodedJournal.parse(raw); } catch (error) { await LocalQuarantine.store(...); ... return JournalReplayOutcome.quarantinedCorrupt; }
:198-203  cancellationActor: data['cancellation'] is Map ? (data['cancellation'] as Map)['actor'] as String? : null,
          cancellationReasonCode: data['cancellation'] is Map ? (data['cancellation'] as Map)['reasonCode'] as String? : null,
:324-331  parse only checks cancellation['actor'] == 'driver' for released statuses
refuted.suggested_fix: Validate the `cancellation` map's field types inside `_DecodedJournal.parse` (so a bad value is quarantined), or wrap the whole of `_replay` so an unexpected decode error quarantines the entry instead of propagating.

verdicts.reason: The only writer cannot produce this state. The only writer of the key is finish(), at completion_journal.dart:82-132. It writes `cancellation.reasonCode` and `actor` only from `String?` parameters (`cancellationActor ?? 'unknown'`), so they are always strings. A non-string value needs hand-edited SharedPreferences or a writer bug that does not exist. Nothing in the app produces that input. The cast gap at :198-203 / :216-217 is real in principle, but it is only defensive hardening. There is no runtime path to it.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: grepped for writers of the journal key (only finish()); finish's signature types cancellationReasonCode/cancellationActor as String?. No test run.

refuted.title: After a restart, a restored trip filters next-trip offers by its destination with no time limit
refuted.description: AcceptRide.fromPersisted restores destinationModeActive, the address and the point from the snapshot (accept_ride.dart:288-290). The restarted process has a fresh DestinationModeSession, so _activeSince is null and _timedOut is false. timeLeft() returns null, and expired() is false because null != Duration.zero. OnTripDestination.follows therefore keeps applying the destination filter, along a straight line because routeTo() is empty, indefinitely. The admin time limit, which otherwise turns the filter off after it expires, can no longer apply. The flag is also copied to every secured next trip (accept_ride_trip.dart:954-956, 973-975).
refuted.failure_scenario: At 08:00 the driver sets a destination (2 h limit) and accepts a trip. The browser tab is killed at 09:50 and reopened at 10:30, inside the 6 h freshness window. The trip restores with destination mode on. Although the limit ended at 10:00, next-trip offers whose drop-off is not toward the old destination are still suppressed, and that carries into the next secured trip. Worked out from the code.
refuted.suggested_fix: Persist the destination's start time in the snapshot and restore it into DestinationModeSession, or treat a restored destination whose start time is unknown or past the limit as expired.

verdicts.reason: The claimed harm, real next-trip offers being held back by a stale filter, cannot happen. The only path to the filter is _presentOnTripOffer (accept_ride_trip.dart:1155). While destination mode is on, the one offer it checks is built by _onTripRadarOfferForDestination (accept_ride_trip.dart:1060-1080) with dropoffPosition = the destination itself. Offers here are simulated (comment at accept_ride_trip.dart:1109); no other offer reaches this filter. With the drop-off on the destination, DestinationFilter.follows (destination_filter.dart:34-47) passes for focus 'final destination' and 'both'. For focus 'on the way' it rejects the offer whether or not the session has expired, because nearFinal is true. That is a separate quirk and does not depend on the restart. The trip screen also never turns destination mode off when the time limit ends; it has no timer for it, only Home does (home_map_sheet.dart:312-318). So a restart does not change what the driver sees.
verdicts.repro: Traced every caller of OnTripDestination.follows: the only one is _dropoffFollowsDestination (accept_ride_trip.dart:1050), called only from _presentOnTripOffer (:1155). Read how that offer is built (:1060-1080) and checked DestinationFilter.follows with dropoff == destination.

refuted.title: Recenter or auto-resume during a GPS outage switches the trip to 'following' but never moves the camera
refuted.description: recenter() sets _mode = following, cancels the resume timer, then calls _request. _request returns early when the last location is older than 30 s (isUsableAt). The map stays where the driver panned. Meanwhile the screen treats the camera as following: _exitBrowse stops the browse pulse and springs the sheet back, the map padding and anchor switch to the 0.75 driving anchor, and the 12 s auto-resume (onAutoResume calls _exitBrowse) does the same on its own. locate() also latches _policy._locating, so the next fix, possibly minutes later, flies to the locate zoom unexpectedly.
refuted.failure_scenario: In a tunnel with no fixes for over 30 s, the driver pans the map and taps Recenter. The pulse disappears and the map shifts with the padding change but stays on the panned area, not the car, until GPS returns and the camera suddenly jumps. Verified by reading the code; not run.
refuted.evidence: driver_camera_controller.dart:599-608 `void recenter() { ... _mode = DriverCameraMode.following; _resumeTimer?.cancel(); ... _request(immediate: true); }` ; 713-716 `if (!_canFollow || location == null || !location.isUsableAt(_now())) { return; }` ; accept_ride.dart:1236-1237 `cameraAnchor: _camera.isGuidance && _camera.mode == DriverCameraMode.following ? .75 : .5`
refuted.suggested_fix: When there is no usable fix, recenter to the last known pose (or keep browse mode and show the location warning) instead of switching mode without moving.

verdicts.reason: Waiting for a usable fix after recenter is intended. _request skips moving the camera when the last fix is unusable (driver_camera_controller.dart:715). That fix is unusable when it is older than 30 s or less accurate than 50 m (driver_location_repository.dart:48-66), so following a stale pose is deliberately refused. The pose builder says so: 'A locate that waited for a usable fix still flies' (driver_camera_controller.dart:333-335). The camera stays in following mode and goes to the car on the first usable fix. The suggested fix, flying to a last pose older than 30 s, is what the freshness gate exists to prevent. What remains is a padding/anchor change with no camera move during a GPS outage, which is cosmetic.
verdicts.repro: Read recenter/locate (:592-608), _request (:713-716), the policy comment at :333-335, isUsableAt, and the trip-screen callers _exitBrowse and onAutoResume (accept_ride_trip.dart:803-827).

refuted.title: Answering 'No' to 'Is the car in a safe place?' or 'Is the other person OK?' never reaches the safety alert
refuted.description: RideCheckQuestion.updatesAlert only forwards 'Yes' and 'Not sure' (or every answer when alerts:true, which only whoNeedsHelp sets). For carSafe and otherPersonOk the question is phrased the other way round, so 'No' is the dangerous answer: the car is not in a safe place, or the other person is not OK. RideCheckController.answer (ride_check_controller.dart:199) queues services.alerts.update only when updatesAlert is true, so these answers are saved to the trip record but never sent to admin or Dispatch. Meanwhile the harmless 'Yes' (the car is safe, the other person is OK) is sent. The authors saw this polarity problem for whoNeedsHelp ('Any answer updates the alert, not only Yes or Not sure') but not for these two questions. The existing tests check this rule as written (test/core/ride_check_test.dart:422), so they cannot catch it.
refuted.failure_scenario: The driver reports 'Accident or collision', then answers 'Is the car in a safe place?' -> No and 'Is the other person OK?' -> No. The safety team's alert only says 'Accident or collision', with no sign that the car is in an unsafe spot or that the other party is hurt. If the driver had answered that everything was fine ('Yes'), those answers would have been sent.
refuted.evidence:
ride_check.dart:189 `static const carSafe = RideCheckQuestion('Is the car in a safe place?', [yes, no]);`
ride_check.dart:193 `static const otherPersonOk = RideCheckQuestion('Is the other person OK?', [yes, no, notSure]);`
ride_check.dart:213 `bool updatesAlert(String answer) => alerts || answer == yes || answer == notSure;`
ride_check_controller.dart:199 `if (_topic?.red == true && question.updatesAlert(option)) { _queueAlert(...update...) }`
Throwaway test: open, choose(accident), answer anyoneHurt 'No', carSafe 'No', otherPersonOk 'No' -> printed `alert answers: [Ride check=Accident or collision]`
refuted.suggested_fix: Define the alarming answers for each question (for example, carSafe and otherPersonOk alert on No and Not sure), or forward every follow-up answer on red topics.

verdicts.reason: The rule that only 'Yes' or 'Not sure' updates the alert is the shared RC4 spec, applied the same way in both apps, not an oversight. The rider app states it at /home/user/movera-rider-app/lib/features/safety/domain/ride_check_questions.dart:39-48 for the same questions ('Is the car in a safe place?' at :202-203, 'Is the other person OK?' at :208). The rider contract /home/user/movera-rider-app/docs/API_V1_MOCK.md:122 says 'a later Yes / Not sure for the same checkId updates that alert. Every answer (OK or not) is kept for admin's Ride check log.' The driver side encodes the same rule on purpose: ride_check.dart:212-213 and test/core/ride_check_test.dart:421-439 ('Yes and Not sure update the alert; No does not', with carSafe 'No' expected not to update). The accident row is red, so the alert has already gone to admin and Dispatch at once (ride_check_controller.dart:187). The 'No' answers are still saved to the trip record (the same test expects 4 saved answers). Whether 'No' should also update the alert is a product question about the spec, not a code defect.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of RideCheckController.choose/answer (ride_check_controller.dart:181-203) and RideCheckQuestion.updatesAlert, compared with the rider app's RC4 implementation, the rider API_V1_MOCK.md contract, and the existing driver test that asserts this behaviour.

refuted.title: Not a bug: the inbox rebuilds on pop because pushSingle's ModalRoute.of(context) makes it depend on the route's status
