refuted.suggested_fix: await pushSingle(...) and then call setState(() {}) when mounted, or make the tickets a ValueNotifier that the list listens to.

verdicts.reason: _open (support_inbox.dart:427-437) calls pushSingle without awaiting it and never calls setState after the route returns. _ConversationState.saveMessage changes widget.ticket.preview inside the conversation's own setState (support_inbox.dart:~670-676). The build of the inbox and of _TicketCard depends on no inherited widget that changes on pop, so the Text(ticket.preview) widget is never rebuilt and keeps the old string.
verdicts.repro: Wrote test/_audit_u172_test.dart with a stub LocalSupportRepository returning ticket 'Fare wrong' with preview 'Rider paid cash'. It opens the ticket, enters 'Here is the receipt', taps local-reply-save, then pageBack. Output: 'OLD=1 NEW=0', 'All tests passed!' (the stale preview is still shown and the new one is absent). The file was deleted afterwards.

verdicts.reason: In a real run, the inbox card shows the new preview after Back. Something rebuilds the inbox route when the conversation pops; the card reads ticket.preview at support_inbox.dart:604, and the conversation mutates that same object at :675-678. So the stale preview described in the finding does not happen.
verdicts.repro: Wrote test/_audit_u172_support_test.dart: a seeded ticket 'Fare wrong' with preview 'Rider paid cash'; the test opens it, saves 'Here is the receipt' with local-reply-save, then pops. Output: "saved: [...preview: Here is the receipt...]", "old preview shown: 0", "new preview shown: 1", "All tests passed!". Deleted the file afterwards.

verdicts.reason: The finding rests on the claim that the inbox depends on no InheritedWidget that changes on pop, and that claim is false. _open (support_inbox.dart:432) calls pushSingle with the inbox State's own context. pushSingle runs `ModalRoute.of(context)?.isCurrent` first (lib/widgets/single_route_entry.dart:11). ModalRoute.of calls InheritedModel.inheritFrom<_ModalScopeStatus>(context, aspect: null) (/opt/flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/routes.dart:1316-1317). With a null aspect, the SupportInboxScreen element becomes a dependent that is notified on every change. When the conversation route pops, the inbox route's isCurrent goes from false to true, so _ModalScopeStatus.updateShouldNotify returns true (routes.dart:1032-1038). That marks the inbox element for a rebuild even though its page widget is cached. The rebuild makes new _TicketCard widgets, and they re-read the same _Ticket object that _ConversationState.saveMessage changed (support_inbox.dart:675-678). The card's Text(ticket.preview) at support_inbox.dart:604 therefore shows the new reply. The tracer's opposite result most likely came from a stub where the save did not succeed: on failure, saveMessage puts previousPreview back at support_inbox.dart:690-691. My own run, with a stub whose update succeeds, shows the new preview after Back.
verdicts.repro: I wrote test/_audit_u172_decider_test.dart. Its LocalSupportRepository subclass returns the ticket 'Fare wrong' (preview 'Rider paid cash'), and its update() succeeds and records the value. The test pumps MaterialApp(home: SupportInboxScreen(repository: repo)) and taps 'Fare wrong'. It then enters 'Here is the receipt', taps ValueKey('local-reply-save'), calls pumpAndSettle, then tester.pageBack() and pumpAndSettle again. Output: "saved: [[{subject: Fare wrong, preview: Here is the receipt, status: LOCAL DRAFT, unread: false, messages: [...Rider paid cash..., ...Here is the receipt...]}]]", "OLD=0 NEW=1", "00:07 +1: All tests passed!". So the inbox card shows the new preview and not the old one. I deleted the file afterwards.
verdicts.corrected_title: Not a bug: the inbox rebuilds on pop because pushSingle's ModalRoute.of(context) makes it depend on the route's status

refuted.title: An out-of-order GPS fix is ignored by navigation but returned as drawable, so the car, camera and arrival check jump back to an older position
refuted.description: setVehicle returns true for a fix older than the last accepted one. Its contract says true means 'the caller should draw it'. _applyDriverPosition then writes that older fix into _driverPosition and _lastLocation, feeds it to the camera (which accepts any fix under 30 s old) and moves the marker. Navigation progress and the banner stay on the newer fix, so the screen and navigation disagree until the next fix.
refuted.failure_scenario: After a resume, the provider delivers a batched or cached fix stamped earlier than the last accepted one. The marker and camera snap back along the road while the banner distance stays put, and _nearArrivalTarget is evaluated from the older point. Verified by reading the code; not run.
refuted.evidence: navigation_controller.dart:221-226 `if (at != null && _lastMeasuredAt != null && at.isBefore(_lastMeasuredAt!)) { return true; }` ; accept_ride_trip.dart:655-669 `if (!_navigation.setVehicle(location)) { return; } ... _driverPosition = next; ... _camera.update(location: location, ...); _vehicle.moveTo(...)`
refuted.suggested_fix: Return false for out-of-order fixes (as for held jumps) so the caller drops them too.

verdicts.reason: The setVehicle contract states the behaviour: navigation_controller.dart:203-204 says 'Returns false only for a fix held back as a GPS jump ... Every other fix returns true.' The finding describes a real path to no out-of-order fix. Fixes come from Geolocator.getPositionStream (driver_location_service.dart:91-97), which delivers in time order. On resume, _startLiveLocation (accept_ride_trip.dart:614-648) awaits a fresh getCurrentPosition and applies it synchronously before any stream event, and it subscribes only after that. Any fix older than 30 s, or with accuracy worse than 50 m, is already dropped by isDisplayableAt (driver_location_repository.dart:35-58). Even if an older fix did arrive, the marker would move back once by a few metres and be corrected by the next fix. The scenario is speculative.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: navigation_controller.dart:203-232, accept_ride_trip.dart:610-690, driver_location_service.dart:91-106. No source that delivers fixes out of order was found.

refuted.title: Picked document is accepted without checking its type; on web any file passes and is shown as a PDF
refuted.description: allowedExtensions is passed to FilePicker.platform.pickFiles, but on web it only sets the input's accept attribute, which is a hint. The user can switch the dialog to 'All files', and a selectFile port can return anything. After the pick the code checks only that the bytes are not empty, then stores the name and bytes and shows 'File selected successfully'. _buildFilePreview shows every non-png/jpg file with the red PDF icon, so a .docx, .heic or .zip looks like an accepted PDF.
refuted.failure_scenario: On the web build the driver opens 'Tap to upload', picks 'All files' and chooses notes.docx. The step shows a green 'File selected successfully' snackbar and a PDF icon labelled notes.docx.
refuted.suggested_fix: After the pick, check file.extension (lower-cased) against the allowed list, and ideally the magic bytes too, and show couldNotReadSelectedFile for anything else.

verdicts.reason: The effect is harmless. The picked bytes are used only for the 60x60 preview in vehicle_document_upload.dart:199-201. Nothing reads selectedFileBytes or selectedFileName outside this State (grep: they are only written at :256-257 and :220-221 and read in _buildFilePreview). Nothing is uploaded or submitted, and the step's Continue button (additional detail/navigation.dart:159-160, controller.moveToNextStep) does not depend on whether a file was picked. So on web a .docx picked through 'All files' changes only the icon shown. On Android and iOS, FileType.custom with allowedExtensions does filter the picker. The selectFile hook is a test injection port. No document review exists that could accept the wrong file (REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:45 says document review is not a connected service).
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _pickAnyFile, _buildFilePreview, the VehicleRegisteration and VehicleInsurance wrappers, and navigation.dart's Continue handler. Grep for selectedFileBytes usages.

refuted.title: Camera capture of vehicle registration/insurance is downscaled into an 800x400 box, so portrait document photos come out at about 300x400 px
refuted.description: The registration and insurance camera capture passes both maxWidth: 800 and maxHeight: 400 to pickImage. image_picker keeps the aspect ratio and fits the image inside both limits. A normal portrait photo (3024x4032) of an A4 or A5 registration certificate becomes 300x400 px, and a landscape one becomes 533x400. That is too low to read the document's text. The Add vehicle document capture in add_vehicle.dart:850-853 uses only maxWidth: 1024 for the same kind of document.
refuted.failure_scenario: The driver holds the phone upright and photographs a registration certificate on the Vehicle registration step. The returned XFile is about 300x400 px and the certificate text cannot be read in the preview or by any later review.
refuted.suggested_fix: Drop maxHeight, or use a symmetric bound such as maxWidth: 1600, maxHeight: 1600, with an imageQuality setting so the size stays bounded.

verdicts.reason: maxWidth: 800 and maxHeight: 400 at vehicle_document_upload.dart:276-278 do downscale the photo. But the captured bytes are only drawn as a 60x60 BoxFit.cover thumbnail (:200) and never go anywhere else. There is no upload, no review and no later reader (bytes are only used in _buildFilePreview, and Continue in navigation.dart:159 ignores them). So 'the text cannot be read by any later review' cannot happen, and the preview cannot show legible text at any resolution. Document review is documented as not connected (REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:45). This only becomes a real problem if a document upload is wired up later.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _openCamera, _buildFilePreview and the parent stepper's Continue. Grep for selectedFileBytes readers: only :186.

refuted.title: A waiting.byCategory block that omits a category drops the seed per-category rules, so XL loses its contract default of 3 free minutes and 3 min no-show
refuted.description: When `waiting.byCategory` is present, _waiting builds the category map only from the entries the document lists. The seed rules (xl: 3 free minutes and 3 min no-show; premium per-minute) are kept only when byCategory is missing altogether. contract.json#configDefaults says the apps fall back to the defaults (freeWaitMin default 5, xl 3) 'when a document lacks a field or has a bad value', and the contract's own sample document lists byCategory for economy and comfort only. With that document, termsFor(category: 'Movera XL') gives 5 free minutes and a 5 min no-show instead of 3/3. An XL driver waits 2 extra unpaid minutes before the waiting fee starts and before the no-show button appears. A broken xl entry ('xl': 'three') also falls to 5, and a test asserts that.
refuted.failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. Applying the contract sample config (DriverAppConfig.fromJson(contract fixture).apply()) and starting an XL pickup: WaitingRules.current.termsFor(category: 'Movera XL').freeMinutes is 5, not 3. The waiting clock bills from minute 5 and the no-show button appears at 5 min.
refuted.evidence:
driver_app_config.dart:257-263 `final byCategory = _map(json['byCategory']); final categories = <String, WaitingRule>{}; if (byCategory == null) { for (final entry in seed.categories.entries) {...} } else { for (final entry in byCategory.entries) {`
contract.json configDefaults: `"freeWaitMin": {"default": 5, "xl": 3}`
contracts/fixtures/config/driver_app_config.json byCategory: only "economy" and "comfort"
refuted.suggested_fix: Start from the seed category rules (rebased to the document currency) and override them with the entries the document provides, instead of replacing the whole map whenever byCategory exists.

verdicts.reason: Leaving the seed rules out when byCategory is present is a consistent contract reading, not a mismatch. byCategory is the admin's full per-category map (CONTRACT.md:198/209/217), and configDefaults says 'Admin exports them where no setting exists yet' (contract.json:649). The real admin exports list every category, xl included with freeWaitMin 3 and noShowAfterMin 3 (test/fixtures/config/driver_app_config.Z001.json, also FR-PC and TN-TC). So a published zone document does not leave XL out. The contract sample fixture is a schema sample, not a published zone. The rider app does the same thing: rider_app_config.dart:385-405 builds byCategory only from the entries listed, so a category that is not listed falls back to the headline terms. Both apps therefore agree on XL. The behaviour for a broken xl entry is pinned on purpose by test/contract/driver_app_config_test.dart:142,165.
verdicts.repro: Traced driver_app_config.dart:237-292 and compared it with rider_app_config.dart:382-405. Checked the waiting.byCategory keys in contracts/fixtures/config/driver_app_config.json (economy and comfort only) against the admin exports in test/fixtures/config/*.json (all 8 categories, xl at 3/3).

refuted.title: Pickup-pay line on Radar offer cards is hard-coded English ('incl. … pickup') in fr/sv
refuted.description: RadarOfferCard renders PickupPayLine(quote: offer.pickupPay) under the fare (radar_offer_card.dart:386). When admin chooses PickupPayDisplay.fareWithPickupLine, the line text comes from PickupPayQuote.line, which concatenates the English words 'incl.' and 'pickup' around the localized amount and leg label.
refuted.failure_scenario: Admin sets pickup pay to 'fare with pickup line'. A French or Swedish driver sees Radar cards reading 'incl. 21,60 kr pickup · 4.2 km · 9 min'.
refuted.evidence:
pickup_pay.dart:48-49 `String? get line => hasPay && display == PickupPayDisplay.fareWithPickupLine ? 'incl. ${pay.formatted} pickup · ${leg.label}' : null;`
radar_offer_card.dart:386 `PickupPayLine(quote: offer.pickupPay),`
refuted.suggested_fix: Move the template to the ARB files (e.g. tr.pickupPayIncluded(amount, leg)).

verdicts.reason: The English line cannot appear in the shipped app. PickupPayQuote.line returns text only when display == PickupPayDisplay.fareWithPickupLine (pickup_pay.dart:48). That display comes from PickupPayConfig.current (pickup_pay.dart:92-96), which is a const PickupPayConfig() with display defaulting to totalOnly (pickup_pay_config.dart:190,200). Nothing in lib/ assigns PickupPayConfig.current or uses fareWithPickupLine. Only test/widget/pickup_pay_card_test.dart and test/core/pickup_pay_test.dart do. No admin or config parser exposes the setting. The untranslated template is latent and needs moving to the ARB files before the display option is wired up.
verdicts.repro: Searched all of lib/ for PickupPayDisplay, fareWithPickupLine, 'PickupPayConfig.current =' and 'display:'. The only production references are the enum definition, the totalOnly default and copyWith.

refuted.title: A malformed Ride-check log is logged with its raw contents and then silently overwritten, losing every saved check
refuted.description: _read catches FormatException and logs it with `$error`. FormatException.toString includes a source excerpt, so trip IDs, reasons containing road names and the driver's free-text 'What happened' note reach the log channel (the same class as the known prefs_trip_history/prefs_active_ride findings, at a new site). It then returns an empty list. The next _save writes only the new record over the key, so all earlier checks are destroyed. Individual rows that fail RideCheckRecord.fromJson are also dropped and erased on the next save. Unlike the support repository (LocalQuarantine.storeOnce) and the other stores, nothing is preserved.
refuted.failure_scenario: A truncated localStorage write (for example, the Safari tab killed mid-write, as recorded in DECISIONS.md) leaves movera_driver_ride_checks undecodable. The next Ride check logs the raw blob and replaces the whole history with one row, and the past checks shown in trip details are gone.
refuted.evidence:
ride_check_log.dart:103-106 `} on FormatException catch (error) { DriverLog.warn('Ride check log malformed: $error'); } return <RideCheckRecord>[];`
ride_check_log.dart:66-76 `final rows = _read(prefs)..removeWhere(...)..add(record); ... prefs.setString(key, jsonEncode({... rows ...}))`
refuted.suggested_fix: Quarantine the raw value (LocalQuarantine.storeOnce) before overwriting, and log only a generic message without the exception's source excerpt.

verdicts.reason: There is no realistic way to reach the malformed state. The only writer of movera_driver_ride_checks is PrefsRideCheckLog._save (lib/core/safety/ride_check_log.dart:62-77). It writes the whole value with a single jsonEncode + prefs.setString, and saves are serialised through _enqueue. On the web, localStorage.setItem is atomic, so a tab kill cannot leave a truncated value. Native SharedPreferences writes are atomic too. The 'Safari tab killed mid-write' premise is not in DECISIONS.md: docs/DECISIONS.md:79-81 is about HtmlElementView rebuilds causing tab crashes, not about partial writes. Rows the app wrote itself always pass RideCheckRecord.fromJson. docs/LOCAL_DATA.md:16-18 also records the intended behaviour: 'A corrupt value is treated as missing by the readers'. The FormatException excerpt in the log (line 104) and the overwrite are both real code, but they only run on externally tampered storage. That is speculative, and the local ride-check log is demo data.
verdicts.repro: Read ride_check_log.dart end to end (the single writer, the _enqueue serialisation, _read's catch). Checked docs/LOCAL_DATA.md:16 (corrupt treated as missing) and docs/DECISIONS.md:79-81 (Safari crash cause, nothing about truncated writes). No test run, because the trigger needs storage that was tampered with outside the app.

refuted.title: Island spring is under-damped although docs/driver-trip-island.md specifies a critically damped spring
refuted.description: The doc states 'IslandMorph owns one critically damped spring controller for width, height and corner geometry'. The spring uses mass 1, stiffness 210, damping 25. Critical damping is 2·sqrt(210) ≈ 28.98, so the damping ratio is about 0.86 (under-damped) and the motion overshoots past 1. The value is then clamped by `_phase`, so the geometry sits pinned at the target while the spring is still overshooting, and the settle takes longer than the visible motion.
refuted.failure_scenario: A resize with incoming velocity (up to 3.0 carried in) overshoots past 1. The clamp holds the island at the target size until the spring comes back, and the outgoing layers only clear when the spring settles. This differs from the documented critically damped motion.
refuted.evidence:
island_morph.dart:146 `const SpringDescription(mass: 1, stiffness: 210, damping: 25),`
island_morph.dart:64 `double get _phase => _motion.value.clamp(0.0, 1.0);`
refuted.suggested_fix: Use damping = 2*sqrt(stiffness*mass) (≈ 29), or update the doc.

verdicts.reason: The mismatch with the doc is real but has no visible effect. With mass 1, stiffness 210 and damping 25 (island_morph.dart:146), the damping ratio is 25/(2*sqrt(210)) ≈ 0.862. Peak overshoot is exp(-ζπ/sqrt(1-ζ²)) ≈ exp(-5.34) ≈ 0.5%. That excursion is clamped by _phase (line 64), and the default AnimationController bounds of 0..1 clamp it as well. The geometry therefore stays at the target during an overshoot of about 0.005 and a short return. The tolerance (distance .001, velocity .01) means settle, and so the clearing of outgoing layers in _settled (lines 67-72), comes only a few ms after the visible motion ends. The code comment ('a soft settle, like the iPhone island') shows the value was chosen on purpose. At most the doc wording in docs/driver-trip-island.md:11 is imprecise.
verdicts.repro: Computed the damping ratio and the overshoot by hand from the SpringDescription at island_morph.dart:146. Traced _phase (line 64), _settled (lines 67-72) and the didUpdateWidget animateWith path.

refuted.title: Fallback location subscription after a failed first fix cannot recover; on web, granting location later leaves Home without GPS
refuted.description: The catch branch in _startDriverLocation says 'Continuous updates can recover when permissions/provider return' and calls _listenToDriverLocation. But DriverLocationService.watchPosition is an async* generator that first awaits _ensurePermission. When permission is denied or location services are off, that throws, the stream emits one error and closes. The onError handler only sets _startLocationFailed and does not resubscribe. Nothing retries until a lifecycle resume, a Recenter tap or Go online. On web, enabling location in the browser's site settings fires no lifecycle event, so Home keeps the grey GPS dot and no car.
refuted.failure_scenario: Web/PWA first launch: the driver blocks location, then allows it from the address-bar permission icon. Home stays without a car and with a grey GPS indicator until they tap Recenter or go online.
refuted.evidence: home_map_sheet.dart:52-55 `// Continuous updates can recover when permissions/provider return. _listenToDriverLocation();`; driver_location_service.dart:91-97 `Stream<DriverLocation> watchPosition(...) async* { await _ensurePermission(); yield* Geolocator.getPositionStream(...)`; home_map_sheet.dart:74-77 onError only `_rebuild(() { _hasLiveDriverLocation = false; _startLocationFailed = true; });`
refuted.suggested_fix: Retry the location subscription with backoff after an error (or listen to permission changes), or correct the comment and offer an explicit retry.

verdicts.reason: The 'no recovery until resume/Recenter/Go online' premise is wrong in practice, because Home restarts location on every lifecycle change. home.dart:188-190 didChangeAppLifecycleState calls _resumeHomeUpdates, which calls _startDriverLocation (home.dart:207) whenever _liveVisible. On web the Flutter engine maps window blur/focus to inactive/resumed (engine web_ui app_lifecycle_state.dart:72-96). Clicking the address-bar permission icon blurs the page, and returning to the page fires focus, which restarts the location start with permission now granted. On Android/iOS, changing permission or location services in Settings or the shade also produces inactive/paused then resumed. The finding's web scenario, where enabling location fires no lifecycle event, therefore does not hold. The comment at line 53-54 is loose but has no user-visible effect.
verdicts.repro: Traced home.dart:188-210 lifecycle handling and /opt/flutter/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/platform_dispatcher/app_lifecycle_state.dart:62-111 (focus->resumed, blur->inactive, visibilitychange). No test run.

refuted.title: WaybillPayment hard-codes 'kr' and öre, so EUR/TND fares get wrong waybill amounts and wrong currency
refuted.description: Money, the contract and DriverAppConfig (currency + rebased waiting rules) support EUR and TND zones. WaybillPayment.fromFare only matches up to 2 decimals (`\d+(?:[.,]\d{1,2})?`), multiplies by 100 and always formats with a ' kr' suffix. So a '24,50 €' fare comes out as '24,50 kr', and a TND fare '125,000 DT' (exponent 3) is read as 125,00 and shown in kr. The same code path drives the offer card's net fare (offer_rules.dart:157 `OfferCardDetails.fare`) and the waybill sheet's 'Paid by the passenger', 'Movera fee' and 'Your earnings' rows.
refuted.failure_scenario: In a zone whose DriverAppConfig currency is EUR, the waybill of a 24,50 € trip lists 'Paid by the passenger 24,50 kr' and 'Your earnings 18,37 kr'. With net-fare offer cards enabled, the card shows '18,37 kr'. In a TND zone the amounts are also off by the exponent (12,500 DT is read as 12,50).
refuted.evidence:
waybill.dart:296 `final match = RegExp(r'\d+(?:[.,]\d{1,2})?').firstMatch(fare);`
waybill.dart:301 `final fareOre = (value * 100).round();`
waybill.dart:333 `return '${_comma ? text.replaceAll('.', ',') : text} kr';`
Throwaway test: EUR 24,50 € → fare=24,50 kr earn=18,37 kr; TND 12,500 DT → fare=12,50 kr earn=9,37 kr
refuted.suggested_fix: Parse with Money.parseLabel (currency-aware, thousands-aware), compute in minor units of that currency, and format with Money.formatted.

verdicts.reason: No shipped path puts an EUR or TND fare on a waybill. docs/DECISIONS.md P2 records SEK/Stockholm as the market. Home builds its dispatch as `widget.dispatchRepository ?? DemoDispatchRepository()` (lib/presentation/driver/home/home.dart:463), and every demo offer is `Money(minorUnits: ...)`, which defaults to SEK (lib/core/dispatch/demo_dispatch_repository.dart:24-438, money.dart:6). OfferWire/ApiDispatchRepository (lib/core/dispatch/api_dispatch_repository.dart:22,136) is the only parser that can produce a non-SEK fare, and only test/round3/driver_admin_offers_dispatch_test.dart constructs it. So the hard-coded 'kr' and 2-decimal parse in WaybillPayment.fromFare (waybill.dart:296-333) cannot be reached with another currency today. It is latent and should be fixed when the API dispatch is wired. A related real limitation: an SEK fare of 1 000 kr or more, written with a thousands space ('1 234,50 kr'), parses as 1,00 kr. Demo fares stay under 300 kr, so this is not reachable today either.
verdicts.repro: Traced the fare sources: grep for ApiDispatchRepository (only tests), the Home dispatch default, and the demo offer Money values (all SEK). Throwaway test test/_audit_u3b5_test.dart (since deleted) printed `big fare=1.00 kr` for WaybillPayment.fromFare('1 234,50 kr').

verdicts.reason: The waybill code does hard-code ' kr' and two decimals (lib/core/waybill/waybill.dart:296-301, 335), but no real runtime path ever gives it a EUR or TND fare. Every fare comes from Money(minorUnits: …) with the default currency 'SEK' (lib/core/money/money.dart:6; lib/core/dispatch/demo_dispatch_repository.dart:24-459). DriverAppConfig is only ever the const seed (currency 'SEK', driver_app_config.dart:36). Nothing in lib passes `appConfig:` to DriverHomeAdminContentService (driver_home_admin_content.dart:607-632), and DriverAppConfig.fromJson has no caller in lib. docs/DECISIONS.md P1/P2 fixes the market as SEK/Stockholm. The Contract v0.3 notes also record that 'Other trip models still carry SEK labels (follow-up)', so this is a known, documented follow-up and not a bug that can be reached today.
verdicts.repro: Grepped lib for currency sources and DriverAppConfig/appConfig injection. All fares are SEK Money, and no runtime code builds a non-SEK config. Not run: the EUR/TND input cannot be produced from any real caller.

refuted.title: Destination mode's per-day limit is read from 'destinationsPerDay' but the contract field is 'perDay', so the admin's limit from a contract document is ignored
refuted.description: The contract's DriverAppConfig schema (contracts/tools/gen_openapi.py:380 and openapi.yaml) defines destinationMode as {perDay: integer >= 0}, and the contract fixture contracts/fixtures/config/driver_app_config.json sends `"destinationMode": {"perDay": 2}`. DestinationModeRules.fromJson reads only json['destinationsPerDay'] and falls back to 2. A contract document with perDay 4 (or 1) is therefore silently treated as 2. DestinationModeSession.refusal then blocks or allows destinations on the wrong count. A perDay of 0, which the contract allows, can never be expressed because _positive rejects 0. The admin export fixtures happen to carry both keys, and the contract-fixture test never asserts destinationsPerDay, so no test can catch this.
refuted.failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. A backend that follows openapi.yaml publishes destinationMode {perDay: 1}. DriverHomeAdminContentService(appConfig: DriverAppConfig.fromJson(doc)).load() returns destinationsPerDay 2, and Home sets DestinationModeRules.current to it. The driver can set a second destination that the zone does not allow.
refuted.evidence:
trip_rules_admin_config.dart:94-95 `destinationsPerDay: _positive(json['destinationsPerDay'], 2).round(),`
contracts/fixtures/config/driver_app_config.json:155-157 `"destinationMode": { "perDay": 2 }`
contracts/tools/gen_openapi.py:380 `("destinationMode", {"type": "object", "properties": {"perDay": i(minimum=0)}}),`
refuted.suggested_fix: Read `perDay` (falling back to `destinationsPerDay` for older exports), accept 0, and add a contract-fixture assertion that uses a value other than the default.

verdicts.reason: The parse mismatch is real: DestinationModeRules.fromJson reads only 'destinationsPerDay' (lib/core/admin/trip_rules_admin_config.dart:94-95), while the contract uses 'perDay', and {perDay: 4} yields 2. But no shipped code feeds it a contract document. Home loads `const LocalDriverHomeConfigRepository().load()` (home.dart:466-468), which uses `const DriverHomeAdminContentService()` with appConfig == null and rulesExport == null. load() (driver_home_admin_content.dart:630-640) then returns null trip rules, and the defaults stay in place. A grep shows no production caller passing `appConfig:` or DriverAppConfig.fromJson output into the service; only tests do. So the admin-limit-ignored scenario cannot happen today. It is a latent contract mismatch to fix when the config document is wired.
verdicts.repro: Traced Home -> LocalDriverHomeConfigRepository -> DriverHomeAdminContentService.load(); grep for `appConfig:` and DriverAppConfig.fromJson in lib found no production caller. Throwaway test printed `perDay4 -> 2`, which confirms the parser gap in isolation.

refuted.title: The contract's nextTrips.on switch is ignored: admin cannot turn next-trip offers off
refuted.description: The contract defines nextTrips as {on: boolean} (gen_openapi.py:381), and both the contract fixture and the admin export send `"on": true`. NextTripRules has no on/off field, and fromJson never reads json['on']. A document with `nextTrips: {on: false}` gives the defaults (offerTypes exclusive + exclusiveReservation, 5 km / 10 min), so NextTripGate.allows still lets next-trip offers through during a trip in a production build (demo: !driverProductionRequested).
refuted.failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. Admin switches next trips off for the zone, so the document says nextTrips {on: false}. The driver app loads it through DriverHomeAdminContentService, and Home sets NextTripRules.current to the defaults. Near the drop-off the driver is still offered a next Exclusive trip.
refuted.evidence:
trip_rules_admin_config.dart:137-158 `factory NextTripRules.fromJson(Object? json) { ... return NextTripRules(offerTypes: types is List ? [...] : base.offerTypes, withinKmOfDropoffOn: ..., ...` (no 'on')
contracts/tools/gen_openapi.py:381 `("nextTrips", {"type": "object", "properties": {"on": b()}}),`
next_trip_gate.dart:28-30 `final r = rules ?? NextTripRules.current; if (r.offerTypes.isEmpty) { return false; } if (r.wholeLastLeg) { return true; }`
refuted.suggested_fix: Parse `on` (default true). When it is false, return rules with an empty offerTypes list (which NextTripGate already treats as off), or add an explicit enabled flag.

verdicts.reason: The parser does ignore 'on': NextTripRules.fromJson (lib/core/admin/trip_rules_admin_config.dart:137-158) never reads it, and {on:false} gives [exclusive, exclusiveReservation]. But the scenario needs a DriverAppConfig to reach Home, and none does. Home's config comes from `const DriverHomeAdminContentService()` with no appConfig or rulesExport (home.dart:466-471, driver_home_admin_content.dart:630-640), so NextTripRules.current stays at its defaults whatever a document says. No production caller passes a parsed contract document. Today this is unreachable: a latent contract mismatch, not a live failure where an admin switch is ignored.
verdicts.repro: Same trace as driver-u7 (no `appConfig:` caller in lib). Throwaway test printed `on:false -> [exclusive, exclusiveReservation]`, which shows the parser gap in isolation.

refuted.title: Older history rows without completedAt are never shown in any period, so they cannot be reached in History
refuted.description: The repository accepts rows with no `completedAt`: the decoder only validates it when present. The screen even prepares them: `day: at == null ? tr.previous : ...`, and the detail screen's `_when` falls back to `whenLabel` 'for an older record without a time'. But `_periodRidesList` returns false for `at == null` in every period. The overview and the All rides list both read only `_periodRidesList`, so such rides are never listed under Today, Week or Month and their detail screen cannot be opened.
refuted.failure_scenario: A receipt saved before completedAt existed, or a legacy row without a time, stays in storage, but the driver can never see it in Earnings & history.
refuted.evidence:
ride_history.dart:102-104 `return _rides.where((ride) { final at = ride.completedAt; if (at == null) { return false; } ...`
ride_history.dart:75 `day: at == null ? tr.previous : DriverDates.numericDate(at),`
history_detail.dart:46-52 `/// ... the saved words for an older record without a time.` `return at == null ? _ride.whenLabel : ...`
prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:251-253: completedAt is only validated when non-null.
Reproduced with a throwaway test: a record with no completedAt ('Pick → Drop') was not found under Today, Week or Month.
refuted.suggested_fix: Show undated rows in an 'Earlier'/'Previous' group, for example in Month or an All view, or count them under the period that their whenLabel implies.

verdicts.reason: Every current writer stamps completedAt. PrefsTripHistoryRepository.add uses `completedAt ?? DateTime.now()` (prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:188, 229), and the completion journal always writes terminalAt (completion_journal.dart:104). It also requires completedAt when reading back (completion_journal.dart:338). An undated row can only be a hand-edited or legacy save, and the earliest version of the repository in git already wrote completedAt. History is also designed to show only Today, Last 7 days and This month: _periodRidesList (ride_history.dart:100-110) feeds both the overview and the All rides list, so every row older than the current month is unreachable in the same way. An undated row is treated like an old row, which matches that design. Nothing is lost from storage either: the row stays and is still counted toward the 500-row cap.
verdicts.repro: Read _periodRidesList and the write paths in prefs_trip_history_repository.dart and completion_journal.dart. Ran `git log --follow` on the repository file: the first version (dfe3ed3) already writes 'completedAt': at.toIso8601String().

refuted.title: Earnings & history crashes (ArgumentError currency mismatch) as soon as the period holds a non-SEK cash trip
refuted.description: `_periodCashBalance` folds every cash trip's balance with `CashBalance.total`, which starts from `Money.ore(0)`, and that is always SEK (cash_balance.dart:54: `balances.fold(Money.ore(0), (sum, item) => sum + item.balance)`). `TripHistoryRecord.cashBalance` builds the balance with `Money.parseLabel`, which keeps the label's own currency ('24,50 €' becomes EUR, '12,500 DT' becomes TND). `Money.operator +` calls `_sameCurrency`, which throws `ArgumentError.value(other.currency, 'currency', 'mismatch')`. `_buildOtherEarningsRow` reads `_periodCashBalance` on every build of the overview, so the throw happens inside build. CashBalanceSheet.build (cash_balance_sheet.dart:49) has the same fold. The contract and ZoneSettings support EUR and TND zones (zone_settings.dart:66-67, 104-105), and RideOffer.fare is a `Money` that keeps its currency, so a cash trip in one of those zones is archived with a non-SEK fare label.
refuted.failure_scenario: A driver in a EUR or TND zone finishes one cash trip, then opens Earnings & history. The overview build throws and the screen shows the red error widget in debug, or a grey box in release. The cash balance sheet throws the same way.
refuted.evidence:
ride_history.dart:141-143 `Money get _periodCashBalance => CashBalance.total(_periodCashTrips.map((trip) => trip.cashBalance!));`
cash_balance.dart:53-54 `static Money total(Iterable<CashBalance> balances) => balances.fold(Money.ore(0), (sum, item) => sum + item.balance);`
money.dart:198-201 `if (other.currency != currency) { throw ArgumentError.value(other.currency, 'currency', 'mismatch'); }`
Reproduced with a throwaway widget test: pumping `DriverRideHistory(loadHistory: () async => [TripHistoryRecord(fare: '24,50 €', paymentMethod: 'Cash', completedAt: now-5min, ...)])` gave `tester.takeException()` = `Invalid argument (currency): mismatch: "EUR"`.
refuted.suggested_fix: Start the fold from the currency of the first balance, or group the totals per currency. Do not add Money values of different currencies.

verdicts.reason: The fold in CashBalance.total (lib/core/earnings/cash_balance.dart:53-54) does throw on a non-SEK balance, but nothing the app runs can put a non-SEK fare into history. History fares come from offer.fareLabel = fare.formatted (lib/core/dispatch/dispatch_repository.dart:114). The only dispatch repository that is wired up is DemoDispatchRepository (lib/main.dart:91, home.dart:463, ride_requests.dart:187), and every demo fare is Money(minorUnits: …), which defaults to SEK (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:24-354). ApiDispatchRepository, which could send EUR or TND, has no caller. DECISIONS.md:44 fixes the market as SEK/Stockholm, and DECISIONS.md:112 records that trip models other than RideOffer still carry SEK labels as an open follow-up. _periodEarnings (ride_history.dart:128-133) is SEK-only in the same way. The crash needs a multi-currency backend that does not exist yet, so it is latent work for the currency follow-up, not a reachable failure.
verdicts.repro: Traced the history fare from TripHistoryRecord.cashBalance (trip_history.dart:63) to CashBalance.fromLabels to Money.parseLabel, back to ride_requests.dart:164 and home_offer_radar.dart:130 (offer.fareLabel), then to the RideOffer sources: only DemoDispatchRepository is constructed, and all its fares are SEK. Ran grep for ApiDispatchRepository( : the definition is its only hit.

refuted.title: The daily destination limit lives only in memory, so restarting or reloading the app resets it
refuted.description: usedToday() counts entries in _started, an in-memory list on a process-wide singleton. Nothing persists it, and LOCAL_DATA.md lists no key for it. refusal() is the only enforcement of the admin's destinationsPerDay, and it is checked when the picker opens on Home (home_map_sheet.dart:273) and on the trip (next_trip_gate.dart:65). The admin limit is described as 'How many destinations one driver can set per day', but a cold start, PWA reload or crash recovery brings the count back to 0.
refuted.failure_scenario: Under the defaults (2 per day) the driver sets Solna at 09:00 and Kista at 11:00. A third try shows 'Today's destinations are used'. They close and reopen the app (or reload the web page) and can set two more destinations the same day, with no limit on how often they repeat this. Worked out from the code.
refuted.suggested_fix: Store the day's start times (for example a dated list in SharedPreferences, added to localDataInventory) and load them when DestinationModeSession is created, or take the count from the backend.

verdicts.reason: The code is as described. The counter is an in-memory list (destination_mode_session.dart:14) and nothing persists it. But the contract gives enforcement of this limit to the backend: contracts/CONTRACT.md:168 lists Destination mode as 'Filters, limits' in the driver column and 'Dispatch filter' in the backend column. DestinationModeRules.current (trip_rules_admin_config.dart:48-49) is itself an in-memory stand-in 'until a backend sets it'. DECISIONS.md:57 and :69 record that each app keeps its current mock and that repositories under lib/core are in-memory seams. The client refusal is a UX pre-check that the documents intentionally keep in memory, not the place where the admin limit is enforced. Setting another destination after a reload does not show the driver a success that did not happen: the mock dispatch has no server-side limit to break.
verdicts.repro: Static trace. Read destination_mode_session.dart:6-50. Its only callers are home_map_sheet.dart:273/309 and next_trip_gate.dart:52-73. Checked contracts/CONTRACT.md:168 (backend 'Dispatch filter'), DECISIONS.md:57/69 and LOCAL_DATA.md (frontend-only demo state; production storage belongs to the server).

refuted.title: DocumentExpiryStore is never reset on logout, so document renewal/approval state and the 'warned' set carry into the next session
refuted.description: _logout in main.dart resets the waybills, dispatch, safety alerts and session singletons, but not DocumentExpiryStore.instance, whose reset() is never called from lib. A renewal sent or approved in one session stays: 'in review', or the document now runs a year. The _warned set also survives, so after logout and back in, the 7-day insurance warning is not issued again and Documents shows the previous session's approval.
refuted.failure_scenario: The driver taps Upload new and then Approve (demo) on the insurance card, logs out, and taps Return to demo. Documents no longer lists the expiring insurance and Home issues no insurance warning, though a fresh session would show 'expires in 7 days'.
refuted.suggested_fix: Call DocumentExpiryStore.instance.reset(), and the notification feed equivalent, from _logout next to the other in-memory resets.

verdicts.reason: main.dart:179-195 does not reset DocumentExpiryStore, but this does no harm. The driver's documents and their review or approval state belong to the driver account (in production the backend supplies them through DocumentExpiryStore.load, document_expiry.dart:110-115). They are not device data. LOCAL_DATA.md:7-14 lists what logout clears, and documents are not on that list. 'Return to demo' (starter.dart:113) signs back into the same single demo driver, so the approved insurance still being approved is the correct account state. The _warned set is documented as 'Warnings not given yet, each step once' (document_expiry.dart:146-147), so not repeating a warning the same account already received is intended. There is no second account that the old state could leak into.
verdicts.repro: Static trace. Read _logout in main.dart:179-195 and DocumentExpiryStore in document_expiry.dart:105-195, and grepped DocumentExpiryStore callers (home_account.dart, document_renewal.dart, driver_notifications_screen.dart). The only re-login path is the single demo account in starter.dart:113.

refuted.title: Home offer-route line animation rebuilds the keyed Home map about 19 times a second (up to 30) and sends up to 7 light polylines per step. This is the intended rate; no harm shown.
refuted.description: `_resumeRouteLine` starts `Timer.periodic(_lineTick /*33 ms*/)`. For the first 2.35 s of every 3.6 s cycle each tick computes a new `OfferLinePhase` and assigns `lightLine.value = OfferRouteLine.light(frame.road, phase)`. That builds 6 soft-edge slices plus one 'rest' polyline, each a `routeSlice` walk over the whole road. The Home map is wrapped in `ValueListenableBuilder(valueListenable: _offerRouteFrame.lightLine)` (home_map_sheet.dart:749), so every tick rebuilds `CustomGoogleMap`. The rebuild recomputes `homeMapLayers`, `DriverRouteStyle.sized`, `OfferRouteLine.sized` (a copyWith on every polyline) and the fade wrappers. `GoogleMap.didUpdateWidget` then diffs every polyline (full-route point lists compared element by element) and sends the 7 changed light polylines to the platform, each re-converted to a JS LatLng path on web. CustomGoogleMap.didUpdateWidget also makes the web.configure/vehicle/gestures JS calls on each tick. The Radar deck, Exclusive sheet or reservation sheet can stay up for a long time while online, so this runs continuously. DECISIONS.md records that per-frame rebuilds of the HtmlElementView map made Safari kill the tab, and fixed it by throttling map updates to 5 Hz. RouteFade's own doc says 'The map takes new markers and lines a few times over the fade, not every frame'. This path brings back a 30 Hz map rebuild on Home.
refuted.failure_scenario: Driver online on web/Safari with Radar offers on the deck: for every 3.6 s cycle, about 70 Home-map rebuilds and about 490 polyline replacements are sent to Maps JS. That is roughly 8,000 map updates in a 1-minute offer window, which causes jank on low-end phones and the same memory and GC pressure the Safari fix was meant to remove. Worked out from the code; not run.
refuted.evidence:
home_offer_route.dart:61 `const Duration _lineTick = Duration(milliseconds: 33);`
home_offer_route.dart:287-296 `frame..linePhase = phase..lightLine.value = OfferRouteLine.light(frame.road, phase, zoom: _routeZoomStep); ... frame.line = Timer.periodic(_lineTick, (_) => tick());`
home_map_sheet.dart:747-756 `ValueListenableBuilder<Set<Polyline>>(valueListenable: _offerRouteFrame.lightLine, builder: (context, light, _) { final layers = layersWith(light); return CustomGoogleMap(...polylines: ...OfferRouteLine.sized(DriverRouteStyle.sized(layers.polylines, ...` 
offer_route_line.dart:125-148 builds up to softSteps(6)+1 polylines per call
refuted.suggested_fix: Throttle the light-line updates to the documented 5 Hz (or fewer steps per sweep), keep the outline and core out of the per-tick rebuild by pushing only the light polylines through a platform `updatePolylines` call (as the live marker does), or draw the sweep in the JS adapter on web.

verdicts.reason: The mechanism is real: a 33 ms Timer.periodic (home_offer_route.dart:61, :296) sets lightLine.value about 2.25 s out of every 3.6 s cycle, and home_map_sheet.dart:747-756 rebuilds CustomGoogleMap on every change. CustomGoogleMap.didUpdateWidget (custom_google_map.dart:311-318) then makes the web.configure, vehicle and gestures calls each time. Two things weigh against it being a bug. The rate looks deliberate: the code comment says '~30 a second at most (light on web)', and 'Only the map redraws for each step of the line animation'. And the 5 Hz fix in DECISIONS.md:79-85 is scoped to AcceptRide markers, not made a general rule. The map is also keyed (_homeMapKey), so the platform view is not recreated, only diffed. No jank or Safari tab kill has been shown.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the tick, the ValueListenableBuilder and didUpdateWidget. What would settle it: profiling Home on Safari/iOS or a low-end Android device with a Radar offer left up for about 1 minute, watching memory, frame times and whether the tab gets killed.

verdicts.reason: home_offer_route.dart:61 sets _lineTick to 33 ms. The Timer.periodic at line 300 assigns lightLine.value whenever the phase changes. home_map_sheet.dart:747-756 wraps CustomGoogleMap in a ValueListenableBuilder on lightLine, so every assignment rebuilds the map widget. That rebuild re-runs homeMapLayers, DriverRouteStyle.sized and OfferRouteLine.sized (a copyWith per polyline), and CustomGoogleMap.didUpdateWidget (custom_google_map.dart:311-319) makes web.configure, vehicle and gestures JS calls with no throttle or web check. This goes against the 5 Hz map-update throttle that DECISIONS.md:81-85 adopted after Safari killed the tab when an HtmlElementView map was rebuilt every frame.
verdicts.repro: Worked from OfferRouteLine.phaseAt (offer_route_line.dart:76-82). Over k in [0, 0.25) light changes every tick. Over [0.25, 0.35) the phase stays (1, 0) and ticks are skipped. Over [0.35, 2.35) front changes every tick. Over [2.35, 3.6) the line is dark and skipped. That gives about (0.25+2.0)/0.033 ≈ 68 map rebuilds per 3.6 s cycle, roughly 1,130 per minute. light() (lines 120-150) builds up to 6 soft slices plus 1 rest polyline on each of them. Not run on a device, so jank or a crash is not shown; the update rate follows directly from the code.

verdicts.reason:
The update rate is real, but it is a deliberate design choice. No documented rule forbids it and no failure has been shown. Four points decide it.

(1) The intent is written down. home_offer_route.dart:60-61 says "The animation's beat: ~30 a second at most (light on web)", and commit c0c319e (#297) deliberately raised it from the old 80 ms / 12.5 Hz glow tick. home_map_sheet.dart:748 says the rebuild is kept to the map on purpose: "Only the map redraws for each step of the line animation".

(2) The precedent the finding cites does not apply. DECISIONS.md:79-85 is scoped to AcceptRide markers, and the earlier audit (docs/audit-2026-10-21/AUDIT.md L2) already found that this 5 Hz throttle no longer exists: AcceptRide's live marker runs on a 33 ms ticker. That audit names the no-remount D-07/D-08 design, not a 5 Hz cap, as what prevents the Safari crash.

(3) The rebuild does not remount anything and sends only what the animation needs. The map has a stable GlobalKey (home.dart:217, home_map_sheet.dart:753). GoogleMap.didUpdateWidget sends only diffs (google_map.dart:482-531). Measured: the outline, the core and the pins are never re-sent. The JS calls in CustomGoogleMap.didUpdateWidget (custom_google_map.dart:311-319) are no-ops or trivial: configure returns early when the padding is unchanged (web/driver_map_camera.js:639-641), and gestures only sets a flag (:224-235).

(4) The only overhead beyond the animation's own polyline changes is the Dart-side diff: about 1.1 ms per update in a debug JIT run on a 1,000-point road. No jank, memory growth or tab kill has been shown. The finding's own failure scenario says "not run". Reducing the rate (the suggested fix) is a product trade-off for the R14-2 animation, not a fix for a defect.
verdicts.repro:
Throwaway test /home/user/Movera-driver-app/test/_audit_u137_test.dart (deleted after the run). It stepped OfferRouteLine.phaseAt in 33 ms ticks over one 3.6 s cycle with the same skip guard as home_offer_route.dart:284. Each kept tick built OfferRouteLine.light on a 1,000-point road, applied DriverRouteStyle.sized and OfferRouteLine.sized, and diffed against the previous set with PolylineUpdates.from. Output: "ticks/cycle=110 mapUpdates/cycle=70 maxLightLines=7 changedPolylines/cycle=395 maxChangedPerTick=7 outlineOrCoreResent=0 dartCostPerUpdate=1113.8us", then "All tests passed!".

So about 70 map rebuilds per cycle (about 19 Hz average, 30 Hz peak) and about 5.6 light polylines sent per rebuild. The outline and core are never re-sent, and the Dart cost is about 1.1 ms per update in debug mode. Nothing was run on a device, and no jank or crash shows up.
verdicts.corrected_title: Home offer-route line animation rebuilds the keyed Home map about 19 times a second (up to 30) and sends up to 7 light polylines per step. This is the intended rate; no harm shown.

refuted.title: ApiDispatchRepository catches only FormatException around offer parsing: a mistyped optional field aborts a list reload halfway or throws out of the SSE listener
refuted.description: `OfferWire.parse` documents that it throws FormatException, but some optional fields are read with casts that throw TypeError: `(json['riderTrips'] as num?)` (line 71), `pickup['address'] as String?` and `dropoff['address'] as String?` (lines 76-77), and `place(stop)['address'] as String?` (line 84). `_upsert` catches only `on FormatException` (306), so a TypeError escapes. In `_load` the maps were already cleared (233-234) before the loop. The exception reaches the outer `catch (_)` ('Offline: the list stays as it was'), `_emit()` is skipped, and `_offers`/`_nextTrips` are left with only the rows parsed before the bad one. The UI keeps the old list, while `claimOffer`'s `_find` and new subscribers' snapshots use the half-filled maps. In the SSE path the TypeError is thrown out of the `listen` onData callback (only FormatException is caught at 267) to the zone, after `_lastSequence` has already moved past the event, so the event is lost and `_emit` never runs.
refuted.failure_scenario: The backend sends one open offer with `riderTrips: "12"` (or a numeric address). Refresh clears the cache, stops at that offer, and never emits: the driver sees stale cards, and Match on one of them returns 'unavailable' because `_find` no longer has it. Over SSE the same offer throws an uncaught error and the feed silently skips that event.
refuted.suggested_fix: Catch all errors in `_upsert` (or make `OfferWire.parse` type-check every field and throw FormatException). Build the new maps in locals and swap them in only after the loop.

verdicts.reason: ApiDispatchRepository is not built anywhere in lib/. grep finds it only in test/round3/driver_admin_offers_dispatch_test.dart:55. Every screen defaults to DemoDispatchRepository (ride_requests.dart:187). No runtime path reaches OfferWire.parse or _upsert with server data. The trigger also requires a contract violation: contracts/openapi.yaml:5513-5515 types riderTrips as integer and :4802-4803 types address as string, so a server that follows the contract cannot produce the TypeError. The narrow catch at api_dispatch_repository.dart:306 is a hardening point for the future adapter, not a reachable defect.
verdicts.repro: Traced the cited lines (71, 76-77, 84, 233-241, 267, 303-308), which match the finding. Then grep -rn ApiDispatchRepository over lib/ and test/: no production instantiation. Checked the contract types in contracts/openapi.yaml.

refuted.title: Offer claim, decline and list calls have no timeout, so a stalled connection leaves 'Matching' on screen with no end
refuted.description: Unlike `RoadRouteService` (`.timeout(timeout)` at road_route_service.dart:96), `ApiDispatchRepository` calls `_client.post`, `_client.get` and `_client.send` with no timeout, and package:http has no default one. Every caller treats only a thrown error as `networkError`: Home `_claimHomeRadarOffer` (home_offer_radar.dart:541-546), `_claimAdminAssign`, `_claimReservation`, `_claimAssignment`, RideRequests `_claimTrip`, and ScheduledRides `_claim`. A request that hangs (half-open TCP on a mobile network) never resolves. `_homeRadarMatchingOfferId` / `_matchingOfferId` / `claimingId` stay set, the Matching spinner never stops, and no other offer can be matched. This class is the contract adapter meant to replace the demo dispatch.
refuted.failure_scenario: With the API adapter installed, the driver taps Match as the phone switches from Wi-Fi to cellular. The POST never completes. The card stays on 'Matching trip…' indefinitely, every other Match is ignored because `_matchingOfferId != null`, and the offer expires server-side unseen.
refuted.evidence:
api_dispatch_repository.dart:347-351
        response = await _client.post(
          _uri('/offers/${Uri.encodeComponent(offerId)}/accept'),
          headers: await _headers(mutation: true),
          body: jsonEncode({'expectedVersion': version}),
        );   // no .timeout
ride_requests.dart:322-330  try { result = await _dispatch.claimOffer(trip.id); } catch (_) { result = const ClaimResult.networkError(); }

verdicts.reason: Same reachability problem: ApiDispatchRepository is never installed in the app. Its only construction is in test/round3/driver_admin_offers_dispatch_test.dart:55. All the cited callers (ride_requests.dart:187 and the Home, scheduled-ride and notification screens) receive DemoDispatchRepository or an injected test double, and the demo does no network I/O. The missing .timeout on _client.post/get/send at api_dispatch_repository.dart:347-351 cannot leave 'Matching' stuck in the shipped app. It should be fixed when the adapter is wired in.
verdicts.repro: grep -rln api_dispatch_repository lib test integration_test returns only the round3 test. Read ride_requests.dart:186-187 (defaults to DemoDispatchRepository) and the post/get/send calls in the adapter.

refuted.title: Analytics crashes with StateError when admin's Stockholm work stats have no inner areas
refuted.description: _demand takes the strongest area with stats.innerAreas.reduce(...). Iterable.reduce throws StateError('No element') on an empty list. StockholmWorkStatsConfig.innerAreas is admin content (DriverHomeAdminContentService is documented as the only thing that changes when the admin backend is connected). An admin who clears the inner-city list, or a zone that has none, makes the Analytics screen throw in build and show the red error box. IslandWaitingSignals handles an empty list correctly, so only Analytics breaks.
refuted.failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. When the admin content sends stockholmWork.innerAreas = [], opening Side menu > Analytics throws 'Bad state: No element' during build.
refuted.evidence:
analytics.dart:186-189 `final strongest = stats.innerAreas.reduce((current, next) => next.demandPercent > current.demandPercent ? next : current,);`
analytics.dart:139 `_demand(const DriverHomeAdminContentService().load().stockholmWork),`
refuted.suggested_fix: Skip the 'strongest area' card when innerAreas is empty (or use a fold with a nullable result).

verdicts.reason: The only caller is analytics.dart:139, `const DriverHomeAdminContentService().load()`, built with no rulesExport or appConfig. stockholmWork therefore always comes from the const seed in driver_home_admin_content.dart:709-730, which has four innerAreas. No code path feeds admin data into this call, so an empty innerAreas list cannot reach reduce today. The crash is hypothetical future admin wiring.
verdicts.repro: Traced the stockholmWork construction in driver_home_admin_content.dart and every reference to innerAreas/stockholmWork in lib (analytics.dart:139 and island_waiting_signals.dart only).

refuted.title: Side menu and Analytics read DriverPerformanceConfig.sample and a fresh content service instead of Home's injected admin config, so they can show different numbers from Home
refuted.description: Home reads performance and work stats from widget.homeConfigRepository (DriverHomeConfigRepository, 'Local seed today, remote later'). The side menu reads DriverPerformanceConfig.sample directly. Analytics uses the static _sample and builds its own `const DriverHomeAdminContentService().load()`, and AcceptanceRate/CancelationRate default to sample. The UI-10 comment says these screens show the same value. Once a repository returns admin numbers, or hides a metric with showRating/showAcceptanceRate = false, Home shows the admin value or hides the row, while the side menu and Analytics keep the sample and ignore the show flags.
refuted.failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. With a homeConfigRepository whose performance rating is 4.61 and showCancellationRate false, the Home performance sheet shows 4.61 with no cancellation row. The side menu shows 4.88, and Analytics shows 4.88 / 94% / 2.4%.
refuted.evidence:
side_menu.dart:289,301 `DriverPerformanceConfig.sample.ratingLabel`
analytics.dart:20 `static const DriverPerformanceConfig _sample = DriverPerformanceConfig.sample;`
analytics.dart:139 `_demand(const DriverHomeAdminContentService().load().stockholmWork),`
home.dart:463-465 `_adminHomeConfig = (widget.homeConfigRepository ?? const LocalDriverHomeConfigRepository()).load();`
refuted.suggested_fix: Pass the loaded DriverHomeAdminConfig (or the repository) to the side menu and Analytics, and respect the show* flags there.

verdicts.reason: No real runtime path today has Home and the side menu disagreeing. The only repository the app wires up is `const LocalDriverHomeConfigRepository()` (lib/main.dart:92, passed at main.dart:204). Its load() calls DriverHomeAdminContentService.load() (lib/core/admin/driver_home_config_repository.dart:16), which sets `performance: DriverPerformanceConfig.sample` (lib/core/admin/driver_home_admin_content.dart:641). The show* flags default to true (driver_home_admin_content.dart:47-49). So Home, the side menu and Analytics all show the same sample values with every row visible. The 4.61 / hidden-row case needs a remote repository that does not exist yet. That is a hazard for a future refactor, not a current bug.
verdicts.repro: Traced every DriverHomeConfigRepository use (grep found only main.dart and home.dart). Read LocalDriverHomeConfigRepository and DriverHomeAdminContentService.load(). Confirmed that performance is DriverPerformanceConfig.sample and the show flags default to true.

refuted.title: RideOffer.reservation throws ArgumentError for any admin reservation whose fare, boost or cash label is not in SEK
refuted.description: Reservation previews come from admin content (ScheduledRidesAdminConfig.homeRequests, dispatch reservations). RideOffer.reservation converts their fare, fareBoost and cashToCollect labels with Money.parseSekLabel and throws when parsing fails. home_scheduled.dart:82 (_soonReservationOffer, the Exclusive step), :233 (Leave now) and :368 (the assigned-ride Exclusive card), plus demo_dispatch_repository.dart:198/549, call it with no try/catch. A EUR or TND reservation ('24,50 €', '12,500 DT'), or a SEK label written as '126,75 SEK kr', raises an uncaught ArgumentError inside a Home timer or build path. The code notes 'Reservation previews still carry SEK labels', but nothing stops a non-SEK zone from sending one, and Money.parseLabel already handles every contract currency.
refuted.failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. In a FR-PC zone, admin sends a reservation preview with fare '32,00 €'. When it reaches its Exclusive step, _soonReservationOffer calls RideOffer.reservation, which throws 'Not a SEK amount'. The Exclusive offer never shows and the error goes to the global error hook. Accepting an assigned EUR ride throws in the same way.
refuted.evidence:
dispatch_repository.dart:88-92 `static Money? _amount(String? label, String field) { if (label == null) return null; return Money.parseSekLabel(label) ?? (throw ArgumentError.value(label, field, 'Not a SEK amount')); }`
home_scheduled.dart:80-83 `return _HomeDirectOffer.fromRide(RideOffer.reservation(request), reason: ExclusiveReasons.pickupSoon);`
refuted.suggested_fix: Parse with Money.parseLabel (which reads €, DT and kr), and skip or log a preview it cannot read instead of throwing in UI paths.

verdicts.reason: No path delivers a reservation that isn't in SEK. DriverHomeAdminContentService.load() (lib/core/admin/driver_home_admin_content.dart:642-648) always builds ScheduledRidesAdminConfig with newRequest: DemoReservations.main and newRequests: DemoReservations.homeRequests. Those are hard-coded seeds with SEK fares ('126.75 kr', '249.25 kr', '248.40 kr', '312.40 kr' at :392/:415/:446/:467). The only other ReservationRequestPreview constructor is the seeded 'scheduled rides' list ('184.00 kr', scheduled_rides.dart:435-437). Nothing reads ReservationRequestPreview from JSON or from admin, and its fields are not tied to the zone currency. DECISIONS.md:112 records that the other trip models still carry SEK labels as a known follow-up. So the ArgumentError at dispatch_repository.dart:88-92 is a strict guard that no reachable input trips today. It becomes a concern only when a real admin reservation feed is wired.
verdicts.repro: Searched lib for every ReservationRequestPreview( constructor and every homeRequests source; all are SEK seed constants. Read DriverHomeAdminContentService.load and DECISIONS.md:112.

refuted.title: Blocked sheet says 'Document approved · You can go online now' while another expired document still blocks going online
refuted.description: showDocumentBlockedSheet decides `cleared` from the one document it was opened for. DocumentExpiryStore.blocking, which the going-online gate in home_account.dart uses, returns the first expired document among all of them. When two documents are expired, approving the first one turns the sheet green: 'Document approved', 'You can go online now.', Done. The next go-online attempt is still refused and another blocked sheet opens. The store's documented job is to receive several documents from a backend through load().
refuted.failure_scenario: Reproduced with a throwaway widget test. I used a store with two expired documents A and B, opened the blocked sheet for A, then called uploadNew('A') and approve('A'). Output: 'AUDIT sheet says go online: true; still blocking: B'.
refuted.suggested_fix: Compute cleared as documents.blocking == null. When another document is still blocking, show that document's state instead of 'You can go online now'.

verdicts.reason: Two expired documents cannot happen in the shipped app. DocumentExpiryStore.load() (lib/core/documents/document_expiry.dart:113) has no caller in lib/. The store therefore always uses demo() (lines 84-108), which builds documents relative to the launch time: expiry in 7, 214 and 320 days, with the real clock (ScheduledClock.realNow; the fast clock is not used here). Only DOC-INS-418 can be expired in a realistic session, so when it is cleared, `blocking` is null and 'You can go online now' is true. The mismatch shows up only with a hand-built two-document seed, as in the finding's test. That is a latent issue for a future backend, not a current runtime path.
verdicts.repro: Traced the DocumentExpiryStore construction, the demo seed and the callers of load() with grep (none in lib/). Read showDocumentBlockedSheet (document_renewal.dart:129-228) and `blocking` (document_expiry.dart:128-135).

refuted.title: Turning Cash rides off (or switching a category off) while a Radar Match claim is in flight drops the won trip and leaves Home stuck in 'Matching'
refuted.description: _setAcceptsCash(false) calls _dismissRadarHomeOffer on every cash card, whatever its match state. _onCategoriesChanged (line 33-35) does the same for cards in a category that was switched off. _dismissRadarHomeOffer (home_offer_radar.dart:479-492) removes the card and its match state but never clears `_homeRadarMatchingOfferId` or `_claimedHomeOffer`. When the claim then succeeds, _claimHomeRadarOffer still matches the id (line 546) and calls _resolveHomeRadarMatchWon. _acceptRadarHomeOffer then returns because the card is no longer listed (line 926), so the trip never opens. `_homeRadarMatchingOfferId` stays set for good: every other card's Match is disabled (onMatch null at line 1127), the radar orb reads 'Matching / Please wait' with no tap, and _scheduleVisibleOffers returns early on every resume (line 1167-1171). The Home sheet that holds the Cash switch can be dragged open while a Radar card is matching, because only an Exclusive offer locks it. The known finding at home_offer_radar.dart:895 covers only the × path into the same function.
refuted.failure_scenario: A cash Radar card is on the deck. The driver taps Match, swipes the Home sheet up and turns 'Cash rides' off before dispatch answers. Dispatch answers success. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test: AcceptRide 0; radar orb 'Matching / Please wait', onTap disabled; the other card's Match button disabled; 20 s later still no trip and only the one claim sent. The driver won a trip they never get, and Home cannot match anything else until they go offline and back online.
refuted.suggested_fix: Skip resolving or claimed cards in _setAcceptsCash and _onCategoriesChanged. Alternatively, have _dismissRadarHomeOffer clear `_homeRadarMatchingOfferId` and `_claimedHomeOffer` when they name the removed offer, and tell dispatch to release a won claim the driver can no longer take.

verdicts.reason: A guard stops this. _dismissRadarHomeOffer starts with `if (offer.id == _homeRadarMatchingOfferId) { return; }` (lib/presentation/driver/home/home_offer_radar.dart:482), added in commit e319b40 'Audit fix D2: a Radar claim in flight is answered before it can be dropped'. When _setAcceptsCash(false) (home_offer_rules.dart:52-56) or _onCategoriesChanged (lines 31-35) dismisses the card being matched, that call returns without removing it. The card stays in _radarHomeOffers, and the claim resolves through _claimHomeRadarOffer (lines 541-568). On success, _acceptRadarHomeOffer finds the card and opens the trip. The removeWhere on _pendingRadarHomeOffers does not touch it either, because a card being matched is on the deck, not pending. The claimed stuck 'Matching' state does not occur.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of home_offer_rules.dart:26-60, home_offer_radar.dart:478-568, and `git log -L` on the guard lines, which shows the D2 fix.
